sold_at: Juvenile product stores, mass merchandisers and other stores nationwide and on various websites from March 2011 through December 2011 for between $14 and $35.

heading: Children's Slides Recalled by Landscape Structures due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: The Slalom Glider is a playground slide that lacks a transition platform on the top and sides on the chute. Children can fall when moving from the ladder to the slide and when descending the chute.
action: Consumers should immediately stop children from using the recalled gliders and owners will be contacted by Landscape Structures regarding removal instructions. Customers will be given the option of replacing the Slalom Glider with another piece of playground equipment, receiving a refund, or receiving credit towards a future purchase.
incidents_text: CPSC and the firm have received 16 reports of injuries to children under 8-years old, including one bruised arm, 14 fractures to arms and legs, one fractured collar bone and one bruised spleen.
sold_at: To schools and other facilities with playground equipment nationwide between January 2006 and December 2011 for about $2300.

product_name: Carter's Watch the Wear Bodysuits and Sleep 'n Play Garments
heading: Weeplay Kids Recalls Infant Bodysuits Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The snaps can detach from the fabric of the garment, posing a choking hazard to infants and young children.
action: Consumers should immediately discontinue use of garments and contact Weeplay to receive free replacement garments.
incidents_text: The firm has received approximately 30 reports of snaps detaching from the garments. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Big Lots, Century 21, Conway, Cookies, Cost Mart, DD's Discount, Edison Childrenswear, Gabriel Bros., Kiddy Time, Kids Place, Kidstown, National Stores, Pamida Stores, Real Value, Regine's, R.H. Reny, Ross, Shoppers World, Valley Wholesale, Variety Wholesalers and Youngland stores nationwide. Recalled garments sold from November 2010 through August 2011 for about $4 to $9.

heading: Bumbleride Recalls Indie & Indie Twin Strollers Due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: The front wheel can break at the axle hub, causing the stroller to tip and posing a fall hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled strollers and contact Bumbleride to receive a free front wheel retrofit kit.
units: About 28,000 (an additional 2,700 were sold in Canada)
incidents_text: There have been 36 incidents of the front wheel cracking, including two reports of the stroller tipping over resulting in minor injuries.
sold_at: Buy Buy Baby and other baby product stores nationwide, online at Bumbleride.com, and other online retailers between January 2009 and January 2012 for between $500 and $700.

heading: LTD Commodities Recalls Sleeper Ottomans Due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: The welding joints on the legs can break, posing a fall hazard to consumers.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the product and contact the firm to obtain instructions on how to obtain a full refund. LTD Commodities is directly notifying known purchasers about the recall.
incidents_text: The firm has received four reports of ottoman legs that have broken, including two reports of minor injuries.
sold_at: LTD Commodities, ABC Distributing and The Lakeside Collection both online and through catalogs between June 2011 and October 2011 for about $170.

heading: Infant Rattles Recalled by Lee Carter Co. Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The rattle's handle is small enough to fit into a child's throat, posing a choking hazard and violating federal rattle standards.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled rattles away from infants and return them to Lee Carter Co. for a full refund or credit towards a replacement product.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Various Mexican specialty craft stores nationwide from February 2001 through October 2011 for about $4.

heading: Mexican Wrestling Action Figures Recalled by Lee Carter Co. Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
hazard_text: The surface paints on the action figures contain excessive levels of lead which is prohibited under federal law.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled action figures away from children and return them to Lee Carter Co. for a full refund or credit towards a replacement product.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Various Mexican specialty craft stores nationwide from June 2000 through October 2011 for between $12 and $14 per pack.

product_name: Travelin' Chef Expandable Thermal Food Carrier
heading: Food Carriers Recalled by California Innovations Due to Freezer Gel Pack Ingestion Hazard
hazard_text: Gel that contains diethylene glycol and ethylene glycol can leak out of damaged freezer gel packs, posing a poisoning hazard if ingested by children or adults.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the gel packs and dispose of them according to federal, state and/or local regulations. It is recommended that consumers contact their local waste disposal authority for instructions. Consumers may return the gel pack to Walmart for a refund of $6 or contact California Innovations customer service at (800) 722-2545 for the same refund.
sold_at: Walmart between August 2008 to December 2011 for about $22.

product_name: Expandable Insulated Lunch Box with Freezer Gel Pack
heading: Expandable Lunch Boxes Recalled by California Innovations Due to Freezer Gel Pack Ingestion Hazard
hazard_text: Gel that contains diethylene glycol and ethylene glycol can leak out of damaged freezer gel packs, posing a poisoning hazard if ingested by children or adults.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the gel packs and dispose of them according to federal, state and/or local regulations. It is recommended that consumers contact their local waste disposal authority for instructions. Consumers may return the lunch box set to Costco for a full refund or may receive a $5 cash refund for the gel pack only by contacting California Innovations.
incidents_text: The firm has received two separate reports of a dog chewing and ingesting gel from the gel pack. One dog reportedly died from ingestion of the gel. The other was reported to have received treatment and has recovered.
sold_at: Costco Wholesale Clubs, Leon Korol and Cost U Less stores between May 2007 and September 2008 for about $10.

product_name: Chariot bicycle trailers and bicycle trailer conversion kits
heading: Chariot Carriers Recalls Child Bicycle Trailers and Conversion Kits Due to Injury Hazard
hazard_text: The bicycle trailer's hitch mechanisms can crack and break, causing the trailer to detach from the bicycle. This poses an injury hazard to children in the bicycle trailer.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled bicycle trailers and bicycle trailer conversion kits and contact Chariot Carriers for a free repair kit which the consumer can install.
units: About 44,000 bicycle trailers and 70,000 bicycle trailer conversion kits
incidents_text: The firm has received 24 incident reports worldwide, three of which occurred in the United States, involving the bicycle trailers and the conversion kits. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty bicycle stores nationwide and on various websites from December 2005 through August 2010 for between $400 and $925 for Chariot bicycle trailers and from October 2002 through August 2011 for between $40 and $70 for bicycle trailer conversion kits.

heading: The Land of Nod Recalls Bed Frames Due to Entrapment Hazard
hazard_text: A child's torso can become lodged in the gap between the footboard's top rail and the mattress, posing an entrapment hazard to the child.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled footboard and contact The Land of Nod for a replacement footboard with a closed-gap design.
incidents_text: The firm has received one report of a child becoming entrapped in the gap. The child was freed by her parents without injury.
sold_at: The Land of Nod stores in Illinois and Washington, The Land of Nod catalog and website from September 2009 through October 2011 for about $600 for the twin size and $700 for full size.

product_name: Bicycle helmets for children and youth
heading: Bicycle Helmets Recalled by Triple Eight Distribution Due to Risk of Head Injury
hazard_text: Product testing demonstrated that these helmets do not comply with CPSC safety standards for impact resistance. Consumers could suffer impact head injuries in a fall.
action: Consumers should stop using the product immediately and contact Triple Eight for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Bicycle and sports stores and other retailers nationwide and online from August 2006 through November 2011 for about $40.

heading: Children's Chairs and Stools Recalled by Elegant Gifts Mart Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
hazard_text: The yellow surface paint on the metal frame of the children's chairs and stools contains excessive levels of lead which is prohibited under federal law.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled tables and folding chairs away from children and return them to any 1 to Seven store in Puerto Rico or contact Elegant Gifts Mart for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: 1 to Seven stores in Puerto Rico from September 2010 through June 2011 for between $5 and $6.

heading: IKEA Recalls to Repair High Chairs Due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: he high chair's restraint buckle can open unexpectedly, posing a fall hazard to the child
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the high chairs and contact IKEA to obtain a free replacement seat restraint.
units: About 169,000 (133,000 in the U.S. and 36,000 in Canada)
incidents_text: KEA has received eight reports worldwide of restraint buckles that opened unexpectedly, including three reports of children who received minor injuries after falling from the high chair.
sold_at: IKEA stores nationwide from August 2006 through January 2010 for about $20.

heading: Madeline Bed Canopy Recalled by Pottery Barn Kids Due to Impact Hazard
hazard_text: The connections of the posts to the top rails of the canopy can come apart, allowing components of the canopy to fall and posing an impact hazard to consumers.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the canopy from the bed and contact Pottery Barn Kids to schedule a free repair.
units: About 7,700 in the United States and 230 in Canada
incidents_text: The firm is aware of 33 reports of components of the canopy falling, including one report of a cut that required stitches and nine other reports of minor cuts, bruises and/or bumps.
sold_at: Pottery Barn Kids stores nationwide, online at potterybarnkids.com and through Pottery Barn Kids catalogs from December 2003 until August 2011. When sold separately, the canopy sold for $150 to $300.

heading: Petit Lem Children's Pajamas Recalled Due to Violation of Federal Flammability Standard
hazard_text: The pajamas fail to meet the federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear posing a risk of burn injury to children.
action: Children should stop wearing the recalled pajamas immediately and consumers should return them to the retailer where they were purchased or Group Lemur for a refund, exchange or store credit.
sold_at: Specialty children's stores and websites from January 2009 to November 2009 for about $30.

heading: Children's Robes Recalled by Hanna Andersson Due to Violation of the Federal Flammability Standard
hazard_text: These children's robes fail to meet the federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear, posing a risk of burn injury to children.
action: Consumers should take these recalled robes away from children immediately and return them to the retailer where purchased for a refund, exchange or store credit.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Hanna Andersson retail stores, catalogs nationwide and the Hanna Andersson website from September 2011 through November 2011 for about $50.

heading: Build-A-Bear Recalls Colorful Hearts Teddy Bears Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The teddy bear's eyes could loosen and fall out, posing a choking hazard to children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled teddy bear from children and return it to any Build-A-Bear store to receive a coupon for any available stuffed animal from Build-A-Bear.
units: 284,000 in the United States and 13,200 in Canada
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Build-A-Bear Workshops nationwide and online at www.buildabear.com from April 2011 through December 2011 for about $18 in the U.S. and $23 in Canada.

heading: Bugaboo Bee Strollers Recalled by Bugaboo Americas Due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: The front swivel wheels can lock while the stroller is in motion, causing the stroller to tip and posing a fall hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled strollers and contact Bugaboo or the retailer where the stroller was purchased to receive free replacement swivel wheels.
units: About 7,000 in the United States and 260 in Canada
incidents_text: Four incidents have been reported where the stroller's swivel wheels locked and the stroller tipped over. In two of these incidents, a baby and a toddler suffered minor injuries.
sold_at: Toys R Us, Buy Buy Baby and other baby product stores nationwide, online at Bugaboo.com and other online retailers between February 2011 and September 2011 for about $650.

heading: Target Recalls Circo Childrens' Travel Cases Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
hazard_text: The surface coating on the travel cases contain excessive levels of lead, violating the federal lead paint standard.
action: Consumers should stop using the product immediately and return it to any Target store for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Target stores nationwide and Target.com from April 2011 through August 2011 for approximately $21.

heading: Bugaboo Car Seat Adapter Recalled Due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: When the adapter is used on a stroller that also has a wheeled board accessory attached for transporting a standing toddler, and the car seat is positioned so the child faces forward, the car seat can disconnect from the adapter and fall.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the adapter and contact Bugaboo for a free service kit and decals.
incidents_text: Bugaboo received one report of the car seat disconnecting from the adapter and stroller frame, causing a minor injury.
sold_at: Babies "R" Us, Buy Buy Baby, Neiman Marcus, other department stores and independent juvenile stores, Bugaboo.com and other online retailers nationwide from December 2005 to July 2011 for about $45.

heading: Toys Distribution Inc. Recalls Rattles Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The recalled rattles can break into small parts, posing a choking hazard to young children and violating the federal safety requirements for rattles. In addition, the size of the handle on some of the rattles is small enough to enter an infant's mouth, lodge in the throat and cause a choking hazard or lead to bruises and lacerations.
action: Consumers should take the recalled rattles away from children immediately and return them to the place of purchase or contact Toys Distribution Inc. to receive a full refund or replacement product.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Small toy stores in Colorado and Texas from December 2009 through December 2010 for about $2.

heading: Children's Pajamas Recalled by Bella Bliss Due to Violation of Federal Flammability Standard
hazard_text: The pajamas fail to meet the federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear posing a risk of burn injury to children.
action: Children should stop wearing the recalled sleepwear immediately and consumers should return it to the retailer where the product was purchased for a refund, exchange or store credit.
sold_at: Bella Bliss catalog and website, and specialty clothing retailers and online stores from January 2008 to June 2011 for about $48 to $58.

heading: Collective Brands Recalls KEDS Girls' Shoes Due to Laceration Hazard
hazard_text: Ornamental stars on the heel of the shoe can loosen, posing a laceration hazard.
action: Consumers should take these shoes away from children immediately and contact Collective Brands to receive a gift card for $30 redeemable at Stride Rite stores or striderite.com.
incidents_text: The firm has received 27 reports of cuts and scratches resulting from metal stars that loosened from the heel of the shoe.
sold_at: Various department stores and online retailers from June through October 2011 for about $23.

heading: Children's Animal Slippers Recalled Due to Choking Hazard; Sold Exclusively at Family Dollar Stores
hazard_text: The animal's eyes can detach from the slippers, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the slippers away from children and return them to any Family Dollar store for a full refund.
incidents_text: Family Dollar has received one report of the eyes detaching from the slippers. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Family Dollar stores nationwide from September 2011 through October 2011 for about $5.

product_name: Swimwear Set With Inflatable Inner Tube
heading: Build-A-Bear Recalls Teddy Bear Swimwear Set Due to Strangulation Hazard
hazard_text: The inner tube accessory can be pulled over a small child's head, posing a strangulation hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the inner tube and return it to any Build-A-Bear Workshop® store to receive a $5 store coupon. If it is not possible to return the inner tube to a store, consumers may contact the company for information about how to receive a refund.
units: About 19,720 units in the United States and 1,100 units in Canada
incidents_text: Build-A-Bear received one report of an incident in which a 3-year-old girl pulled the inner tube over her head and had difficulty removing it.
sold_at: Build-A-Bear Workshop® stores nationwide and online at www.buildabear.com from April 2011 to August 2011 for $12.50.

heading: Boy Scouts of America Recalls Cub Scout Wind Tech Jackets Due to Strangulation Hazard
hazard_text: The jackets have retractable cords with toggles at the hood/neck area and at the waist, which can pose a strangulation or entrapment hazard to children. In February 1996, CPSC issued guidelines which were incorporated into an industry voluntary standard in 1997, to help prevent children from strangling or getting entangled on the neck and waist drawstrings in upper garments, such as jackets and sweatshirts.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the cords from these jackets to eliminate the hazard, or return the jacket to Boy Scouts of America for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Boy Scouts of America retail outlets nationwide and online at www.scoutstuff.org from November 2009 through July 2011 for approximately $32.

heading: Dutailier Group Recalls Drop-Side Cribs Due to Entrapment and Fall Hazards
hazard_text: The slats on the drop side can detach from the top and bottom rails creating a space between the slats. An infant or toddler's body can become entrapped in the space, which can lead to strangulation and/or suffocation. A child can also fall out of the crib.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled cribs and contact Dutailier Group to receive a free repair kit which consists of a new fixed side to replace the drop-side of the crib. In the meantime, parents are urged to find an alternate, safe sleeping environment for the child, such as a bassinet, play yard or toddler bed depending on the child's age.
incidents_text: The firm is aware of 16 reports in which the slats on the drop side became detached from the top or bottom of the drop side rails of a crib. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Children's products stores and other baby specialty stores from January 2009 through February 2010 for between $425 and $775.

heading: Battat Recalls Magnetic Sketchboards; Magnetic Pen Tip Poses Choking Hazards
hazard_text: The magnetic tip of the drawing pen can dislodge from the pen, posing a choking hazard to children.
action: Consumers should immediately take recalled sketchboards away from children and contact Battat to receive a free replacement sketchboard.
units: About 95,000 in the United States and 4,300 in Canada
incidents_text: Battat has received 19 reports of the magnetic tip separating from the pen. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide and by various online retailers from March 2010 to March 2011 for about $16.

product_name: Microfiber Glider Recliners with Ottomans and Leather Glider Recliners with Ottomans
heading: Big Lots Recalls Glider Recliners with Ottomans Due to Entrapment and Finger Crushing Hazards
hazard_text: An exposed gap between the moving parts of the chair and the base framework can allow access to toddlers and infants, posing an entrapment hazard. In addition, other exposed moving parts on the chair and the ottoman can pose finger pinching and crushing hazards to older children and adults.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the chairs and contact Big Lots for a free repair kit that covers the base framework and the moving parts of the chair and ottoman.
incidents_text: CPSC received two reports of children under age two who were found trapped at the neck between horizontal components of the frame at the back of the chair. In both incidents, adults were able to release the children who suffered no permanent injuries.
sold_at: Big Lots stores nationwide from January 2005 through December 2009 for about $170.

heading: Target Recall Children's Frog Masks Due to Suffocation Hazard
hazard_text: The plush frog masks lack proper ventilation. When secured in place across a child's face, it presents a suffocation hazard to the child.
action: Consumers should immediately take masks from young children and return the product to any Target store for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide from August 2011 through September 2011 for about $1.

heading: Guidecraft Recalls Twist 'n Sort Toys Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The small pegs on three of the four posts can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled toys from children and contact Guidecraft to receive a replacement or another product of equal value.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Specialty toy stores and gift shops nationwide, catalogs and online from September 2009 through November 2010 for about $20.

heading: LittleLife Baby Carriers Recalled by Lifemarque Due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: The carriers were sold without bolts that attach the carrier's main frame to the metal stand. Missing bolts cause the carrier to disconnect from the stand and fall backwards, posing a fall hazard to a child in the carrier.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the carriers and check to make sure there are two bolts on each side where the carrier's main frame attaches to the metal stand. If the bolts are missing, contact LittleLife for a free replacement product.
units: About 40 in the United States and 10 in Canada
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Outdoor stores nationwide, Champaign Surplus in Champaign, Ill., Skinny Skis in Jackson, Wy. , Base Camp stores in Montana, and online at www.amazon.com, www.skinnyskis.com, www.thebasecamp.com, and www.MadAthlete.com from January 2011 through July 2011 for about $200.

product_name: "Innovations" and "At Home with Meijer" Roman shades and roll-up blinds
heading: Additional Retail Sales Prompt CPSC and Meijer to Re-announce Roman Shades and Roll-Up Blinds Recall; Strangulation Hazard Posed
hazard_text: Roman Shades - Strangulation can occur when a child places his/her neck between the exposed inner cord and the fabric on the backside of the blind or when a child pulls the cord out and wraps it around his/her neck. Roll-up Blinds - Strangulation can occur if the lifting loops slide off the side of the blind and a child's neck becomes entangled on the free-standing loop or if a child places his/her neck between the lifting loop and the roll-up blind material.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the Roman shades and the roll-up blinds and contact the Window Covering Safety Council for a free repair kit at (800) 506-4636 anytime or visit www.windowcoverings.org. Consumers can also return the products to any Meijer store for a full refund.
units: About 3,200 units (240,000 originally recalled in March 2010)
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Discount retailers, dollar stores, flea markets and other retail liquidators nationwide from March 2010 through September 2011 at various prices. Originally the products were sold at Meijer stores between January 2004 and December 2009 for about $40 before being recalled.

heading: Jogging Strollers Recalled by B.O.B. Trailers Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The stroller canopy's embroidered logo's backing patch can detach, posing a choking hazard to babies and young children.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled strollers until they remove the embroidery backing patch from the interior of the canopy's logo. Consumers should contact B.O.B. Trailers for instructions on removing the backing.
units: About 411,700 in the United States and 27,000 in Canada (357,000 units were recalled in February 2011 due to strangulation hazard posed by canopy drawstring)
incidents_text: The firm has received six reports of children mouthing the detached patch. Gagging and choking were reported in two incidents. The backing was removed from the children's mouth without injury. In each of the reported incidents, the children were seated in an infant car seat attached to the stroller.
sold_at: REI, Babies R' Us and other children's product and sporting goods stores nationwide and Amazon.com between November 1998 and October 2011 for between $280 and $600.

heading: IKEA Recalls Children's Folding Tent Due to Laceration and Puncture Hazards
hazard_text: The steel wire frame of the tent can break, producing sharp wire ends that can protrude through the tent fabric, posing a laceration or puncture hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately take it away from children and return it to their nearest IKEA store for a full refund.
units: About 58,000; 51,000 in the United States and 7,000 in Canada
incidents_text: Three incidents were reported, including one injury. No incidents were reported in the US or Canada
sold_at: IKEA stores nationwide from August 2011 through September 2011 for about $8.

heading: Yu Wei Recalls Drop-Side Cribs Sold Exclusively at JC Penney Due to Entrapment and Suffocation Hazards
hazard_text: The drop-side rails on the crib can malfunction, detach or unexpectedly fall down, causing part of the drop side to fall out of position. When this happens, a space is created into which an infant or toddler can roll and become wedged or entrapped, which can lead to strangulation or suffocation. A child can also fall out of the crib. Drop-side incidents can also occur due to incorrect assembly and due to age-related wear and tear.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled cribs and contact JC Penney to receive a refund based on consumer use of the product.
incidents_text: CPSC and the firms are aware of nine incidents involving drop side rails that malfunctioned or detached, including one report of a child who sustained minor abrasions to the arm.
sold_at: JCPenney.com and in the jcpenney catalog from January 2006 through December 2010 for between $300 and $450.

heading: Shermag Recalls to Repair Drop-Side Cribs Due to Entrapment, Suffocation and Fall Hazards
hazard_text: "The drop-side rail hardware on the cribs can break or fail, allowing the drop side to detach from the crib. When the drop side detaches, a hazardous gap is created between the drop-side rail and the crib mattress in which infants and toddlers can become wedged or entrapped, posing risks of suffocation and strangulation. In addition, children can fall out of the crib when the drop-side rail falls unexpectedly or detaches from the crib. Drop-side rail failures can also occur due to incorrect assembly or with age-related wear and tear."
action: "Consumers should stop using these cribs immediately and contact the firm to request a free repair kit that will immobilize the drop-side. In the meantime, parents are urged to find an alternate, safe sleeping environment for the child, such as a bassinet, play yard or toddler bed depending on the child's age."
incidents_text: CPSC and the firm are aware of 21 incidents involving drop sides that failed or detached. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The Land of Nod and other baby specialty stores from September 2004 through December 2008 for between $400 and $800.

heading: Musical Wooden Table Toys Recalled by Battat Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: "Small pegs on the xylophone toy can loosen and detach, posing a choking hazard to young children."
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled toys away from children and contact Battat to receive a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Battat have received nine reports of loose and detached pegs. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Music and toy stores nationwide and on the Internet from September 2006 to October 2010 for about $30.

product_name: OZOfire™ Pourable Gel Fuel (Formula 4) and SUREFIRE™ Pourable Gel Fuel (Formula 4) Bottles
heading: Fuel Barons Recalls Pourable Gel Fuels Due to Burn and Flash Fire Hazards
hazard_text: The pourable gel fuel can ignite unexpectedly and splatter onto people and objects nearby when it is poured into a firepot that is still burning. This hazard can occur if the consumer does not see the flame or is not aware that the firepot is still ignited. Gel fuel that splatters and ignites can pose fire and burn risks to consumers that can be fatal.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the pourable gel fuel in firepots. Consumers should discard the pourable gel fuel and bottles in accordance with local and/or state environmental regulation(s).
incidents_text: Fuel Barons has received one report of an incident where a man sustained second-degree burns to his hand and wrist.
sold_at: Online at Windflame.com as well as other online retailers from January 2010 until August 2011 for between $8.50 and $22.

heading: LM Import & Export Recalls Toy Cars Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
hazard_text: "Surface paint on the toy cars contains excessive levels of lead, a violation of the federal lead paint standard."
action: Consumers should take these toys away from children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: "Mega Wholesale stores throughout Miami, Florida from September 2010 through January 2011 for between about $2 and $3 per set."

product_name: Little Tikes® Workshop and Tool Sets
heading: Little Tikes Expands Recall of Toy Workshop and Tool Sets Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The recalled workshop and tool sets have oversized, plastic toy nails that can pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the toy nails away from young children and contact the firm for free replacement toy nails.
units: More than 1.7 million additional units (This recall was first announced in August 2009)
incidents_text: The firm has reported two additional incidents, occurring prior to the August 2009 recall, of children who choked when the toy nail became lodged in their throat. Both children were treated in a hospital and made a full recovery.
sold_at: Mass merchandise retailers nationwide from 1990 through 2004 for between $25 and $100.

product_name: Chloe, Sophie and Audrey soft dolls
heading: Dolls Recalled by Pottery Barn Kids Due To Strangulation Hazard
hazard_text: The hair on the Chloe and Sophie dolls may contain loops that are large enough to fit around a child's head and neck, and the headband on the Audrey doll, if loosened, can form a loop that fits around a child's head and neck. These loops can pose a strangulation hazard.
action: Consumers should take the dolls away from children immediately and cut the looped hair of the Chloe and Sophie dolls and remove the headband of the Audrey doll to eliminate the hazard. Consumers may also call Pottery Barn Kids for instructions on how to return the affected dolls for a merchandise credit.
units: About 81,000 in the United States and 1,300 in Canada
incidents_text: The firm has received five reports of dolls with looped hair, including one report in which a loop of the Chloe doll's hair was found around the neck of a 21-month old child. The child was not injured.
sold_at: Pottery Barn Kids stores nationwide, online at www.potterybarnkids.com and through Pottery Barn Kids catalogs from July 2006 to April 2011 for about $40.

heading: Wooden Rattle Recalled by Manhattan Group Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The toy's U-shaped parts can break, posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should take the rattles away from children immediately and return them to the store where purchased to receive a full refund.
units: About 3,300 in the United States and 145 in Canada
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Baby and gift and specialty stores nationwide and online at ManhattanToy.com from March 2011 through July 2011 for about $12.

heading: Pacific Cycle Recalls Swing Sets Due to Fall Hazard; Sold Exclusively at Toys R Us
hazard_text: "The sling-style swing seats can crack or split prematurely, posing a fall hazard to consumers."
action: "Consumers should immediately stop using the sling-style swing seats, remove the seats from the swing set and contact Pacific Cycle to obtain free replacement seats."
incidents_text: "Pacific Cycle has received five reports of the sling-style swing seats breaking during use, including reports of minor injuries involving bruises and scrapes."
sold_at: Toys R Us stores nationwide from January 2011 through May 2011 for about $270.

heading: Riding Toy Recalled by Radio Flyer Due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: The riding toy can tip over allowing a child to fall forward while riding, posing a fall hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled products away from children and contact Radio Flyer to receive a free replacement unit or refund.
incidents_text: The firm received reports of ten incidents with six injuries, including three where teeth were loosened or removed, and three with chin lacerations requiring stitches.
sold_at: Walmart and other retailers, and online at Amazon.com and Target.com from August 2010 through August 2011 for about $20.

heading: Build-A-Bear Workshop Recalls Lapel Pins Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
hazard_text: Surface paints on the lapel pin contain excessive levels of lead which is prohibited under federal law.
action: Stop using the lapel pins and return the lapel pin to any Build-A-Bear Workshop store to receive a $5 store coupon. If it is not possible to return the pin to a store, you can contact the company for alternate instructions on receiving a refund.
units: About 26,500 pins in the United States and 2,200 in Canada
incidents_text: No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Build-A-Bear Workshop stores nationwide and online at www.buildabear.com from July 2009 through October 2010 for $3.50 in the US and $4 (CDN) in Canada.

heading: Toy Keys with Remote Recalled by Battat Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The metal toy keys and the plastic key ring can break, posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled toy keys away from children and contact Battat to receive replacement keys.
units: About 1,080,000 in the United States and 3,600 in Canada
incidents_text: CPSC and Battat have received 17 reports of keys breaking, and 14 reports of key rings breaking. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Retailers nationwide and online sellers from April 2010 to May 2011 for B. FunKeys, and from January 2006 to December 2009 for Parents Magazine keys for about $9.

heading: Strollers Recalled by phil&teds USA Due to Risk of Injury from Brake Failure
hazard_text: "The brake mechanism on the strollers can fail, posing an injury hazard."
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the product and contact phil&teds to arrange to receive a upgraded brake assembly. Explorer owners will receive a new frame fitted with an upgraded brake assembly. Consumers can perform an in-home swap out of the affected frame. Hammerhead owners will receive a pre-paid return shipping container in order to return the stroller to phil&teds where the brake assembly will be replaced and the stroller returned.
units: "Explorer: 7,400 in the U.S. and 1,900 in Canada; Hammerhead: 160 in the U.S. and 65 in Canada"
incidents_text: Eight incidents have been reported globally; none in North America. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: "Sold online at philandteds.com, pishposhbaby.com, and albeebaby.com; and at Babies R Us and specialty juvenile retailers in the United States and Canada from August 2010 through June 2011 for between $475 and $500."

heading: Prime-Line Products Recalls Child Bathtub Non-Slip Pads Due To Fall Hazard
hazard_text: "Some pads do not stick to the bathtub surface, posing a fall hazard to consumers."
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the pads and contact Prime-Line to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: Prime-Line has received one report of the pad failure. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: "Ace Hardware & Menards nationwide between May 24, 2010 and June 13, 2011 for about $6."

heading: Child Safety Latches and Outlet Covers Recalled by Prime-Line; Screw Breaks Can Allow Unintended Access
hazard_text: The screws on the safety latches and outlet covers can loosen and/or break. When this happens, young children can gain access to electrical outlets and other potentially hazardous items.
action: Consumers should immediately contact Prime-Line to receive a free replacement kit.
incidents_text: Prime-Line has received four reports of screws breaking. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Drawer and cabinet latches were sold at Ace Hardware, Bostwic-Braun, Cal-Do-It Centers, Do-It-Best, Friedman Brothers, Menards, Orgill, The Andersons Inc. and True Value stores nationwide between October 2010 and June 2011 for between $2.50 and $2.70. Outlet covers were sold at Ace Hardware, Cimarron Lumber & Supply, Do-It-Best, Friedman Brothers, Handy Hardware, Menards and W.E. Aubuchon stores nationwide between October 2009 and June 2011 for about $3.50.

heading: Target Recalls Children's Task Lamps Due to Laceration and Fire Hazards
hazard_text: "Lamps can overheat, causing the adhesive inside the lamp socket to melt and migrate into the bulb area of the socket. The cooled glue can adhere to the light bulb base and make the bulb difficult to remove which can result in a broken light bulb, posing a risk of laceration to consumers. Melted flammable glue that migrates onto the electrical components of the lamp poses a risk of fire."
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the lamps and return them to any Target store to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: Target has received six reports of glue on the lamp socket melting and migrating into the bulb area of the socket. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide and Target.com from January 2011 to April 2011 for about $13.

heading: Mini Stars Building Sets Recalled by Edushape Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: Plastic knobs can break from the center of the stars, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled Mini Star building sets away from children and contact Edushape for a free replacement set or credit towards another Edushape product of equal or lesser value.
units: About 18,000 (additional star building sets were recalled in September 2010)
incidents_text: CPSC and Edushape have received two reports of the knobs breaking off from the center of the stars. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Small retail stores nationwide, online at Toys R Us.com, Amazon.com and CSN on walmart.com from January 2007 through December 2009 for between $10 and $50.

product_name: GNC Women's Ultra Mega®, Ultra Mega Active, Ultra Mega Energy and Metabolism, and GNC Prenatal Formula with Iron multivitamins
heading: Women's Multivitamins Recalled by GNC Due to Failure to Meet Child-Resistant Closure Requirements
hazard_text: The product contains iron, but does not have child-resistant packaging as required by federal law. If ingested by a child, these vitamins could cause serious injury or death.
action: Consumers should keep these products out of the reach of children and return them to the GNC store where they were purchased to be exchanged for a replacement bottle or refund.
incidents_text: No incidents or injuries have been reported.
sold_at: GNC retail stores nationwide and at the GNC website from March 2011 through May 2011 for between approximately $9 and $35.

heading: Risk of Strangulation Prompts Recall to Repair Roman Shades by The Shade Store
hazard_text: Strangulations can occur when a child places his/her neck between the exposed inner cord and the fabric on the backside of the blind or when a child pulls the cord out and wraps it around his/her neck.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled shades and call the Window Covering Safety Council (WCSC) for a free repair kit toll-free at (800) 506-4636 anytime or visitwww.windowcoverings.org. The Shade Store is contacting all known customers.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Five showroom locations and online at www.theshadestore.com from February 2006 through March 2011 for between $120 and $355 per shade.

heading: Children's Sleepwear Recalled by Sage Creek Organics Due to Violation of Federal Flammability Standard
hazard_text: The garments fail to meet the federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear posing a risk of burn injury to children. The garments are being recalled because they do not meet the tight-fitting sizing requirements.
action: Consumers should immediately return the garments to either the place of purchase or to Sage Creek Organics for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Small boutiques nationwide and online at the company's website www.sagecreekorganics.com from August 2010 to February 2011 for approximately $35.

heading: International Vitamin Corporation Recalls Live Better Vitamins Due to Failure to Meet Child-Resistant Closure Requirement
hazard_text: The iron supplements are not in child-resistant packaging as required by the Poison Prevention Packaging Act. Ingesting multiple iron supplement tablets at once can cause serious injury or death to young children.
action: Consumers should keep this product out of reach of children and call International Vitamin Corporation to receive a free replacement child-resistant cap.
incidents_text: No injuries or incidents have been reported.
sold_at: "A& P Liquor, A&P, Pathmark, Waldbaum's, The Food Emporium, Super Fresh and Food Basics grocery stores in CT, NY, NJ, PA, DE, MD, MA, VA and the District of Columbia between June 2009 and October 2010 for about $8."

heading: Cost Plus Inc. Recalls Wooden Animal Drum Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
hazard_text: The paint used on the drum is in excess of the maximum allowable level of 90 ppm, a violation of the federal lead paint standard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the toy and return it to Cost Plus World Market for a full refund.
sold_at: Cost Plus World Market stores nationwide from December 2010 through May 2011 for about $7.

heading: Swing Sets Recalled by Adventure Playsets due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: The wood in the posts of the fort sections on the swing sets can weaken due to rotting, posing a fall hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled swing sets and contact Adventure Playsets to obtain a free repair kit. Repair kits will include the appropriate angled or vertical upright posts for each model with instructions for dissembling and reassembling each set.
units: Approximately 240,000; a number of these products were recalled in November 2009 for a similar hazard, which listed 275,000 playsets in the U.S. and 6,800 in Canada.
incidents_text: Adventure Playsets has received more than 500 complaints reporting concern over the weakened wood in the 2x4 plastic-coated uprights. One report of a fall was received when the ladder failed resulting in bruises and scratches.
sold_at: Academy Sports (the Yukon); Mills and Menards (the Ventura/II) all from 2005 to 2007; Mills (the Belmont) in 2004; Toys-R-Us (the Bellevue/II); and Walmart (the Tacoma/II, Durango/II, and Sedona). The units sold for $300-$600.

heading: GAMMA Sports Recalls Children's Tennis Racquets Due to Risk of Lead Exposure
hazard_text: The orange grip tape on the tennis racket's handle contains high levels of lead. Lead is toxic if ingested by young children and can cause adverse health effects.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled tennis racquets away from children and contact GAMMA Sports for a free replacement grip kit. GAMMA Sports is directly contacting all known purchasers of the recalled tennis racquets.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Online at www.gammasports.com, www.atssports.com and www.holabirdsports.com from December 2010 through March 2011 for about $15.

heading: Rugby Children's Pain & Fever Concentrated Drops Recalled Due To Failure to Meet Child-Resistant Closure Requirement
hazard_text: " This over the counter medicine contains acetaminophen which calls for child-resistant packaging as required by the Poison Prevention Packaging Act. Although the original bottle has child-resistant packaging, a separate dropper unit provided for dispensing the drug to children does not. When in use, a child can access the medicine, posing serious health problems or death if more than the recommended dosage is consumed."
action: "Consumers should immediately store this product with the child-resistant closure in place and keep it out of the reach of children. To arrange for a free replacement dropper, contact Altaire Pharmaceuticals at (800) 258-2471 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday."
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: "Drug stores, grocery stores and other retailers nationwide between January 2009 and June 2011 for about $4."

heading: Target Recalls Infant Girls Sandals Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: "The decorative plastic flowers can detach, posing a choking hazard."
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the sandals and return them to any Target store to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: Target has received eight reports of the decorative flowers detaching from the sandals. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Target stores and Target.com nationwide from January 2011 to May 2011 for about $10.

heading: Britax Recalls B-Nimble Strollers Due to Risk of Brake Failure
hazard_text: An audible click heard when the brake pedal is pressed can give a false impression that the brake is fully engaged when it is not. When the brake is not engaged, the stroller can move unexpectedly posing a risk of injury to the child occupant.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using their strollers and contact Britax for information and to request an improved replacement stroller. Consumers who resume use of their strollers while awaiting the replacement should always ensure that the brake is fully engaged.
units: About 20,000 in the United States and 800 in Canada
incidents_text: Britax has received seven reports of the brake not being fully engaged. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile product and mass merchandise stores nationwide and online retailers between September 2010 and June 2011 for about $200.

heading: Child's Entrapment Death Prompts Big Lots Recall of Metal Futon Bunk Beds
Emma's Garden Polka-Dot Girls' Dresses Recalled by TJX Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The decorative buttons on the front of the dress can detach, posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately take the dresses away from children and return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.
units: About 21,000 in the U.S.; 2,600 in Canada
incidents_text: None reported in the United States or Canada
sold_at: T.J. Maxx sold the pink and white design and Marshalls sold the black and white design in the United States from February 2011 through May 2011 for about $13. Winners stores sold both designs in Canada, from March 2011 through April 2011 for about $17.

heading: Target Expands Recall of Child Booster Seats Following Additional Reports of Falls
hazard_text: The booster seat's restraint buckle can open unexpectedly, allowing a child to fall from the chair and be injured.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled booster seats and return them to any Target store for a full refund.
units: About 375,000 (This recall was first announced in Aug. 2009)
incidents_text: Target has received 10 additional reports of booster seat buckles opening unexpectedly, including three reports of bumps and/or bruises when a child fell forward out of the booster seat, hitting an object or the floor.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide from January 2005 through June 2009 for about $13.

heading: Excite USA Recalls Toy Helicopters Due to Laceration Hazard; Sold Exclusively at Rite Aid Stores
hazard_text: The plastic blades of the helicopter can detach during operation, posing a laceration hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled helicopters away from children and return the product to any Rite Aid store for a full refund.
incidents_text: Three incidents were reported, two to Excite and one to CPSC. Two of these included laceration injuries.
sold_at: Exclusively at Rite Aid Corporation stores nationwide from January 2011 through May 2011 for about $7.

product_name: American Girl Crafts™ Pearly Beads & Ribbon Bracelets kit
heading: EKSuccess Brands Recalls American Girl Crafts Jewelry Kit Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
hazard_text: The surface coating on some of the beads contains excessive levels of lead, which is prohibited under federal law.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled kits and any finished bracelets made from the kits away from children and contact the company for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Michaels Stores and other retailers nationwide from September 2009 through June 2011 for about $8.

heading: Kahn Enterprises Recalls Beeni Baby Hats Due to Asphyxiation Hazard
hazard_text: "A baby can spit up during use, posing an asphyxiation hazard."
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the hats and contact Kahn Enterprises to receive a full refund. Kahn Enterprises will provide consumers with a postage paid label to return the product. The firm is directly contacting consumers who purchased the recalled baby hats.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Beeni Baby's website www.beeni.net from January 2009 through May 2011 for about $25.

heading: Lan Enterprises Recalls Zooper Strollers Due to Strangulation Hazard
hazard_text: The opening between the armrest bar/snack tray and seat bottom of the stroller can allow an infant's body to pass through and become entrapped at the neck, posing a strangulation hazard to young children when a child is not harnessed. When using a stroller, parents are encouraged to always secure children by using the safety harness, and never leave the child unattended.
action: LAN Enterprises LLC is no longer in business. The remedy for this recall is no longer available.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Juvenile product and mass merchandise stores nationwide and online retailers, including at Amazon.com, Costco.com and Dmartstores.com from May 2009 to May 2011 for between $200 and $800.

heading: Dream on Me Recalls Drop-Side Cribs Due to Entrapment, Suffocation, Laceration, and Fall Hazards
hazard_text: Full-Size Cribs: The drop-side rail hardware can break or fail, allowing the drop side to detach from the crib. When the drop-side rail partially detaches, it creates a space between the drop side and the crib mattress. An infant or toddler's body can become entrapped in the space, which can lead to strangulation and/or suffocation. A child can also fall out of the crib. Portable Cribs: The drop-side rail hardware can break or fail, allowing the drop side to detach from the crib or fall unexpectedly. In addition, the portable crib mattress support hardware and the drop-side release latch can break easily, and the slats can loosen or break and detach from the crib. Children can also cut themselves on exposed hardware inside the cribs.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these cribs and contact the company. Full-Size Cribs: Consumers will be given a free kit that will immobilize the drop side. Kits will be available beginning June 30, 2011. Portable Cribs: Consumers can receive a free replacement portable crib with fixed sides. Replacement cribs will be available in mid-July 2011.
incidents_text: CPSC and the firm know of 69 reports of incidents involving these cribs. A 1-year-old boy sustained a scratch to the nose when he became trapped between the mattress support and side rail of his portable crib. An 8-month-old girl sustained a minor injury on her head from exposed plastic hardware inside the portable crib.
sold_at: Toys R Us, Walmart and Target stores nationwide and online at Amazon.com. The full-size cribs were sold from January 2006 to December 2009 for about $200. The portable cribs were sold from September 2007 to December 2009 for about $150.

heading: Additional Fingertip Amputations and Lacerations Prompt Reannouncement of November 2009 Recall of Strollers by Maclaren USA
hazard_text: The stroller's hinge mechanism poses a fingertip amputation and laceration hazard to the child when the consumer is unfolding/opening the stroller.
action: The recall remedy is no longer available. Destroy and discard the recalled strollers.
units: About one million (this product was first announced in November 2009)
incidents_text: Maclaren has received a total of 149 reported incidents with the strollers, including 37 reported injuries that occurred after the stroller was recalled in November 2009. These reported injuries include five additional fingertip amputations, 16 additional lacerations and 16 additional fingertip entrapments/bruising. At the time of the original recall, there were 15 incidents, including 12 reports of fingertip amputations in the United States.
sold_at: Juvenile product and mass merchandise retailers nationwide from 1999 through November 2009 for between $100 and $360.

product_name: Bumble Bee and Lady Bug Infant Slipper Socks
heading: Meijer Recalls Infant Slipper Socks Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The balls at the end of the bug's antennae can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled slipper socks away from children and return them to any Meijer store for a full refund.
incidents_text: Meijer received one report of a ball detaching from the antennae. It was found in a child's crib. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Meijer stores in Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan and Ohio from June 2009 through March 2011 for about $4.

heading: UJ Trading Recalls Knight Hawk Toy Helicopters Due to Fire Hazard
hazard_text: The battery housing under the helicopter canopy can overheat while charging, posing a fire hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled helicopters away from children and contact UJ Trading to receive a full refund. UJ Trading will provide consumers with a postage paid label to return the product.
incidents_text: None reported by UJ Trading.
sold_at: Toy, hobby and other stores, including mall kiosks, nationwide and online at www.UJToys.com from April 2010 through April 2011 for about $36.

heading: CPSC Alert: Consumers Urged To Stop Using phil&teds USA Clip-on Chairs Due To Serious Dangers Posed To Children
hazard_text: The clamps can detach from a variety of different table surfaces. Additionally, the chairs can detach when children move around or use their feet to push against other objects. Staff also determined that the lack of adequate space between the horizontal metal bar at the front of the chair and the clamps can cause children's fingers to be severely pinched, lacerated, crushed or amputated if caught between the bar and the clamp when the chair detaches.
action: CPSC is urging consumers to stop using some metoo clip-on chairs immediately.
incidents_text: CPSC staff is aware of numerous incidents involving the affected metoo chairs.

heading: G.A. Gertmenian and Sons Recalls Toy Story 3 Bowling Game Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
hazard_text: The red paint used on some bowling pins has been measured to be in excess of the maximum allowable level of 90 ppm, a violation of the federal lead paint standard.
action: Consumers should stop using the bowling pins immediately and contact the manufacturer for a free replacement set.
incidents_text: G.A. Gertmenian and Sons, LLC has received no reports of incidents or injuries.
sold_at: Walmart Stores in the U.S. between September 1, 2010 and September 25, 2010 for about $18.

heading: Girl's Hooded Sweater Recalled by El Gringo Imports Due to Strangulation Hazard
hazard_text: The hooded sweaters have drawstrings through the hood which can pose a strangulation or entrapment hazard to children. In February 1996, CPSC issued guidelines, which were incorporated into an industry voluntary standard in 1997, to help prevent children from strangling or getting entangled on the neck and waist drawstrings in upper garments, such as jackets and sweatshirts.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the drawstring from the sweatshirt to eliminate the hazard or contact El Gringo Imports for instructions on how to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Pike Place Market in Seattle from November 2009 to August 2010 for between $20 and $25.

heading: Sandbox Medical, LLC Recalls Pacifier Clip Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: "The clip can break apart, posing a choking hazard to young children."
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the pacifier clip and throw it away. Consumers should contact Sandbox Medical for a free replacement.
incidents_text: Sandbox Medical has received two reports that the clip broke apart during use. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Sandbox Baby's website - www.gumdroppacifier.com - from February 2011 through March 2011 for about $3.

heading: Cribs Recalled by ducduc Due to Fall and Entrapment Hazards
hazard_text: The bottom rails on the crib sides can separate from the sides when the mattress is in the lowest position, causing the spindles to separate and the mattress to drop. This poses fall and entrapment hazards for young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these cribs immediately if the mattress is in the lowest position. Consumers should contact ducduc, if the company has not already contacted them, for a free repair kit which includes new crib sides. Ducduc is contacting each customer directly. In the meantime, parents are urged to find an alternate, safe sleeping environment for their child, such as a play yard, bassinet or toddler bed, depending on the child's age.
incidents_text: The manufacturer has received five reports of separated rails. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: ducduc New York showroom, online at www.ducducnyc.com, at specialty stores and through interior designers nationwide from January 2009 through February 2011 for between $1,500 and $1,800.

heading: Children's Scooters Recalled by Kiddieland Due to Laceration Hazard
hazard_text: A child's finger can get caught in the hinge mechanism between the steering column and the platform, posing a laceration hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled scooters away from children and contact Kiddieland for a free repair kit.
units: About 16,000 in the United States and 700 in Canada
incidents_text: CPSC and Kiddieland have received two reports of children whose fingers got caught in the hinge mechanism and required stitches.
sold_at: Toys R Us and JCPenney from January 2009 through February 2011 for about $40

heading: Wrist Rattles and Baby Booties Recalled by Midwest-CBK Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: "The pom-poms attached to the wrist rattles and booties can detach, posing a choking hazard."
action: "Consumers should immediately take these recalled products away from children and return them to the store where they were purchased or to Midwest-CBK for a full refund. If you are unable to return the product to the store where it was purchased, contact Midwest-CBK to receive a prepaid shipping label."
units: "More than 10,000 wrist rattles and 11,000 pairs of baby booties in the United States and 600 wrist rattles and 700 pairs of baby booties in Canada"
incidents_text: The firm has received one report of a pom-pom detaching from the wrist rattle. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: "Gift stores, drug stores, décor outlets and variety stores nationwide from June 2009 through March 2011. The wrist rattles sold for about $5 and the booties sold for about $13."

heading: Girl's Clothing Recalled by My Michelle Due to Risk of Lead Exposure
hazard_text: The jewelry and decorative trim attached to the girl's garments contain high levels of lead. Lead is toxic if ingested by young children and can cause adverse health effects.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled garments away from children and contact My Michelle for information on receiving a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Burlington Coat Factory, Dillard's, J.C. Penney, Kohl's, Army and Air Force Exchange (AAFES), K & G Fashion Superstore and other retail stores nationwide from January 2011 through March 2011 for about $38.

heading: Fashionviews Inc. Recalls P.Jamas Children's Sleepwear Due to Violation of Federal Flammability Standard
hazard_text: The garments fail to meet federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear, posing a risk of burn injury to children.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled sleepwear immediately and return the product to the retailer where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Boutique shops nationwide and the www.p-jamas.com website from January 2006 through October 2010 for between about $50 and $100.

heading: Pampers® Natural Stages Pacifiers Recalled by Key Baby Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: The pacifiers fail to meet federal safety standards and pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled pacifiers away from infants and contact Key Baby for instructions on returning the product for a full refund or $10 coupon toward the purchase of any Pampers® Natural Stages products.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Retail stores nationwide from April 2010 through February 2011 for about $6.

heading: Arm's Reach Concepts Recalls Infant Bed-Side Sleepers Due to Entrapment, Suffocation and Fall Hazards
hazard_text: When the fabric liner is not used or is not securely attached, infants can fall from the raised mattress into the loose fabric at the bottom of the bed-side sleeper or can become entrapped between the edge of the mattress and the side of the sleeper, posing risks of suffocation.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled bed-side sleepers and visit www.armsreach.com/instructions to view and download assembly instructions and to make sure that the product is properly configured. Consumers should also contact the company by phone or via the company website to receive hard-copy instructions by mail and an assembly/warning label. Consumers who are missing the fabric liner or other components should immediately contact Arm's Reach for an alternative remedy.
incidents_text: CPSC and Arm's Reach have received 10 reports of infants falling from the raised mattress into the bottom of the sleeper or becoming entrapped between the edge of the mattress and the side of the bed-side sleeper. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Burlington Coat Factory, Babies R Us and other retail stores nationwide from September 1997 through December 2001 for about $160.

heading: Infantino Recalls Toy Activity Trucks Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: "The plastic beads on the activity truck's bead runs can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children."
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled toy away from children and contact Infantino to receive a free replacement toy.
units: "About 40,500 in the United States and 1,900 in Canada"
incidents_text: "Infantino has received 28 reports of the plastic beads detaching from the bead runs on the activity trucks, including two reports of young children gagging on the plastic beads."
sold_at: "Babies R Us, Toys R Us, Meijer, TJ Maxx, Marshalls and other toy stores nationwide from September 2009 through February 2011 for about $15."

hazard_text: Missing safety pegs can create a situation where the crib's drop-side rail disengages from the track. This can create a hazardous space in which an infant can become entrapped and suffocate.
action: CPSC urges parents and caregivers to immediately stop using cribs that are missing a safety peg on either leg of the drop side and contact Delta to receive a free, easy-to-install repair kit. Parents and caregivers are encouraged to find a safe, alternative sleep environment for their child until the repair kit, with new safety pegs, is safely installed on the recalled cribs.
incidents_text: At the time of the October 2008 recall announcement, there were reports of two entrapments and nine detachments in cribs without safety pegs.
sold_at: The cribs were sold at major retail stores including Kmart, Target and Walmart between January 1995 and December 2005 (through September 2007 for model 4624) for about $100.

heading: Girls' Jeans for Toddlers Recalled by Parigi Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: Decorative rhinestones and sequins on the jeans' pockets can pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the jeans away from children and return them to the retail store where they were purchased for a full refund, or contact the firm for instructions on how to return the product by mail for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Various specialty stores nationwide and online through Amazon.com from May 2010 through June 2010 for about $13.

heading: Matilda Jane Recalls Girl's Chelsa Dress Due to Choking Hazard
hazard_text: "The buttons can come off, posing a choking hazard."
action: Anyone possessing this dress should return it for repair or refund by contacting Matilda Jane Clothing.
incidents_text: Matilda Jane has received one report of an incident with no injuries.
sold_at: "In-home trunk shows and online from February 1 through February 25, 2011."

heading: Atico International USA Recalls Holiday Rattle Baby Slippers Due to Choking Hazard; Sold Exclusively at Walgreens
hazard_text: The internal stuffing and rattle inside the slippers decorative figures can be pulled out, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: The firm is out of business, the remedy is no longer available, and the product should be discarded or destroyed.
incidents_text: Atico received one report of a 7-month old baby that was found beginning to turn blue with the slippers' stuffing in its' mouth. The baby's father removed the stuffing. hazard_text: Roman Shades: Strangulations can occur when a child places his/her neck between the exposed inner cord and the fabric on the backside of the blind or when a child pulls the cord out and wraps it around his/her neck. Roll-up Blinds: Strangulations can occur if the lifting loops slide off the side of the blind and a child's neck becomes entangled on the free-standing loop or if a child places his/her neck between the lifting loop and the roll-up blind material. Roller Blinds: Strangulations can occur if the blind's continuous loop bead chain or continuous loop pull cord is not attached to the wall or the floor with the tension device provided and a child's neck becomes entangled in the free-standing loop.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using all Roman shades with inner cords, all roll-up blinds, and all roller blinds that do not have a tension device, and contact the Window Covering Safety Council at (800) 506-4636 anytime for free repair kits or visit www.windowcoverings.org.
