incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Longs Drug Stores nationwide from April 2006 through May 2006 for about $40.

product_name: Jet StreamersTM Water Blasters Pool Toys

hazard_text: The handlebars, wheels and wheel brakes can break and detach, causing the rider to lose control, fall and possibly suffer injuries.

heading: Speed Buckle Harnesses Used During Mountain and Rock Climbing Recalled for Fall Hazard
hazard_text: The harness could be threaded incorrectly. If threaded incorrectly, the webbing will easily slip when loaded. Incorrectly threaded buckles can loosen, which could cause climbers to slip out of the harness and fall.

incidents_text: None reported

action: Parents should stop their children from wearing the recalled lounge pants immediately and return them to the place of purchase for a refund. If consumers are unable to return their recalled item back to the place of purchase, they should contact the firm.

incidents_text: Aqua-Leisure and CPSC are aware of nine incidents. There have been six reported injuries, including a concussion, a broken arm, fractured ribs and a wrist sprain.

heading: Juicy Couture Children's Jewelry Recalled for Lead Poisoning Hazard

heading: Bicycle Child Carriers Recalled Due to Fall Hazard
hazard_text: If the seat is not fully seated on the rack, the plastic guide tabs on the carrier can break. If these tabs break, it could cause the seat to fall off. This poses a risk of serious injury to a child seated in the carrier.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the bicycle child carriers. Do not return the carrier to store. Contact PTI Sports for a free safety bracket and revised installation instructions.

heading: Metal Charms Sold with Twentieth Century Fox DVDs Recalled for Toxic Lead Hazard
hazard_text: The recalled charms contain high levels of lead. Lead is toxic if ingested by young children and can cause adverse health effects.

heading: Trendset Originals Recalls Girls' Sweaters with Drawstrings Due to Strangulation Hazard
hazard_text: A drawstring is threaded through the hood of the garment, posing a strangulation hazard to children. In February 1996, CPSC issued guidelines to help prevent children from strangling or getting entangled on the neck and waist by drawstrings in upper garments, such as jackets and sweatshirts.
action: Consumers can remove the drawstrings to eliminate the hazard or return the hooded drawstring sweater to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Exclusively at Gordman's Department stores nationwide from September 2005 through November 2005 for about $10.

heading: Child's Death Prompts Replacement Program of Magnetic Building Sets
hazard_text: Tiny magnets inside the plastic building pieces and rods can fall out. Magnets found by young children can be swallowed or aspirated. If more than one magnet is swallowed, the magnets can attract to each other and cause intestinal perforation or blockage, which can be fatal. This product is unsuitable for young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the magnetic sets and return the sets to Rose Art for a free replacement product suitable for young children under the age of 6. Consumers should be sure to keep all small magnet parts out of the hands of children who mouth objects, especially children under the age of three.
incidents_text: CPSC is aware of 34 incidents involving small magnets, including one death and four serious injuries. A 20-month-old boy died after he swallowed magnets that twisted his small intestine and created a blockage. Three children ages ranging from 3 to 8 had intestinal perforations that required surgery and hospitalization in intensive care. A 5-year-old child aspirated two magnets that were surgically removed from his lung.

hazard_text: The band on the watch contains liquid petroleum distillates. If punctured the watch band could leak. Petroleum distillates could be harmful if ingested and cause irritation to the skin or eyes on contact.
action: Consumers should immediately take these watches away from young children and return the watches to the store where purchased for a refund or contact the firm.
incidents_text: CPSC and Almar Sales Co. have received one report of a 2-year-old child who ingested the petroleum distillate after biting into the watch band. The child suffered irritation of the mouth and throat.
sold_at: Exclusively at Dollar General Stores nationwide from March 2005 through July 2005 for about $2.

heading: CPSC, The Gymboree Corp. Announce Recall of Baby Sandals
hazard_text: A plastic flower attached to the sandals can pull or snap off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the sandals and return them to a Gymboree store for a refund. Consumers also can return the sandals to Gymboree via mail. Contact Gymboree for return instructions.
incidents_text: Gymboree has received four reports of the plastic flower coming off of the sandals. One child reportedly pulled the flower off of the sandal, placed it in her mouth and started to choke, and another child was reported to have bitten a flower off of the sandal.
sold_at: Gymboree stores and Web site nationwide from May 2005 through July 2005 for between $22 and $28.

product_name: Kelty Speedster Deluxe and Speedster Deuce Jogging Strollers
heading: CPSC, Kelty Announce Recall of Speedster Jogging Strollers
hazard_text: Stroller handle can disconnect from stroller frame during use.
action: Consumers should stop using these recalled strollers and return them to the store where purchased for a refund. Contact Kelty for a free daypack. Known purchasers were sent direct mail notification of this recall. All affected units in distribution have been located.
incidents_text: Kelty received two reports of a handle disconnecting during use. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile baby product stores, sporting goods stores and Web retailers from May 2005 thru June 2005 for between $335 and $410.

heading: CPSC, Fourstar Group Announce Recall to Repair Kid's Folding Chairs
hazard_text: The chair's safety lock can fail, allowing the chair to collapse or fold unexpectedly. Children's fingers can become caught or entrapped in the hinge and slot areas of the chair, posing a pinch or cut hazard. This can cause severe lacerations and fingertip amputations to children's fingers.
action: Consumers should stop using the chairs immediately and contact Fourstar for instructions on how to receive a free repair kit to replace the locking pin.
incidents_text: CPSC and Fourstar Group are aware of three incidents involving children. One resulted in a laceration to the finger and three finger fractures, the second incident resulted in a fracture and laceration to the fingers, and the third incident resulted in a pinched finger.
sold_at: Discount and grocery stores nationwide from July 2003 through July 2005 for about $5 individually or about $25 for a set.

heading: CPSC, Idea Nuova Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Children's Folding Chairs
hazard_text: The chair's safety lock can fail, allowing the chair to collapse or fold unexpectedly. Children's fingers can become caught or entrapped in the hinge and slot areas of the chair, posing a pinch or cut hazard. This can cause severe lacerations and fingertip amputations to children's fingers.
action: Consumers should stop using these chairs immediately and contact Idea Nuova for instructions on how to receive a free repair kit to replace the locking pin.
incidents_text: CPSC and Idea Nuova are aware of five incidents involving children. In one incident, there was a fingertip amputation, the second incident involved a fingertip amputation and a laceration, and the third incident involved a finger fracture and a laceration. There were no injuries reported in the other two incidents.
sold_at: Discount department and toy stores nationwide from September 2004 through June 2005 for between $15 and $25 per set.

heading: CPSC, Meco Corp. Announce Recall of Children's Folding Chairs
hazard_text: Children's fingers can become caught or entrapped in the hinge and slot areas of the chair, posing a pinch or cut hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the chairs and contact Meco for instructions on receiving a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Meco are aware of three incidents. Two resulted in pinched fingers and there was one laceration to a child's finger.
sold_at: Furniture and wholesale club stores nationwide from July 2003 through May 2005 for between $25 and $40.

heading: CPSC, H&M Announce Recall of Baby Denim and Knit Jackets
hazard_text: The metal buttons can come loose and detach from these garments, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Take these jackets away from young children immediately and return the jacket to any H&M store for a full refund.
incidents_text: H&M has received one report of the metal buttons detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: H&M retail stores nationwide from January 2005 through May 2005 for about $15.

heading: CPSC, Radio Flyer Inc. Announce Recall of Toddler Walker Wagon
hazard_text: The tips of the clickers, which make a clicking sound when the Walker Wagon wheels move, can break off. The broken clickers pose a choking or aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these recalled Walker Wagons away from young children and contact Radio Flyer for free replacement clickers.
incidents_text: Radio Flyer has received 11 reports of the tips breaking off the clickers on these Walker Wagons. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Toy, department and discount stores, in catalogs, and by Web retailers from August 2003 through May 2005 for about $80.

product_name: "So Hot Way Cool Free Wheel Trucks"
heading: CPSC, Target Announce Recall of Children's Toy Trucks
hazard_text: Small parts could break off the truck, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toy trucks away from children and return them to the nearest Target store for a gift card in the amount of a full refund ($5.00, plus applicable state taxes).
sold_at: Target Stores nationwide from April 2005 through May 2005 for about $5.

product_name: Nature's Bounty and Natural Wealth Brand Multivitamins
heading: CPSC, NBTY Inc. Announce Recall of Multivitamins
hazard_text: The vitamins contain iron, but do not have child-resistant packaging as required by federal law. They could cause serious injury or death if ingested by a child.
action: Consumers should keep this product out of the reach of children and return it to the store where it was purchased or contact NBTY for information on receiving a refund or replacement.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Various drug and grocery stores and independent distributors nationwide from July 2004 through March 2005 for about $4.

heading: CPSC, Pokémon USA Announce Recall of Pokémon Plush Toys

product_name: Graco Duo Tandem Stroller, Graco MetroLite Stroller
heading: CPSC, Graco Children's Products Inc. Announce Recall of Duo Tandem and Certain MetroLite™ Strollers
hazard_text: These strollers can fail to latch properly and unexpectedly collapse while in use. This can result in broken bones, cuts, bumps, bruises and other injuries to young children riding in the stroller and consumers pushing the stroller.
action: Consumers should stop using these strollers immediately and contact the firm to receive a free repair kit. The kit includes a custom-designed latch that consumers should attach to the stroller's frame to ensure it is properly latched. The repair kit will be available in approximately 1 to 2 weeks.
units: About 1 million Duo Tandem and about 143,000 MetroLite strollers
incidents_text: For the Duo Tandem strollers, Graco has received reports of 306 collapses causing 230 reported injuries, including a broken arm, and a cut to a child requiring 46 stitches. For the MetroLite strollers, Graco has received reports of 223 stroller collapses causing 34 reported injuries including 18 bumps and bruises to the head or body. Other injuries associated with both strollers include cuts, scrapes, scratches, pinched fingers and muscle pulls.
sold_at: The Duo tandem strollers sold at: Discount, department and juvenile product stores nationwide from January 1994 through December 2000 for between $80 and $150. The MetroLite strollers sold at: Discount, department and juvenile product stores nationwide from November 2000 through December 2002 for between $100 and $200.

heading: CPSC, Dorel Juvenile Group Issue Alert on Safety 1st Tubside Bath Seats
CPSC, Pottery Barn Kids Announce Recall of Outdoor Trunks
hazard_text: A problem with the lid support on the trunk could cause the lid not to stay open, posing the risk of an impact injury to a child's head, fingers or hands.
action: Consumers should immediately stop young children from using these outdoor trunks and contact Pottery Barn Kids to determine if their trunk is included in the recall. Pottery Barn Kids will provide consumers with a replacement trunk or refund.
incidents_text: No injuries or incidents have been reported.

heading: CPSC, Pottery Barn Kids Announce Recall of Toy Chests
hazard_text: A problem with the lid support on the toy chest could cause the lid not to stay open, posing the risk of an impact injury to a child's head, fingers or hands.
action: Consumers should immediately stop young children from using these toy chests and contact Pottery Barn Kids to determine if their toy chest lid support needs replacement. Pottery Barn Kids will provide consumers with a free lid support replacement kit.
incidents_text: No injuries or incidents have been reported.
sold_at: Pottery Barn Kids' Web site, catalog and retail stores nationwide from December 2003 through April 2005 for $349.

heading: CPSC, Prestige Toy Corp. Announce Recall of Spinning Water Teethers
hazard_text: The plastic spinner in the center of the teether can break, causing small beads to fall out. This poses a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these teethers away from young children and return the item to Prestige Toy Corp. for a full refund.
incidents_text: Prestige Toy Corp. received one report from a consumer that the spinning component of one of these teethers broke apart, releasing two small beads. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: Carter's Stores nationwide from March 2005 through April 2005 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Nashbar Direct Announce Recall of Bicycle Trailers
hazard_text: The bicycle trailers can become unstable when changing directions due to incorrectly assembled hitch mechanisms, posing a risk of injury to the riders.
action: Consumers should stop using the bicycle trailers immediately and contact Nashbar for instructions on how to return the product and receive a full refund, plus a $20 gift certificate toward your next purchase.
incidents_text: Nashbar has received eight reports of misassembled hitch mechanisms. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Nashbar catalog and Web site sales from October 27, 2004 through May 10, 2005 for about $150.

heading: CPSC, Shakespeare Fishing Tackle Division Announce Recall of Children's Fishing Poles
hazard_text: The paint on the rods of these fishing poles contains lead. Lead is toxic if ingested by young children and can cause adverse health effects.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled fishing poles and contact Shakespeare Fishing Tackle for information on receiving a free replacement fishing kit.
incidents_text: The firm has not received any reports of complaints related to this product. This voluntary recall is being conducted to prevent any possibility of injury or illness.
sold_at: Discount department, sporting good and toy stores nationwide from August 2001 through June 2005 for between $9 and $13.

heading: CPSC, Kids II Inc. Announce Recall of Doorway Baby Jumpers
hazard_text: The plastic clamp that attaches the jumper seat to a door frame can break, which can cause the unit to fall to the floor. This poses an injury hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the product immediately and disable the jumper by cutting a one-inch portion of the yellow strap just below the clamp. To receive a free replacement product, consumers should cut out the white warning label from the canvas seat and mail the label and the one-inch portion of the yellow strap to Kids II at 555 North Point Center East, Suite 600, Alpharetta, GA 30022.
incidents_text: Kids II have received 49 reports of the clamp breaking with 12 reported injuries, including a possible mild concussion, skinned knee, cut lips, and bumps and bruises.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and juvenile specialty stores nationwide from December 2003 through May 2005 for about $30.

product_name: Baby Connection Fun Frog Soft Gym
heading: CPSC, Wal-Mart Stores and Infantino Announce Recall of Fun Frog Soft Gyms
hazard_text: A cap on the wire supports inside the soft gym's upright arms can detach, allowing the wire to poke through the fabric. This poses a laceration and puncture hazard to babies.
action: Consumers should return the recalled soft gyms to their nearest Wal-Mart store to receive a refund.
incidents_text: Infantino has received four reports of incidents involving the support wire poking through the soft gym's fabric arms. Of the four incidents reported, two involved babies being scratched by the exposed wire.
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores nationwide from October 2004 through May 2005 for about $20.

product_name: Fisher-Price® Power Wheels ® Lightning PAC Scooters and Fisher-Price® Power Wheels® MX3TM Mini Bikes
heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Scooters and Mini Bikes
hazard_text: If tires are over-inflated, the plastic rim within the wheel can break, causing the tire to rupture. This poses the risk of facial and hand injuries while inflating the tire. Note: These scooters and mini bikes were previously recalled in 2003 due to motor control circuits that could malfunction causing the scooters and mini bikes to continue to run after the power or throttle button was released.
action: Consumers should take the recalled scooters and mini bikes away from children immediately and contact Fisher-Price to receive new warning labels and a free tire gauge to provide assistance during inflation. To prevent over-inflation, Fisher-Price recommends using a manual pump to inflate the tires.
incidents_text: For the Lightning PAC Scooter, Fisher-Price has received six reports of incidents, including two reports of facial injuries and two reports of hand injuries to children and adults. For the MX3 Mini Bike, Fisher Price received one report of a facial injury.
sold_at: Discount department and toy stores nationwide from November 2001 through April 2003 for about $250 for the scooters and $200 for the mini bikes.

heading: CPSC, The Perrigo Co. Announce Recall of Multivitamins
hazard_text: The vitamins contain iron, but do not have child-resistant packaging as required by federal law, which could cause serious injury or death if ingested by a child.
action: Consumers should keep this product out of the reach of children and return it to the nearest H.E.B. retail store for a refund or replacement.
incidents_text: No injuries or incidents have been reported.
sold_at: H.E.B. retail stores, only in Texas, from December 2003 through April 2005 for about $4.

heading: CPSC, Summit Marketing International LLC Announce Recall to Repair Children's Folding Chairs
hazard_text: The chair's safety lock can fail, allowing the chair to collapse or fold unexpectedly. Children's fingers can become caught or entrapped in the hinge and slot areas of the chair, posing a pinch or cut hazard. This can cause severe lacerations and fingertip amputations to children's fingers.
action: Consumers should stop using the chairs immediately and discard or destroy them. The firm is out of business, and a remedy is no longer available.
incidents_text: The firm had received seven reports of the chairs collapsing, resulting in four fingertip amputations, one laceration, and bruises to children's fingers.
sold_at: Hardware, discount department, toy, grocery and drug stores nationwide from September 2002 through May 2005 for about $10 individually and for about $45 for a set.

heading: CPSC, Delta Enterprise Corp. Announce Recall of Lov's Pacifiers
hazard_text: The pacifiers are banned under federal law. They failed federal safety tests when the nipples separated from the base. This poses a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should discard the pacifiers and contact the firm for instructions on how to obtain a refund or replacement product.
incidents_text: CPSC has received one report of a 6-month-old child who was found gagging on the nipple that had separated from the pacifier. The child was not injured.
sold_at: Small retail stores from November 2001 through December 2004 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Pamela Drake Inc. Announce Recall of Wooden Push Toys
hazard_text: Small parts can break off posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these recalled push toys away from young children and return the toys to Pamela Drake Inc. or their local retailer for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Toy and hobby stores nationwide from February 2005 through March 2005 for between $15 and $24.

heading: CPSC, Dollar General Corp. Announce Recall of Metal Heart-Shaped Pendants
hazard_text: The recalled heart-shaped pendant contains high levels of lead, posing a serious risk of lead poisoning to young children. Lead poisoning in children is associated with behavioral problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation.
action: Consumers should take these necklaces away from children immediately and return them to Dollar General stores for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Dollar General stores nationwide from May 2003 through April 2005 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, RadioShack Announce Recall of Video Head Cleaner
hazard_text: The cleaning solution bottle, which is labeled as containing isopropanol, actually contains methanol. Methanol can be fatal or cause blindness if swallowed. It is much more toxic than isopropanol. Also, the cleaning solution bottle does not have special cautionary labeling and child-resistant packaging, as required by Federal regulation for methanol.
action: Consumers should immediately place this product out of reach of children and return the product to the nearest RadioShack store for a refund, or dispose of the bottle of cleaning fluid in accordance with all state and local requirements.
incidents_text: RadioShack has received 39 reports from their poison center of children accessing this product. No injuries or illnesses have been reported.
sold_at: RadioShack stores nationwide and www.radioshack.com from December 1995 through January 2005 for about $13.

product_name: Fisher-Price Lil' Wagster Dragster push toys
heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Push Toys
hazard_text: A young child's chin, jaw, and teeth can get lodged in the opening at the top of the push toy's round-shaped handle and incur injuries.
action: Consumers should take the recalled push toys away from young children immediately and contact Fisher-Price to receive a repair kit and installation instructions.
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has received nine reports of injuries associated with the push toy's handle including loose teeth, cut gums and bruises to the mouth and chin.
sold_at: Discount department stores and toy stores nationwide from December 2002 through February 2005 for about $13.

heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Pogo Sticks
hazard_text: An internal metal pin can wear down, causing the pogo sticks to remain stuck in the down position and release unexpectedly, posing a risk of fall or facial impact injuries to children.
action: Consumers should take the products away from children immediately and contact Fisher-Price to receive a free replacement pogo stick.
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has received 17 reports of incidents with the pogo sticks, including one report of two teeth being lost and one report where stitches were required. Other injuries involved cuts and bruises to the face, arms and legs from fall injuries.
sold_at: Discount department and toy stores nationwide from January 2002 through August 2004 for between $25 and $30.

heading: CPSC, Simplicity Inc. Announces Recall of Cribs

action: Consumers should contact Simplicity Inc. to receive a refund.
incidents_text: Simplicity Inc. has received four reports of consumers who noticed paint peeling off their crib. No injuries have been reported.

hazard_text: The chair's safety lock can fail, allowing the chair to collapse or fold unexpectedly. Children's fingers can become caught or entrapped in the hinge and slot areas of the chair, posing a pinch or cut hazard. This can cause severe lacerations and fingertip amputations to children's fingers.
action: The firm is out of business, the remedy is no longer available, and the product should be discarded or destroyed.
sold_at: Hardware, discount department, toy, grocery and drug stores nationwide from September 2002 through April 2005 for about $10 individually and for about $30 for a set.

product_name: Okie Dokie® Striped Bodysuits with Puffy Appliqué
heading: CPSC, J.C. Penney Corp. Announce Recall of Children's Bodysuits
hazard_text: The appliqué can detach from the garment, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled bodysuits immediately and return them to any J.C. Penney store for a full refund.
incidents_text: J.C. Penney has received three reports of the appliqués detaching from the bodysuit. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: J.C. Penney stores and Web site from October 2004 through February 2005 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Royal Seating Ltd. Announce Recall of Children's Chairs
hazard_text: The seat portion of the chair can detach from the leg base possibly causing a child to fall to the floor.
action: Owners who have not already been directly contacted by Royal Seating should visit the firm's Web site or call Royal Seating toll-free to receive information about having chairs tested and replaced if needed.
incidents_text: Royal Seating Ltd. has received three reports of the chair's legs separating from the seat. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: Furniture dealers and catalogs to schools and similar institutions between February 1, 2004, and November 20, 2004, for $29. This recall includes only chairs bought during this time period.

product_name: Light-up Pacifier, New Style Piano, and High Toys Choochoo Toy Train
heading: CPSC, California International Trading Announce Recall of Pacifiers and Two Electronic Toys
hazard_text: The pacifiers and toys can easily break apart, exposing small parts. This poses a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled pacifiers and toys away from young children and call California International Trading to find out how to get a refund and postage reimbursement.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Swap meets and flea markets in the Los Angeles area from July 2004 through February 2005 for between $1 and $2.

heading: CPSC, Carter's® Announce Recall of Carter's Brand Children's Overalls
hazard_text: The plastic center of the decorative snaps on these garments can detach, posing a choking hazard.
action: Contact Carter's to receive a refund.
incidents_text: Carter's has received 14 reports of snap centers detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Style 435-646 was sold exclusively through Carter's retail stores from July 2004 through March 2005 for about $26. Style 435-092 was sold through Carter's retail stores and other retailers nationwide from August 2004 through March 2005 for about $28.

heading: CPSC, Zebco Announce Recall of Children's Fishing Poles
CPSC, Wal-Mart Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Karaoke Cassette Player/Recorders
hazard_text: The paint on the five control buttons of the karaoke player contains excessive lead, posing a lead poisoning hazard to young children. Lead poisoning in children is associated with behavioral problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems, and growth retardation.
action: Consumers should return the recalled karaoke players to their nearest Wal-Mart store to receive a refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores nationwide from June 2003 through March 2005 for about $20.

product_name: My First Crayon-BallTM and My First Crayon-BallTM Activity Set
heading: CPSC, Baja Products Announce Recall of My First Crayon-Balls™ and My First Crayon-Ball™ Activity Sets
hazard_text: Small crayon balls can break loose from the plastic base of the products. This can pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or call Baja Products for a replacement product.
incidents_text: None reported

product_name: Flashing Pacifier or 2-in-1 Flashing Pacifier with Whistle Necklace
heading: CPSC, Solar Inc. Announce Recall of Flashing Toy Pacifiers
hazard_text: The nipple can detach from the base, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should discard the pacifiers or return them to the place where purchased to obtain a refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Small retail stores, distributors, dollar stores and on Solar's Web site from January 2004 through February 2005 for about $1.

product_name: Reebok Children's Windwear and Fleece Jacket and Pant Sets
heading: CPSC, Reebok, and Adjmi Announce Recall of Children's Reebok Jacket and Pant Sets
hazard_text: The zipper slider and pull on the jackets can detach, if pulled when the jacket is open. The detached zipper slider and pull can pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled product away from young children and contact Adjmi recall hotline to receive a replacement product.
incidents_text: Reebok has received three reports of zipper sliders/pulls that detached. No injuries have been reported.

heading: CPSC, Graco Children's Products Announce Recall of Toddler Beds
hazard_text: A child's arm, leg or foot can become entrapped between the slats in the guard rails or footboard. This can result in broken bones, sprains and other injuries to young children.
action: Consumers should remove the guard rails from the recalled Graco toddler beds immediately and call the firm to receive a free retrofit kit. The kit includes custom designed mesh coverings that must be attached to the guard rails and footboard to prevent entrapment. The mesh coverings will be available in 6 to 8 weeks.

heading: CPSC, Delta Enterprise Corp. Announce Recall to Repair Portable Cribs

hazard_text: The zipper-pull mechanism can detach from the zipper, posing a choking hazard to children.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled sweaters immediately and return them to any J.C. Penney store for a full refund.

incidents_text: QSP has received five reports of overheating. There have been no reports of injury.

action: Consumers should immediately take these metal charms away from children and contact Hirschberg Schutz & Co. at (800) 651-0616 anytime to receive a refund.

heading: CPSC, Ocean Desert Sales Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Stuffed Yarn Bunnies
hazard_text: The eyes can detach from the stuffed animal, posing an aspiration hazard to young children. Additionally, the heart and flower button decorations also can detach, posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately take the toy away from young children and return it the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported

product_name: Lands' End Infant and Toddler Squall Parkas, Sport Squalls, Squall Snow Suits and Squall Bibs
heading: CPSC, Lands' End Announce Recall of Zipper Pulls on Children's Outer Wear

sold_at: Lands' End Catalogue and Internet sales from August 2004 through December 21, 2004 for between $54.50 and $79.50.

heading: CPSC, Tiffany and Company Announce Recall of Farm Teether Rattles

The beads can pose an aspiration hazard to young children. The breakage also can create ragged edges on the ring, posing a laceration hazard.
action: Consumers can return the product to Tiffany and Company for a full refund, credit or a new rattle.
incidents_text: CPSC and Tiffany and Company have received one report of a farm animal figure that was found in the mouth of a 7-month-old child. The child was not injured.

heading: CPSC, Dollar Tree Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Electronic Musical Toys
hazard_text: The ball on the end of the drumstick sold with these toys can break off during use, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumer should take these toys away from young children immediately and return the recalled toys to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Dollar Tree, Only $1, and Dollar Bills stores nationwide from March 2004 through January 2005 for $1.

heading: CPSC, Playtex Products Inc., Announce Recall of Hip Hammock Child Carriers

action: Consumers should stop using the carrier immediately and contact Playtex Products Inc., for instructions on returning the carrier for a replacement.
incidents_text: The company has received two reports of the shoulder strap detaching from the infant carrier. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile product stores, discount stores nationwide, catalog and internet sites from June 2004 through February 2005 for about $40 (Basic model) and $60 (Deluxe model).

heading: CPSC, Charles Products Announce Recall of Toddler Drinking Cups
CPSC, Dollar General Corp. Announce Recall of Dive Sticks
hazard_text: Children can fall or land on these upright dive sticks in shallow water and suffer impalement injuries. CPSC banned pre-weighted dive sticks in 2001.
action: Consumers should take these dive sticks away from children immediately and return them to Dollar General stores for a refund, or discard them.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Dollar General stores nationwide from April 2004 through September 2004 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Wal-Mart Stores Announce Recall of Reef Rocker Infant Toys
hazard_text: The seam on the plastic balls can separate, releasing the small toy inside and posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the toy away from small children and return it to their nearest Wal-Mart store for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores nationwide from May 2004 through January 2005 for between $8 and $10.

heading: CPSC, HIS International Announce Recall of Jumper Sets
CPSC, Big Save International Announce Recall of Baby Walkers
hazard_text: The walkers fit through a standard doorway and are not designed to stop at the edge of a step. Additionally, these walkers can tip-over. Babies using these walkers can be seriously injured or killed.
action: Stop using the recalled walkers immediately and return the walkers to the retailer where they were purchased to receive a refund.
sold_at: Toy and juvenile product stores nationwide for between $15 and $25. Model 9026 walkers were sold from June 1998 through December 2002 and all other models were sold from December 2003 through December 2004.

product_name: Winnie the Pooh Plate Set with plastic fork and spoon
heading: CPSC, Giftco Announce Recall of Fork in Winnie the Pooh Baby Plate Set
hazard_text: The plastic fork prongs in the plate set can break posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Stop using the fork immediately. Return just the fork or the entire plate set to Giftco for a full refund or consumers can just throw the fork away.
incidents_text: Three reports of the fork prongs breaking with one child choking on a broken plastic piece of the fork, without injury.
sold_at: School holiday shops.

heading: CPSC, New Star Toys & Gifts Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Cars
CPSC, Arett Sales Corp. Announce Recall of Multi-Purpose Barbecue Lighters
hazard_text: Sold under the brand name ΓÇ£Kitchen Works,ΓÇ¥ the lighters lack child-resistant mechanisms that meet federal safety standards.
action: Consumers should stop using the lighters immediately and return them to the place of purchase for a full refund or dispose of the lighters in a manner that is in compliance with all state and local requirements. Lighters should not be incinerated or punctured.
incidents_text: ASC has not received any reports of incidents or injuries involving these barbecue lighters.
sold_at: Dollar stores nationwide sold the barbecue lighters from January 2001 through July 2004 for about $1.

product_name: Flashing Pacifier with Whistle Necklace and Flashing Pacifier Shock Baby Necklace
heading: CPSC, Todo Dollar Wholesale Announce Recall of Pacifiers
hazard_text: The nipple can detach from the pacifier, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Return the pacifiers to the store where purchased to receive a refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Internet sales, distributors and small retail stores from January 2004 through November 2004 for about $1.

product_name: Girls' Cardigan Sweaters with Faux Fur Trim
heading: CPSC, H & M Announce Recall of Girls' Sweaters with Faux Fur Trim
hazard_text: The furry trim on the sweaters is dangerously flammable.
action: Consumers should return the recalled sweaters to any H & M location to receive a refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: H & M stores in the northeastern United States from November 2004 through December 2004 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Once Upon a Family Announce Recall of Memory Trunks
hazard_text: The lid can fall on a child who is looking or reaching inside entrapping the child at the neck, which poses a risk of strangulation. Also, the lid can close and self-fasten, entrapping the child inside the trunk, which poses a suffocation hazard.
action: Consumers should keep the Memory Trunk out of reach of children and contact the firm to receive a free repair kit. The repair kit includes a warning sticker and a padlock so that the Memory Trunk can be locked. Consumers can also request a free replacement lid that is not attached by hinges, which eliminates the risks of entrapment and strangulation.
incidents_text: CPSC and Once Upon A Family are aware of one incident where the lid of a trunk fell on a 2-year-old boy, entrapping him between the lid and the base. The child was not injured.
sold_at: Sales consultants at home events nationwide from November 2002 through October 2004 for about $100.

heading: CPSC, Jumpking Inc.® Announce Recall of Trampolines, Enclosures
hazard_text: Welds on the frame of these trampolines can break during use, resulting in falls and possible injuries. Additionally, the mounting brackets of the FunRing enclosures have sharp edges, which can cause lacerations.
action: Consumers should stop using the trampolines and/or the enclosures and contact Jumpking to receive free repair kits.
incidents_text: Jumpking has received 47 reports of one or more welds breaking on these trampolines. This resulted in 21 reports of a variety of injuries, including a concussion; head, neck and back injuries; a broken arm; sprains; lacerations; and bruises. The firm also received 12 reports of other incidents, including nine reports of serious lacerations, when children came into contact with the sharp edges of the enclosure brackets.
sold_at: The trampolines with enclosures were sold at discount, department and toy stores nationwide and in Canada from July 1999 through December 2003 for between $350 and $450. Trampolines without FunRing enclosures were sold from July 1999 through February 2004 for between $180 and $220. FunRing enclosures were sold separately for between $150 and $250.

heading: CPSC, Pottery Barn Kids Announce Recall of Chamois Blankets
hazard_text: The decorative stitching on the blanket's edge can come loose, allowing a child to become entangled in the yarn. This poses a strangulation hazard to young children.
action: Consumers can remove the decorative stitching or contact Pottery Barn Kids for information on how to receive a replacement or refund.
incidents_text: Pottery Barn Kids has received four reports of incidents involving the decorative stitching coming loose. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Pottery Barn Kids' stores nationwide, through the Pottery Barn catalog, and PotteryBarnKids.com from December 2002 through December 2004 for about $30.

product_name: Fun Years Music Big Drum Musical Set
heading: CPSC, Kids Station Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Musical Drum Set Sold Exclusively at Toys "R" Us
hazard_text: Small parts can break off during use, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Return the recalled Big Drum Musical Set to your nearest Toys "R" Us store for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Toys "R" Us stores nationwide exclusively from August 2004 through December 9, 2004 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Riviera Trading Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Costume Bracelets
hazard_text: The bracelets contain high levels of lead and pose a lead poisoning hazard to children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these bracelets away from young children and contact the company to receive a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Belk, Bloomingdales, Carson Pirie Scott, Kohl's, Parisians and Proffitts Department stores nationwide from October 2003 through November 2004 for about $6.

product_name: Adams Trail-a-Bike or Adams Slipstream Bicycle Attachment
heading: CPSC, Norco Products Ltd. Announce Recall of Bicycle Attachment
hazard_text: The hardware used in the assembly of the universal hitch may come loose causing the unit to separate from the lead bicycle, which could lead to a serious injury or death to the rider of the bicycle attachment.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the product and contact their local bicycle dealer to arrange for an inspection and to receive a no charge repair kit to be installed for free.
incidents_text: Norco Products has received two reports of hardware falling out of the hitch assembly. One minor injury reported.
sold_at: Independent bicycle stores nationwide from January 1996 through October 2004 for between $125 to $295.

heading: CPSC, Orbelle Trade Inc. Announce Recall of Cribs
hazard_text: The Amber model crib included in this recall does not comply with crib safety standards due to a gap between the side rail and the crib mattress support, posing an entrapment hazard to infants. All other model cribs included in this recall do not have proper assembly instructions and diagrams required for cribs. They are also missing cautionary and warning labels as required by federal law. If the cribs are not assembled properly, they could pose an entrapment hazard to infants.
action: If you own the Amber model crib, contact the firm to schedule an in-home repair or request a replacement crib. For all other model cribs, contact the firm to receive new assembly instructions and warning labels.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Juvenile furniture stores in New York and New Jersey from January 2003 through August 2004 for between $135 and $335.

heading: CPSC, The Step 2 Co. Announce Recall to Repair Toddler Swings
hazard_text: The straps on these swings could break, causing a child riding in the swing to fall to the ground and suffer injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using these swings and contact the firm to determine if their swing is involved in the recall. If it is, the firm will provide a free repair.
incidents_text: None Reported.
sold_at: Toy and discount department stores nationwide from May 2003 through December 2004 for between $17 and $20.

heading: CPSC, Raymond Geddes Co. Announce Recall of Children's Necklaces
hazard_text: The necklaces contain high levels of lead. CPSC regulations ban children's products from containing high levels of lead due to the risk of lead poisoning resulting from contact with these products. The necklaces also contain a sharp point, posing a laceration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these necklaces away from young children and contact the company to receive a refund.
incidents_text: The company has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Mail order catalogs nationwide and on the Internet from August 1998 through November 2004 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Norton McNaughton of Squire, Inc. Announce Recall of Girls' Hooded Sweaters with Drawstrings
hazard_text: The hooded sweaters have drawstrings, posing a strangulation hazard to children. In February 1996, the CPSC issued guidelines to help prevent children from strangling or getting entangled on the neck and waist drawstrings of upper garments such as jackets and sweatshirts. These garments were identified by the Wisconsin Bureau of Consumer Protection.
action: Consumers can remove the drawstrings to eliminate the hazard or return the hooded drawstring sweater to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Various retailers nationwide from July 2004 through November 2004 for between $15 and $25.

heading: CPSC, Meijer Distribution Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Snow Suits, Jackets
hazard_text: These snow suits and jackets have decorative compasses and corded zipper pull tags that can come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers can cut off the compasses and corded zipper pull tags from the zipper pulls, or return the recalled snow suits and jackets to Meijer retailers for a refund.
incidents_text: The firm received one report of a young child who removed the decorative compass from a jacket and placed a plastic piece in her mouth. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Meijer retail stores in Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and Illinois from August 2004 to October 2004. The snow suits sold for between $15 and $43.

heading: CPSC, Hanna Andersson Announce Recall of Children's Corduroy Overalls
hazard_text: The buttons on the front and side panels of the overalls can detach from the garment, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Hanna Andersson will notify all known purchasers by mail regarding a refund.
incidents_text: The firm has received two reports of the buttons detaching from the garment. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Exclusively through Hanna Andersson's catalog, Hanna stores and website from July 12, 2004 through October 15, 2004 for about $38.

product_name: Okie Dokie Alligator Football Pajama Set
heading: CPSC, J.C. Penney Corporation Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Pajama Sets
hazard_text: The heat-sealed patches on the front of the garment can detach, posing a possible choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the pajama sets and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: There has been one report of a patch detaching. No injuries reported.
sold_at: J.C. Penney stores nationwide from June 2004 through September 2004 for about $22.

heading: CPSC, Petit Bateau Announce Recall of Children's Bathrobes
hazard_text: These robes fail to meet the children's sleepwear flammability standards, posing a risk of burn injury to children due to the possible ignition of the garment.
action: Return the recalled bathrobes to Petit Bateau USA Inc., 45 Essex Street, Suite 200, Millburn, NJ 07041 to receive a full refund including postage and a special gift.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Petit Bateau retail stores and other outlets nationwide from February 2002 through June 2004 for about $65.

heading: CPSC, International Playthings, Inc. Announce Recall of Rattles
hazard_text: The spiral section of the rattle can come apart, releasing small balls inside. This can pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled rattle away from young children and contact International Playthings for a refund or replacement.
incidents_text: The firm has received one report of the spiral section of the toy coming apart. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty toy stores nationwide from August 2004 through September 2004 for about $9.

product_name: Toy Ice Cream Car, Police Car, and Washing Machine
heading: CPSC, Tai Tung International Recall Car and Washing Machine Toys
hazard_text: The multicolored beads inside the toys can become accessible to children, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled toys away from young children and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Toy and discount stores nationwide from June 2000 through September 2004 for about $3.

heading: CPSC, Zippo Announce Recall of Multi-Purpose Utility Lighters
hazard_text: The utility lighters may spill fuel from the nozzle when first used, causing a potential fire hazard through a secondary source of ignition.
action: Free replacement multi-purpose lighter when consumer sends to the company the black adjuster knob from the bottom of the lighter.
incidents_text: There have been 27 reports that the butane fuel spills out of the nozzle when first used. There have been no reports that the product ignited or caused any injury. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: The Zippo Multi-Purpose Lighters were sold at Lowes, Bed Bath & Beyond, select Yankee Candle stores, Barbeque Galore, Harrington and Hammacher Schlemmer Catalog, select Wal-Mart stores and other convenience, hardware and home, hearth and patio stores from October 2003 to September 1, 2004.

heading: CPSC, Avanti Products Inc. Announce Recall of Water Dispensers
hazard_text: The hot water faucet on these units has a child-resistant safety feature to prevent young children from accessing the hot water. The device can malfunction so that the faucet will not turn off, causing burn injuries to children.
action: Consumers with small children should immediately disable the hot water by turning the red switch on the back of the dispenser to off and contact Avanti to get a free repair.
incidents_text: Avanti has received 10 reports of the hot water not shutting off, nine of which resulted in burn injuries to children, including a 10-month-old baby who suffered burns on his arm and chest.
sold_at: Office Depot, Staples, and other appliance and electronic stores nationwide from July 2000 through August 2004 for between $120 and $250.

heading: CPSC, IKEA Home Furnishings Announce Recall of Fargglad Multi-Color Children's Chair
hazard_text: Choking hazard from red plastic feet that can detach from chair legs.
action: Full refund. Take the Fargglad multi-color children's chair away from young children immediately and return it to the "Returns and Exchanges" department at any IKEA U.S. store for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: IKEA stores sold the recalled children's chair from May 2003 through September 18, 2004, for about $15.

product_name: Care Bears Lunch Kits with Water Bottles
heading: CPSC, Sky High International Announce Recall of Care Bears Lunch Kits Sold at Kohl's Department Stores
hazard_text: The pull-up drinking spout can detach from the bottle, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers are advised to stop using the water bottles immediately and contact Sky High International for a refund of the water bottle.
incidents_text: The firm has received two reports of the drinking spouts detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Kohl's Department Stores nationwide from July 2004 through September 2004 for about $13.

heading: CPSC, PlayKids USA Announce Recall of Baby Walkers
hazard_text: The walkers will fit through a standard doorway and are not designed to stop at the edge of a step. Babies using these walkers can be seriously injured or killed if they fall down stairs.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled walkers immediately and contact PlayKids to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Small independent specialty juvenile retailers nationwide sold the baby walker from February 2003 through April 2004 for between $29 and $39.

heading: CPSC, Sauder Woodworking Co. Announce Recall of TV/VCR Carts
hazard_text: The carts can tip over and the television can fall off, posing a risk of serious injury or death if the TV and cart fall on a child.
action: Consumers should stop using the TV/VCR carts immediately and do the following:Remove the television and all contents.Turn the cart over and remove the four casters from the bottom of the cart. This will bring the tip-stability of the cart into compliance with the latest industry standards.Contact Sauder Woodworking Co. to receive a free retrofit kit and safe use information.When updated, this cart will be suitable for use with TVs weighing 50 pounds or less. This includes most TVs that are 20 inches or smaller.
incidents_text: Sauder Woodworking received one report of a cart tipping over, though no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Department, discount and home electronic stores nationwide sold the 3355, 6355 and 7755 model from October 1991 through May 1999 for between $80 and $100. The 9855 and 9755 models were sold exclusively at Target stores.

heading: CPSC, Natura Products Downey Inc. Announce Recall of Pacifiers
hazard_text: The pacifiers are banned under federal law. They failed federal safety tests, come apart, and can pose a choking hazard to infants and small children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the pacifiers away from young children and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC has received one report of a pacifier nipple that detached from the pacifier while in the mouth of a seven-month-old. The child was not injured.
sold_at: Various small Mexican supermarkets and commercial retailers nationwide from March 2004 through August 2004 for between $0.35 and $1.

heading: CPSC, Delta Enterprise Corp. Announce Recall to Repair Director's Chairs for Children
hazard_text: The chair can inadvertently be misassembled so that the fabric seat can come off the chair's frame and expose metal support rods. If fabric seat comes off the frame, there is a laceration and fall hazard to young children.
action: Consumers are advised to stop using the chair immediately and contact Delta Enterprise Corp., to receive a free repair kit consisting of new assembly instructions and four straps, which will prevent the fabric seat from coming off.
incidents_text: Delta Enterprise Corp., has received six reports of the fabric seat coming off. In two of these reports, children received lacerations from the exposed metal seat support rod, with one child requiring stitches. There were two additional reports of minor injuries.
sold_at: The product was sold at discount department and toy stores nationwide from April 2004 through July 2004 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Reebok International Announce Recall of Toddler's Athletic Shoes
hazard_text: The I-3 logo tag on the tongue of the shoe can be peeled off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these shoes away from young children and contact Reebok to receive a refund.
incidents_text: Reebok has received a report of an 8-month-old child mouthing the logo-tag. The tag was removed without injury.
sold_at: Reebok, independent retailers, children's apparel and athletic shoe stores nationwide from March 2004 through August 2004 for about $35.

heading: CPSC, NCR Corp. Announce Recall of NCR Universal Inkjet Refill Kits
hazard_text: The product does not have required child-resistant packaging or required warning labels. The product contains ethylene glycol, posing an ingestion hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the kits out of the reach of young children and return to the store where purchased to receive a refund or a free replacement kit.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Big Lots and Walgreens nationwide from April 2004 through June 2004 for about $12.

heading: CPSC, Baby Swede, LLC Announce Recall to Repair "Baby Björn" Infant Carriers
hazard_text: The back support buckle can detach from the shoulder straps, posing a fall hazard to the baby.
action: Consumers should stop using the carrier immediately and contact Baby Swede, LLC for instructions on returning the carriers for repair.
incidents_text: The firm has received 93 reports of the back support buckle detaching from the shoulder straps on the infant carrier. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty retail stores, catalogs and internet sites from September 2003 through August 15, 2004 for about $120.

heading: CPSC, Hasbro Inc. Announce Recall of Monster Rockets
hazard_text: The cap on the water tank can unexpectedly and forcibly project off when it is quickly unscrewed from the tank, posing a risk of impact injuries to users or bystanders. In addition, the rocket's tail can strike a user or bystander on descent, if the rocket is not fully launched, posing a risk of injury.
action: Consumers should stop using the rockets immediately and contact Hasbro to receive a replacement product of equal value.
incidents_text: Hasbro has received four reports of the cap being unexpectedly projected off the rocket, resulting in three injuries, including a slight concussion and a cut requiring stitches. Additionally, Hasbro has received four reports of children being struck by the descending rocket, including three cuts that required stitches.
sold_at: Toys 'R' Us, Wal-Mart, Target, KB Toys stores and other toy retailers nationwide sold the rockets from January 2004 through August 2004 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, Regal Lager Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Stroller Attachments
hazard_text: The Buggy Board's red connecting pins can break, causing the board to partially detach from the stroller or carriage, posing a fall hazard to the user.
action: The manufacturer is providing free repair kits to consumers consisting of orange replacement pins for these Buggy Boards.
incidents_text: Regal Lager Inc. has received two reports of the Buggy Board disengaging from a stroller or carriage, resulting in falls to children. One minor injury was reported.
sold_at: Specialty retail stores, catalogs and internet sites from January 2003 through July 2004 for about $88.

heading: CPSC, Boston Billows Inc. Announce Recall of Nursing Pillows
hazard_text: If infants are placed on these pillows and left unattended, there is a risk of suffocation. Infant pillows and cushions are banned under the Federal law. Infant pillows have a flexible fabric covering, are loosely filled with plastic beads, easily flattened, intended for use by infants under 1 year old, and capable of conforming to the body or face of an infant.
action: Consumers should stop using these pillows immediately and contact the firm for information on receiving a refund. Update: A December 19, 2008 decision by the Commission to exempt this product has superseded this recall action. As a result, this recall action is no longer in effect.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Hospitals and independent specialty stores from February 2000 through December 2003 for between $34 and $38.

product_name: Big V Maternity and Nursing Pillows
heading: CPSC, Theraline Inc. Announce Recall of Maternity and Nursing Pillows
hazard_text: If infants are placed on these pillows and left unattended, there is a risk of suffocation. Infant pillows and cushions are banned under the Federal law. Infant pillows have a flexible fabric covering, are loosely filled with plastic beads, easily flattened, intended for use by infants under 1 year old, and capable of conforming to the body or face of an infant.
action: Consumers should stop using these pillows immediately and contact the firm for information on receiving a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Independent specialty stores sold the pillows from June 2003 through May 2004 for about $60.

heading: CPSC, Aviva Sports Announce Recall to Repair Astroslide Water Slides
hazard_text: These water slides have an excessive length of rope attached to the safety mat that presents a risk of entanglement in the water. This poses a drowning hazard to users.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these slides and contact Aviva Sports to request a free repair kit. After making the repair, consumers can resume using the product.
incidents_text: Aviva has received one report of a child being tangled on the rope in the water. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Sporting goods stores nationwide from January 2004 through May 2004 for about $99.

product_name: Kid's Essentials Five-Piece Folding Furniture Set
heading: CPSC, Meco Corp. Announce Recall of Red Chairs from Children's Furniture Sets
hazard_text: The red paint on the chair contains excessive lead levels, posing a lead poisoning hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using this red chair immediately and contact the firm for instructions on returning the red chair and receiving a free replacement chair.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Furniture and wholesale club stores nationwide from July 2003 through June 2004 for between $25 and $40.

heading: CPSC, PTI Sports Inc. Announce Recall of Schwinn Toddler Bicycle Helmets
hazard_text: The helmets do not comply with impact testing requirements in the Consumer Product Safety Act.
action: Return the recalled helmet to the store where purchased for a replacement or refund. Consumers also can send the helmet back to the manufacturer.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Wal-Mart, Target, Academy, and Mills Fleet & Farms stores nationwide from January 2004 through July 2004 for between $17 and $20.

product_name: NikeTM Get-Go and Little Get-Go Children's Athletic Shoes
heading: CPSC, NIKE Announce Recall of Children's Athletic Shoes
hazard_text: The 1.5-inch to 1.75-inch rubber tab at the top of the heel can detach from the shoe, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled shoes away from young children and contact Nike to receive a refund voucher.
incidents_text: Nike has received three reports of heel tabs separating from shoes. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Nike stores, major athletic shoe stores, independent shoe stores and children's stores nationwide from June 2004 through August 2004 for between $35 and $45.

product_name: Wooden bunk beds: Twin/Twin, Twin/Double, and Loft Bunk
heading: CPSC, PJ Sleep Shop Announce Recall to Repair Bunk Beds
hazard_text: These bunk beds have gaps between parts of the upper bunk end structure that violate the federal safety standard because they pose entrapment or strangulation hazards to children. The spaces exceed that allowed by the federal bunk bed safety standard, which is designed to protect children from entrapment and strangulation.
action: Stop using the recalled bunk beds and get a free repair kit from the manufacturer to cover up the entrapment hazards. Consumers can install the repair kit easily at home.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: PJ Sleep Shop in Portland, Oregon, and Banner Furniture stores in Portland and Hillsboro, Oregon, between June 1, 2000, and February 29, 2004. Model #1000 sold for about $199, Model #2000 sold for about $325, and Model #3000 sold for about $349.

heading: CPSC, HearthSong Announce Recall of Children's Toy Balls
hazard_text: The wooden rings on the holes of the product may crack, allowing the small wooden heads to fall out and pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: HearthSong will notify all known purchasers by mail regarding a refund and a discount towards the next purchase.
incidents_text: The firm has received one report of a child placing the small wooden head in its mouth. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Exclusively through HearthSong's catalog and website from October 2001 through March 2004 for about $10.

product_name: Pokémon plush dolls, beanbags, and key chains
heading: CPSC, TOMY Company Announce Recall of Pokémon Plush Toys
hazard_text: Tips of sewing needles have been found in the stuffing, posing a puncture hazard.
action: Parents should take these toys away from children immediately and contact TOMY Company for information on receiving a refund or free replacement toy.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Pokémon Center NY, 10 Rockefeller Plaza, New York City and on the firm's website at www.pokemoncenter.com nationwide from January 2004 through August 2004 for between $4.99 and $34.95. A limited number were given away as a promotional item.

heading: CPSC, Determined Productions Announce Recall of Plush Toys Sold at Kohl's Department Stores
hazard_text: The seams in the toy can tear open and expose small plastic pellets, posing a choking or aspiration hazard to young children who mouth the pellets.
action: Consumers are advised to stop using the toy immediately and contact Determined Productions or stop at a local Kohl's Department Stores to receive a refund or store credit.
incidents_text: Determined Productions has received one report of seam breakage on the toy, resulting in a child choking on the plastic pellets. The child was taken to the hospital and released without any injury after a procedure to look for aspirated beads.
sold_at: Kohl's Department Stores sold the toys exclusively throughout July 2004 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Kmart Corporation Announce Recall of Pool Pump Water Guns
hazard_text: The cone-shaped nozzle can unexpectedly come off the water gun and be propelled, causing injury.
action: Consumers should stop using the water guns and return them to a Kmart store for a full refund.
incidents_text: There have been four reports of injuries to children including cuts and bruises to the face and head.
sold_at: Kmart stores nationwide from January 2004 through June 2004 for about $2.

heading: CPSC, Target Announce Recall of Summerville™ Toy Truck Sets
hazard_text: Components on the trucks could detach, posing a choking and sharp point hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should return the recalled trucks to Target for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide from February 2004 through May 2004 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Graco Children's Products Announce Recall of Travel Lite™ Swings
hazard_text: The swing's carrying handle can fail to stay in place properly and drop or be pushed down, hitting a child in the head. Additionally, the 3-point seatbelt can fail to prevent a child from leaning forward or to either side, posing a risk that the child can fall forward and strike his/her head on the floor or the swing's frame.
action: Consumers who have a Travel Lite swing with a 3-point seatbelt (waist belt and crotch strap only) or a Travel Lite swing without a red handle release button should stop using it immediately and contact Graco for a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Graco has received about 28 reports of incidents involving the handle falling down on young children; in addition, Graco has received 100 reports of children falling forward or to the side. Injuries resulting from these incidents include bloody or swollen lips, red marks, bumps and bruises.
sold_at: Discount, department and juvenile stores from June 2003 through June 2004 for about $60.

product_name: Arch Swing and Arch Swing Add-A-Bay
heading: CPSC, Playworld Systems Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Swing Sets
hazard_text: The weld between the side arch support and the top rail can fail. If that happens, the swings can collapse, causing children on the swings to fall and be injured by the falling top rail.
action: The swing set seats should immediately be removed from the swing set until a repair kit is installed. The firm will contact the owner directly by mail and provide a repair kit.
incidents_text: Playworld has received one report of the top rail detaching resulting in two injuries. One child bruised his knee while the second child bruised his shoulder.
sold_at: Sales representatives sold the swing sets directly to day care centers and children's learning centers or playgrounds nationwide from February 1998 through May 2004. The Arch Swing Add-A-Bay sold for $488 while the Arch Swing sold for $653.

heading: CPSC Announces Recall of Metal Toy Jewelry Sold in Vending Machines Firms agree to stop importation until hazard is eliminated
hazard_text: CPSC has determined that some of this toy jewelry contains dangerous levels of lead, posing a risk of lead poisoning to children.
action: Consumers should throw away recalled jewelry.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The toy jewelry was sold in vending machines located in malls, discount, department and grocery stores nationwide from January 2002 through June 2004 for between $0.25 and $0.75.

heading: CPSC, Dorel Juvenile Group USA Announce Recall to Inspect and Replace COSCO® "Rock 'N Roller" Baby Strollers
hazard_text: If the stop pins are bent or missing or the seat is not fully attached, the seat can partially detach from the frame during use and the infant occupant can be injured in a fall.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled "Rock 'N Roller" strollers with detachable seats immediately and call the firm to determine how to inspect the stroller for possible replacement.
incidents_text: There have been 77 reports of problems related to the stroller seats. Injuries included one child that fell and had a slight concussion and another child that cut his forehead and required stitches. Additionally, there were 46 reports of bumps and bruises.
sold_at: Wal-Mart, Kmart, Sears, Toys R Us, Target, JC Penney's, Service Merchandise and other toy and children's furniture stores nationwide from April 1996 through August 2002 for between $79 and $179.

heading: CPSC, Lakeshore Learning Materials Announce Recall of Doll Sets
hazard_text: The head and boot of the dolls can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the wooden dolls away from young children immediately and contact Lakeshore Learning Materials for information on how to receive a free replacement doll set.
incidents_text: The company received reports of the boot and head detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Lakeshore Learning Materials' mail order catalogs nationwide from January 2003 through April 2004 for about $10 per set.

product_name: Basic Editions Infant and Toddler Girls' Rompers
heading: CPSC, Kmart Corp. Announce Recall of Girls' Rompers
hazard_text: The crocheted cherry-shape tassels and plastic buttons may pull off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should return the rompers to the Kmart store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: The firm has received two reports of children pulling off the crocheted cherry-shape tassels. No injuries reported.
sold_at: Exclusively at Kmart stores nationwide from February 2004 through May 2004 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Samara Brothers Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Swimsuit Cover-ups
hazard_text: The zipper-pull on the cover-up can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these cover-ups and contact Samara Brothers for instructions on receiving a free repair or replacement cover-up.
incidents_text: Samara Brothers has received one report of a zipper-pull coming off. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Department stores and specialty shops nationwide from January 2004 through April 2004 for between $10 and $20.

heading: CPSC, GapKids Announce Recall of Girls' Straw Cowboy Hats
hazard_text: The straw hat is constructed using a thin wire within a seam. The tip of the wire can break free from the seam, posing a laceration hazard.
action: Consumers should return the hats to any Gap store for a refund and a complimentary $5 appreciation card.
incidents_text: GapKids has received two reports of customers who received minor scratches from the exposed wire tip. A 7-year-old child received a scratch on the leg and a 12-year-old received a scratch on the forehead.
sold_at: Exclusively at GapKids stores and gap.com nationwide from April 2004 through May 2004 for about $18.50.

heading: CPSC, The Land of Nod® Announce Recall of Children's Wooden Chairs
hazard_text: The leg supports can crack, causing the chair to collapse. Children sitting in these chairs can fall.
action: Consumers should stop using these chairs immediately and contact The Land of Nod for instructions on how to return these chairs. The company is offering an exchange, credit or refund. Those who choose an exchange for new chairs, and who respond before July 15, 2004, will receive an additional $50 gift certificate to be used toward a future purchase.
incidents_text: The Land of Nod has received three reports of the chairs collapsing, including one injury in which a child bumped her head.
sold_at: The Land of Nod catalog and website nationwide, and the Land of Nod stores in Illinois and Washington between August 2002 and January 2004 for between $69 and $79.

heading: CPSC, Far East Brokers and Consultants Inc. Announce Recall of Kiddie Car Cruisers Sold Exclusively at Big Y Stores
hazard_text: The Kiddie Car Cruiser can continue to run when the accelerator is no longer depressed, which could result in the rider losing control of the car.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled car immediately and return it to a Big Y store to receive a refund.
incidents_text: FEBC has received 10 reports of the Kiddie Car Cruiser continuing to run when the accelerator was not depressed. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Big Y Stores in Massachusetts and Connecticut from May 6 to May 13, 2004, for about $100 with a Big Y Express savings card and about $300 without a savings card.

heading: CPSC, Old Navy Announce Recall of Children's Zippered Outerwear
hazard_text: The plastic zipper pull can detach from the zipper, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should return the garments to any Old Navy store for a refund and a complimentary $5 appreciation card.
incidents_text: Old Navy has received 13 reports of the zipper pulls detaching, including one report of a child mouthing the object. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Old Navy stores and oldnavy.com nationwide from November 2003 through May 2004 from between $14 and $34.

product_name: Smart FitTM and Teeny ToesTM Athletic Shoes
heading: CPSC, Payless ShoeSource Announce Recall of Children's Athletic Shoes
hazard_text: The metal eyelet lace holder at the top of the shoes can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the recalled shoes away from young children immediately and should return the shoes to a Payless ShoeSource store for a cash refund or exchange.
incidents_text: Payless ShoeSource has received one report of a child starting to choke on a detached eyelet from one of these shoes.
sold_at: Payless ShoeSource stores and website nationwide from December 2003 through April 2004 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Dream On Me Industries Announce Recall of Baby Walkers
hazard_text: The walkers will fit through a standard doorway and are not designed to stop at the edge of a step. Babies using these walkers can be seriously injured or killed if they fall down stairs.
action: Stop using the recalled walkers immediately and return the walkers to the retailer where purchased to receive a refund.
incidents_text: No injuries have been reported with the baby walkers.
sold_at: Small toy and juvenile product stores in the metropolitan New York area from April 2002 through March 2004 for about $25 for model 408 and about $30 for model 423.

heading: CPSC, Backyard Products Announce Recall of Swings
hazard_text: Chains on the swing can detach during use and cause the child to fall to the ground and possibly suffer injuries.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: The company had received 31 reports of chains breaking, resulting in five reports of injuries including a sore back, cut lip, and bumps and bruises.
sold_at: Department, toy and discount stores nationwide from December 2003 through April 2004 for between $300 and $1,200 for the sets. The swings were sold separately from January 2004 through April 2004 for between $12 and $16.

heading: CPSC, Front Porch Classics Announce Recall of "Old Century Dread Pirate™" Coffee Table Games
hazard_text: The surface coating and the metal in the ships contain lead and pose a risk of lead poisoning to young children. A child could ingest lead by swallowing a broken part of the ship or by repeatedly mouthing the ships.
action: Take the recalled "Dread Pirate" ships away from children immediately and call Front Porch for free replacement toy ships that do not contain lead and will not break.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Approximately 170 toy and game stores, online and catalog vendors, and gift stores sold the "Dread Pirate" games from October 2003 through March 2004 for about $100.

heading: CPSC, Baby Trend Announce Recall of Certain Baby Trend "Passport" Strollers
hazard_text: The fold joint can collapse unexpectedly, causing the baby to fall.
action: Consumers should stop using the stroller and contact Baby Trends, Inc. immediately. Baby Trend will ask the consumer to send a cut-out section of the seat with restraint strap attached. Baby Trend will send the consumer a new replacement stroller.
incidents_text: Baby Trend has received four reports from consumers of the stroller collapsing. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Babies "R" Us nationwide from July 2003 through February 2004 for about $29.

product_name: Metal Twin/Twin and Twin/Full Bunk Beds
heading: CPSC, Coaster Co. of America Announce Recall of Bunk Beds
hazard_text: A gap between the step of the built-in ladder and the top bunk allows enough room for a child's body to slip through but will not allow for a child's head to pass through. This poses a serious strangulation risk. Federal standards for bunk beds are designed to protect children against entrapment and strangulation.
action: Consumers should stop using the bunk beds immediately and call Coaster of America for a free repair kit.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Furniture stores nationwide sold the bunk beds from June 2000 through February 2004 for between $150 and $250.

product_name: Children's Board Books with Sound Maker
heading: CPSC, DK Publishing Announce Recall of Children's Board Books with Sound Maker
hazard_text: The sound maker mounted inside a plastic covering on the last page of the books poses a choking hazard to young children if removed.
action: Consumers should take these books away from young children immediately and contact DK Publishing to receive a replacement book of equal value or a refund.
incidents_text: DK Publishing has received one report of a 22-month-old child detaching the sound maker of one of the books and putting it in his mouth. The child was not injured.
sold_at: Bookstores, gift stores, news stands, discount department stores and warehouse clubs nationwide, and directly to consumers by phone order from March 2001 through April 2004 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Casio Inc. Announce Recall of Piano Benches
