hazard_text: The screws and bracket assemblies attaching the legs to the bench can weaken and detach, causing the bench seat to collapse during normal use.
action: Consumers should stop using the benches immediately and contact Casio for instructions on how to return the product for a full refund plus an incentive payment. Consumers who purchased a Casio Eighty Eight key digital piano, model AP31 from Costco Wholesale Corporation should return only the bench to their local Costco retailer. Consumers who purchased a Casio Eighty Eight key digital piano, model AP31 or PX100 from Sam's Club will receive a box, instructions, and a return label to return the bench back to Casio. Do not return benches to Sam's Clubs. Consumers who purchased the keyboard and bench together will receive $125 toward the purchase of a replacement bench and consumers who purchased a bench separately will receive a full refund of the purchase price plus a $25 incentive payment.
incidents_text: Casio has received four reports of bracket assemblies failing, including one report of a consumer sustaining a fractured wrist when their bench collapsed.
sold_at: Music instrument retailers, Sam's Club, Costco Wholesale and on Casio's Web site nationwide between September 2003 and March 2004 for about $99. The benches sold by Sam's Club and Costco were unassembled and included a Casio Electronic Piano and piano stand. The benches distributed by music instrument retailers were assembled and sold as stand-alone products.

product_name: Ashley "Trails End," "Cottage Retreat," and "Stages" bunk beds
heading: CPSC, Ashley Furniture Industries Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Bunk Beds
hazard_text: There are gaps between parts of the bunk bed that violate federal safety standards and can be entrapment or strangulation hazards to children. For model B383, the gap between the end rails on the upper bunk is too large. For models B213 and B233, the gap between the guardrails of the upper bunk can be widened with pressure, presenting an entrapment hazard. Federal standards for bunk beds are designed to protect children against entrapment and strangulation.
action: Stop using the recalled bunk beds and get a free repair kit from the retailer to cover and close the entrapment gaps. Consumers can install the repair kit easily at home.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The bunk beds being recalled for repair were sold at furniture stores nationwide. Model B383 was sold beginning in December 2000. Model B213 was sold beginning in May 2003. Model B233 was sold beginning in June 2003. All sales of the recalled bunk beds ended in February 2004. Model B383-57T sold for around $299, model B383-58T sold for around $699, and Models B213 and B233 sold for around $599.

heading: CPSC, Kids II Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Mirror Books
hazard_text: The mirror in the books can crack or break, posing a laceration hazard to young children.
action: Parents should take the product away from small children immediately and detach and mail the mirror page of the product to Kids II at 1015 Windward Ridge Parkway, Alpharetta, GA 30005 for a refund.
incidents_text: Kids II has received 26 reports of the mirror cracking or breaking, including four reports of cuts and one report of a pinched finger.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and juvenile specialty stores nationwide from December 2001 through March 2004 for between $4 and $8.

heading: CPSC, Tek Nek Toys Announce Recall of Ride-On Toys
hazard_text: The screw and nut assembly attaching the steering wheel can come loose, posing a choking and aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these recalled ride-on toy vehicles away from young children immediately and contact Tek Nek Toys for free replacement parts.
incidents_text: Tek Nek Toys has received six reports of the screw and nut coming loose, including the death of an 18-month-old boy who aspirated a screw.
sold_at: Wal-Mart, Toys R Us, Kmart, Meijer and Shopko sold the ride-on toys nationwide from December 2002 through March 2004 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, Nikko America Announce Recall of Radio-Control Toy Trucks
hazard_text: A problem with the circuit board causes the toy truck to overheat, posing a fire and burn hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using the toy trucks and contact Nikko America for instructions on returning the product for a free circuit board replacement.
incidents_text: Nikko America has received five reports of the toy trucks overheating, resulting in minor property damage caused by fire and smoke. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Major toy and discount department stores nationwide sold the toy trucks from July 2003 through February 2004 for about $60.

heading: CPSC, H&M Announce Recall of Promotional Water Bottles
hazard_text: The pull-up, black plastic drinking spout can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Return the water bottle to any H&M store for a free $5 coupon towards another H&M purchase.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: H&M clothing stores nationwide distributed the water bottles as a free premium with purchase of children's wear between February 2004 and March 5, 2004.

heading: CPSC, Sauder Woodworking Co. Announce Recall of TV/VCR Carts that Can Tip Over Easily, after Baby's Death
hazard_text: The carts can tip over and injure or kill children and adults when the cart and the television fall.
action: Consumers should stop using the TV/VCR carts immediately and do the following: Remove the television and all the contents from these carts. Turn the cart over and remove the four casters from the bottom of the cart. This will improve the stability of the carts. Contact Sauder Woodworking Co. to receive a free repair kit that will further reduce the potential for the cart and television to tip. Do not use the cart until the repair kit has been installed.
incidents_text: Sauder Woodworking has received 13 reports of these carts tipping over. The firm received a report of the death of a 19-month-old girl in North Wales, Pa., who suffered a fractured skull when the cart and television fell on her. There were four reports of additional injuries involving children and adults. One report involved a skull fracture to a child who recovered, and three reports involved bumps and bruises.
sold_at: Department, discount and home electronic stores nationwide sold these TV/VCR carts from January 1993 through December 1999 for about $100.

heading: CPSC, Valley Dynamo Announces Recall of Air Hockey Tables
hazard_text: The blower motor, located under the table, has an opening large enough for a child's finger, posing a laceration hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using the product and contact Dynamo for instructions on receiving a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Valley Dynamo is aware of a minor laceration injury to a child who crawled under the air hockey table and stuck his finger in an exposed opening.
sold_at: Sporting good and specialty stores nationwide since 1994 for between $1,000 and $2,200.

heading: CPSC, Kingfisher Publications Announce Recall of Children's Easter Books
hazard_text: A sponge "touch-and-feel" item inside the book can detach or small pieces can be torn away, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these books away from young children immediately, and return the books to Kingfisher Publications PLC, Customer Service, 181 Ballardvale St., Wilmington, MA 01887 for a refund and postage reimbursement.
incidents_text: The firm has received one report of a child who began to choke. No reports of injuries.
sold_at: Retailers nationwide from February 2004 through March 2004 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Babies "R" Us and Playwell Announce Recall of Snail Push Toys
hazard_text: The screw securing the toy handle to the push toy could detach, posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should take the push toy away from small children immediately and return it to Babies "R" Us for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Sold only at Babies "R" Us stores from July 2003 through November 2003 for about $8.00 each.

heading: CPSC, Stanley Furniture Company Inc. Announce Recall of Cribs
hazard_text: An incorrect screw (used to attach the movable gate) was provided for the assembly of some of these cribs. The crib cannot be assembled using this screw. However, if consumers have substituted their own screw, it may not properly hold the movable gate in place. The result is a potential risk that a child could fall from the crib or become entrapped between the gate and the mattress.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Department and furniture stores nationwide from November 2003 through February 2004 for about $980.

heading: CPSC, Palliser Furniture Ltd. Announce Recall of "Poof" Chairs
hazard_text: A metal rod can protrude through the fabric and its sharp edges could cause scratches or cuts.
action: Consumers should take the product away from children immediately and return the chairs and table to the retailer for a full refund.
incidents_text: Palliser received one report of a consumer who was scratched.
sold_at: Furniture stores nationwide and in Canada from June 2003 through January 2004 for between $150 and $200.

heading: CPSC, Lado Co. of America Announce Recall of Hair Dryers
hazard_text: These hair dryers do not have an immersion protection device or ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) on the power cord, which poses a serious electrocution hazard if dropped in water.
action: Stop using these hair dryers immediately and return the unit to the firm for a refund or replacement.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Retail beauty supply stores in the metropolitan New York area from March 2003 through December 2003 for about $50.

heading: CPSC, Tristar Products Inc. Announce Recall of Revised Design Steam Cleaner
hazard_text: Hot water and steam can escape from the steam cleaner's handle and inner hose, posing a burn hazard to consumers.
action: Consumers who experience a burst hose should stop using the steam cleaner and contact Tristar for information on how to return the product for a replacement or refund.
incidents_text: The firm has received about 20 reports of hot water and steam escaping from the steam cleaner, including eight reports of scald injuries to the hands and arms.
sold_at: HSN LLP (Home Shopping Network) from June 2002 through September 2002 for about $129. Also, shipped as replacement units to consumers in the earlier recall between April and September 2002.

heading: CPSC, Brand Imports, LLC Announce Recall of Children's Rings
hazard_text: The rings contain high levels of lead, posing a risk of lead poisoning to young children.
action: Consumers should throw the ring away or contact the company for more information.
incidents_text: None Reported
sold_at: Vending machines in malls, discount department and grocery stores nationwide from December 2002 through August 2003 for about 25 cents.

product_name: Nibo Space 5 and Nibo Space 19 Novelty Lighters
heading: CPSC, Quality Fresh Cigars Announce Recall of Lighters
hazard_text: These novelty lighters were imported without first being tested to show compliance with CPSC requirements that the lighters be child-resistant. They pose fire and burn hazards to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately. Consumers should dispose of the lighter in a manner that is in compliance with any state or local requirements. The lighters should not be incinerated or punctured. Consumers can obtain a gift certificate for $19.95 if purchased or $5.00 if received as a gift by mailing a copy of the signed Disposal Notification Form to Quality Fresh. Consumers should send correspondence to: QFC-Nibo Recall, 1241 Chicago Road, Troy, MI 48083.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The lighters were sold through the firm's catalog from April 2003 to September 2003 for about $20. The lighters were also given away as premiums in conjunction with purchase.

heading: CPSC, Schylling Associates Announce Recall of Wooden Music Radio Boxes
hazard_text: A wooden turning knob and antenna top can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children and exposing a sharp point.
action: Parents should take these toys away from children immediately and contact the firm for information on receiving a refund or free replacement toy.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Specialty stores, gift shops, department stores and book stores nationwide from September 2003 through January 2004 for about $12.

heading: CPSC, Child Craft Industries Announce Recall of Cribs
hazard_text: The slats on the drop side rail can loosen and detach. When this happens, the space created by the gaps can allow a baby to become entangled, strangle or fall.
action: Consumers should stop using the cribs and contact Child Craft to receive a replacement drop side rail.
incidents_text: There have been 12 reports of the slats on the drop side rail completely detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile furniture stores nationwide from March 2002 through January 2004 for between $399 and $549.

heading: CPSC, Mary Meyer Corp. Announce Recall To Replace Plush Spider Baby Toys
hazard_text: The round stuffed feet on the spider can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Return the toy to Mary Meyer Corp. to receive a replacement product of equal value.
incidents_text: Mary Meyer Corporation has received five reports of the round stuffed feet of the plush spider toy detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Department and specialty stores nationwide from January 2002 through September 2003 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, PlayWell Toy Company Ltd. Announce Recall of Activity Cubes
hazard_text: Small parts can detach from the cube, posing a choking hazard to small children.
action: Consumers should take the product away from small children immediately and contact PlayWell for instructions on returning the product for a full refund.
incidents_text: PlayWell has received three reports of small parts detaching, including one report of a child mouthing a piece of the activity cube. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Shopko Stores nationwide from October 2003 through January 2004.

heading: CPSC, Meijer Announce Recall of Children's Sweatshirts with Drawstring Hoods
hazard_text: The sweatshirts have drawstrings in the hood. Children can get entangled and strangle in the drawstrings that can catch on playground equipment, fences or tree branches. In February 1996, the CPSC issued guidelines to help prevent children from strangling or getting entangled on the neck and waist drawstrings of upper garments, such as jackets and sweatshirts. From January 1985 through January 1999, CPSC received reports of 22 deaths and 48 non-fatal incidents involving the entanglement of children's clothing drawstrings.
action: Consumers can return the sweatshirts to Meijer retailers for a full refund or consumers can remove the drawstrings to eliminate the hazard.
incidents_text: No injuries or incidents have been reported.
sold_at: Meijer retail stores in Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and Illinois from August 2003 and January 2004 for between $20 and $22.

product_name: Kids Falls Creek PU Jacket with Polar Fleece in Hood
heading: CPSC, Meijer Distribution Announce Recall of Children's Jackets
hazard_text: The zipper-pull on the jacket can come off and pose a choking hazard to small children.
action: Consumers should stop using these jackets and contact Meijer Distribution for instructions on returning the jacket for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Meijer retail stores in Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and Illinois from August 2003 through December 2003 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, Swing-N-Slide Announce Recall of "Mega Rider" Swings
hazard_text: The plastic handle on the Mega Rider swing could crack at the seat connection allowing the metal connecting rod to pull out. If this occurs, a child on the swing could fall to the ground.
action: Consumers should stop using the "Mega Riders" immediately and return them to the company for a replacement product with increased material thickness. Swing-N-Slide will provide consumers with a self- addressed box to return the product.
incidents_text: There has been one report of a swing breaking. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Lowe's and Home Depot stores by special order and through Ace, DIBC, TruServ, Handy Hardware, Emery Warehouse, and Federated co-ops and buying groups nationwide from March 2003 through October 2003 for about $90.

heading: CPSC, Hasbro Inc. Announce Recall of NERF® Big Play Football™
hazard_text: The football contains a hard plastic interior frame that can pose a risk of facial cuts if a child is hit during play.
action: Consumers should stop using this football immediately and return it to the company for a replacement NERF product of equal value. Hasbro will provide consumers with a postage-prepaid label to return the product.
incidents_text: There have been nine reports of facial injuries, including eight requiring stitches or medical attention.
sold_at: Toys R Us, Wal-Mart, Target, KB Toys stores and other toy retailers nationwide from August 2003 to January 2004 for about $10.

product_name: Discovery Kids Imaginative Arts Pottery Wheel Kits
heading: CPSC, Curiosity Kits Inc. Announce Recall of Discovery Kids Pottery Wheel Kits Sold at Discovery Channel Stores
hazard_text: The brown clay contained in the Pottery Wheel kits could contain excess levels of bacteria, posing a risk of illness to users.
action: Consumers should stop using the pottery wheel kits and return the kits to any Discovery Channel store, or contact Discovery Channel stores' customer service, to receive a full refund or credit of the $39.95 purchase price or a replacement Pottery Wheel Kit and a $5 Discovery Channel store gift certificate.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Discovery Channel stores and catalogs, and on http://shopping.discovery.com during October 2003 for about $40.

heading: CPSC, Sassi America Inc. Announce Recall of Acrylic Primer for Nail Care
hazard_text: This methacrylic acid primer is not packaged in child-resistant packaging, as required by the Poison Prevention Packaging Act.
action: Consumers should return the acrylic primer and kits to the store where purchased to receive a refund.
incidents_text: Sassi America has received a report of a 2-year-old girl in Pompano Beach, Fla., who sustained severe external and internal chemical burns after swallowing the liquid primer.
sold_at: Grocery and beauty supply stores nationwide sold the primer from June 2000 through January 2004 for between $2 and $10.

product_name: "Mud Boggers" and "Street Shredders" Pump Up Racers
heading: CPSC, K'NEX Industries Announce Recall of Children's Toys
hazard_text: The air motor in the toy cars can burst while being pumped up, causing parts of the motor or car to break off. Some of these parts can have sharp points and pose a risk of eye or laceration injuries.
action: Consumers should stop children from using these toy cars immediately and contact the company for a free replacement air motor or alternative product.
incidents_text: K'NEX has received two reports of bursting air motors, though no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Toys R Us, Wal-Mart, and Target stores nationwide sold the toys between November 2003 and December 2003 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Kindermusik International Announce Recall of "Lily Pad Clacker" Instruments
hazard_text: The green coating on the Lily Pad Clacker instruments contains high levels of lead, posing a risk of poisoning to young children.
action: Return the Lily Pad Clackers to Kindermusik International in the postage paid box provided by the firm. Kindermusik will replace the product with a product of comparable value.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Do-Re-Me & You! consultants in North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Virginia and Texas from October 2003 through December 2003 for about $30 for the music kit.

product_name: Bumble Bee Toys with blue antennae sold with certain Graco high chairs and Graco mobile entertainers, and also sold separately as an accessory and replacement part
heading: CPSC, Graco Children's Products Announce Recall of Bumble Bee Toys with Blue Antennae
hazard_text: The blue antennae on the Bumble Bee toy can break, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should discard immediately any Bumble Bee toys with blue antennae in their possession and contact Graco to receive a free replacement toy.
incidents_text: Graco has received 26 reports of the antennae breaking off of the Bumble Bee toys, including five reports of children who started to choke on the broken antennae. One child's throat was scratched when the child's mother removed the broken antenna from the child's mouth. `
sold_at: Discount, department and juvenile product stores from November 2001 through March 2003 on high chairs and mobile entertainers for between $39 and $89, and individually, as accessories, for $5.

heading: CPSC, Mr. Christmas Inc. Announce Recall of Christmas Candleholders
hazard_text: The candleholders do not allow for the safe burning of a candle, which poses a fire hazard to consumers.
action: Return the candleholders to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Gift stores nationwide between November 2003 and December 2003 for about $12.50.

heading: CPSC, Avon Products Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Jack-In-the-Box Toys
hazard_text: A spring mechanism attached to the lid can break and detach from the toy, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Call Avon toll-free at (800) 445-AVON between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. ET Monday through Friday for information on how to receive instructions to remove the spring mechanism. Known purchasers are being sent direct mail notification of this recall.
incidents_text: Avon has received one report of the spring mechanism detaching from the toy. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: Independent Avon sales representatives and the Avon Web site from August 2003 through November 2003 for about $13.

product_name: Craftsman 16-gallon and RIDGID 12- and 16-gallon wet/dry vacuums
heading: CPSC, Emerson Tool Company Announce Recall of Wet/Dry Vacuums
hazard_text: The exhaust blower ports on the wet/dry vacuums are large enough for a small child to reach inside and touch the spinning blower wheel. This poses a laceration hazard to small children.
action: Consumers should contact Emerson toll-free number to request a free insert. The insert is installed inside the blower port to eliminate the hazard.
incidents_text: Emerson Tool Company has received 10 reports of children inserting their arms into the ports and receiving minor cuts and abrasions to their fingertips.
sold_at: Home Depot stores and RIDGE Tool distributors nationwide from March 1999 through October 2002 and Sears Roebuck &. Co. stores nationwide from September 1998 through October 2002 for between $70 and $300.

heading: CPSC, First & Main Inc. Announce Recall of Plush Toys
hazard_text: The decorative gem stone on the toy's wings could detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Return the toys to store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Flower shops and small gift shops nationwide from July 2002 through November 2002 for about $15.

heading: CPSC, Zutopia (a division of Wet Seal Inc.) Announce Recall of Girl's Loungewear
hazard_text: The loungewear failed to meet federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear posing a risk of serious burn injuries to children. The standard requires sleepwear, including loungewear, to be flame resistant and if the garment ignites, the flame must self-extinguish.
action: Parents should stop their children from wearing this loungewear and return the item(s) to any Zutopia store for a full refund or exchange and receive $10 in Zu Dollarz for a future purchase.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Zutopia stores nationwide from January 2003 through October 2003 for between $18 and $26.50.

product_name: "Jack-In-the-Box" type toys: "Cat in the Hat" and "Olivia the Pig"
heading: CPSC, Schylling Associates Inc. Announce Recall of More "Jack-In-the-Box" Type Toys
hazard_text: The bead on the crank of the toy can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Take these toys away from children immediately and contact the firm for information on receiving a refund or replacement toy.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Specialty stores, gift shops, department stores and book stores nationwide from June 2003 through November 2003 for about $25.

heading: CPSC, American Greetings Corp. Announce Recall of Cloth Santa Decorations Sold at Wal-Mart
hazard_text: The beaded nose on the cloth Santa decoration could detach, posing an aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately remove these decorations from any display and keep out of reach of children. Consumers should return the item to Wal-Mart for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores nationwide from October 2003 through November 2003 for less than $5.

heading: CPSC, American Greetings Corp. Announce Recall of Zipper Pulls
hazard_text: The product could separate and detach from the zipper, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should dispose of the zipper pulls immediately. Consumers can contact the firm for a coupon redeemable wherever American Greetings' products are sold.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The product was sold at discount, toy, drug, grocery, party and specialty/gift stores nationwide from January 2001 through November 2003 for about $4.

heading: CPSC, American Greetings Corp. Announce Recall of Crazy Bounce Balls
hazard_text: The balls could break apart, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these balls away from young children and dispose of the balls immediately. Consumers can contact the firm for a coupon redeemable wherever American Greetings' products are sold.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The product was sold at discount, toy, drug, grocery, party and specialty/gift stores nationwide from November 2002 through August 2003 for about $3.

heading: CPSC, The May Department Stores Co. Announces Recall of Girls' Hooded Fleece Jackets
hazard_text: The zipper pull could detach from these jackets, posing a possible choking hazard to young children.
action: Return the jacket to the store where purchased for a refund or store credit.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: May Department Stores Co. department stores, including Lord & Taylor (which sold the "Angel Fish" brand exclusively), Filene's/Kaufmann's, Robinsons-May/Meier & Frank, Hecht's/Strawbridge's, Foley's, Famous-Barr/L.S. Ayres/The Jones Store, from July 2003 through October 2003 for about $13.

heading: CPSC, Toys "R" Us, Inc. Announce Recall of Solid-colored and Multi- colored Sidewalk Chalk
hazard_text: The multi-colored and solid-colored sidewalk chalk contains high levels of lead, posing a risk of poisoning to young children.
action: Return the sidewalk chalk to Toys "R" Us for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The sidewalk chalk was sold at Toys "R" Us stores nationwide from March 2003 to November 2003 for about $4.99 per package.

heading: CPSC, Meijer Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Jackets
hazard_text: These jackets have hood drawstrings. Children can get entangled and strangle in the drawstrings that catch on objects, including playground equipment, fences and tree branches. CPSC knows of numerous deaths from neck/hood drawstrings.
action: Consumers should stop their children from wearing the jacket immediately and contact Meijer toll-free at (866) 280-8419 anytime for information on how to return the jacket for a full refund. Parents also can remove the drawstring, which will make the jacket safe for children to wear.
incidents_text: Meijer has not received any reports of incidents.
sold_at: Meijer stores in Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, and Kentucky sold the jackets from July 2003 through October 2003 for between $26 and $33.

heading: CPSC, Merit Furniture Distributors Announce Recall of Bunk Beds
hazard_text: The bunk beds have openings between the guardrails and in the end structures that are too large. A child's body could slide between the openings and could become trapped by the head, posing a serious strangulation hazard.
action: Consumers should contact Merit for information on how to return their bunk bed and receive a full refund.
incidents_text: Merit has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Furniture stores nationwide sold the bunk beds from May 2002 through August 2003 for about $150.

product_name: "Cherry Bentwood" model television stands sold at Circuit City
heading: CPSC, Planet 3 Announce Recall of Television Stands Sold at Circuit City
hazard_text: The television stand can tip over when a television is placed on it, possibly causing injuries to nearby consumers or death to young children.
action: Consumers should remove televisions from these stands immediately and return the stands to Circuit City for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Circuit City stores nationwide from July 2003 through September 2003 for about $250.

heading: CPSC, Schylling Associates Inc. Announce Recall of Jack-In-the-Box-Type Toys
hazard_text: The red bead on the crank of the toy can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Take these toys away from children immediately and call Schylling Associates Inc. at (800) 767-8697 between 9 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, or visit the firm's website at www.schylling.com for information on receiving a refund or replacement toy.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Specialty stores, gift shops and book stores nationwide from August 2003 through October 2003 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Target Corporation Announce Recall of Multicolored Sidewalk Chalk
hazard_text: The multicolored sidewalk chalk contains high levels of lead, posing a risk of poisoning to young children. The Wisconsin Department of Health tested the chalk and identified the lead in the chalk.
action: Consumers should return the multicolored sidewalk chalk to Target stores for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The sidewalk chalk was sold at Target stores from March 2003 to July 2003 for about $1 per package.

product_name: Lightning PAC Scooters and MX3 Mini Bikes
heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Scooters and Mini Bikes
hazard_text: The motor control circuits can malfunction causing the scooters and mini bikes to continue to run after the power or throttle button is released, posing a risk of injury to children.
action: Consumers should take the toy vehicle(s) away from children immediately and contact Fisher-Price at (800) 528-7153 anytime or log on to www.service.mattel.com to receive information on how to have their toys serviced for free at a certified Power Wheels Service Center. The Service Centers will make modifications to the toy vehicles' circuitry.
units: About 30,000 Lightning PAC Scooters, and about 55,000 MX3 Mini Bikes
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has received 56 reports of incidents with the scooters, including one report of a chipped tooth and one report of a broken arm. Fisher-Price has received 24 reports of incidents involving the mini bike, including one report of a leg laceration.
sold_at: Mass merchants and toy stores nationwide sold scooters between November 2001 and October 2003 for about $250 and sold mini bikes between May 2003 and September 2003 for about $200.

product_name: "Amazing BabyTM Listen and Play" activity books
heading: CPSC, Advantage Publishers Group Announce Recall of Children's Activity Books
hazard_text: The hub of the pink dial embedded in the inside back cover can come off during use in some of these books, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these books away from young children. Consumers should call Advantage Publishers Group toll-free at (866) 748-3731 anytime to order a replacement activity book without the dial.
incidents_text: Advantage Publishers Group received one report from a consumer of a hub coming off. There are no reports of injuries or choking incidents.
sold_at: Retail stores, national book chains, wholesalers and distributors, and membership warehouse clubs nationwide sold the activity books from May through October 2003 for $16.

heading: CPSC, BRIO® Corp. Announce Recall of Toy Drums
hazard_text: The three rubber feet, which are screwed into the bottom of the drum, could be removed in some cases, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers who purchased recalled drums should take them away from young children immediately and call BRIO® for information on receiving a refund or replacement product.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Specialty toy stores, Internet retailers and mail order catalogs sold the recalled toy drum nationwide from March 2003 through September 2003 for about $15.

heading: CPSC, Style Asia Inc. Announce Recall of Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The cigarette lighters do not have qualified child resistant mechanisms and pose a fire hazard to children.
action: Return the lighters to Style Asia for a refund and discount coupon.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The lighters were sold nationwide primarily through internet sales.

heading: CPSC, The Sarut Group d/b/a City Limit Announce Recall of Fish-Shaped Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters lack the required child resistant mechanisms and can expose children to fire hazards.
action: Return the lighters to the retail firm or Sarut Group for a full refund and a discount coupon on your next purchase.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The lighters were sold through internet sales and distribution to retail firms from 2002 to 2003.

heading: CPSC, Neurosmith Announce Recall of Children's Plush Toys
hazard_text: Any of the four plastic button covers can detach, posing a small parts choking hazard to young children.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: Three incidents reported, none resulting in injury.
sold_at: Sold exclusively at Target stores nationwide from August 2003 through October 2003 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Magic Cabin Announce Recall of Wooden Toy Cars
hazard_text: The wheels on the toy car can come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toy away from small children immediately and return the toy to Magic Cabin - Attention: Returns 3700 Wyse Road, Dayton, OH 45414-2541 for a full refund, including postage.
incidents_text: There have been no incidents or injuries reported.
sold_at: Magic Cabin catalogs and website from December 2002 through August 2003 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Home Line Industries Announce Recall of Bunk Beds
hazard_text: These bunk beds have openings between the guardrails and between guardrails and the end structures that are too large. A child's body could slide between the opening and become trapped by the child's head. This poses a strangulation hazard to children.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Furniture stores nationwide from September 2002 through May 2003 for about $190.

product_name: "Pack 'n Play" portable play yards with raised changing tables
heading: CPSC, Graco Children's Products Announce New Safety Instructions to Prevent Injuries with Portable Play Yards with Raised Changing Tables
hazard_text: When children are placed in these portable play yards when the changing table is still in place, they can crawl under and lift the table up. If this occurs, a child's head and neck can become trapped between the changing table and the play yard rail, causing a strangulation hazard. The recall is designed to warn consumers of this hazard, and to provide warning labels to affix to the changing tables.
action: Consumers should never place a child in these portable play yards when the changing table is still in place. Consumers should immediately contact Graco to receive a free warning label to be affixed to the changing table.
incidents_text: The commission and Graco are aware of the death of a 13-month-old girl, who strangled when her neck became trapped between the Pack 'n Play rail and the raised changing table.
sold_at: Discount, department and juvenile product stores nationwide sold these portable play yards from October 2001 through September 2003 for between $99 and $119.

heading: CPSC, Apothecary Products Inc. Announce Recall of "Comforts" Pacifiers
hazard_text: These pacifiers fail federal safety tests, come apart, and can pose a choking hazard to infants and small children.
action: Return the pacifiers to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Many Kroger-owned stores from August 2002 through August 2003 for about $3.50 to $5.

product_name: Dora the Explorer Children's Board Book
heading: CPSC, Simon & Schuster Announce Recall of Children's Books
hazard_text: A plastic replica of a balloon attached to the book can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these books away from young children immediately and contact Simon & Schuster at the Consumer Contact number indicated below to receive a replacement book.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Discount department stores and bookstores nationwide during August 2003 for about $10.

product_name: Bottled Water with Push-Pull Sports Cap in 8 oz., 8.5 oz., and .33 liter bottle sizes
heading: CPSC, Firm Announce Recall of Bottled Water with Sport Caps
hazard_text: When pulled to open, the drinking spout on the sports cap can unexpectedly come off, posing a choking hazard for young children.
action: Consumers should take the bottled water with the sports cap away from children immediately and return it to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: There have been 10 complaints with no injuries reported.
sold_at: The bottled water with this sports cap was sold at a variety of retail outlets including gas stations, grocery, convenience, mass merchandise and drug stores from March 2002 through September 2003 for between $0.59 for a single bottle and $3.29 for multi-packs.

heading: CPSC, SunTech Enterprises Inc. Announce Recall Baby Walkers
hazard_text: The walkers will fit through a standard doorway and are not designed to stop at the edge of a step. Babies using these walkers can be seriously injured or killed if they fall down stairs.
action: Return to the store where purchased or contact the firm to receive a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Small retailers and flea markets in Texas and California sold the walkers from November 2002 through April 2003 for between $15 and $25.

heading: CPSC, Swimways Corp. Announce Recall of Swim Trainers
hazard_text: The nylon body strap on the swim trainer can detach or tear from the flotation device and release a child into water, posing a serious drowning hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the swim trainers immediately and return them to the company for a full refund. Swimways will provide consumers with a self-addressed envelope to return the product.
incidents_text: There have been seven reports of the body straps detaching and two reports of the seams splitting, though no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty pool and toy stores nationwide and Internet retailers sold the flotation devices from January 2003 through July 2003 for about $12.

heading: CPSC, L.M. Becker & Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Necklaces
hazard_text: The necklace's pendant contains high levels of lead, posing a risk of poisoning to young children.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: The firm received one report of a child who swallowed the necklace's pendant, which reportedly resulted in high blood lead levels.
sold_at: Vending machines in malls, discount department and grocery stores nationwide from March 2002 through April 2003 for about 50 cents.

heading: CPSC, CDX Trading Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Jets
hazard_text: Small parts of the toy jet can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Return the toy jets to the place of purchase for a full refund or purchasers from street-sale or flea markets can mail the toy to: C.D.X. Trading Inc. at 1576-78 Gates Avenue, Ridgewood, NY 11385-2728 to receive a refund including postage.
incidents_text: No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Variety and gift stores, flea markets and street-sale vendors sold the toy jets in the New York and New Jersey region from November 2002 through December 2002 for between $5 and $7.

heading: CPSC, Small World Toys Announce Recall of Children's Puzzle
hazard_text: One of the puzzle pieces (a stack of newspapers) poses a small parts choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop young children from playing with these puzzles immediately and return the puzzle to the store where it was purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Small toy stores nationwide sold the puzzles between February 2003 and August 2003 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, HearthSong Announce Recall of "Happyvillagers" Toy Sets
hazard_text: The head can detach from the body of the villagers, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the Happyvillagers away from young children immediately and return to HearthSong for a full refund including the cost of postage. Send the Happyvillagers to HearthSong, Attn: Returns, 3700 Wyse Road, Dayton, OH 45414-2541.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: HearthSong sold the Happyvillagers Toy Sets through their catalog and website from Sept. 30, 2002 through March 11, 2003 for about $15.

product_name: Big Boy Trucks (Dump Truck & Tow Truck)
heading: CPSC, MagicCabin Announce Recall of Toy Trucks
hazard_text: Small parts can break off of the toy trucks, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toys away from young children immediately and return to Magic Cabin for a refund, including the cost of postage. Send the toy trucks to Magic Cabin, Attn: Returns, 3700 Wyse Road, Dayton, OH 45414-2541.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Magic Cabin sold the toy trucks through their catalog and Web site from September 2002 through March 18, 2003 for about $16.

heading: CPSC, Hedstrom Corp. Announce Recall of Trampolines
hazard_text: Welds on the frame of these trampolines can break during use, causing consumers to fall to the ground and suffer injuries.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: Hedstrom had received about 700 reports of one or more welds breaking from the trampoline frame rails during use, resulting in 10 minor injuries.
sold_at: Department, toy, and discount stores nationwide between January 2003 and May 2003 for between $160 and $225 for the single trampolines, and between $320 and $360 for the trampolines banded together with safety enclosures.

heading: CPSC, Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. Announce Recall of Kids Sling Chair
hazard_text: The small plastic bolt covers pose a choking hazard to small children.
action: Consumers should remove the plastic bolt covers or return the chair to Wal-Mart for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Wal-Mart have received two reports of children removing the small covers and placing them in mouths. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores nationwide sold these chairs from Nov. 2002 through May 2003 for about $13.

heading: CPSC, International Playthings Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Stacking Rings
hazard_text: Plastic knobs on the rings can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should contact the company for instructions on how to return the toy to receive a free replacement item of similar value.
incidents_text: The firm has received three reports of small parts detaching from the rings, though no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty toy stores nationwide sold these toys from April 2002 through March 2003 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, De Bon Sales Announce Recall of Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The novelty lighters are not equipped with child-resistant mechanisms. They pose fire and burn hazards to young children.
action: Return the lighters to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Dollar stores in Texas from November 2002 through December 2002 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, DesignPac Announce Recall of Lamp Oil
hazard_text: The bottles of paraffin oil in these sets do not have the child-resistant closures required by federal law.
action: Return the oil lamp sets to any Target store for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide from February 2003 through March 2003 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Small Small World Announce Recall of "Egg Dippers" Easter Plush Toys
hazard_text: The toys' seams can separate and allow small beads to be released, presenting an aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should call the firm on information on getting a free replacement toy.
incidents_text: There have been two reports of children ingesting beads coming out of these plush toys. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Department and specialty stores nationwide sold these toys from February 2003 through April 2003 for about $8.

product_name: Cosco Arriva and Turnabout infant car seats/carriers
heading: CPSC, NHTSA, and Dorel Juvenile Group Inc. Announce Extended Recall of Infant Car Seats/Carriers
hazard_text: When the seat is used as a carrier, the plastic handle locks can unexpectedly break or release from the carrying position, causing the seat to unlatch or flip forward. When this happens, an infant can fall to the ground and suffer injuries.
action: Consumers should continue to use the Arriva and Turnabout as a car seat but should stop using it as a carrier immediately and contact Dorel Juvenile Group to receive a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Dorel Juvenile Group has received 416 reports of the handle locks on the additional recalled infant car seats/carriers breaking or unlatching, resulting in nine injuries to children. These reports include bruises and scratches to the head and face. According to the reports, some injuries occurred to children restrained in the seat.
sold_at: Juvenile product, mass merchandise, department stores and major discount stores nationwide sold the Arriva and Turnabout infant car seats/carriers from Sept. 10, 1997 through December 2000 for between $30 and $60 when sold alone or $90 to $140 when sold with strollers.

heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Crib Mobile Toys
hazard_text: If batteries used in the mobile leak, the caustic liquid can seep out of the battery compartment, posing a risk of chemical burns to babies.
action: Firm providing free repair kits containing a seal for the battery compartment, which will prevent battery leakage.
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has received 30 reports of batteries leaking from the toy's battery compartment, including six reports of minor burn injuries to babies.
sold_at: Discount department stores and toy stores nationwide sold these mobiles between December 1999 and December 2001 for about $25.

heading: CPSC, Creative Kids Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Art Supply Sets
hazard_text: The sets contain mini-cutters with razor blades, which pose a laceration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should remove the mini-cutters from the set and return them to Creative Kids to get a free pack of colored paper clips.
incidents_text: The Commission and Creative Kids are aware of an incident where an 8-year-old girl received minor cuts to her finger when she used the mini-cutter.
sold_at: Bigg's stores in Ohio and Kentucky from August 2002 through March 2003 for about $16.

heading: CPSC, Babi Italia/LaJobi Industries Announce Recall to Replace "Tiffany" and "Josephine" Crib Drop-Side Rails
hazard_text: The slats on the drop-side rails can come loose or detach. A child's head can get caught in the space left by loose or missing slats, presenting an entrapment hazard. In addition, children can fall through the slat opening.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: CPSC and LaJobi have received 41 reports of slats separating from rails of the crib. One child became entrapped between slats that came loose. Ten children fell out of the crib when the slats came out of the drop-side rail. No serious injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Babies R Us sold the recalled cribs exclusively from July 2001 through January 2003 for about $500.

heading: CPSC, Starbucks Coffee Co. Announce Recall of Children's Tumbler Cups
hazard_text: When the flexible straw on the cups is chewed, small pieces of plastic can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Parents and caregivers should stop young children from using these cups immediately, and return the cups to any Starbucks location for a refund and a free beverage of any size.
incidents_text: Starbucks has received two reports of pieces of the straws becoming detached in the children's mouths. No injuries have been reported; however, in one instance, a child reportedly began to choke on a detached piece of the straw and the Heimlich Maneuver was administered by the parent to remove the small piece.
sold_at: Starbucks stores in the United States, Canada and Taiwan sold the recalled cups from April 2003 through May 2003 for approximately $7 (U.S.).

heading: CPSC, The Step2 Company Announce Recall of Toy Drumsticks
hazard_text: The tip of the drumstick can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Contact Step2 to receive a replacement set of drumsticks.
incidents_text: CPSC and Step2 are aware of one incident where a child reportedly began to choke on the top of the drumstick. The child's parent performed the Heimlich maneuver to remove the small part.
sold_at: Toy stores and online retailers sold the drum sets nationwide from February 2002 through April 2003 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, International Playthings Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Vehicles
hazard_text: Small parts on the vehicles can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should contact the company for information on receiving a replacement toy.
incidents_text: International Playthings has received one report of small parts detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty toy stores nationwide sold these toys from April 2002 through March 2003 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Swimways Corp. Announce Recall of Pool Dive Sticks
hazard_text: Children can fall or land on these dive sticks in shallow water and may suffer impalement injuries.
action: Consumers should take these dive sticks away from children immediately and contact Swimways for information on receiving a refund or free replacement product.
sold_at: Specialty pool stores nationwide sold these dive sticks from December 2002 through May 2003 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Amen Wardy Home Announce Recall of Multi-purpose Lighters Shaped Like Matchsticks
hazard_text: The lighters lack child-resistant mechanisms that meet federal safety standards. Young children could operate these lighters, which poses a fire hazard.
action: Contact Amen Wardy Home for instructions on how to obtain a refund for these lighters. Dispose of the lighters in a manner that is in compliance with all state and local requirements. The lighter should not be incinerated or punctured.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The Amen Wardy Home store in Caesar's Palace, at Las Vegas, Nev., and the firm's website sold these lighters from July 2002 through January 2003 for between $10 and $20.

product_name: Wooden convertible cribs sold under the following model names: "Always Crib," "Crib 4 Life," "Legendary Crib," "Set 4 Life," and "Crib-2-College"
heading: CPSC, Baby's Dream Furniture Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Cribs
hazard_text: The three hinges along the fold-down drop gate can crack or break and allow babies to have their fingers pinched. Additionally, a misaligned latch where the latch trigger does not lock securely can allow the drop gate to open if a child leans on it, and the child could fall out.
action: Consumers owning these Baby's Dream cribs should call Baby's Dream at (800) TEL CRIB (835-2742) between 7:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET or visit the firm's website at www.babysdream.com to receive a repair kit for hinges and/or latches or for specific instructions for examining their latches.
incidents_text: Baby's Dream has received 38 reports of broken or cracked hinges, but there have been no injuries reported.Baby's Dream and CPSC have received two reports of injuries to children when the latches did not hold. Injuries included one report of a child whose head was bruised after falling onto the floor when the drop gate latch failed and one report of a crushed finger when the rail unexpectedly moved inward when the parent leaned into the crib. There were five additional reports of children falling out of cribs who received no injury.
sold_at: Juvenile furniture and retail stores nationwide sold these cribs for between $300 and $400.

heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Little People® Animal Sounds Farms
hazard_text: Two small metal screws that hold the toy "stall doors" in place can come off, posing an aspiration or choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toy away from young children immediately and contact Fisher-Price toll-free at (866) 259-7873 anytime to receive a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has received 33 reports of the screws coming off of the toy, including four reports where a screw was found in the child's mouth and one report of a child that aspirated a screw into his lung. The latter case required the child to be hospitalized and undergo emergency surgery to remove the screw from his lung.
sold_at: Mass merchants and toy stores nationwide sold these toys between July 2002 and December 2002 for about $30.

product_name: Toy Drumsticks (sold with the Parents Bee Bop Band drum sets)
heading: CPSC, Battat Incorporated Announce Recall of Drumsticks Sold with Toy Drum Sets
hazard_text: The end piece of the drumstick handle can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children. Additionally, the screw at the end of the drumstick can loosen and detach, posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately take these drumsticks away from young children and contact Battat for a replacement set of drumsticks.
incidents_text: Battat and CPSC have received about 240 reports of drumsticks breaking and children mouthing the small pieces, including one report of a child who began to choke.
sold_at: Target, Sam's Club and smaller retailers sold the Parents Bee Bop Band drum sets nationwide from November 2001 through March 2003 for about $25.

heading: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall of Magic Start Crawl 'n Stand Toys Sold Only at Wal-Mart
hazard_text: The toy, which is designed to encourage crawling babies to pull themselves up and stand, can tip over during use and strike falling babies in the head, face or neck, resulting in injuries.
action: Consumers should take this toy away from children immediately and contact Playskool to get information on how to return the product to receive a free replacement item of similar value.
incidents_text: Playskool has received 44 reports of the toys tipping over during use. There have been 26 reports of babies suffering injuries, including one minor concussion, and various bumps, bruises, black eyes and cut lips.
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores nationwide sold these toys from November 2002 through April 2003 for about $14.

heading: CPSC, Kindermusik International Announce Recall of "Fiddlesticks" Instruments
hazard_text: Some of the Fiddlesticks have caps that can become loose, allowing ball bearings to spill from the inside of the sticks. Both the caps and the ball bearings pose a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the Fiddlesticks immediately and return them to their Kindermusik educator for a free replacement. Kindermusik will replace this product with either re-designed Fiddlesticks or an instrument of comparable value.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Kindermusik educators sold the music kits, including the Fiddlesticks, in the United States and Canada from December 2002 through January 2003.

heading: CPSC, TNT Fireworks Announce Recall of Party Poppers Sold at Wal-Mart
hazard_text: The cone-shaped top can pop off rapidly, and can hit and injure both children and adults.
action: Consumer should stop using these Party Poppers immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and TNT have not received any reports of incidents involving the Party Poppers.
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores sold these Party Poppers nationwide from January 2003 through March 2003 for about $2.

product_name: Lamaze Flower Stroller Wrap and Lamaze Soft Bead Buddies activity toys
heading: CPSC, Learning Curve Int'l Inc. Announce Recall of Lamaze Activity Toys
hazard_text: The paint on the metal wires of these toys contains excess levels of lead. Lead poisoning is a serious hazard to children and is associated with behavioral problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toys away from infants and young children. Consumers should contact RCE/LCI for return and replacement instructions at (800) 704-8697 between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. CT, Monday through Friday.
incidents_text: RCE/LCI has not received any reports of incidents or injuries involving these toys.
sold_at: These toys were sold in March 2003 through specialty and toy stores nationwide for around $19.99.

product_name: Christmas House Plush Bear" and "Christmas House Christmas Plush" dolls
heading: CPSC, Dollar Tree Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Plush Bears and Snowman Dolls
hazard_text: Buttons on the jacket of these toys can be pulled off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Parents and caregivers should take these toys away from young children immediately, and return the toys to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Dollar Tree have received no reports of injuries or incidents.
sold_at: Dollar Tree, Only One Dollar, Only $1, Dollar Express, and Dollar Bills stores nationwide sold these toys from June 2002 through March 2003 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Raymond Oak Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Chests
hazard_text: The toy chest's lid support hinges can fail, allowing the lid to fall onto a child's head, neck, fingers or hands. In addition, spaces at the end of the hinge on the lid can cause pinch, crush or laceration injuries to children's fingers.
action: Consumers should stop children from using the recalled toy chests immediately and contact the firm to receive a $79 refund. Raymond Oak Inc. has contacted all known purchasers by phone or mail. All but 20 of the toy chests have been returned.
incidents_text: CPSC and Raymond Oak Inc. have received one report of a 7-year-old girl whose finger was bruised after the toy chest lid slammed down on her left index finger.
sold_at: Furniture stores nationwide sold the recalled toy chests from May 2000 through January 2002 for about $99.

heading: CPSC, Walt Disney Parks and Resorts Announce Recall of Woody Dolls
hazard_text: The Woody doll's clothing has buttons that can detach, posing a choking hazard for young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the doll away from children and contact Walt Disney Parks and Resorts at (866) 228-3664 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: Walt Disney Parks and Resorts has received one report of a child removing a button from the Woody doll. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The Woody dolls were sold at the WALT DISNEY WORLD® Resort in Lake Buena Vista, Florida, DISNEY'S VERO BEACH Resort, Magic of Disney and Flight Fantastic shops located at the Orlando International Airport, and Disney's Worldport shop located at Pointe Orlando, from January 2000 through January 2003 for about $12.

heading: CPSC, S. Rothschild & Co. Announce Recall to Repair Girls' Hooded Winter Jackets
hazard_text: The rubber petal and metal snap can break off of the jacket, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these jackets immediately and contact S. Rothschild and Co. at (800) 301-3411 between 8 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to arrange for the jacket to be repaired and returned free of charge.
incidents_text: S. Rothschild has received two reports of the rubber petal coming off the jacket, including one child who reportedly put the petal in her mouth. The snaps have come off in subsequent testing.
sold_at: Major retail stores nationwide sold the jackets from May 2002 through December 2002 for about $25 to $45.

product_name: Lands' End Little Girl's Fur Trimmed Parka and Little Kids' Reversible Down Parka
heading: CPSC, Lands' End, Inc., Announce Recall of Little Kids' Parkas
hazard_text: The zipper box may detach, allowing the zipper slide to detach. The small parts, if detached, could pose a risk of choking.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using this product and contact Lands' End toll free at (800) 200-6212 or visit the website at www.landsend.com Many purchasers were contacted directly by letter and provided with a replacement parka. If you have not received a letter regarding this product, please contact Lands' End to discuss the return, refund or replacement of your child's parka.
incidents_text: Lands' End, Inc. has received reports of the zipper detaching, but no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The parkas were sold through the Lands' End catalog, website and certain Sears, Roebuck and Co. retail stores from November 2002 through mid-January 2003 for $79.50 or below.

heading: CPSC, Random House, Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Board Book Sets
hazard_text: The book sets were sold in cardboard boxes with plastic snaps. The plastic snaps can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately cut off the lid of the box with the plastic snaps and throw away the rest of the box. Send the lid with the plastic snaps to Tri-State, c/o Anthony Armetta, 325 Rabro Drive, Hauppauge, NY 11788 to receive a free replacement book set, and a refund for postage.
incidents_text: CPSC and Random House have not received any reports of injuries involving these book sets.
sold_at: Book, discount department stores and online retailers sold the recalled books nationwide from August 2002 through January 2003 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, The Betesh Group Announce Recall of "Busy Bug" Plush Toys
hazard_text: The antennae of the plush toy can be chewed or pulled off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the plush toys away from young children and return to the place of purchase or mail the toy to The Betesh Group at One East 33rd Street, New York, NY 10016, Att: Consumer Relations, to receive a refund including postage.
incidents_text: CPSC and The Betesh Group have received two reports of children gagging on the fabric antennae ends that separated from the toy.
sold_at: Discount department stores sold these recalled toys from August 2002 through January 2003 for about $7.

heading: CPSC, The First Years® Inc. Announce New Safety Instructions to Prevent Injuries for Combo Baby Tubs/Step Stools
hazard_text: When used as a tub, babies' body parts can be pinched if the product's footrest is not fully extended so that it clicks into place firmly.
action: Consumers should not use the bathtub until they receive revised instructions on the use of the tub to prevent the pinching hazard. Consumers should contact The First Years at (800) 533-6708 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive free revised instructions and a warning label to attach to the product.
incidents_text: CPSC and The First Years have received 20 reports of babies being pinched while using these tubs, including one bruising of a baby boy's genitalia and 10 reports of abrasions to toes and feet. This recall to replace the stools' instructions is being conducted to prevent further incidents.
sold_at: Mass merchants nationwide sold these bathtub/stools between January 1999 and February 2002 for about $17.

heading: CPSC, BRIO Corp. Announce Recall of Toy Trumpet
hazard_text: A small knob on the side of the trumpet can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toy trumpets away from young children immediately and return them to BRIO for a replacement toy trumpet or another toy of equal value.
incidents_text: BRIO has not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these toy trumpets.
sold_at: Back to Basics Toys, a mail order catalog, sold the trumpets nationwide from September 2001 through November 2002 for about $13.

heading: CPSC, Playnation Play Systems Announce Recall of "Fun Buckets" on Backyard Play Sets
hazard_text: As children play on the play set's slide or platform, the 6- to 8-ft free-hanging rope can become entangled around the child's neck. This presents a strangulation hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take down the "Fun Buckets" immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or a credit toward another product.
incidents_text: Playnation is aware of two incidents where the bucket's rope became entangled around the necks of two 4-year-olds. Both of the children were freed without injury. However, CPSC knows of 135 children who have died in the last 10 years from all types of ropes, leashes or jump ropes that were attached to backyard play sets.
sold_at: Distributors of backyard play sets nationwide sold the fun buckets from February 1998 through February 2003 for about $25.

heading: CPSC, Young's J.K. Inc. Announce Recall of Novelty Lighters
hazard_text: These lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children can ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using the lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC has received one report of a 2-year-old using one of these lighters to ignite an upholstered chair. The fire resulted in the death of his 6-year-old brother and permanent brain damage to the 2-year old.
sold_at: Gas stations, smoke shops, grocery, gift and liquor stores sold the lighters in Oregon and Southwest Washington from 1996 through October 2001 for between $8 and $20.

heading: CPSC Announces Recall of Baseline Design Beanbag Chairs
hazard_text: Some of these beanbag chairs have zippers that can be opened, allowing access to the polystyrene beads inside the chairs. This poses a suffocation hazard to young children who can unzip the chair and inhale the small beads.
action: Consumers should check if they can unzip their Baseline Design beanbag chairs. If the zippers can be unzipped freely, Baseline Design will provide owners with a free replacement beanbag chair with zippers that do not open. Consumers should be sure young children cannot use the chairs if the zipper can be opened freely and should be sure children are not exposed to the beads inside the chair.
incidents_text: Baseline Design is aware of three incidents in which the chairs were unzipped freely. Two of the incidents involved young children who were able to open the beanbag chair zippers and handle the small polystyrene beads, including one child who received medical attention after inhaling the beads.
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores located in the Northeast U.S. sold the beanbag chairs from September 1999 through December 1999 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, Magic Cabin Announce Recall of Wooden Teething Rings
hazard_text: It is a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the teething rings away from children and contact Magic Cabin for a full refund and a $15 gift certificate.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Magic Cabin sold the teething rings through its catalog and website from September 2002 through November 2002 for about $15.

heading: CPSC, Hufco-Delaware Company and Evenflo Company Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Gerry® and Evenflo® Portable Wood Cribs
hazard_text: If the hardware used to assemble the crib is not tight, the mattress support platform and mattress can fall to the floor. This poses a risk of injury to young children in the crib.
action: Consumers should stop using these portable wood cribs immediately, and call (800) 582-9359 anytime for a free upgrade kit that provides additional support for the mattress platform.
incidents_text: There have been 41 reports of mattresses falling through portable wood cribs. Of these incidents, 17 children suffered bumps, bruises or scratches.
sold_at: Department and baby product stores nationwide sold these portable wood cribs from January 1991 through December 2002 for about $99.

heading: CPSC, Build-A-Bear Workshop Announce Recall of "Founding Bear" Stuffed Bears
hazard_text: The nose of the stuffed bear can be pulled or twisted off, posing a choking hazard to a young child.
action: Consumers should take these stuffed bears away from young children immediately. Build-A-Bear Workshop will exchange the bear for any other item they sell of equal value or provide a Build-A-Bear Workshop gift card. Consumers should return the stuffed bears to any Build-A-Bear Workshop store or contact the firm for instructions on mailing the bear.
incidents_text: Build-A-Bear Workshop has not received any reports of injuries resulting from these stuffed bears.
sold_at: Build-A-Bear Workshop stores and website sold these stuffed bears nationwide between March 2000 and December 2002 for between $22 and $25.

heading: CPSC, Pace Products Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Soap Making Kits
hazard_text: The soap may get too hot when heated in the microwave oven and leak from the tray mold, posing a burn hazard to children.
action: Consumers should take these soap kits away from children immediately and contact Pace Products at (800) 541-7670 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive instructions on returning the soap kits for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC has received three reports of burn injuries from the heated soap, including a 6-year-old girl who received burns to her hand.
sold_at: Scholastic Book Clubs and Book Fairs sold the recalled soap kits at schools nationwide from March 2000 through November 2002 and bookstores sold the recalled soap kits from March 1998 through November 2002 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Kmart Corp. Announce Recall of Wooden Toy Vehicles
hazard_text: These products may be given to children as toys. The wheels on the wooden toys may break off into small parts, which may pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take them away from children immediately and return them to any Kmart store for a full refund.
incidents_text: Kmart has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Kmart stores nationwide sold these wooden vehicles from November 2002 through December 2002 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Elkton Sparkler Announce Recall of Bamboo-Stick Sparklers
hazard_text: The sparklers' bamboo-stick handles can catch fire, burn and disintegrate and emit burning fragments during use. The sparklers present a fire hazard and a risk of burn injury.
action: Consumers should stop using these sparklers immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Elkton Sparkler have received four reports of burns and clothing igniting. Injuries include a 6-year-old girl who received second-degree burns to her ankle and a 3-year-old boy who received a minor burn to his leg when his sweatpants caught on fire.
sold_at: Variety Stores sold these sparklers nationwide from January 2002 through May 2002 for between $2 and $5 a box.

heading: CPSC, Lovee Doll & Toy Co., Inc. Announce Recall of Talking Dolls
hazard_text: Buttons on the dolls' outfit could detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these dolls away from children immediately and return the dolls to the store where it was purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: Lovee Doll & Toy Co., Inc. has not received any reports of incidents involving these dolls. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Toy and discount department stores sold the dolls nationwide from June 2002 through December 2002 for between $10 and $15.

heading: CPSC, Kohl's Department Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Fleece Pant Sets
hazard_text: Small pieces of fabric at the end of the sleeves, along the hem and on the pockets of the tops can be torn off easily, posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using the set immediately and return it to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: Kohl's Department Stores Inc. has received two reports of young children putting torn pieces of fabric in their mouths. One child reportedly began to choke on a piece of material.
sold_at: Kohl's Department Stores sold the pant set nationwide from September 2002 through early November 2002 for about $18.

heading: CPSC, Zutano Inc. Announce Recall of Stuffed Bunny Toys
hazard_text: The buttons on the front of the bunnies' jacket can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these recalled bunny toys away from young children immediately and contact Zutano Inc. to receive a replacement outfit.
incidents_text: Zutano has not received any reports of injuries relating to these stuffed bunny toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Department and specialty stores nationwide sold the recalled bunny toys from July 2000 through December 2002 for about $18.

heading: CPSC, Wear Me Apparel Corp. Announce Recall of Infant Girls' Garments
hazard_text: The paint on the "smiley face" zipper-pull attached to the sweat jacket of these garments contains lead. Young children could ingest lead from the zipper-pull, presenting a lead poisoning hazard.
action: Consumers should return the clothing sets to any Kmart store to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: Wear Me Apparel Corp. and CPSC have not received any reports of injuries involving these garments. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Kmart stores nationwide exclusively sold these garments from August 2002 through October 2002 for between $10 and $13.

heading: CPSC, Montrose Wholesale Candies & Sundries Inc. Announce Recall of Illegally Imported Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Montrose Wholesale Candies & Sundries are not aware of any injuries involving these lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Convenience, gas, and grocery stores in the central U.S. sold these disposable cigarette lighters from September 2002 through December 2002 for about $1.

product_name: Kid's Tent Set (only the tunnel is recalled)
heading: CPSC, The Lakeside Collection Announce Recall of Kid's Tent Set
hazard_text: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible lacerations.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the tent set and contact The Lakeside Collection to obtain instructions on how to return the connecting tunnel for a replacement at no charge.
incidents_text: There have been no injuries.
sold_at: They are mostly red, blue and yellow and were sold by The Lakeside Collection from May 2002 through November 2002 for about $23.

heading: CPSC, LTD Commodities, Inc. Announce Recall of Kid's Tent Set
hazard_text: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible lacerations.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the tent set and contact LTD Commodities, Inc. to obtain instructions on how to return the connecting tunnel for a replacement at no charge.
incidents_text: LTD Commodities, Inc received one report, in which a child's leg was cut, requiring nine stitches.
sold_at: They are mostly red, blue and yellow and were sold by LTD Commodities, Inc. from May 2002 through November 2002 for about $23.

heading: CPSC, Good Lad Apparel Announce Recall of Infant Girls' Garment and Shoes
hazard_text: Small, decorative items on the garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these garments and sandals immediately. Consumers should return the garments to the store where purchased to receive a refund.
incidents_text: Good Lad has received three reports of incidents involving the decorative items. A child swallowed a decorative ladybug and two others began to choke on decorative flowers. There have been no reports of injury.
sold_at: Department stores sold the infant garments nationwide from January 2002 through April 2002 for about $15.

heading: CPSC, abc Distributing, Inc. Announce Recall of Kid's Tent Set
hazard_text: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible laceration injuries.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the tent set and contact abc Distributing, Inc. to obtain instructions on how to return the connecting tunnel for a replacement at no charge.
incidents_text: abc Distributing, Inc. has received three reports, two with minor injuries, as a result of the tip of the wire becoming exposed.
sold_at: They are mostly red, blue and yellow and were sold by abc Distributing, Inc. from March 2002 through June 2002 for about $23.

heading: CPSC, Kolcraft Announce Recall of Toy Attachments on Baby Walkers
hazard_text: The flower toys on the baby walker's tray can detach from the stems, exposing sharp edges and posing a laceration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should remove the detachable toy bars or music center toy trays on these walkers immediately.
incidents_text: Kolcraft has received 15 reports of injuries associated with the exposed sharp edges of the toys' stems. The injuries to children included lacerations around the eyes, eyelids, face and tongue.
