sold_at: Discount, department and juvenile product stores sold the walkers with these toys nationwide from December 2000 through October 2002 for between $20 and $40.

heading: CPSC, Baby Trend Announce Recall to Repair Infant Swings Sold at Toys R Us
action: Consumers should stop using these recalled swings immediately and contact Baby Trend to receive a free repair kit.
sold_at: Toys R Us stores sold these swings nationwide from November 2001 through September 2002 for between $60 and $90.

heading: CPSC, Disney Store Announce Recall of Monsters, Inc. Character Plush Dolls
hazard_text: The Boo doll's hair has ponytail holders that could detach, posing a choking hazard for young children.
action: Consumers should immediately remove and discard the two pink ponytail holders and two rubber bands from the Boo doll's hair or return the item to any Disney Store for a full refund.
incidents_text: The Disney Store has not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these dolls and is voluntarily recalling them to prevent future incidents.
sold_at: The Disney Stores nationwide exclusively sold these plush dolls from July 2002 through October 2002 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Estyle, Inc. recall Children's Jackets
hazard_text: The jackets do not meet the Standard for the Flammability of Clothing Textiles under the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
action: Consumers should stop using the jackets immediately and contact Estyle, Inc. for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Estyle sold the jackets on their web site from March 2002 through June 2002 for about $68.

product_name: Flashlights and Batteries Sold in Kids Meals
heading: CPSC, Halo Burger Announce Recall of Flashlights and Batteries Sold in Kids Meals
hazard_text: When disassembled, the flashlights also have small parts that can pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these flashlights and batteries away from children immediately and return the flashlights and batteries to any Halo Burger restaurant to receive a $5 gift certificate, or discard flashlights and batteries in a safe manner.
incidents_text: Halo Burger received two reports of young children who received minor skin irritation on their mouths from leaking flashlight batteries.
sold_at: Halo Burger restaurants distributed the flashlights as a premium with the kids meals in Genesee and Saginaw Counties in Michigan from October 2002 through November 4, 2002. The flashlights were sold individually for about $1.50.

heading: CPSC, Damo Plus Corp. Announce Recall of Children's School Supply Sets
hazard_text: The sets contain razor knives, which pose a laceration hazard to children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these razor knives away from children and return the pencil sets to the store where they purchased them for a refund.
incidents_text: Damo Plus has not received any reports of injuries from these pencil sets. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Discount and dollar stores in California, Texas, Washington, and Maryland sold the sets between June and October 2002 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Eveready Battery Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Kidz Club Flashlights
hazard_text: The flashlights can overheat and cause the batteries to leak, posing a risk of burns to children.
action: Consumers should take these flashlights away from children immediately and remove the batteries and contant Everready for instructions on returning the flashlights and receiving a $12 refund.
incidents_text: Eveready has received three reports of the flashlights overheating, including one report of a 4-year-old boy receiving a minor burn to his hand.
sold_at: Discount department and toy stores sold these flashlights nationwide from April 2002 through October 2002 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, IKEA Announce Recall of Stuffed Teddy Bears
hazard_text: The plastic beads inside of the bears could come out of the seams, posing an aspiration hazard to young children who could inhale the small beads.
action: Consumers should take these bears away from young children immediately and return them to an IKEA store for a $5 gift card towards another IKEA product.
incidents_text: IKEA has not received any report of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: IKEA stores nationwide sold the bears from August 2001 through September 2002 for about $2.

heading: CPSC, BRIO® Corporation Announce Recall of Caterpillar Pull Toy
hazard_text: The antenna on the pull toy can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these caterpillar toys away from children immediately and send them to BRIO® to receive a replacement toy or a refund, including the cost of postage.
incidents_text: BRIO® has not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Specialty toy stores, Internet retailers and mail order catalogs sold the caterpillar toys nationwide from January 2002 through September 2002 for about $15.

heading: CPSC, Oriental International Trading Company Announce Recall of Baby Walkers
hazard_text: The walkers will fit through a standard doorway and are not designed to stop at the edge of a step. Babies using these walkers can be seriously injured or killed if they fall downstairs.
action: Consumers should stop using these walkers immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: Oriental International Trading has not received any reports of injuries involving these walkers. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Independent discount stores located in Arizona, California, Texas, Illinois, North Carolina and New York sold these baby walkers from May 2001 through June 2002 for between $18 and $22.

heading: CPSC, Dollar Tree Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Stuffed Pool Animal
hazard_text: The seams can separate exposing the polyester stuffing and foam beads. The foam beads pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these stuffed animals away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Dollar Tree Stores have received one report of the seam ripping, exposing the polyester stuffing and a plastic bag containing foam beads. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Dollar Tree, Only One Dollar, Only $1, Dollar Express and Dollar Bills sold the stuffed animals nationwide from April 2002 through August 2002 for $1.

heading: CPSC, Dollar Tree Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Sponges
hazard_text: The eyes on the toys can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these sponge animals away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Dollar Tree Stores have received one report of an eye coming off. No injuries have been reported. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Dollar Tree, Only One Dollar, Only $1, Dollar Express and Dollar Bills sold the stuffed animals nationwide from May 2001 through September 2002 for $1.

heading: CPSC, Bikepro, Inc. Announce Recall of Baby Walkers
hazard_text: The baby walkers can fit through a standard doorway and are not designed to stop at the edge of a step. Babies using these baby walkers could be seriously injured or killed if they fall down stairs.
action: Consumers should stop using these walkers immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: Bikepro, Inc. has not received any reports of injuries involving these walkers. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Independent discount stores located in Arizona, California, Colorado, Texas, Michigan, Missouri and New York sold these baby walkers from January 2000 through August 2001 for between $18 and $22.

heading: CPSC, McDonald's Corp. and Bobble Dreams USA Announce Recall of Chicago Bears Bobble Head Figurines
hazard_text: The paint on some of the figurines contains excess levels of lead. If ingested over time by children, the lead from the paint may present a lead poisoning hazard.
action: Consumers should keep these figurines away from children and contact McDonald's at (800) 244-6227 to receive return and refund instructions.
incidents_text: McDonald's has not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these figurines. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: McDonald's restaurants sold the figurines in the greater Chicago area, Northwest Indiana, Central Illinois and Rockford as part of a promotion that ran from August 19, 2002 through September 12, 2002 for about $5.00.

heading: CPSC, Huffy Sports Company Announce Recall to Repair Portable Basketball Hoops
hazard_text: The basketball hoops can have a sharp protruding bolt on the player's side of the pole that can cause serious leg or body lacerations to consumers. Basketball players can be cut when they collide with the pole as they drive toward the basket or when they fall or are pushed into the pole.
action: Consumers should examine their units immediately. If there is a protruding bolt in the area of play, contact Huffy Sports to receive free bolt covers.
incidents_text: CPSC and Huffy Sports have received 11 reports of injuries from protruding bolts that include scrapes and lacerations. Ten consumers required stitches for their injuries.
sold_at: Sporting good, department and toy stores sold the Huffy-brand portable basketball systems from November 2001 through May 2002 for between $100 and $200.

heading: CPSC, Team Beans LLC Announce Recall of "Bottle Cap Bear" Key Chains
hazard_text: A miniature "Coca-Cola" bottle that attaches to the body of the plush bear key chain can come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the key chains away from children immediately and return them to Team Beans for a refund or credit plus postage. Mail the item to Team Beans Forever Collectibles,
incidents_text: Team Beans LLC has not received any reports of bottles attached to the key chains coming off. This recall is being announced to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Select auto racing souvenir shops and collectibles stores nationwide sold the key chains from January 2002 through July 2002 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, XL Machine Ltd. Announce Recall of Playskool Toy Chests Sold at Target
hazard_text: Screws in the chests' lid support hinges can loosen over time, and come out from the base of the toy chests. If this happens, the lids of the toy chests can collapse suddenly, possibly causing injuries to children's head, neck, fingers or hands.
action: Consumers should take these toy chests away from young children immediately and return them to the Target store where it was purchased for a refund or store credit.
incidents_text: CPSC and XL have received one report of screws in the lid support hinge of a toy chest coming out, resulting in one injury, a bruise to the neck.
sold_at: Target stores sold the toy chest nationwide from October 2001 through December 2001 for about $50.

heading: CPSC, Lawn-Boy Announce Recall of Walk-Behind Mowers
hazard_text: The vendor who manufactured the mulch plates for Lawn-Boy used the wrong material, making the plates brittle and easy to crack or break if struck by a stone or stick while mowing. Objects coming through a broken plate or pieces of the plate could possibly injure the operator or bystanders.
action: Consumers should stop using these mowers in the mulching mode immediately and contact Lawn-Boy to receive a replacement cover plate.
incidents_text: Lawn-Boy has received five reports of broken mulch plates. No injuries or property damage have been reported.
sold_at: Lawn-Boy dealers, department and home center stores sold the mowers nationwide from February 2002 to August 2002 for between $250 and $580.

heading: CPSC, S&G Enterprises, Inc. Announce Recall of Statue of Liberty Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and contact S&G Enterprises, Inc. at (718) 832-2931 between 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The lighters were sold nationwide from May 1999 to May 2001 for $9.95.

product_name: Star Clacker wooden toys and Ride-On Duck wooden riding toys
heading: CPSC, Pottery Barn Kids Announce Recall of Wooden Clacker and Ride-On Toys
hazard_text: The wooden peg can come off of the Star Clacker toy and pose a choking hazard. The Ride-On Duck's wheel cap can break, allowing the wheel to come off and release small parts, also presenting a choking hazard to young children. The Star Clacker wooden toys also do not comply with the Federal Hazardous Substance Act for design and construction of baby rattles, due to the handle length.
action: Consumers should take the recalled toys away from young children immediately and return the toys to the store where they were purchased for a refund or replacement toy.
units: About 3,800 Star Clacker wooden toys, and about 3,000 Ride-On Duck wooden riding toys
incidents_text: Pottery Barn Kids has received one report of a wheel coming off of the Ride-on Duck toy. No injuries have been reported for either product.
sold_at: Pottery Barn Kids stores nationwide sold the Star Clacker toys from April 2002 through July 2002 for about $6. Pottery Barn Kids stores nationwide, catalogs and Internet site sold the Ride-On Duck toys from September 2001 through June 2002 for about $49.

heading: CPSC, Radio Flyer Inc. Announce Recall to Replace Steering Wheel on Toy Car
hazard_text: A child can pull the horn from the steering wheel, and a small part inside poses a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these Roadsters from young children immediately and contact Redwagons to order a replacement steering wheel.
incidents_text: Radio Flyer has received 19 reports of horns detaching from the steering wheel.
sold_at: Toy stores, discount stores, catalogues and web retailers sold the Model 8 Roadsters nationwide between January 2001 and July 2002 for about $70.

heading: CPSC, Small World Toys Announce Recall of Sorter Toys
hazard_text: The plastic windows on the "see-inside" sorting blocks can break, causing the beads inside to be released. This presents a choking hazard to children.
action: Consumers should take the recalled shape sorters away from children immediately and return the toys to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: Small World has received one report of a sorter block breaking.
sold_at: Toy stores sold the sorters nationwide from May 2002 through June 2002 for about $20.

product_name: "Toddler ToteTM" toddler activity sets and "Familiar Things" toddler puzzles
heading: CPSC, Lauri® Inc. Announce Recall of Toddler Activity Sets and Puzzles
hazard_text: The dog puzzle included with both of these products and the rubber handle on the box of the activity set can tear apart into small pieces and pose a choking hazard to small children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from children immediately and call Lauri for free replacement pieces.
units: About 110,000 "Toddler ToteTM" toddler activity sets, and about 11,000 "Familiar Things" toddler puzzles
incidents_text: CPSC and Lauri Inc. have not received any reports of incidents or injuries with these puzzles or handles.
sold_at: Specialty toy stores, web retailers and school supply catalogs sold the recalled puzzle and activity sets from January 1999 to July 2002. Toddler Totes were sold for about $15 and Familiar Things were sold for about $20.

heading: CPSC, BRIO® Corporation and Small World Toys Announce Recall of Snail Pull Toy
hazard_text: The eyes on the pull toy can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these pull toys away from children immediately and call BRIO® for a refund. For more information, consumers can contact BRIO® at (888) 274-6869 between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday. Consumers should return the recalled pull toys to BRIO Corp., SAFETY RECALL - Snail, N120 W18485 Freistadt Road, Germantown, Wis. 53022.
incidents_text: CPSC, BRIO® and Small World Toys are not aware of any incidents or injuries involving the pull toy.
sold_at: Specialty toy stores, Internet retailers and mail order catalogs sold the recalled pull-along snails nationwide from June 2001 through June 2002 for about $15.

product_name: Novelty cigarette lighters in the shape of "Coca Cola" and "Budweiser" beverage cans
heading: CPSC, Young's J.K. Inc. Announce Recall of Novelty Lighters
hazard_text: These lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, posing fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Young's J.K. Inc. have not received any reports of injuries or incidents.
sold_at: Grocery, gift, and liquor stores, as well as smoke shops and gas station food marts in Oregon and southwest Washington sold these lighters from October 2001 through February 2002 for about $3.

heading: CPSC, Cane Creek Announce Recall of Bicycle Suspension Seat Posts
hazard_text: The seat post's cradle, which attaches to the bicycle seat, can break, posing the risk of falls and serious injury to riders.
action: Consumers should stop using these seat posts immediately and return them to the company for a free repair.
incidents_text: Cane Creek has received 18 reports of cradles breaking; though, no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Independent bicycle dealers nationwide sold these seat posts between November 2000 and June 2002 for about $140.

heading: CPSC, Jakks Pacific Inc. Announce Recall to Replace Certain Cans of "Smatter" Spray Foam
hazard_text: If the pressurized can is left in a hot automobile, it can forcefully break apart and cause injury to a nearby consumer.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled "Smatter" away from children and contact Jakks Pacific, Inc. at (800) 554-5516 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday, for information on receiving a free replacement "Smatter" product.
incidents_text: Jakks Pacific has received eight reports of the aerosol container breaking apart. One child reportedly suffered a minor bump on the head when a can of spray foam broke apart after being in a hot car. In two cases, car windshields were cracked.
sold_at: Discount department and toy stores sold the recalled "Smatter" products nationwide from February 2002 through June 5, 2002 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Hilton Hotels Corporation Announce Recall of Vacation Station™ Children's Cooler/Chairs
hazard_text: When the chair collapses the folding mechanism can pose a crushing, cutting or severing hazard to consumers' fingers.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled cooler/chairs immediately and contact Hilton Hotels for information on returning the cooler/chairs and receiving a free replacement item.
incidents_text: CPSC and Hilton Hotels are aware of one report in which part of a 2-year-old boy's fingertip was severed when the chair collapsed.
sold_at: Participating Hilton®, Doubletree®, and Hilton Garden Inn® hotels and resorts nationwide distributed the cooler chairs between May 2002 and June 2002 for free to hotel guests with children.

heading: CPSC, L.A. Lighter Inc. Announce Recall of Disposable Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters may have child-resistant mechanisms that do not meet federal safety standards. Young children may be able to operate these lighters, which could pose a fire hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and contact L.A. Lighter at (800) 499-4708 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: L.A. Lighter has not received any reports of incidents.
sold_at: Retailers and distributors nationwide sold these lighters between December 2000 and May 2001 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Hammacher Schlemmer & Co. Announce Recall of Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters were imported into this country without first being tested to ensure they comply with the Consumer Product Safety Commission's requirements that the lighters be child-resistant. Child- resistant requirements were adopted to reduce the risk of fires and deaths caused by children playing with multi-purpose lighters.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately. Consumers should dispose of the lighter in a manner that is in compliance with any state or local requirements. Consumers can obtain a refund by mailing the black plastic case of the lighter and the use instructions that were included in the case to Hammacher Schlemmer® along with a signed statement confirming the lighter has been disposed of. Consumers will receive their choice of a $50 Hammacher Schlemmer® gift certificate or a refund of the $39.95 purchase price for each lighter purchased.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The Hammacher Schlemmer® catalog sold the lighters nationwide between August 2001 and February 2002 for $39.95.

heading: CPSC, Radio Flyer Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Ride-On Push Cars
hazard_text: A child can pull the horn off the car's steering wheel, and a small part inside poses a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should take the recalled cars away from young children immediately and contact Radio Flyer Inc. to receive a replacement steering wheel.
incidents_text: Radio Flyer Inc. has received three reports of the horns being pulled off, but no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Toy stores, catalogues and web retailers sold these cars nationwide from February 1999 through June 2002 for about $60.

product_name: Toy tracks attached to children's activity centers
heading: CPSC and Graco Announce Recall of Toy Track on Activity Centers
hazard_text: The toy track can break, presenting a cut or pinch hazard, and exposed small parts pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these activity centers with toy tracks immediately, and contact Graco to receive a free replacement track.
incidents_text: Graco has received 11 reports of the toy tracks breaking. Four children received minor scratches and one child's finger was pinched.
sold_at: Discount, department and juvenile product stores sold the activity centers nationwide from November 2001 through May 2002 for between $30 and $70.

heading: CPSC, Specialty Sales Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Novelty Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: These lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, posing fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Specialty Sales Co. Inc. have not received any reports of injuries or incidents.
sold_at: Convenience and liquor stores and gas station food markets in northern California sold these lighters from March 1999 through April 2002 for about $4.

heading: CPSC, Little Tikes Announce Recall of Pop 'n Scoot Ride-on Toys
hazard_text: Young children who lean forward can fall forward over the handlebars, causing facial injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using the toys immediately and contact Little Tikes at www.littletikes.com or call (800) 321-0183 anytime to receive a Little Tikes replacement product.
incidents_text: Little Tikes has received 10 reports of children falling forward over the toy's handlebars. Seven injuries to children include damaged teeth, stitches to the chin, cuts and scratches to the mouth and face.
sold_at: Toy stores nationwide sold the riding toys from March 2001 through May 13, 2002 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, D.A.M. Clothing, Inc., Announce Recall of Basic Editions 2 Piece Toddler Girls Short Set
hazard_text: The buttons on the garment are sewn on too loosely, creating a danger of them falling off or being easily pulled off, which poses a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these garments immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: K-Mart stores nationwide sold these short sets from February 2002 to March 2002 for about $7.

heading: CPSC, Lands' End, Inc. Announce Recall of Soft Farm Set
hazard_text: The legs of the chicken and duck figures may detach, posing a risk of choking.
action: Consumers should stop using the toy immediately and either remove the legs from the chicken and duck figures or contact Lands' End to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: Lands' End has received one report of detached legs. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Lands' End Inc. catalog and website sold these sets nationwide from January 2002 to April 2002 for about $34.

heading: CPSC, Southern Wood Products Announce Recall of Children's Toy Box
hazard_text: The middle lid support hinge can collapse suddenly and cause an injury to a child's head, neck, fingers, or hands; or can become an entrapment hazard to young children.
action: Consumers who purchased the toy box should stop using the toy box immediately and contact Southern Wood Products to receive a free replacement hinge.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: JC Penney sold the toy box through its catalogue from Feb 2002 until March 2002.

heading: CPSC, The Sportsman's Guide Announce Recall of the Big Red Wagon
hazard_text: The Big Red Wagon has four rubber wheels that include plastic rims that may break and explode under pressure when being inflated. Parts of the wheel and the tire can strike and injure anyone nearby.
action: Consumers should stop using the Big Red Wagon immediately and contact The Sportsman's Guide to receive free replacement wheels and a $10 coupon.
incidents_text: The Sportsman's Guide is aware of eight incidents in which the tires have exploded. Three of the incidents involved adult consumers who sustained injuries described as lacerations to the hand and abrasions.
sold_at: The Sportsman's Guide sold the red wagon nationwide through its catalogue, the Internet and the Sportsman's Guide retail store from October 2001 through April 2002 for about $60.

heading: CPSC, Spin Master Toys Announce Recall of Firestormer and Skyblazer Toy Planes
hazard_text: The plastic air intake chamber of the air-powered toy planes can burst, throwing plastic pieces, posing a laceration, bruise and abrasion hazard to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using the planes immediately and contact Spin Master Toys at (800) 622-8339 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive a free replacement plane.
incidents_text: Spin Master Toys has received seven reports of Firestormer planes bursting, including four reports of injuries to children. Injuries included one chest abrasion, a cut leg, a bruised shoulder and ringing in the ears. There have been no reports involving the Skyblazer planes.
sold_at: Hobby shops and department stores nationwide, including Wal-Mart, Toys R Us, Target and K-mart sold these planes between January 2002 and May 20, 2002 for about $20.

product_name: Toy steering wheel attachment sold on Kolcraft's Jeep® Cherokee stroller
heading: CPSC, Kolcraft Announce Recall of Toy Steering Wheels Sold on Strollers
hazard_text: The steering wheel can break away from its base, allowing the small plastic turn signal and horn pieces to come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should remove the toy steering wheel on these strollers and contact Kolcraft to receive a free replacement toy steering wheel.
incidents_text: Kolcraft has not received any reports of injury involving these strollers.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and juvenile products stores nationwide sold these strollers from January 2001 through May 2002 for between $80 and $90.

heading: CPSC, Aqua-Leisure Industries Inc. Remind Consumers about Recall of Inflatable Baby Floats
hazard_text: The leg holes in the seat of the float can tear, causing children to unexpectedly fall into the water and possibly drown.
action: Consumers should stop using these recalled floats immediately and contact Aqua-Leisure for a free replacement.
incidents_text: Aqua-Leisure and CPSC have received 12 reports of the float's seats tearing and causing children to fall into the water. There were four incidents of children becoming completely submerged before a caregiver was able to reach them. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile products, specialty and discount department stores nationwide, including Target, K-Mart, Bed Bath and Beyond and Baby Central, sold the baby floats from August 2000 through September 2001 for between $10 and $13.

heading: CPSC, Rose Art Industries Announce Recall to Repair Cotton Candy Machine
hazard_text: The motors on the cotton candy machines can jam and overheat, posing a fire hazard. Additionally, the heating unit can be activated without the spinner in place, presenting a risk of burn to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using these cotton candy machines immediately and contact Rose Art at (888) 262-4474 anytime for a free replacement motor unit, and free samples of flavored sugar to make cotton candy.
incidents_text: CPSC and Rose Art have received 225 reports of the machines overheating. There have been three reports of fire, one resulting in an estimated $2,000 in property damage. CPSC has received a report of two unconfirmed minor injuries.
sold_at: Toy and discount stores sold these cotton candy machines nationwide from September 2001 through April 2002 for about $27.

product_name: Safety 1st and Beatrix Potter "Designer 22" infant car seats/carriers
heading: CPSC, NHTSA, and Dorel Juvenile Group Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Infant Car Seats/Carriers
hazard_text: When the seat is used as a carrier, the plastic handle can unexpectedly release from the carrying position. When this happens, an unrestrained infant can fall to the ground and suffer injuries.
action: Consumers can continue to use the "Designer 22" as a car seat but should stop using it as a carrier immediately and contact Dorel Juvenile Group to receive a repair kit.
incidents_text: Dorel Juvenile Group has received four reports of the handle releasing. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and department stores nationwide sold the "Designer 22" infant car seats/carriers from January 2002 through April 2002 for between $40 and $70. None of the car seats/carriers was sold in Canada.

heading: CPSC, Baseline Design Announce Recall of Bean Bag Chairs
hazard_text: The bean bags contain small polystyrene beads that present suffocation and strangulation hazards to young children who may inhale the small beads. The recalled bean bag chairs have zippers that were not properly sealed to prevent young children from opening the bean bag chairs and being exposed to the small beads.
action: Consumers should inspect their bean bag chairs. If the zippers can be opened freely, Baseline Design will provide owners with a free replacement bean bag chair with zippers that do not open.
incidents_text: Baseline Design is aware of three incidents in which the zippers opened freely. Two of the incidents involved young children who were able to open the bean bag chair zippers, and gain excess to the small polystyrene beads. One child received medical attention at a hospital after inhaling the small beads.
sold_at: Walmart stores sold the bean bag chairs nationwide from September 1999 through December 1999 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, Prestige Toy Corp. Announce Recall of Duckie Ring Rattle/Teethers
hazard_text: The rattle may break, causing small beads to fall out, which presents a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the rattles away from children and return them to the company to receive a replacement toy or refund. Consumer should send the rattle to Prestige Toy Corp., 131 West 33rd Street. Room 606, New York, N.Y. Prestige will reimburse consumers for the cost of postage.
incidents_text: CPSC and Prestige have not received any reports of incidents.
sold_at: Retailers nationwide, including the Fred Meyer Co., The Carters Outlet Stores, Proffits and E.A.T. Gifts, sold the rattles from March 2002 through April 2002 for about $7.

heading: CPSC, Vermont Precision Woodworks Announce Recall of Cribs
hazard_text: The slats on the cribs can loosen and detach from the drop side rail, creating a large opening between the slats where a child's head or neck could become entrapped, resulting in serious injury or death.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these recalled cribs until the repair has been performed. Vermont Precision Woodworks is providing consumers with replacement drop side rails.
incidents_text: Vermont Precision Woodworks has received 21 reports of slats detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile product and furniture stores sold the cribs nationwide from January 2000 through March 2002 for between $500 and $800.

heading: CPSC, InSTEP LLC Announce Recall of Trailer Bikes
hazard_text: The bike's universal joint system can fail, causing a rider to lose control of the bike. This poses a risk of injury to either of the two riders.
action: Consumers should stop using these trailer bikes immediately and contact InSTEP at (800) 242-6110 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday, or by e-mail at info@instep.net, for a free repair kit with instructions.
incidents_text: CPSC and InSTEP have received 10 reports of universal joint systems failing, including three reports of consumers who suffered contusions and abrasions.
sold_at: Retail stores nationwide, including Toys "R" Us, The Sports Authority and One Step Ahead, sold the bikes from February 2001 through May 2001 for between $80 and $110.

product_name: Mongoose and Roadmaster mountain bicycles with Ballistic 105 front suspension forks
heading: CPSC, Brunswick Corp. Announce Another Expanded Recall of Mongoose and Roadmaster Mountain Bicycles
hazard_text: The forks on these bicycles can break apart, causing riders to lose control, fall and suffer serious injury.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these bicycles and call the firm to obtain information on receiving a $65 refund for the bicycle fork. This applies to all owners of bicycles with Ballistic model 105 forks manufactured by Brunswick (except the Mongoose A40), even if they received a new Ballistic model 105 fork as a result of a participating in a previous recall.
incidents_text: There have been 34 reports of forks on these bicycles breaking resulting in 31 riders, including children and teenagers, suffering serious head and bodily injuries, abrasions, bruises and chipped teeth.
sold_at: Discount department stores and toy stores nationwide sold the bicycles with these forks from June 1998 through December 2000 for between $125 and $150. Additionally, consumers could have received a Ballistic model 105 fork as a replacement when participating in one of the previous recalls.

product_name: GL-X200TM Estes AirTM Powered Rocket Systems
heading: CPSC, Estes Industries Announce Recall of Air Powered Rockets
hazard_text: The rocket systems also have weak pump handles that can break during use, posing a risk of hand lacerations to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using the air rockets immediately and call Estes Industries toll free at (800) 576-5811 from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. MT for information on how to get a replacement rocket.
incidents_text: Estes and CPSC have received 16 reports of rocket tips breaking off. Six children were struck in the face by the rockets, including two children who suffered detached retinas and four children who suffered lacerations that required stitches or sutures. There were 68 reports of broken pump handles, including six hand lacerations.
sold_at: Department stores nationwide, including Wal-Mart, Toys R Us and Zany Brainy, as well as e-businesses, catalogers and hobby shops sold these rockets from February 2001 through February 2002 for between $20 and $40.

product_name: Harry Potter Magic Potion Bottle key chains
heading: CPSC, Hallmark Announce Recall of Harry Potter Key Chains
hazard_text: The key chains can leak petroleum distillates, which can pose an ingestion hazard to children.
action: Consumers should take the key chains away from children immediately and contact Hallmark at (800) 425-5627 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Hallmark have not received any reports of incidents.
sold_at: Hallmark, Hallmark Card, Wal-Mart, grocery, drug, and gift stores nationwide sold the key chains from October 2001 through November 2001 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announces Recall for In-Home Repair of Infant Swings
hazard_text: It is possible to misassemble the seats of these swings so that they appear secure, but are not. If the seat of the swing is not properly attached, the seat and baby can flip forward.
action: Consumers should stop using swings immediately and call Fisher-Price for help in inspecting the seat to make sure the seat is properly attached. If the seat is not properly attached, a free replacement seat and revised instructions will be provided.
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has received seven reports of the seats of the swings flipping forward, including four reports of babies hitting their heads on the floor. Though bumps and red marks were reported, there have been no serious injuries.
sold_at: Discount department and juvenile product stores nationwide sold these swings from December 2001 through March 2002 for about $70.

product_name: Up, Down & Around toddler maze toys
heading: CPSC, Discovery Toys Announce Recall of Children's Toy
hazard_text: The plastic tubes can break from the wooden base, releasing beads, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the toy immediately and contact Discovery Toys to receive a free replacement. Purchasers were sent direct mail notification of this recall.
incidents_text: Discovery Toys has received nine reports of the tubes breaking. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Discovery Toys' Educational Consultants sold the recalled toy nationwide from July 2001 to January 2002.

product_name: Greendog® girl's capri pant and shirt sets
heading: CPSC and Federated Merchandising Group Announce Recall of Girl's Capri Pant and Shirt Set
hazard_text: The buttons in the center of the embroidered flowers on the shirt can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these sets immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or store credit.
incidents_text: No injuries or incidents have been reported.
sold_at: Macy's, Burdines, The Bon Marche, Rich's, Lazarus and Goldsmith's sold the capri sets nationwide between January 2002 and February 2002 for about $26.

product_name: Time Out folding mini beach chairs
heading: CPSC, Intercon Merchandising Source Announce Recall of Mini Beach Chairs Given with "Time Out" Cosmetics at Sears
hazard_text: The chairs can collapse, posing crush and amputation hazards to consumer's fingers and toes.
action: Consumer should stop using these mini beach chairs immediately and contact Intercon for a free repair.
incidents_text: CPSC and Intercon are aware of one incident in which the tip of a 3-year-old girl's finger was amputated when the chair collapsed.
sold_at: Sears stores nationwide distributed the mini beach chairs with the purchase of $20 worth Time Out cosmetics from June 2000 through August 2000.

heading: CPSC and Tristar Products Inc. Announce Recall of Steam Cleaner
hazard_text: The internal hose connected to the trigger in the handle can detach, allowing hot water and/or steam to escape, posing a burn hazard to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using the Steam Buggy Deluxe immediately and contact Tristar customer service at (888) 339-4203 for information on how to ship the recalled product and get a replacement or refund. Tristar will pay for all shipping charges to return the product. Consumers were sent direct mail notification of this recall.
incidents_text: CPSC and Tristar Products have received reports of 305 incidents, 214 of which involved consumers receiving burns to hands, arms, feet, and body.
sold_at: HSN LP (Home Shopping Network) sold the Steam Buggy Deluxe nationwide from December 2001 through January 2002 for about $129.

heading: CPSC, Tough Traveler Ltd. Announce Recall of Child Backpack Carriers
hazard_text: A child could fall from a carrier when the seat restraint strap is not doubled-back through the slider if the carrier's safety harness is not used. The seat restraint strap is located between the child's legs when the child is seated.
action: Consumers should stop using these carriers immediately and contact Tough Traveler to receive instructions on doubling back the strap through the slider.
incidents_text: Tough Traveler has received one report of a strap slipping through the slider and the carrier's safety harness not being used. The child did not fall from the carrier. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: These carriers were sold through specialty baby products and outdoor products retail stores, and through the Tough Traveler website and mail order 800 number from December 2000 through February 2002 for between $157 and $186.

heading: CPSC, Lifetime Products Inc. and Escalade Sports Announce Recall to Repair Portable Basketball Hoops
hazard_text: The basketball hoops may have a sharp protruding bolt on the players' side of the pole that can cause serious leg or body lacerations to consumers when the bolt is exposed.
action: Consumers should stop using the basketball hoops immediately and contact Lifetime Products or Escalade Sports to receive free cap nuts to cover the bolts. Consumers should call and get a cap nut regardless of whether their bolt protrudes or not.
units: About 1.7 million Lifetime portable hoops, and about 16,000 Escalade portable hoops
incidents_text: CPSC and Lifetime Products Inc. have received 27 reports of injuries and Escalade Sports has received one report of injury from the basketball hoop bolt. Injuries include scrapes, deep lacerations and bruises. Several consumers required stitches for their injuries. Players have been cut when they bump into the pole as they drive toward the basket.
sold_at: Sporting good, department and toy stores including Wal-Mart, Kmart, Target and Toys R Us nationwide sold the Lifetime basketball hoops between January 1994 and July 2000 and the Escalade Sports basketball hoops between March 1994 and December 2001 for between $80 and $500.

heading: CPSC, Childcraft Education Corp. Announce Recall of Changing Table with Steps
hazard_text: When one of the front doors is open, a child's finger can become stuck inside spaces between parts of the hinges, causing finger crushing or pinching to occur while the door is closing.
action: Consumers should stop using these changing tables immediately and contact Childcraft Education Corp. to receive a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Childcraft Education Corp. has received two reports of children having had their fingers caught inside the hinges. One child required stitches and the other needed surgery.
sold_at: Childcraft Education Corp. sold the recalled changing tables with steps to daycare centers and pre-schools from January 1998 to May 2001 for about $700.

heading: CPSC, Rose Art Announce Recall of Children's Soap Making Kit
hazard_text: The soap may get too hot when heated in the microwave oven and leak from the plastic container posing a burn hazard to children.
action: Consumers should stop using these kits immediately and contact Rose Art or visit the firm's web site at www.roseart.com for information on how to receive a full refund and an additional Rose Art product item at no charge.
incidents_text: CPSC and Rose Art have received 10 reports of children being burned by the hot soap while removing the plastic container from the microwave oven.
sold_at: Toy and discount stores, including Toys R Us, Wal Mart, Kaybee Toys, Target and Value City, sold these kits nationwide between August 1997 through December 2001 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Leiner Health Products Announce Recall of Dietary Supplements Containing Iron
hazard_text: The supplements being recalled are not packaged in child-resistant packaging as required under the Poison Prevention Packaging Act. If ingested by children, these iron-containing supplements can cause serious injury or death.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the bottles from the reach of young children and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Leiner have not received any reports of injuries involving these products. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Albertson's, Jewel, Osco, Sav-on and Acme sold these recalled supplement bottles nationwide from July 2001 through February 2002 for between $8 and $9.

heading: CPSC, Graco Announce Replacement Instructions for Activity Tray
hazard_text: The Snack and Activity Trays are sold with detached suction cups that the consumer installs. If the suction cups are not properly attached, they can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these products immediately. To receive a new instruction sheet, consumers should contact Graco.
incidents_text: Graco has not received any reports of injury from the suction cups detaching. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Discount, department and juvenile product stores, including Sears, nationwide sold these activity trays from August 2001 through February 2002 for about $15.

heading: CPSC, Unilever Home and Personal Care USA Announce Recall of Plush Snuggle® Bears
hazard_text: The eyes and noses of these bears can come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these bears away from young children immediately and contact Unilever Home and Personal Care USA for information on how to receive a coupon for free Snuggle fabric softener.
incidents_text: Unilever Home and Personal Care USA has received 32 reports of the eyes and noses coming off of these bears. In three of these reports, children placed detached eyes from these bears in their mouths. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: Grocery and discount department stores nationwide sold the Snuggle fabric softener that included the 5-inch and 8-inch bears between May 1999 and July 2001. The Pajama and Nightcap 5-inch bears also were given away to consumers who sent in two proofs of purchase for Snuggle fabric softener between November 2001 and December 2001. The 10-inch bears were distributed from May 1997 through May 1998 to consumers who sent in a proof of purchase for Snuggle fabric softener and up to $4.

heading: CPSC, Alpha International Announce Recall of Pedal Cars
hazard_text: The paint coating on some of these pedal cars contains high lead levels. CPSC standards ban toys and other children's products containing high levels of lead. Young children could ingest the lead from the car's paint coating, presenting a lead poisoning hazard.
incidents_text: Alpha International has not received any reports of injuries involving these pedal cars. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: The two "Raley's" cars were sold exclusively at Raley's supermarkets from July 2000 through December 2000. Department, toy, and specialty/collectible stores sold all of the other pedal cars from November 1999 through January 2002 for between $100 and $500.

product_name: Monsters In The Closet Children's Board Book
heading: CPSC and Random House Announce Recall of Children's Book
hazard_text: The snap that secures the book could detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should cut off the snap from these books immediately and mail the snap to: Tri-State, c/o Marie Corsello, 325 Rabro Drive, Hauppauge, NY 11788 to receive a free replacement book valued at about $9.
incidents_text: CPSC and Random House have not received any reports of injuries involving this book. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Book, specialty stores and online retailers sold these books nationwide from October 2001 through January 2002 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Disney Children's Book Group, LLC Announce Recall of Children's Book
hazard_text: The books have a plastic abacus-like toy attached to the back cover that contains five plastic beads. The beads can separate from the book cover, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these recalled books away from young children and return the books to Disney Press for a full refund and postage. Mail the books to Disney Press, Attn: Zowie 123, 114 Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10011 and use six first-class stamps per book. Be sure to include a return address and phone number.
incidents_text: Disney-Press has received one report of a 15-month-old boy who broke a bead from the book cover and placed it in his mouth. An adult was able to remove the bead from the child's mouth without injury.
sold_at: Bookstores nationwide sold the recalled books from January 2002 through February 2002 for about $7.

heading: CPSC, OshKosh B'Gosh Announce Recall of Newborn Girls' Garments
hazard_text: The fabric, heat-sealed flowers on the front of the garments can detach after washing, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these garments immediately and return them to OshKosh B'Gosh for a refund.
incidents_text: OshKosh B'Gosh has received one report of a 6-month-old child who began to choke on one of the detached flowers that had separated from the garment. It was removed from the child's throat without injury.
sold_at: OshKosh B'Gosh and department stores nationwide sold these garments from August 2001 through December 2001 for about $38.

heading: CPSC and Value City, Schottenstein Stores Announce Recall of Gel Candle Kits
hazard_text: When burned, the gel candle can melt the plastic candleholders included with the kit, posing a fire hazard to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using these candles immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC has received two reports of consumers claiming the plastic candleholder melted and started a fire. One report involved substantial damage to the consumer's home, and a consumer reportedly suffered burns to his hands and feet. The other report involved minor damage to furniture.
sold_at: Value City and Schottenstein discount stores nationwide sold these gel candle kits from July 2001 through December 2001 for about $4.

heading: CPSC, Reed & Barton Announce Recall of Infant Teething Rings
hazard_text: The area where the teething ring is soldered together contains flux, which can irritate the skin or mouths of young children.
action: Consumers should take these teething rings away from children immediately and return the rings to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Reed & Barton have not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of health problems related to the handling and ingestion of the flux.
sold_at: Department stores, jewelry stores and gift shops sold these teething rings from March 13, 2001 through October 25, 2001 for about $100.

heading: CPSC, L.A. Baby Announce Recall of Folding Little Wood Cribs
hazard_text: The headboard can separate from the corner post. A child's head or neck could be entrapped in the corner space between the post and the mattress.
action: Consumers should stop using these cribs immediately and contact L.A. Baby to receive a free brace repair kit to prevent an entrapment.
incidents_text: L.A. Baby has received 9 reports of headboard separations. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: L.A. Baby sold the recalled cribs to hotels, daycare centers, and small specialty stores from March 2001 to October 2001 for about $170.

heading: CPSC, LaJobi Industries Announce Recall of Cribs
hazard_text: These cribs have cut-outs in the end panels that allow young children to get their heads entrapped, resulting in strangulation. The cribs fail to meet CPSC's standards.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: LaJobi has not received any reports of injuries involving these cribs but in the past there have been deaths reported in other firms' cribs with end panel cut-outs.

heading: CPSC, Sandberg Manufacturer Co. Announce Recall of Children's Dressers
hazard_text: The dresser can tip over during use, posing a serious injury hazard to consumers.
action: Consumers who have the dressers should immediately stop children from using them. Consumers should contact Sandberg Manufacturer Co. to receive simple instructions for conducting an in-home repair.
incidents_text: Sandberg and CPSC have received one report of a dresser tipping over, though no one suffered injuries.
sold_at: Independent home furnishing stores nationwide sold these dressers from July 1999 through November 2001 for about $230.

heading: CPSC, Kids II Inc. Announce Recall of Pop Links Toys
hazard_text: The tips on the links that snap together like a chain can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the Pop Links toys away from young children and return them to Kids II for a replacement toy.
incidents_text: Kids II has received 11 reports of tips on the links breaking. No injuries have been reported.

heading: CPSC, Baby Buzz'r International Announce Recall of Toy Baby Buzz'r
hazard_text: The red, green and blue button covers on the toy can come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the recalled Baby Buzz'r toys away from young children and contact Baby Buzz'r International to participate in the recall.
incidents_text: Baby Buzz'r has received five reports of button covers coming off. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile specialty stores nationwide, catalogs and internet sites sold the Baby Buzz'r toys from June 2001 through September 2001 for about $13.

product_name: Baby Cool and Kid Cool girls' jackets and vests
heading: CPSC, Kid Cool LLC Announce Recall of Girl's Infant/Toddler Garments Sold Exclusively at Sears
hazard_text: The zipper pull and metal ring on these garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the zipper pull and the metal ring from these garments and dispose of them. Consumers can return the garments to any Sears retail store to receive a replacement garment.
incidents_text: Kid Cool LLC has received one report of a child who removed the zipper pull, placed it in her mouth and began to choke on the metal ring that attaches the zipper pull to the jacket.
sold_at: Sears department stores nationwide exclusively sold these garments from September 2001 through October 2001 for between $16 and $19.

product_name: Lawn-Boy SilverPro and GoldPro Series power mowers
heading: CPSC, Lawn-Boy Inc. Announce Recall of Power Mowers
hazard_text: Stress cracks can develop in the mower's fuel tank, allowing gasoline to leak and posing a risk of fire and burn injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using these recalled mowers immediately and contact Lawn-Boy to arrange for a free replacement fuel tank to be installed.
incidents_text: Lawn-Boy received nearly 400 reports of fuel tanks on these mowers leaking, and one report of a fire. No injuries or property damage were reported.
sold_at: Lawn-Boy dealers, and department and home center stores sold these mowers from December 2000 through November 2001 for between $300 and $600.

heading: CPSC and BRIO® Corp. Announce Recall of Curious George Toys
hazard_text: The toys include fabric-filled mobile phones that can pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from children immediately and call BRIO to get a refund or replacement toy.
incidents_text: CPSC and BRIO Corp. have not received any reports of injuries or incidents.
sold_at: Specialty toy stores, Internet retailers, and mail order catalogs sold the recalled Curious George toys nationwide from July 2001 through November 2001 for about $25.

product_name: Lobster toy (attached to Ocean Friends Stationary Entertainer)
heading: CPSC, Little Tikes Co. Announce Recall of Lobster Toy Attached to Stationary Entertainer
hazard_text: The antennae on the lobster toy can break, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should remove the lobster toy from the entertainer immediately and contact Little Tikes for a replacement toy.
incidents_text: No injuries or incidents have been reported.
sold_at: Toys R Us stores sold the stationary entertainer with the lobster toy nationwide between October 2001 through November 2001 for about $60.

heading: CPSC, Aqua-Leisure Industries Inc. Announce Recall of Inflatable Baby Floats
hazard_text: The leg holes in the seat of the float can tear, causing children to unexpectedly fall into the water and possibly drown.
action: Consumers should stop using these recalled floats immediately and contact Aqua-Leisure for a free replacement.
incidents_text: Aqua-Leisure and CPSC have received 12 reports of the floats' seats tearing and causing children to fall into the water. There were four incidents of children becoming completely submerged before a caregiver was able to reach them. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile products, specialty and discount department stores nationwide, including Target, K-Mart, Bed Bath and Beyond and Baby Central, sold the baby floats from August 2000 through September 2001 for between $10 and $13.

heading: CPSC, Stride Rite Children's Group Inc. Announce Recall of Girl's Shoes
hazard_text: The buckle on these shoes can break, posing a choking hazard for young children.
action: Consumers should take the shoes away from their children immediately and return the shoes to the store where purchased for a refund or replacement shoes.
incidents_text: Stride Rite Children's Group has received four reports of the buckle breaking, and one report of a child putting a broken piece of the buckle in her mouth and starting to choke.
sold_at: Shoe, department and Stride Rite Outlet stores nationwide sold these shoes from January 2001 through September 2001 for about $25.

heading: CPSC, Manley Toy Direct Announce the Recall of Zapper Toys
hazard_text: The balloon tongues and the cylinders holding the tongues on these toys can detach, posing a choking and aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toys away from young children and return the toy to the place of purchase for a refund, or throw them away.
incidents_text: That company received a report of a 3-year-old boy who inhaled a balloon tongue that detached from a Zapper toy into his sinus cavity. He required medical treatment to remove the part from his nose.
sold_at: Arcades, amusement parks and carnivals sold and distributed these toys from January 2000 through August 2001. They were sold for about $1.

heading: CPSC, KB Gear Announce Recall of Computer Mouse Sets
hazard_text: The mouse ball can separate from the mouse and pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: The Cozy Coupe Computer Mouse was distributed by KB Gear under license from Little Tikes Co., of Hudson, Ohio. KB Gear liquidated and as of Nov. 1, 2001, is no longer in business. As a result, the company is unable to provide consumers with a remedy. To encourage consumers to destroy the computer mouse and as a gesture of goodwill, Little Tikes is offering an equivalent $10 Little Tikes toy to consumers who return the retaining ring from the bottom of the mouse.
incidents_text: CPSC received a report of a 2-year-old girl who placed the mouse ball in her mouth. Her parents were able to take the ball away from the girl before she was injured.
sold_at: Internet retailers, toy, electronics and discount stores nationwide sold these computer mouse sets from September 1999 to August 2001 for between $5 and $20.

heading: CPSC, HandsOnToys, Inc. Announce Recall to Replace Rattles
hazard_text: The rattle can break and expose the noisemaker inside the rattle handle, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toy rattles away from children and contact HandsOnToys at (888) 442-6376 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive a replacement toy.
incidents_text: CPSC and HandsOnToys have received 11 reports of the rattles breaking. A 9-month old girl was found with the plastic noisemaker lodged in her throat. Her mother removed it by performing the Heimlich maneuver.

heading: CPSC, JA-RU Inc. Announce Recall of "Blast Balls" Toys
hazard_text: When struck together, the toys create a cracking sound similar to that of a cap gun. The directions instruct consumers to strike one ball against the other in the palm of hand to create the cracking sound. When consumers strike the "Blast Balls" together, sparks can ignite, posing a burn hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the "Blast Balls" and contact JA-RU for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and JA-RU have received six reports of injuries, including minor burns to hands and fingers.
sold_at: Convenience and novelty stores nationwide sold these toys from June 2001 through October 2001 for about $2.

heading: CPSC, Candlewick Press Announce Recall of Children's Board Books
hazard_text: The plastic lamination on the board book may peel off, posing a choking hazard for young children.
action: Consumers should take the recalled "Bunny My Honey" board books away from young children immediately and discard them. Consumers can visit the firm's web site at www.candlewick.com to receive a free replacement book or contact Candlewick Press at (800) 883-0009 (or in the 617 and 781 area codes at (617) 661-3330) between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.
incidents_text: CPSC and Candlewick Press have not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these board books.
sold_at: Bookstores, children's specialty stores and gift shops nationwide sold these books from December 2000 through September 2001 for about $7.

heading: CPSC, Lillian Vernon Corporation Announce Recall of Costumes
hazard_text: Fabric used in these costumes can ignite readily and presents a serious risk of burn injuries in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
action: Consumers should stop wearing these costumes immediately and call Lillian Vernon Corporation's customer service department at 1-800-505-2250, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for information on how to receive a refund.
incidents_text: No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Lillian Vernon sold these costumes in their catalogs nationwide between August 1999 through October 2000 for about $40.

heading: CPSC, Sassy Inc. Announce Recall to Replace Rattles
hazard_text: The sewn-on, spherical shaped fabric eyes on the rattles can detach, posing a choking hazard to small children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toys away from young children and return them to Sassy to receive a free replacement toy. Consumers should call Sassy at (800) 323-6336 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday for information on how to receive the replacement toy.
incidents_text: Sassy has received 129 reports of eyes detaching from the rattles, including some incidents in which eyes were found in children's mouths. One of these children started to choke on a detached eye and a parent used the Heimlich maneuver to remove the eye.
sold_at: Toy and mass merchandise stores nationwide sold these rattles from August 1999 through mid-October 2001 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Discovery Toys Announce Recall of Children's Toy Phones
hazard_text: The blue, hard plastic antenna ball can break off of the toy phone, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the toy phone immediately and call Discovery Toys at 800-341-TOYS (1-800-341-8697) Monday through Friday 7:00 AM - 3:30 PM (PT) for a free repair kit. Consumers also can request a free repair kit by sending an email to productsupport@discoverytoys.net.
incidents_text: Discovery Toys received eight reports of the antenna ball breaking off of the toy phones. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The toy phones were sold nationwide through Discovery Toys sales network. They were sold in the U.S. and Canada from May 1999 through November 2000 for about $10 and have since been discontinued.

heading: CPSC, Palliser Furniture Ltd. Announce Recall of Toy Boxes
hazard_text: The toy box's lid can fall suddenly, posing entrapment and strangulation hazards to young children. In addition, spaces at the end of the hinge on the lid can cause pinched, crushed and lacerated fingers.
action: Consumers should stop children from using these toy boxes immediately, and contact Palliser for a free replacement toy box or a $50 refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Palliser Furniture Ltd. have not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these toy boxes.
sold_at: Furniture stores nationwide and in Canada sold these toy boxes from July 1999 through August 2001 for about $150 (about $200 CAD).

heading: CPSC, Wysco Inc. Announce Recall of "Runt"™ Mini-Bicycles
hazard_text: These bicycles do not have any brakes, which are required by the CPSC standard for bicycles of this type. The CPSC standard also requires these bicycles to have chain guards to prevent riders from getting fingers, toes and clothing caught in the gears.
action: Consumers should stop using these Runt bicycles immediately and get a free repair kit. To order a free repair kit and for more information, call Wysco toll-free at (866) 868-7868 between 7:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. PT Monday through Friday.
incidents_text: Wysco has not received any reports of incidents or injuries involving these mini-bicycles.
sold_at: Bicycle, toy, discount department, convenience, and specialty stores nationwide, and mail order catalogs and websites sold these mini-bicycles from January 2001 through July 2001 for about $100.

heading: CPSC, Little Tikes Announce Recall of Swings
hazard_text: The buckles on the swing can break and the shoulder restraint straps can pull out of the back of the seat, causing young children to fall.
action: Consumers should stop using the swings immediately and contact Little Tikes at www.littletikes.com or call (800) 321-0183 anytime to receive a repair kit.
incidents_text: CPSC and Little Tikes have received 14 reports of problems with the swings. Five injuries to children included abrasions, bruises, cuts and bumps to the head.
sold_at: Juvenile product and toy stores nationwide sold the swings from December 2000 through September 2001 for about $20.

product_name: Home Décor SwingTM wooden baby gates
heading: CPSC, Evenflo Announce Recall to Repair Home Décor Swing™ Wooden Baby Gates
hazard_text: The plastic mounting hardware that attaches to the wall can crack or break, allowing the wooden gate to unlatch. Children can then gain access to restricted areas, such as stairs. Also, the plastic hardware attached to the side of the gate can break, creating small parts that pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these gates immediately, and call Evenflo at (800) 576-0507 anytime to receive free replacement hardware.
incidents_text: Evenflo and CPSC have received nine reports of children falling down the stairs after the mounting hardware broke or cracked. Three of these children suffered bumps and bruises to their heads or arms. One child received two loosened teeth after she fell down the stairs. Also, one child placed broken hardware pieces in her mouth, but was not injured.
sold_at: Catalogs, department and juvenile specialty stores nationwide sold these baby gates from June 1999 through September 2001 for about $100.

heading: CPSC, Safety 1st Announce Recall of Fold-Up Booster Seats
hazard_text: The top half of the seat inserts can separate, and a child can fall from the chair and be injured.
action: Consumers should stop using these seats immediately and contact Safety 1st to receive a free repair kit with instructions.
incidents_text: CPSC and Safety 1st have received 32 reports where the seat halves separated. There were seven reports of injuries from falls including bumps, cuts, bruises and a fractured arm.
sold_at: Major toy, hardware and department stores nationwide sold these seats from January 1994 through August 1999 for about $18.

product_name: Cosco "Zip n Go," "Okie Dokie," and "Carters" playpens
heading: CPSC, Dorel Juvenile Group Announce Recall of Cosco Playpens
hazard_text: The plastic tabs on the playpen that lock the rails into the corners can break or loosen over time, allowing the rails to turn inward, collapse and entrap an infant.
action: Consumers should stop using these playpens immediately and call Dorel Juvenile Group to receive a refund or replacement product. Consumers can contact Dorel at (800) 314-9327 between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.
incidents_text: In June 2001, an 11-month-old baby in Elyria, Ohio, died when his chest was caught in the V-shape created by the collapsed sides of his playpen. Dorel Juvenile Group has received 421 reports of rails not locking or collapsing.
sold_at: Department, Toy and juvenile specialty stores nationwide sold the "Zip n Go" and "Carters" playpens. JC Penney stores nationwide sold the "Okie Dokie" brand playpens exclusively. The playpens were sold from May 1995 through December 1999 for between $40 and $70.

product_name: Rain-X® Super Glass Cleaner Concentrate, Rain-X® Plus Washer Fluid Concentrate, and Rain-X® Washer Fluid Additive
heading: CPSC, Blue Coral Announce Recall of Rain-X® Glass Cleaner and Washer Fluid
hazard_text: The products, which contain methyl alcohol, are not sealed with child-resistant closures as required by federal law. Methyl alcohol, also known as methanol, is toxic and can cause blindness or death if ingested.
action: Consumers should keep these recalled products out of the reach of young children. Consumers should call Blue Coral toll-free at (800) 416-1600 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday for information on receiving replacement child-resistant caps and a coupon toward a Rain-X® product.
incidents_text: Blue Coral has received three reports of ingestion, including two children whose parents called the Blue Coral helpline and were directed to immediate medical treatment.
sold_at: Hardware, automotive and department stores nationwide sold the recalled Rain-X® products from September 1998 through August 2001 for between $1 and $5.

product_name: Drain Opener Clog Remover and Hair Clog Remover sold in 64. oz bottles
heading: CPSC, National Service Industries Inc. Announce Recall of Drain Cleaners
hazard_text: The bottles can leak, allowing the contents of the cleaner to come into contact with consumers. These cleaners can cause irritation and burns to the skin and eyes.
action: Consumers should stop using the cleaners immediately and contact the appropriate company to receive a free replacement cap.
incidents_text: NSI has received 16 reports of the bottles leaking, including three incidents involving skin irritations to the leg and hand, and 13 incidents involving property damage.
sold_at: Home Depot, Wal-Mart, Kmart and hardware stores nationwide sold these cleaners from January 2001 through August 2001 for between $3 and $6.

product_name: Tilt latches on Andersen 200 Series Tilt-Wash Double-Hung Windows
heading: CPSC, Andersen Corporation Announce Recall of Window Latches
hazard_text: The latches on the lower sash of the window can unexpectedly open, posing a potential injury hazard to consumers who can be struck by the window or by shattered glass.
action: Consumers should immediately ensure that the latches are in the closed position. Consumers should call the Andersen WindowCare® Solution Center toll-free at (888) 888-7020 between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. CT Monday to Friday or 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. CT on Saturday, to schedule a free in-home repair with an Andersen service technician.
incidents_text: Andersen has received 11 reports of the latches unexpectedly opening. There have been no reports of injuries.
sold_at: The majority of windows were installed by home builders in the construction of new homes. Independent dealers and home centers nationwide also sold these windows to contractors between May 2000 through August 2001.

heading: CPSC, SBH Restructuring Corp. (formally Storybook Heirlooms) Recall Children's Pajamas
hazard_text: These pajamas fail to meet the Federal Standards for the Flammability of Children's Sleepwear and as a result these pajamas pose a risk of injury to children due to the possible ignition of the garment.
action: Consumers should immediately stop their children from wearing these pajamas and return them to SBH Restructuring Corporation, 348 Poplar Street, Hanover, PA 17331, Attention: Storybook Recall, for a refund of the purchase price and original shipping costs.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Storybook Heirlooms catalog and www.StorybookHeirlooms.com sold these garments from December 1999 through March 2001 for between $8 and $34.

heading: CPSC, Racing Champions Ertl, Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Toy Toolboxes
hazard_text: The toy's carrying handle can break, creating small parts and a sharp plastic edge that pose a choking and laceration hazard to young children.
action: Parents and caregivers should take the toy away from young children immediately and contact RCE at (866) 898-4999 anytime for instructions on returning these toys and receiving a free replacement toolbox.
incidents_text: CPSC and RCE have not received any reports of injuries.
sold_at: John Deere dealers and other farm supply retail stores nationwide sold the toys from June 2001 through September 2001 for about $13.

heading: CPSC, Kids II Announce Recall of Butterfly Baby Toys
hazard_text: The antennae on these butterfly toys contain wire that can pass through the fabric, causing cuts and scratches to babies.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from babies immediately, and return the toy to the store where purchased or contact Kids II for a free replacement butterfly toy.
incidents_text: Kids II has received 27 reports of wires passing through the fabric on the antennae of these toys, resulting in four babies getting cuts to the hand or face, and five babies receiving scratches.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and juvenile specialty stores nationwide sold these butterfly toys from February 2001 through August 2001 for between $15 and $20.

heading: CPSC, Maya Wrap Announce Recall of Infant Carriers/Slings
hazard_text: The welds of the metal rings that support the carriers/slings can break, posing a fall hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these carriers/slings immediately and call Maya Wrap at (888) 629-2972 anytime, or go to the firm's web site at www.mayawrap.com for instructions on how to have the carriers/slings repaired.
incidents_text: Maya Wrap has received 20 reports of the rings breaking. The company received a report that one child fell to the ground but no injuries were reported.
sold_at: Web sites and individual distributors nationwide sold these carrier/slings from January 2001 through July 2001 for between $30 and $40. Also, eight children's boutiques in various states sold these carriers/slings.

product_name: Children's toys: "2 PC Tambourine Set", "Bathtime Water Wheel", "Funny Loco Wind-Up", and "Pull Back Duck in Boat"
heading: CPSC, STK International Announce Recall of Children's Toys
hazard_text: The toys can break causing small balls to be released, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toys away from children immediately, and return them to STK International for a full refund.
incidents_text: STK International and CPSC have not received any reports of incidents.
sold_at: Dollar stores nationwide sold these toys from September 1999 through May 2001 for about $1.

product_name: Little Tree natural wood dollhouse bathroom furniture sets
heading: CPSC, XL Machine Ltd. Announce Recall of Dollhouse Furniture Sets Sold at Target Stores
hazard_text: The yellow paint on the furniture contains lead, which can present a risk of lead poisoning to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these dollhouse furniture sets away from children, and return the sets to the Target store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and XL Machine Ltd. have not received reports of any injuries relating to these dollhouse furniture sets.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide sold these furniture sets from August 2000 through June 2001 for about $15.

heading: CPSC, Recreational Equipment Inc. (REI) Announce Recall of Children's Baseball Caps
hazard_text: The adjustment cords, located on the rear of the hats, use a snap-on plastic pull. The snap-on plastic pull could separate from the cord, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled children's baseball caps immediately and return it to the nearest REI retailer to receive a refund.
incidents_text: REI Product Quality Assurance (PQA) received one report of a parent finding the snap-on plastic pull in the mouth of her two-year old son. No injuries have been reported.

heading: CPSC, Kids "R" Us and Babies "R" Us Announce Recall of Children's Cargo Pants
hazard_text: The toggle on the pockets of the pants can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately remove and discard the two toggles on the leg pockets. The pants then can be worn without the toggle.
incidents_text: Kids "R" Us has received one report of a 9-month old boy who began to choke on a toggle that he removed from the pants. The toggle was dislodged.
sold_at: Kids "R" Us and Babies "R" Us stores nationwide and some Toys "R" Us stores sold these pants from June 2001 through July 2001 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Kolcraft Announce Recall of LiteSport Strollers
hazard_text: Lock mechanisms, found on both sides of the stroller, can break and cause the stroller to suddenly collapse. When the strollers collapse, babies can fall and suffer injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using the strollers immediately and call Kolcraft to receive a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Kolcraft has received 124 reports of the lock mechanisms breaking, including 31 reports of the stroller collapsing. There were 22 reports of injuries, including abrasions, cuts and bruises to children's faces, arms, hands and legs.
