sold_at: Department and juvenile products stores nationwide sold these strollers from December 1997 through December 2000 for about $30.

product_name: Safety 1st Cabinet and Drawer Spring Latches
heading: CPSC, Safety 1st Announce Recall of Cabinet and Drawer Spring Latches
hazard_text: If the safety latch breaks, a small spring could be released. Young children could choke on the small spring or gain access to a cabinet or drawer where dangerous items are stored.
action: Consumers should contact Safety 1st for free replacement latches immediately.
incidents_text: CPSC and Safety 1st are aware of 27 incidents with these latches breaking. There have been two injuries reported. A 13-month-old girl placed the broken spring from one of these latches in her mouth and suffered a minor abrasion inside her mouth. Also, a 2-year-old girl was able to open a cabinet protected by a safety latch, gained access to a bathroom cabinet and sprayed tile cleaner into her mouth. She received chemical burns to her throat.
sold_at: Toy, hardware and department stores nationwide sold the set of three or four latches from January 1993 through December 1999 for about $7.

product_name: Portable bassinet sold under the names Sit & Soothe Portable Bassinet, Soothing Sounds Bassinet, and Soothing Sounds Portable Bassinet
heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Portable Bassinets
hazard_text: Children and adults can be injured when their fingers are pinched or cut between parts of the folding mechanism.
action: Consumers should stop using these portable bassinets immediately and contact Fisher-Price at (800) 285-0324 anytime to order a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has received 24 reports of fingers getting caught or pinched in the bassinet frame, including 10 children with cut fingertips, one infection and one broken finger.
sold_at: Toy, mass merchandise and discount stores nationwide sold these portable bassinets from November 1997 through March 2001 for about $50.

product_name: "Hourglass Space Sprout" and "Look for Me Bumblebee" toddler toys
heading: CPSC, Burger King and Alcone Announce Recall of Two Kids Meal Toys
hazard_text: The toys can break causing small beads or balls to be released, which poses a choking or aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Parents should immediately take the toys away from children and call Burger King's Consumer Affairs at 305-378-3535 for instructions on returning the toy for a free, replacement toy.
incidents_text: Burger King Corporation has received 18 reports of the toys breaking. There are six incidents where children had the balls or beads in their mouth, but no injuries were reported.
sold_at: Burger King® restaurants nationwide distributed the toys inside Kids Meals from January 2001 through July 2001.

heading: CPSC, Acetrike Bicycle Co. Announce Recall of Children's Bicycles
hazard_text: The frames of these bikes can break, causing the riders to fall and suffer injuries.
action: Consumers should stop riding these bicycles immediately, and call (888) 366-3828 between 8 a.m. and 7 p.m. ET Monday through Friday or go to the firm's website at www.huffybikes.com to determine if their bicycle is part of the recall. Consumers with a recalled bicycle will receive a replacement bicycle free of charge.
incidents_text: Acetrike and the distributor of the bicycles, Huffy Bicycle Co., have received four reports of the frames on these bicycles breaking. Two boys, ages 4 and 6, suffered abrasions and contusions, and a 5-year-old boy suffered a contusion. A fourth child was not injured.
sold_at: Discount department, toy, hardware and sporting goods stores, including Ace Hardware, Ames, Blain Supply, Kay Bee Toys, Meijers, Tru*Serv and Wal-Mart, sold these bikes nationwide from October 1999 through March 2001 for between $35 and $70.

heading: CPSC, Basic Comfort Inc. Announce Recall of Infant Seat Pads
hazard_text: The seat pad has two shoulder straps that create a v-shaped opening around the head and neck, presenting a strangulation hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the infant pads immediately and contact Basic Comfort at (800) 456-8687 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. MT to receive a replacement.
incidents_text: Basic Comfort received one report of an 8-month old girl who was caught by the neck in the shoulder straps of the seat pad after falling sideways off a chair. The child was removed from the seat pad without injury.
sold_at: Department and juvenile products stores nationwide including JC Penney and One Step Ahead sold these infant seat pads from October 1998 through May 2001 for about $11.

heading: CPSC, Inca Imports Announce Recall of Stuffed Bears
hazard_text: The noses, bells, and eyes of the bears can detach, presenting a choking hazard to young children. The eyes also present a sharp point hazard.
action: Consumers should take these stuffed bears away from young children immediately and return them to the store where they were purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Inca Imports have not received any reports of injuries.
sold_at: Stores in tourist areas throughout Arizona, California, Colorado, Montana, Nebraska, Oklahoma, and Texas sold the bears from July 1997 through February 2001 for between $20 to $50.

heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Hand Trucks, Baby Walkers

product_name: "CUDDLES FEEDING SET" or "CUDDLES MEAL TIME" toy feeding sets
heading: CPSC, Imperial Toy Corp. Announce Recall of Toy Feeding Sets
hazard_text: The nipple on the toy baby bottle included in these sets could come off, posing a serious choking hazard to small children.
action: Consumers should take these recalled toys away from young children immediately, and return the toy set to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Imperial Toy Corp. are not aware of any incidents or injuries involving these toys.
sold_at: Ben Franklin, Revco and other discount stores nationwide sold the toys from October 1995 through May 2001 for about $2.

product_name: "Let's StartTM Numbers" and "Optical Illusions Lab" educational kits
heading: CPSC, Advantage Publishers Group Announce Recall to Replace Educational Kits
hazard_text: The red painted numbers on the acetate stencil sheet included in the "Let's StartTM" kit contain lead; and the gold paint bearing the words "Kasy's Extrafine" on the black pen included in the "Optical Illusions" kit has lead.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the stencil sheets and pens from the activity kits and discard them. Customers should call Lilian Shia (858-450-3556) or Lynn Brennan (858-457-2500 X-2575) at Advantage Publishers Group to order a replacement piece.
incidents_text: CPSC and Advantage Publishers Group have not received any reports of incidents.
sold_at: Retail stores, national book chains, wholesalers and distributors, and membership warehouse clubs nationwide sold the educational kits from February 1999 through May 2001 for between $13 and $20.

heading: CPSC, Peg Perego USA Announce Recall of High Chairs
hazard_text: When the seat is reclined, the high chairs have a space between the armrest and backrest in which a child's head or arm can become entrapped. This can pose a risk of suffocation or injury to the heads or arms of young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the high chairs immediately. Consumers should call Peg Perego toll-free at (877) 737-3464 anytime to receive free replacement armrests that will eliminate the entrapment hazard. Consumers should not return the high chair to the store where purchased.
incidents_text: Peg Perego and CPSC have received 51 reports of entrapment when children placed their heads or arms in the space between the armrest and backrest. Two children suffered scratches to the head, one had a bruised arm, and another had a scratched arm. There have not been any reports of suffocation.
sold_at: Chain stores and independent retailers, including Babies "R" Us, Right Start, and Burlington Coat Factory, sold these high chairs from June 1996 through October 1999 for about $180.

heading: CPSC, DSI Toys, Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Kittens
hazard_text: These toys contain contaminated water that, if contacted, could cause illness to children.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: CPSC and DSI Toys had not received any reports of illness resulting from contacting contaminated water from these toys.
sold_at: Discount, specialty, and toy stores nationwide sold the kitten toys from September 2000 through May 2001 for between $10 and $13.

heading: CPSC, Raymond Geddes & Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Velcro Wallets
hazard_text: The zipper pull in the wallet contains lead, which can present a risk of lead poisoning to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these wallets away from children, and return the wallets to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Raymond Geddes & Co. Inc. have not received reports of any injuries relating to these wallets.
sold_at: Toy stores nationwide sold these wallets from August 1998 through April 2001 for about $1.

product_name: Twin plantation bed headboards, queen plantation bed headboards, plantation nightstands and antique tin mirrors
heading: CPSC, Neiman Marcus Announce Recall of Plantation Furniture, Antique Mirror
hazard_text: The furniture could be painted with lead-containing paint. Ingestion of lead from deteriorating paint is a major source of lead poisoning for children 6 years old and under.
action: Consumers should call Neiman Marcus at 800-888-4757 between 9:30 a.m. and 6 p.m. CT Monday through Thursday and 7 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. CT Friday to arrange for free pick-up and a full refund.
incidents_text: No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The furniture was sold through Neiman Marcus and Horchow catalogs from May 1998 through May 2001.

heading: CPSC, Chicco USA Inc. Announce Recall of Preschool Toys
hazard_text: Some of the larger-sized ball halves can become stuck on a young child's face, covering the nose and mouth, and causing suffocation.
action: Parents and caregivers should take these balls away from young children immediately and return the toys to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC received a report of a 2-year-old boy who had a ball-half stuck on his face, covering his nose and mouth. A nearby adult was able to pull the toy from his face. No injury to the child was reported.
sold_at: Amazon.com, Army & Air Force Exchanges and other toy stores nationwide sold these toys from January 1999 through April 2001 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Chain Saws and Child Table Seats
CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Remote Controlled Toy Race Cars and Galileo Weather Thermometers

product_name: Electronic Light N' Learn activity gyms
heading: CPSC, KB Toys Announce Recall of Activity Gym Toys
hazard_text: Five detachable hanging rattle toys have small round pegs at the top of the toys that can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately and return the toy to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and KB Toys have received six reports of the pegs breaking off, including two reports of a 6-month-old-boy and a 14-month-old-boy beginning to choke off a broken piece of the rattle attachment.
sold_at: KB Toy store, KB Toy Works, KB Toy Outlet, Big Lots, Odd Lots, Pic N Save and MacFrugals nationwide sold the toys from September 2000 through January 2001 for between $20 and $30. The toys also were sold online at KBKids.com.

heading: CPSC, Century Announce Recall of Multi-Use Strollers
hazard_text: The strollers can unexpectedly collapse or the car seat/carrier adapter can unexpectedly detach. When this happens, an infant or young child inside the stroller or an attached car seat/carrier can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using these strollers and call Graco, which now owns the "Century" brand name, toll-free at (800) 345-4109 anytime to order a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Century has received 681 reports of incidents, including 250 injuries when the stroller unexpectedly collapsed or the car seat/carrier adapter detached. These reports include three concussions, two skull fractures, one fractured elbow, and two chipped teeth. The remaining injuries include bruises and cuts.
sold_at: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and discount department stores nationwide sold these strollers from approximately December 1996 through March 2001 for between $100 and $200.

heading: CPSC, Gymboree Announce Recall of Baby Boy Bodysuits
hazard_text: The wheel-shaped zipper pull can twist off and become a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these outfits and return them to any Gymboree store for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Gymboree have not received any reports of injuries.
sold_at: The Gymboree website and stores nationwide sold these bodysuits from March 2001 through May 2001 for about $17.

product_name: ParentsTM magazine-brand Soft Landing Beanbag cushions
heading: CPSC, Battat Incorporated Announce Recall of Beanbag Cushions Suffocation and Strangulation Hazards to Babies Cited
hazard_text: This product is an infant cushion manufactured by Battat for ParentsTM magazine. Infant pillows and cushions have been banned under the Federal Hazardous Substances Act since 1992 because they pose a suffocation hazard to infants. In addition, two 8- to 9-inch cords, which attach toys to the cushions, pose strangulation hazards.
action: Consumers should take the cushions away from children immediately and return the cushions to a Target store for a refund.
incidents_text: Battat has received one report of the cord attached to the rattle on one of these cushions becoming wrapped around the neck of a 7-month-old baby boy, causing red marks.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide sold the cushions from September 2000 through May 2001 for about $24.

heading: CPSC, BRIO® Announce Recall of Toy Baking Sets
hazard_text: The sets include a hand mixer with a knob that can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the hand mixer away from children immediately and call BRIO toll-free at (888) 274-6869 between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday, for a refund or replacement item.
incidents_text: CPSC and BRIO have not received any reports of incidents.
sold_at: Specialty stores, Internet retailers, and mail order catalogs sold the toys nationwide from March 1999 through April 2001 for $15 to $25.

product_name: Star Cruiser® and Rocket Rider® swings on backyard gym sets
heading: CPSC, Hedstrom® Corp. Announce Recall of Swings on Backyard Gym Sets
hazard_text: Screws that hold the swing together can fall out, causing the seat to fall to the ground, posing an injury risk to children.
action: Consumers should stop using the swings immediately, detach them from the gym set, and discard or destroy them. The firm is out of business and a repair is no longer available.
incidents_text: Hedstrom had received 291 reports of seats separating, including 19 children who suffered lacerations, scrapes and bruises.
sold_at: Department, toy, discount, lumber, and hardware stores nationwide, including Toys "R" Us, Wal-Mart and Kmart, sold the gyms from September 2000 through April 2001 for $150 to $400.

heading: CPSC, Saks Incorporated Announce Recall of Boys' Vests
hazard_text: The elastic toggle cord on the end of the zipper pulls can loosen and come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using the vest immediately and return the vest to any Saks store for a refund.
incidents_text: Saks has received one report of a toggle coming off. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Department stores including Parisian, Carson Pirie Scott, Younkers, McRae's, Proffitt's, Bergner's, Herberger's and Boston Store nationwide sold the vests from July 2000 through January 2001 for about $24.

product_name: Tropical Fish and Rockin' Reptile Push'n Pop toys
heading: CPSC, Raymond Geddes & Co. Inc. Recall Push'n Pop Toys
hazard_text: The balloon tongues and the cylinders holding the tongues on these toys can detach, which poses choking and aspiration hazards to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toys away from young children and take them back to where they were purchased for a refund, or throw them away.
incidents_text: That company received a report of a 3-year-old boy who inhaled a balloon tongue that detached from a Zapper toy into his sinus cavity. He required medical treatment to remove the part from his nose.
sold_at: Toy stores, doctor and dentist offices, and carnivals and circuses sold and distributed these toys from August 1998 through March 2001. They were sold for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Spin Master Toys Announce Recall of Water Rocket Toys
hazard_text: The rockets, once propelled from the launcher, can fly rapidly in unpredictable directions, and can hit and injure children.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled water rocket toys immediately and call Spin Master Toys at (800) 622-8339 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive a replacement rocket.
incidents_text: Spin Master Toys has received five reports of the rockets striking children, including a report of a child being hit by the rocket in the head.
sold_at: Major department stores, wholesale clubs and specialty stores, including WalMart, Toys R US, and Costco nationwide sold the rockets from January 2001 through March 2001 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, COMBI International Corp. Announce Recall of Activity Rockers
hazard_text: One of the toys, a clear plastic ball, can crack and break during use, exposing the small beads inside, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately detach the toy bar from the activity rocker and discard it and call COMBI to receive a free replacement toy bar.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Juvenile specialty stores, including The Right Start, Buy Buy Baby and Burlington Coat Factory nationwide sold the rockers from November 2000 through February 2001 for about $70.

heading: CPSC, Child Craft Industries Announce Recall of Changing Tables
hazard_text: Some changing table joints were not properly glued and can separate, presenting a fall hazard to babies.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled changing tables immediately and call Child Craft at (877) 716-2757 between 8:30 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive information on participating in this recall.
incidents_text: Child Craft has received six reports of the changing tables falling apart, including one report of a baby starting to fall from a collapsing table when she was caught by her mother. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Department and specialty stores nationwide, including Sears and Burlington Coat Factory, sold the changing tables from August 1998 through April 2001 for about $150.

heading: CPSC, Drinkmaker of Sweden AB Announce Recall of Home Soda Machines
hazard_text: Components inside the soda machine can break apart, posing a serious risk of lacerations to consumers who can be struck by shrapnel.
action: Consumers should stop using these soda machines immediately and call The Soft Drink Company, of Seattle, Washington, toll-free at (877) 438-7632 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday to receive a free repair. Unused machines should be discarded to prevent the possibility of injury.
incidents_text: There have been three reports of incidents: a 7-year-old boy suffered lacerations to the neck and arms that required hospitalization; a 44-year-old man suffered multiple fractures and a laceration to his right hand; and a 52-year-old man suffered lacerations to his right hand and chin, a fracture of the little finger and contusions to the stomach.
sold_at: The soda makers were sold at state and county fairs and conventions between 1990 and 1996 for about $200 to $250.

heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Basketball Sets
hazard_text: Some of the nets have enlarged openings. If children put their heads into these enlarged openings, the net can get tangled around their necks and they could strangle.
action: Consumers should stop using the basketball set immediately. Consumers should call Fisher-Price toll-free at (800) 247-9395 anytime to order a free replacement net.
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has not received any reports of injuries.
sold_at: Toy, mass merchandise and discount stores sold these toys nationwide from January 2001 through May 2001 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, Unilever Home and Personal Care USA Announce Recall of Snuggle® Teeny Bean Bears Included with Fabric Softener
hazard_text: The yellow pom-pom can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the bear's pom-pom to eliminate the choking hazard. For additional information, consumers can contact Snuggle at (800)-598-5005 between 8:30 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.
incidents_text: CPSC and Unilever Home and Personal Care USA have received one report of an infant who put the pom-pom in his mouth, gagged and began to choke before his mother removed the pom-pom.
sold_at: Wal-Mart Stores nationwide sold the twin packs containing the bear with the pom-pom on the cap from March 2001 through April 2001 for between $7 and $8.

heading: CPSC, Dynacraft Announce Recall of Mountain Bicycles Sold at Toys R Us
hazard_text: The pedals on these bicycles can loosen and fall off while riding, resulting in serious injury to the rider.
action: Consumers should stop using these bicycles immediately, and call Dynacraft to receive a free replacement pedal/crank set and to arrange for free installation.
incidents_text: Dynacraft and CPSC have received 31 reports of pedals falling off, causing the riders to fall. Injuries to riders include a concussion, broken bones, sprains, abrasions, a laceration and muscle strain.
sold_at: Toys R Us stores nationwide sold these bicycles from January 2000 through mid-April 2001 for about $69.

product_name: The "Hotery Pocke Torch" and "Fire Plug" Pocket Torch
heading: CPSC, Tools Exchange Inc. Announce Recall of Novelty Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.

heading: CPSC, NHTSA, Evenflo Announce Recall to Repair Evenflo® Joyride® Car Seats/Carriers
hazard_text: When the seat is used as an infant carrier, the handle can unexpectedly release, causing the seat to flip forward. When this happens, an infant inside the carrier can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.
action: Evenflo will provide consumers with a free easy-to-install repair kit that helps secure the handle. Consumers should not carry the seat by the handle until it has been repaired. CPSC, NHTSA and Evenflo remind caregivers to always restrain infants according to the instructions when in the car seat/carrier.
incidents_text: There have been 240 reports, in the United States, of handles unexpectedly releasing, resulting in 97 injuries. These reports include skull fractures, concussions, a broken leg, and numerous scratches and bruises.
sold_at: Juvenile product, mass merchandise and major discount stores nationwide sold the car seats/carriers from January 1988 through December 1998 for about $30 when sold alone, $48 when sold as a Travel Tandem® (with a detachable convenience base), and $89 when sold with a matching stroller.

heading: CPSC, Creative Consumer Concepts Inc. and Whataburger Inc. Announce Recall of Kid's Meal Toys
hazard_text: The clear, plastic lens covers on these compass toys can come off and pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Parents should take these toys away from children immediately, and return the toy to any Whataburger Restaurant for a free replacement toy.
incidents_text: Creative Consumer Concepts, Inc. has received four reports of the lens covers of the compass toys coming off. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Whataburger Restaurants in Alabama, Arizona, Florida, Louisiana, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Texas distributed the toys from March 2001 through April 2001.

heading: CPSC, Dynacraft Announce Recall of Boys' Mountain Bicycles Sold at Wal-Mart
hazard_text: The front-suspension forks on these bicycles can break during use, resulting in serious injury.
action: Consumers should stop using these bicycles immediately, and call Dynacraft to receive a free replacement fork and to arrange for free installation.
incidents_text: Dynacraft has received 33 reports of the front-suspension forks on these bicycles breaking, resulting in 32 injuries that included a blood clot in the brain, broken bones, cuts, bruises and chipped teeth.
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores sold these bicycles nationwide from September 1999 through March 2001 for about $130.

product_name: Cigarette lighters packaged in souvenir sets with ashtrays, pencils or pens
heading: Cigarette Lighters Recalled by DFS Group Ltd.
hazard_text: The lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms. Young children can easily ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the DFS store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: DFS stores in Hawaii, Guam, Saipan, San Francisco, Las Vegas, and Portland sold these souvenir sets from January 1996 through April 2001 for between $12 and $15.

heading: CPSC, Disney Store Announce Recall of Children's Costumes
hazard_text: Fabric used in these costumes can ignite readily and presents a serious risk of burn injuries in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
action: Consumers should stop wearing these costumes immediately, and return them to any Disney Store or to the Disney Store catalog for a refund and a $10 gift certificate
incidents_text: CPSC and Disney are aware of two reports of costumes igniting, resulting in one burn injury to a 4-year-old girl.
sold_at: The Disney Store sold the costumes for Halloween from July 2000 through October 2000. The Disney Store catalog and DisneyStore.com sold the costumes from July 2000 through January 2001. The costumes sold for about $29.

heading: CPSC, Gladstrong Investments USA Announce Recall of Disposable Lighters4-Year-Old Girl Died in Fire After Playing with Firm's Lighter
hazard_text: The lighters' child-resistant mechanisms are frequently ineffective. Young children are able to operate the lighters, posing a fire hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Gladstrong Investments have received a report of a 4-year-old girl who died after starting a fire with a Gladstrong Investments lighter and then hid in a closet. The fire caused an estimated $72,000 in damages. In another incident, two brothers, a 4-year-old and a 6-year-old, reportedly ignited clothing and paper inside a car while playing with one of these lighters causing about $1,500 in damages. They were not injured.
sold_at: Convenience, drug and discount stores nationwide sold these lighters from January 1998 through February 2001 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Gladstrong Investments USA Announce Recall of Disposable Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters' child-resistant mechanisms are frequently ineffective. Young children are able to operate the lighters, posing a fire hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Gladstrong Investments have received a report of a 4-year-old girl who died after starting a fire with a Gladstrong Investments lighter and then hid in a closet. The fire caused an estimated $72,000 in damages. In another incident, two brothers, a 4-year-old and a 6-year-old, reportedly ignited clothing and paper inside a car while playing with one of these lighters causing about $1,500 in damages. They were not injured.
sold_at: Convenience, drug and discount stores nationwide sold these lighters from January 1998 through February 2001 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Tony USA Inc. Announce Recall of Easter Egg Garlands
hazard_text: The string can break and release the eggs, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these garlands immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Tony USA have not received any reports of injuries.
sold_at: Discount stores nationwide sold the decorative items from February 2001 through April 2001 for about $2.

heading: CPSC, Fleetwood EXIM Inc. Announce Recall of Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters have child-resistant mechanisms that do not work. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using the lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Fleetwood EXIM Inc. have not received any reports of injuries.
sold_at: Convenience, gas, and grocery stores in the southeastern region of the U.S. sold the recalled cigarette lighters from June 2000 through February 2001 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Cosco Inc. and Safety 1st Announce Recall of Bungee Baby Jumpers and Wipe Warmers
CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Infant and Toddler Toys
hazard_text: Two red knobs on the toy can break off, creating small parts that can pose a choking hazard for young children.
action: Consumers should take the toys away from young children immediately and contact Fisher-Price toll-free at (800) 220-7137 anytime to order a free repair kit with replacement knobs.
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has received 32 reports of the knobs breaking off the toys. A 14-month old child was found with a knob in her mouth. Her mother removed it and no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Toy, mass merchandise and discount stores sold these toys nationwide from October 2000 through March 2001 for about $70.

product_name: Levi's infant (12-24 month) and toddler (2T to 4T) garments with metal inseam snaps
heading: CPSC, Levi Strauss & Co. Announce Recall of Infant and Toddler Garments
hazard_text: Parts from the metal inseam snaps can detach from the garment, posing a choking risk for young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the garments away from children and contact Levi Strauss & Co. at 800-USA-LEVI (800-872-5384) for assistance in determining if the garment is part of this recall. If so, Levi Strauss & Co. will provide instructions on returning the garment postage paid to receive a full refund.
incidents_text: Levi Strauss & Co. has received two reports of snaps detaching on jeans. No injuries have been reported.

heading: CPSC, Gymboree Announce Recall of Children's Fleece Pants
hazard_text: The cord locks on the pants can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these pants away from children immediately and return them to any Gymboree store for a full refund.
incidents_text: Gymboree has received one report of a cord lock that broke off, and was found in a child's mouth. The child's parent was present and removed the lock from the child's mouth. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Gymboree's website and stores nationwide sold these pants from September 2000 through February 2001 for about $15.

product_name: Children's bathrobes sold under the brand names Lollypop, Bath Magic and Color Block
heading: CPSC, Arusa International Recall Children's Bathrobes
hazard_text: These bathrobes fail to meet the Standard for the Flammability of Children's Sleepwear, and pose a risk of burn injury to children due to the possible ignition of the garment.
action: Consumers should stop their children from wearing this bathrobe immediately, and return the robes to Arusa International, 261 Fifth Avenue, Suite 1905, New York, NY 10016 for a refund including the cost of the robe, shipping, handling, and return shipment.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The website www.bathrobesonline.com sold these robes from October 1999 through December 2000 for between $17 and $23.

heading: CPSC, Eight Firms Announce the Recall of Zapper Toys
hazard_text: The balloon tongues and the cylinders holding the tongues on these toys can detach, posing a choking and aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toys away from young children and take them back to where they were purchased for a refund, or throw them away.
incidents_text: The Promotional Resources Group of Companies Inc., of Topeka, Kan., previously recalled about 105,000 Bug Zapper toys on June 6, 2000. That company received a report of a 3-year-old boy who inhaled a balloon tongue that detached from a Zapper toy into his sinus cavity. He required medical treatment to remove the part from his nose.
sold_at: Toy stores, doctor and dentist offices, and carnivals and circuses sold and distributed these toys from October 1998 through March 2001. They were sold for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Meijer Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Wands
hazard_text: The batteries can short-circuit, causing the wands' handles to become very hot and melt the plastic, posing a risk of burn injuries to children.
action: Consumers should take these wands away from children immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: Meijer has received two reports of the wands short-circuiting, causing the wands to become hot to the touch and the plastic to melt. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Meijer stores in Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan and Ohio sold these wands from January 2000 through January 2001 for between $2 and $4.

heading: CPSC, Radica USA Ltd. Recall Baseball Video Games to Replace Bats
hazard_text: The bats can separate during a swing. Broken pieces can hit a bystander and cause injury.
action: Consumers should immediately take these recalled toys away from children and contact Radica to arrange for the return of the Play TV Baseball to receive a replacement of Play TV Baseball III.
incidents_text: Radica USA Ltd. has received seven reports of consumers, including children, being hit by pieces of the broken bat, resulting in a split lip, facial lacerations, a bump on the head and bruising.
sold_at: Major retail stores nationwide sold this video game from June 2000 through January 2001 for about $50.

product_name: Water bottles included with girl's Mongoose Heart Breaker bicycles
heading: CPSC, Pacific Cycle LLC Announce Recall of Water Bottles Included With Girls' Bikes
hazard_text: The drinking valve on the cap can detach, presenting a potential choking hazard.
action: Consumers should take the bottles away from children immediately and discard them. To receive a replacement water bottle, call Pacific Cycle toll-free at (800) 626-2811 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday, or visit the Pacific Cycle website at www.mongoose.com.
incidents_text: Pacific Cycle has received two reports of drinking valves detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The bicycles with the water bottle were sold at Wal-Mart stores nationwide and on the Wal-Mart website from July 2000 through January 2001 for about $60.

heading: CPSC, Burger King and Alcone Announce Recall of Kid's Meal Toys
hazard_text: Metal pins with plastic caps that attach the paddle wheel to the riverboat toy can come out and pose a choking hazard.
action: Parents should immediately take the toy away from children and call Burger King Consumer Affairs at (305) 378-3535 for instructions on returning the toy for a free, replacement toy.
incidents_text: Burger King Corp. has received 10 reports that the pin on the toy came out. One child was found with the pin in her mouth. Her father removed it and no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Burger King restaurants nationwide distributed the riverboat toys inside Kid's Meals in January and February 2001.

heading: CPSC, McDonald's Announce Recall of "Scooter Bug" Happy Meal Toys
hazard_text: The bug's antenna can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Parents should take the toy away from children immediately and return the toy to any McDonald's restaurant for a replacement toy.
incidents_text: McDonald's has received two reports of children choking and one report of a child gagging on the broken off antenna.
sold_at: McDonald's restaurants in the U.S. and Canada distributed the toys with Happy Meals from November 2000 through February 2001.

heading: Children's Brooms Recalled by EMSCO Inc.
hazard_text: The paint on the handles of these brooms contain high lead levels. CPSC standards ban toys and other children's products containing high levels of lead. Young children could ingest lead from the broom handles, presenting a lead poisoning hazard.
action: Consumers should take these brooms away from children immediately, and return the brooms to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Toy, discount and grocery stores sold these brooms from April 2000 through February 2001 for about $9.

product_name: "Concept Classification Activity Kits" and "Opposites Take-Home Pack" educational games
heading: Educational Games Recalled by Lakeshore Learning Materials
hazard_text: Metal weights found in the games contain lead, which presents a lead poisoning hazard to children. Lead poisoning in children is associated with behavioral problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation.
action: Consumers should immediately remove and discard the metal discs. To receive a lead-free replacement piece, call Lakeshore Learning Materials toll-free at (800) 421-5354 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The Concept Classification Activity Kits were sold to teachers and schools nationwide between January 1992 and January 2001 for $50. The Opposites Take-Home Pack, a transparent backpack with blue trimming, was sold to teachers and schools nationwide between January 1999 and January 2001 for $10.

heading: Toy Drums Recalled by Eden LLC
hazard_text: The mallet sold with the toy drum has spheres on each end that can pose a choking hazard if they become lodged in a young child's throat.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Department, specialty, gift and toy stores, including FAO Schwarz, sold the toys nationwide from May 2000 through February 2001 for about $12 when sold alone to $45 when sold as part of a set.

product_name: Home and Roam and Baby Express portable cribs/play yards
heading: Recent Death Prompts Search for Recalled Play Yards/Cribs
hazard_text: These cribs/play yards can collapse and entrap an infant.
action: Consumers should search their homes and day care centers for these portable cribs/play yards. Stop using them immediately and call Baby Trend toll-free at (800) 328-7363 to get a free, new play yard.
incidents_text: In January 2001, a 9-month-old baby in Longview, Wash., died of asphyxiation when her neck was caught in the V-shape created by the collapsed sides of her crib/play yard. There have been three other deaths and three reports of babies found not breathing (who were revived) associated with these products.
sold_at: The cribs/play yards were priced from $60 to $130 and were sold nationwide from 1992 to 1994.

product_name: Ballistic front suspension forks installed on Mongoose S-20 and MGX S-20 bicycles and Roadmaster Ridge Rider bicycles
heading: CPSC, By Us International Co. Ltd. Announce Expanded Recall of Bicycle Forks Installed on Mountain Bicycles
hazard_text: The forks on these bicycles can break apart, causing riders to lose control and fall.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these bicycles and call the firm to determine if the fork on their bike is part of the recall. Consumers with recalled forks will receive a free replacement fork and free installation.
incidents_text: There have been 26 reports of forks on these bicycles breaking resulting in nine riders, including teenagers, suffering serious head and bodily injuries, abrasions, bruises and chipped teeth.
sold_at: Discount department stores, including Wal-Mart, and toy stores sold the bicycles with these forks nationwide from June 1998 through June 2000 for between $125 and $150.

heading: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall of Highchairs
hazard_text: The chair's legs can come out, causing the chair to fall to the ground. Children can suffer serious injuries from the fall.
action: Consumers should stop using the highchairs immediately and call Graco at (800) 345-4109 anytime to receive a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Graco has received 108 reports of the highchair legs coming out of the seat, including 105 injuries. Injuries have included a mild concussion, two broken noses, six cuts requiring stitches, black eyes, and bumps and bruises.
sold_at: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and discount department stores nationwide sold these highchairs from January 1995 through June 1998 for between $30 and $35.

heading: CPSC, Simmons Announce Recall to Repair Cribs
hazard_text: Bracket hooks that are used to position the height of the mattress can break, causing the mattress to collapse. Babies can become trapped and suffocate when this happens.
action: Update: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.Simmons is offering a free repair kit, which includes replacement brackets and instructions. The repair can be made easily in the home.
incidents_text: In the past four months, Simmons has received more than 800 reports of bracket hooks breaking. In one case, a 6-month-old hit his chin on the side rail when the mattress dropped.
sold_at: Discount, mass merchandise, juvenile product and department stores, including Sears, sold the cribs nationwide from January 1998 through December 2000 for between $200 and $600.

heading: CPSC, IMT Accessories Announce Recall of BarbieTM Sunglasses
hazard_text: The frames of the sunglasses can break, allowing the petroleum distillate and floating glitter to leak out. Petroleum distillates could be harmful to children's eyes and skin and could be fatal if ingested.
action: Consumers should stop children from wearing the sunglasses immediately. Return the sunglasses to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: IMT Accessories has received one report of a six-year-old child who received chemical burns in her right eye as a result of petroleum distillates leaking from the sunglasses when she was playing.
sold_at: The sunglasses, manufactured under license with Mattel®, were sold nationwide in Target, Walgreens and Bradlee's, from June 1999 through August 2000 for about $6.

heading: CPSC and Chick-fil-A Inc. Announce Recall of "Planet Discovery" Kid's Meal Toy
hazard_text: The suction cup on the toy can come off, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Parents should immediately take away the toy from young children. Throw away the toy or return the planet toys to a Chick-fil-A restaurant for a free replacement premium or a small Icedream®.
incidents_text: Chick-fil-A has received seven reports that the suction cup on the toy came off. In one case, a child began choking but the parent removed the suction cup before medical treatment was needed.
sold_at: The toys were distributed at 800 Chick-fil-A restaurants nationwide during January 2001 and during January 1999.

product_name: Pottery Barn Wooden Dog Pull Toys
heading: CPSC, Pottery Barn Kids Announce Recall of Wooden Pull Toys
hazard_text: Wooden pegs can come off of these pull toys, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these pull toys away from young children immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: Pottery Barn Kids has received a report of one peg coming off of the toy. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The Pottery Barn Kids store in Corte Madera, Calif., and Pottery Barn Outlet stores in Virginia, Texas, Georgia, Tennessee and Ohio sold these pull toys from June 2000 through January 2001 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Kolcraft Announce Recall of Tot Rider Walkers
hazard_text: The cover on the walker's removable music center can break off, allowing small parts to fall from the product, creating a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should remove the music center and call Kolcraft to receive a free replacement tray.
incidents_text: Kolcraft has not received any reports of injuries.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and juvenile products stores nationwide sold these walkers from February 2000 to January 2001 for between $40 and $50.

heading: CPSC, Carter's® Announce Recall to Repair Infant Jumpsuits
hazard_text: A ribbon that runs through the zipper pull tab can detach, resulting in a potential choking hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately remove and discard the ribbon. The garment then can be worn without the ribbon.
incidents_text: Carter's® received four reports of children detaching the ribbons, putting them in their mouths, and starting to gag or choke. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Outlet, department and specialty stores nationwide sold these jumpsuits from May 2000 through December 2000 for $14 to $20.

product_name: 2001 Torker Blaster 16-inch Boy's bicycles and Sunflower 16-inch Girl's bicycles
heading: CPSC, Seattle Bike Supply Announce Recall of Children's Bicycles
hazard_text: Because the bikes' pedals are too low to the ground, they fail to meet federal bicycle standards. Children can lose control when a pedal strikes the ground, causing falls and injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using the bicycles immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a free repair.
incidents_text: Seattle Bike Supply has received one report of a 4-year-old boy whose pedal struck the ground while riding one of these bikes causing him to fall. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: Bicycle stores sold these bicycles nationwide from September 2000 through December 2000 for about $130.

heading: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall to Replace Certain "Busy School Bus" Toys
hazard_text: On certain units, the yellow "awning" piece above the bus' door can break loose, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately, and contact Playskool at (800) 752-9755 to receive a free toy of equal value.
incidents_text: Playskool has received five reports of the yellow awning piece breaking loose. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and toy stores sold these toys nationwide for about $10. The toys were sold from June 1999 through January 2001.

product_name: Ocean Pacific® girls' sweatshirts with drawstrings
heading: CPSC, Trends Clothing Corp. Announce Recall of Girls' Sweatshirts
hazard_text: These sweatshirts have hood drawstrings. Children can get entangled and strangle in the drawstrings that catch on objects, including playground equipment, fences and tree branches. To help prevent children from strangling by their clothing drawstrings, in 1996 CPSC issued guidelines for drawstrings on children's outerwear, which were subsequently incorporated into a voluntary standard.
action: Consumers should remove the drawstring from these garments immediately, or return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Trends Clothing Corp. have not received any reports of injuries involving these sweatshirts.
sold_at: Upton's, Lamont's, Gottschalks, and Sports Authority stores nationwide sold these sweatshirts from August 1999 through October 1999 for about $30.

product_name: BABY GUESS and GUESS GIRLS jeans and overalls
heading: CPSC and Designer Classics LLC Announce Recall of Children's Jeans and Overalls
hazard_text: The small decorative metal appliques on the legs of the garments can come loose and separate, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these garments immediately and call the company for instructions on returning the garment for another garment of the same size.
incidents_text: The company has received one report of a child mouthing a metal piece that had separated from the garment.
sold_at: Department and specialty stores nationwide sold the garments from October 2000 to December 2000 for between $36 and $42.

heading: CPSC, BBC International Ltd. Announce Recall of Crayola® Toddler Boots
hazard_text: The toggle, a small plastic ball attached to the laces, can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should remove the toggles from the laces of these boots immediately and throw the toggles in the trash. Consumers can return the boots to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and BBC International are not aware of any injuries or incidents involving the toggles on these boots.
sold_at: Discount department stores, including Ames, Bradlees, Anne & Hope and Forman Mills, sold these boots from September 1999 through December 1999 for about $20.

product_name: Scoop Pour 'N Squirt squirting fish bath toy
heading: CPSC, Sassy Announce Voluntary Recall to Remove Squirting Fish from Bath Toys
hazard_text: The fish's size, texture, shape and easy compressibility make it possible for an infant to compress the toy and place it in his or her mouth. If the toy reaches the back of the mouth and expands, it may block the child's airway.
action: Consumers should immediately take these squirting fish away from young children and throw them away.
incidents_text: CPSC and Sassy are aware of one report of an infant who put the toy fish in his mouth gagged and vomited and two other reports of infants who put the toy fish in their mouths and started to choke.
sold_at: Mass merchandise stores and toy stores sold these toys nationwide from February 1999 to December 2000 for about $5.

product_name: Excite Super Speeder II and Viper scooter
heading: CPSC, Excite Ltd. Announce Recall of Scooters
hazard_text: The front of the folding mechanism, where the steering column meets the base of the scooter, can create a pinch-point. Fingers can be injured while folding or unfolding the scooter.
action: Consumers should stop using these Excite scooters immediately and contact Excite Ltd. to receive a free cap that will cover the front of the folding mechanism.
incidents_text: Excite has received nine reports of pinch-point injuries to children including one partially amputated fingertip and eight lacerations, one of which required eight stitches.
sold_at: Rite Aid stores nationwide exclusively sold the Super Speeder II and Viper scooters from August 2000 to December 2000 for about $49.

product_name: Kolcraft Ranger and Ranger Quattro strollers
heading: CPSC, Kolcraft Announce Recall of "Ranger" Strollers
hazard_text: Lock mechanisms, found on both sides of the stroller, can break and create a pinch-point hazard. Young children can be injured when their fingers, arms or hands are pinched between parts of the locking mechanism.
action: Consumers should stop using the strollers immediately and call Kolcraft to receive a free repair kit.
incidents_text: Kolcraft has received 39 reports of the lock mechanisms breaking, including one report of a baby's arm being pinched.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and juvenile products stores nationwide sold these strollers January 2000 through November 2000 for about $80.

heading: Stuffed Toys Recalled by Pier 1 Imports
hazard_text: The toys have small parts, which could come loose, posing a possible choking hazard to young children.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
units: About 600 stuffed snowmen and 1,300 stuffed reindeer toys
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Pier 1 Imports stores nationwide sold these toys from August 2000 through October 2000 for about $6.

product_name: Leap Frog "Alphabet Pal" electronic pull toys
heading: CPSC, LeapFrog Announce Recall to Repair "Alphabet Pal" Educational Pull Toys
hazard_text: The toy has a two-part, red plastic connector on the pull string designed to separate under tension. The plastic pieces can detach from the string when the connector is pulled apart and could pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should cut the red plastic string connector off of these toys immediately, or return it to the firm to receive a free replacement toy without a plastic connector.
incidents_text: LeapFrog has received nine reports of the red plastic connector detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Toy, department and specialty stores nationwide sold these toys from June 1999 through November 2000 for about $20.

product_name: Sesame Street Busy Poppin' Pals toys
heading: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall of Additional 170,000 Busy Poppin' Pals Toys
hazard_text: Small springs inside these toys can break loose, posing a choking and laceration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately, and contact Playskool at (800) 752-9755 anytime or visit the firm's website at www.hasbro.com to get information about how to receive a free redesigned replacement toy.
incidents_text: Playskool has received eight reports relating to the springs in its Sesame Street Busy Poppin' Pals toys, including one report that a child put the broken spring in his mouth. No injuries were reported. Playskool received 16 reports of springs breaking in the Busy Poppin' Pals toy recalled earlier. This resulted in five children putting the broken springs in their mouths, and two of these children suffering lacerations.
sold_at: Mass merchandise stores and toy stores sold these toys (Playskool model 5446 made in China) nationwide from November 1994 through 1996 for about $10.

product_name: Kent Kickin' Mini-Scooters and Kash 'N Gold Racer X20TM Scooters
heading: CPSC, Kent International and Kash 'N Gold Ltd. Announce Recall of Scooters
hazard_text: The Kent scooter handles can unexpectedly come out of the steering column if the clamp holding them in is not tight, causing the rider to lose control, fall and possibly suffer injuries. For the Kash 'N Gold scooters, the plastic "T" joint between the handlebars can break, causing the rider to lose control, fall and possibly suffer injuries.
action: Kent: Consumers should stop riding these Kent scooters immediately, and call Kent International to receive a free replacement handlebar with pins to secure the handlebars.Kash 'N Gold: Consumers should stop riding these scooters immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or a new scooter with a metal "T" joint.
units: About 90,000 Kent Kickin' Mini-Scooters and about 7,500 Kash 'N Gold Racer X20TM Scooters
incidents_text: Kent has received four reports of the handles coming out, resulting in four children suffering injuries, including broken arms, a broken wrist, bruises, abrasions and a cracked tooth.Kash 'N Gold has received two reports of the joint breaking, resulting in two injuries including a bump on the head and a chest bruise.
sold_at: Kent: Toys R Us stores nationwide sold the Kent scooters from May 2000 through September 2000 for about $60.Kash 'N Gold: Discovery and Mervyn's stores sold these scooters nationwide from August 2000 through September 2000 for between $70 and $100.

heading: CPSC and Small Beginnings Inc. Announce Recall of "Pacee" Pacifiers
hazard_text: The pacifiers failed CPSC testing standards. These pacifiers present a choking hazard to infants.
action: Consumers should take the pacifiers away from infants immediately, and return them to the firm for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Small Beginnings are not aware of any injuries involving these pacifiers.
sold_at: Various hospitals and medical supply distributors sold these pacifiers nationwide from October 1999 through April 2000 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Cosco Announce Recall to Repair High Chairs
hazard_text: In the recline position, the seats can separate from the frame and fall to the ground. In the upright position, the seats can slip from their set height position to the lowest position or can fall to the ground. Additionally, some seats were sold with a metal restraint anchor that can slip through the back of the seat allowing the child to fall to the ground. Infants and toddlers can suffer head, face and bodily injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using these high chairs immediately. Repair kits are no longer available. New cash incentive is being offered or replacement product. Do not use these products. Please discard or destroy these products.
incidents_text: Cosco and CPSC have received 168 reports of incidents involving the high chairs' seats or restraints, including 57 injury reports, primarily to the head and face. Two children reportedly suffered slight concussions; twelve children were monitored for head injuries; and others suffered swollen eyes, bloody noses and lips, bumps and bruises.
sold_at: The Options 5 High Chairs subject to this recall were manufactured from December 1, 1997 through August 11, 2000. Mass merchandise, juvenile products and major discount department stores nationwide sold the high chairs for about $40 to $50.

product_name: Plush rabbit toys: Natalie Nibblenose and Nickie Nibblenose
heading: CPSC, Small Small World Announce Recall of Plush Rabbit Toys
hazard_text: The eyes on these toys could detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a free replacement toy.
incidents_text: Small Small World has not received any reports of injuries associated with these toys.
sold_at: Specialty stores sold these toys nationwide from December 1999 through September 2000 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, L.L. Bean Inc. Announce Recall of Toddlers' Slippers
hazard_text: The drawcord around the ankle of these slippers can break and release the toggle used to tighten the drawcord. The toggle presents a choking hazard to young children. L.L. Bean has received one report of a 12 month-old baby pulling the toggle off of his slipper.
action: Consumers should take these slippers away from young children immediately, and return them to L.L. Bean for an exchange or refund.
incidents_text: No injuries were reported.
sold_at: The L.L. Kids Store in Freeport, Maine, the L.L. Bean Store in McLean, Va., and the L.L. Bean catalogs and website sold the slippers nationwide from August 2000 through October 2000 for about $18.

heading: Curious George Musical Pull Toys Recalled by Prestige Toy Corp.
hazard_text: The toy has two elastic cords that form a loop, posing a strangulation risk to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these toys immediately and return it to Kmart for a replacement toy.
incidents_text: Prestige Toy Corp. has received a report of a child found with the cords of the toy wrapped around his neck. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Kmart stores nationwide sold these toys from June 1999 through September 1999 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Dolgencorp Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Xylophones Sold at Dollar General Stores
hazard_text: The red mallet sold with the toy xylophone can get lodged in the throats of young children, posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately take this toy away from children and return it to their local Dollar General store for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Dolgencorp Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these toy xylophones.
sold_at: Dollar General stores nationwide sold these toy xylophones from July 1998 through October 2000 for $3.

product_name: window blinds with pull cords and inner cords
heading: CPSC, Window Covering Industry Announce Recall to Repair Window Blinds
hazard_text: The recall involves millions of window blinds with pull cords and inner cords that can form a loop and cause strangulation.
action: Consumers who have window blinds with cords in their homes should call the Window Covering Safety Council toll-free (800) 506-4636 to receive a free repair kit for each set of blinds in the home. You can also visit their website - www.windowcoverings.org - to get more information on checking your window covering.
incidents_text: Since 1991, CPSC has received reports of 130 strangulations involving cords on window blinds. 114 strangulations involve the outer pull cords, and 16 involve the inner cords that hold the blind slats.

heading: CPSC, The Betesh Group Announce Recall of "John Lennon" Crib Mobiles
hazard_text: The screws that connect the mobile's arm assembly and crib clamp can become loose if overtightened. The arms can detach and fall into the crib, injuring the baby inside.
action: Consumers should stop using these mobiles immediately, and call The Betesh Group to receive a free replacement plastic mobile with stuffed animals.
incidents_text: CPSC and The Betesh Group has received seven reports of bumps and scratches to babies after the mobiles attached to their cribs fell on them.
sold_at: Department and specialty stores sold these mobiles from June 1999 through August 2000 for about $39.

heading: CPSC, Playworld Systems Announce Recall of Playground Slides
hazard_text: The welding of the slide bed to the slide sidewall can crack and separate and children's fingers can get caught in the space, posing a risk of amputation.
action: Contact Playworld Systems at (800) 233-8404 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive a new slide.
incidents_text: There has been one report of a severed fingertip of a 6-year-old child.
sold_at: Playworld Systems sold these slides to schools, parks and playgrounds from January 2000 through September 2000 for between $1,500 and $4,000.

heading: CPSC, Appliance Manufacturers Announce Voluntary Recall Initiative for Old Chest Freezers - A Deadly Play Area for Children
action: Consumers should properly dispose of these non-working freezers immediately or disable the latch if disposal is impossible. AHAM has set up a special toll-free number (800) 267-3138 from which consumers will be sent detailed information on identifying the affected units and how to dispose of them or disable the latch. Even if a consumer has a pre-1970 chest freezer that is working, they should still call the toll-free number to get information on what to do when the freezer is no longer working.
incidents_text: Tragically, 27 children have died from suffocation between 1980 and 1999 after becoming trapped in the freezers. The deaths occurred in non-working freezers stored outside, in basements or garages. Victims ranged in age from two to fourteen. In many cases, more than one child suffocated inside the freezer.

heading: CPSC, Pottery Barn Kids Inc. Announce Recall of Bunk Beds
hazard_text: The side rail and guardrails on these beds can break, causing the bed to collapse and allowing children to fall out of the beds.
action: Consumers should stop using the bunk beds and contact Pottery Barn Kids at (800) 671-8312 to schedule a home pick-up. The firm will refund the purchase price, including shipping, and provide a $200 gift certificate.
incidents_text: Pottery Barn has received two reports of beds collapsing. Two 3-year-old girls suffered minor scrapes and bruises in separate incidents.
sold_at: The recalled bunk beds were sold through Pottery Barn Furniture Outlets in Leesburg, Va.; Memphis, Tenn.; Dawsonville, Ga.; and Jeffersonville, Ohio; and nationwide through the Pottery Barn Kids catalog from September 1999 through July 2000 for about $1,100.

heading: CPSC, NHTSA and Century Announce Recall of Infant Car Seats/Carriers
hazard_text: When the seat is used as an infant carrier, the handle can break. An infant inside the carrier can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.
action: Graco, which now owns the "Century" brand name, will provide consumers a free easy-to-install replacement handle. Consumers should not carry the seat by the handle until it has been replaced. Consumers can continue to use the product as a car seat.
incidents_text: Century has received more than 2,700 reports of handle-related problems, including handles breaking, cracking or possibly not being locked while the seat is being used as a carrier. In addition to these reports, Century has also received over 200 reports of injury, including concussions, skull fractures, lacerations, broken bones, bruises, and scratches as a result of such handle-related problems.
sold_at: Juvenile product, mass merchandise and major discount stores nationwide sold the car seats/carriers for about $40 when sold alone to about $130 when sold with a stroller.

heading: CPSC, Playworld Systems Announce Recall of Playground Swings
hazard_text: The swings connectors, which attach the top bar to the end supports, can crack and the top bar can break off and hit children on the swings.
action: Consumers should stop using the swings immediately and call Playworld Systems at (800) 233-8404 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m ET Monday through Friday to receive a repair kit.
incidents_text: There have been two reports of children being injured including a fractured toe and bruises.
sold_at: Playworld Systems sold the swings from February 1998 through May 2000 for between $640 and $975.

product_name: Rainbow Play Systems Play Set Swing Chains
heading: CPSC, Rainbow Play Systems Inc. Announce Recall of Play Sets to Replace Swing Chains
hazard_text: The chains can break while children are swinging and cause the swing seats to fall to the ground. Children can suffer injuries from falling to the ground while swinging.
action: Consumers should stop using the swings on these play sets immediately and contact the company to determine if the chains are defective. If so, remove the chains and return them to the store where purchased for free replacement chains.
incidents_text: Rainbow Play Systems has received seven reports of chains breaking. A 3-year-old boy suffered scrapes and a bruise to his head when he fell to the ground after a chain broke. During inspections, distributors found four defective chains.
sold_at: Rainbow Play System stores nationwide sold the play sets with the defective chains from March 2000 through June 2000 for between $1,200 and $6,000.

heading: CPSC, Halpern Import Co. Announce Recall of Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: These lighters can burn with a high flame and can fail to extinguish, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers immediately should stop using these lighters and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Halpern Import Co. have received one report of a woman who received second degree burns on her chest when the lighter failed to extinguish and ignited her clothing.
sold_at: Tobacco and thrift stores nationwide sold these lighters from June 1999 through May 2000 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, The Maya Group Inc. Announce Recall of Toys
hazard_text: One of the toys, a car, can break during use resulting in a small plastic part that poses a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should remove the toy car from the toy bar immediately and call Maya for a free replacement toy at (888) 521-2202 anytime.
incidents_text: The Maya Group Inc. has received six reports of toy cars breaking. There have been no reports of injuries.
sold_at: Catalogs and specialty stores nationwide sold the toys from August 1999 through August 2000 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, Hamacas Recall Baby Hammocks
hazard_text: Without spreader bars to hold the mini-hammock bed open, the mini-hammocks can suddenly twist around children's' necks and strangle them. Also, infants sleeping on soft bedding can become wedged in positions in which they cannot breathe.
action: Consumers with one of these hammocks should stop using it immediately. For additional information, contact Hamacas at (360) 493-6600 or e-mail Hamacas at info@hamacas.com to receive an adult replacement hammock.
incidents_text: No injuries have been reported with these hammocks, but between 1984 and 1995, CPSC received reports of 12 deaths of children in other mini-hammocks.
sold_at: Hamacas sold these hammocks on their web site as model number HA005 from January through April 2000 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall to Replace Infant Toys
hazard_text: The toy's brightly colored end knobs can detach and allow small, geometric-shaped pieces to come loose, posing a choking hazard to infants and young children.
action: Parents and caregivers should take the toy away from infants and young children immediately, and contact Playskool anytime at (800) 752-9755 to receive a free, redesigned replacement toy.
incidents_text: Playskool has received 10 reports of the toy's knobs detaching to release small parts, including four reports of a small part from the toy being found in the mouths of infants and young children. There have been no reported injuries.
sold_at: Toy and mass merchandise stores, including Toys "R" Us and Wal- Mart, sold these toys from October 1997 through September 2000 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Vaid Enterprises Announce Recall of "BIC" Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Vaid Enterprises are not aware of any injuries involving these cigarette lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Convenience, gas, grocery and thrift stores in the Eastern U.S. sold these disposable cigarette lighters from January 2000 through April 2000 for about $1.

product_name: "Power Drivers" and "Buddy L" battery-powered children's riding vehicles
heading: CPSC, Empire Industries Announce Recall of Children's Riding Vehicles
hazard_text: The vehicles' battery chargers can overheat, presenting fire and injury hazards to children.
action: Consumers should stop using the vehicles immediately. Empire Industries is no longer in business and cannot provide charger adapters or other replacement parts. Consumers should discontinue use of these products, and discard or destroy them.
incidents_text: CPSC and Empire have received about 100 reports of chargers overheating, melting or burning. Five house fires have been reported resulting in at least $100,000 in property damage. One child and one adult received burns to hands on overheated charger jacks.
sold_at: Toy stores and retail catalogs sold the vehicles nationwide from July 1995 through December 1997 for about $130 to $250.

heading: CPSC, KinderkidsTM Announce Recall of Inflatable Playrings for Babies
hazard_text: When a baby leans his or her face against the side of the playring, the soft surface covers the baby's nose and mouth, restricting airflow, and posing the risk of suffocation.
action: Consumers should stop using the playrings immediately and discard or destroy these products. The firm is out of business and cannot be contacted, and a refund is no longer available.
incidents_text: CPSC has received one report of a 6-month-old baby found gasping for air after falling asleep face down in the playring. The baby was removed from the playring without injury. CPSC is aware of infant suffocation deaths when their airflow is restricted from contact with soft surfaces.
sold_at: Walmart stores, and One Step Ahead, a mail-order company, sold the playrings from July 1998 through April 2000 for between $20 and $35.

product_name: Pasta Pals toys included with Fazoli's Kids Meals
heading: CPSC, Fazoli's Announce Recall of Toys Included with Kids Meals
hazard_text: The toy is a plastic, barrel-shaped container with small, plastic tomato and ravioli figures inside. The bottom of the container can fit over a child's nose and mouth, which could pose a suffocation hazard to children under 3 years of age.
action: Consumers should immediately take the barrel-shaped container away from young children. Discard the container or return it to any Fazoli's restaurant for a free Italian Lemon Ice.
incidents_text: Fazoli's has received one report of a child putting the container over his mouth. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Fazoli's restaurants nationwide included the Pasta Pals toys with Fazoli's Kids Meals from January 2000 through August 2000.

heading: CPSC, The Children's Place Announce Recall of Shirts and Rompers
hazard_text: The buttons can come off, posing a small parts choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these clothes away from their children immediately. Consumers should return the clothes to the nearest The Children's Place store for a full refund and a 10 percent discount coupon.
incidents_text: The Children's Place has received three reports of buttons detaching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The Children's Place stores nationwide sold the shirts and rompers from January 2000 through July 2000. The shirts cost about $12 and the rompers cost about $14.

product_name: Gel pens included with Icee Black notebooks and Icee Black notepads
heading: Gel Pens Recalled by Colorbök
hazard_text: Because these pens contain an extra spring, the end caps can shoot off with great force, posing a risk of eye and facial injuries.
action: Stop using these gel pens immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a replacement pen.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Department, drug, grocery, and toy stores sold the notebooks and notepads with these pens from June 2000 through July 2000 for about $5.

product_name: Fisher-Price "Lift & Lock Swings" and "Get Up & Go Walkers"
heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Swings and Toys
hazard_text: Life & Lock Swings: Children can maneuver out of the restraints and fall out of the swings, resulting in serious injuries.Get Up & Go Walkers: Young children leaning forward on the front of the toys can tip them over and fall. Also, the windshield wipers on some of the toys, which stick out, can injure young children when they fall.
action: Life & Lock Swings: Consumers should stop using the swings immediately. Fisher-Price will provide a free repair kit with a supplemental waist and crotch restraint belt.Get Up & Go Walkers: Consumers should stop children from using the toys immediately and call Fisher-Price for a free repair kit that will eliminate the front bar and windshield wiper.
units: About 2.5 million Lift 'n Lock Swings, and about 246,000 Get Up & Go Walkers
incidents_text: Lift & Lock Swings: Eight children suffered serious injuries, including a fractured skull, leg, arm and two collarbones; two concussions; and stitches to the forehead. Thirty children received minor injuries including bumps, bruises and scrapes.Get Up & Go Walkers: Fisher-Price has received 330 reports of children falling while using or near the product. A total of 132 children received injuries such as bumps, bruises, scratches and cuts.
sold_at: Life & Lock Swings: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and discount department stores sold these swings from January 1991 through August 2000 for about $19.Get Up & Go Walkers: Toy, mass merchandise and discount stores sold these push-behind toys from July 1997 through August 2000 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, Kids Line Inc. Announce Recall to Repair "Le Cradle" Bassinets
hazard_text: Infants can become entrapped in an opening between the bassinet's side and mattress platform and suffocate. Additionally, fabric can separate from the metal frame. Infants can be injured when they scrape against or become caught in the frame.
action: Consumers should stop using the bassinets immediately and contact Kids Line for a free in-home repair kit.
incidents_text: Kids Line has received one report of a 3-month-old boy in Oakland Park, Fla. who died when he suffocated after becoming trapped between the bassinet's side and mattress platform. Three other infants were scraped and bruised from contact with the metal frame that became exposed when the fabric separated from the frame.
sold_at: Children's products stores nationwide sold the bassinets from January 1989 through May 2000 for between $100 and $200.

heading: Girl's Nightshirts Recalled by the William Carter Co.
hazard_text: The nightshirts, which fail to meet federal children's sleepwear flammability standards, could ignite easily and present a serious risk of burn injuries in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
action: Take these nightshirts away from children immediately, and call Carter's toll-free at (888) 339-2129 anytime for instructions on returning the nightshirts for a refund and a $15 Carter's gift certificate.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Carter's, department and specialty stores sold these pajamas nationwide from May 2000 through August 2000 for between $10 and $13.

heading: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall to Replace Busy Poppin' Pals Toys
hazard_text: Small springs inside the toy can break loose, posing a choking and laceration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately and contact Playskool at (800) 752-9755 anytime to receive a free, redesigned replacement toy.
incidents_text: Playskool has received 16 reports of the springs breaking. Five children put the broken springs in their mouths, resulting in two children suffering lacerations.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and toy stores, including Toys R Us, sold these toys nationwide for about $10. The toys were sold from January 1996 through August 2000.

product_name: Tangled Treeples toys included with KFC Kids Meals
heading: CPSC, KFC Corporation Announce Recall of Toy Included With KFC Kids Meals
hazard_text: The bottom of the container can fit over a child's nose and mouth, which could pose a suffocation hazard to children under three years of age.
action: Consumers should immediately take the green plastic container away from children under the age of three. They should discard the container or return it to any KFC restaurant for an individual-sized side item, such as macaroni and cheese.
incidents_text: A 19-month-old girl reportedly had the Tangled Treeples container stuck over her face, causing her distress. When her mother removed the container, there was a red mark left on the child's face.
sold_at: KFC restaurants nationwide included the Tangled Treeples toys with KFC Kids Meals from June 2000 through July 2000.

heading: CPSC, Kmart Announce Recall of Children's Swim Masks
hazard_text: The mask's glass lens can break into sharp pieces, causing lacerations to a child's face, eyes or hands.
action: Consumers should stop using these swim masks immediately and return them to the nearest Kmart or Super Kmart store for a refund.
incidents_text: Kmart has received one report of the glass lens shattering. No injuries have been reported.
