sold_at: Kmart and Super Kmart stores nationwide sold the swim masks from February 2000 to July 2000 for about $3.

heading: CPSC, Safety 1st Announce Recall to Repair Baby Walkers
hazard_text: Babies can lose their lower teeth when the teeth are caught in parts of the three-spoke steering wheels. Also, on some of these walkers, the telephone could break apart, releasing small parts and posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using these walkers immediately, and contact Safety 1st. Repair kit no longer available. New cash incentive is being offered or replacement product. Do not use these products. Please discard or destroy these products.
incidents_text: Safety 1st has received eight reports of babies catching their teeth in parts of the three-spoke steering wheels. Six babies lost lower front teeth. There also are 44 reports of the telephone button loosening. One 6-month-old baby girl gagged on a telephone button from a phone that came apart.
sold_at: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and major discount department stores nationwide sold the walkers from April 1998 through April 1999 for about $50.

product_name: Magic Years® Novelty Pacifier Buddy Clips
heading: CPSC, Rashti & Rashti Announce Recall of Pacifier Clips
hazard_text: The metal clip and the small rivet that attaches the clip to a small, stuffed animal on the pacifier holder can break apart easily, exposing babies to small parts. This poses a choking and aspiration hazard to babies.
action: Consumers should take these pacifier clips away from babies immediately, and call Rashti & Rashti at (800) 4-RASHTI between 9 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. ET Monday through Friday for information on receiving a refund.
incidents_text: Rashti & Rashti received one report of a pacifier clip breaking apart. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Gift and specialty stores sold the pacifier clips from September 1999 through June 2000. The pacifier clips sold individually for about $3, and the bib/pacifier clip sets sold for about $5.

product_name: Gerry® TrailTechTM backpack baby carriers with plastic frames
heading: CPSC, Hufco-Delaware Co. Announce Recall to Repair Gerry® TrailTech™ Backpack Baby Carriers
hazard_text: Small infants can shift to one side, slip through the leg openings of these carriers and fall.
action: Consumers should stop using these backpack carriers immediately. Evenflo, which is now the responding company for this recall, no longer has any service parts for this product nor the capability of producing these parts. As repair kits are no longer available, consumers should destroy these products.
incidents_text: CPSC and Hufco-Delaware have received four reports of infants slipping through the leg openings of these carriers. There were two reports of infants suffering fractured skulls and two reports of infants suffering bumped heads when they fell to the ground.
sold_at: Department and baby products stores nationwide sold these backpack carriers from January 1996 through July 2000 for about $65.

product_name: Plush Shape Sorter Toys and Plush Stacking Toys
heading: CPSC, Gymboree Announce Recall of Plush Shape Sorters and Stacking Toys
hazard_text: The stuffing of the toys can contain sewing needles and sharp metal pieces. Young children could ingest or be cut by these sharp metal pieces.
action: Stop using the toys immediately, and return it to the store where purchased for a refund.
units: About 19,000 Plush Shape Sorter toys, and about 12,000 Plush Stacking toys
incidents_text: There has been one report of a part of a sewing needle in the stuffing of the plush shape sorter toy. After searching through its inventory, the firm found additional plush shape sorter and plush stacking toys with sharp metal pieces. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Gymboree and Play & Music Stores, and the Gymboree website sold the toys nationwide from November 1998 through June 2000 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Shelcore Inc. Announce Recall Children's Play Tables to Replace Mallets
hazard_text: The xylophone mallet that comes as part of this table set can be lodged into the throats of young children, posing a choking hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately throw the recalled mallets in the trash, and call Shelcore for a free replacement mallet.
incidents_text: Shelcore received a report of the mallet being jammed into the throat of a 13-month-old boy after he fell while teething on the ball end of the mallet. Lacerations in the throat resulted when an adult had to forcibly remove the mallet to prevent choking.
sold_at: Toy stores nationwide sold these play tables from March 1996 through March 1999 for between $18 and $20.

heading: CPSC, Child GuidanceTM Announce Recall to Replace Caterpillar Toys
hazard_text: Young children can choke on the small balls attached to these toys.
action: Parents and caregivers should take these toys away from young children immediately. Consumers should send the toy back to the firm to receive another toy of similar value. The firm will pay postage costs.
incidents_text: CPSC has received one report of a 5-month-old girl in El Paso, Texas, choking to death after one of the small balls attached to these toys lodged in her throat. CPSC also received reports of two children starting to choke on a ball from this toy.
sold_at: Toy and discount department stores nationwide sold the caterpillar toys from May 1998 through June 2000 for about $13.

product_name: "Hop, Skip, Jumper" activity seats and Big Action Construction Toys
heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Baby Jumper Seats and Construction Toys
hazard_text: Hop, Skip, Jumpers: The spring that suspends the jumper seat from the doorway can break. Babies can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.Construction toys: The crane has a bucket that is attached by a 25-inch strap. Children can wrap the 25-inch strap around their necks, posing a strangulation hazard.
action: Hop, Skip, Jumpers: Consumers should stop using the jumpers immediately. Fisher-Price will provide a free repair kit with a new, suspension strap to support the jumper seat if the spring breaks. The repair can be done quickly and easily in the home.Construction toys: Consumers should cut the 25-inch strap off of the toy immediately and throw the strap away. Fisher-Price will provide a free replacement crane boom and bucket with a 12-inch strap so that children cannot wrap it around their necks.
units: About 882,000 Hop, Skip, Jumpers; and about 267,000 Big Action Construction toys
incidents_text: Hop, Skip, Jumpers: Fisher-Price has received 80 reports of the springs breaking. Twenty babies have been injured. The injuries include nine lacerations to heads, five of which required stitches or staples, a dislocated tailbone, a black eye and bumps, bruises and scrapes.Construction toys: Fisher-Price has received 16 reports of children wrapping the strap around their necks. Seven children suffered minor injuries.
sold_at: Hop, Skip, Jumpers: The Hop, Skip, Jumpers were sold by mass merchandise, juvenile products and discount stores from January 1987 through January 1994 for about $25.Construction toys: Toy, mass merchandise and discount stores sold the Big Action Construction toys nationwide from January 1997 through June 2000 for about $60.

product_name: Whoozit® Touch and TeetheTM teething toys
heading: Teethers Recalled by Manhattan Group LLC
hazard_text: The teether can pull apart easily and expose small pieces. This poses choking and aspiration hazards to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toys away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or exchange for another toy.
incidents_text: The firm has received four reports of teethers coming apart and exposing small pieces. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty stores and gift shops sold the teethers from February 2000 through May 2000 for about $12.

heading: CPSC, Dollar Tree Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Doll Feeding Sets
hazard_text: The doll bib in the set has snaps that detach, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take this recalled toy away from young children immediately and return it to any Dollar Tree Store for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Dollar Tree Stores Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these bibs.
sold_at: Dollar Tree Stores nationwide sold the doll feeding sets during December 1999 for about $1.00.

heading: CPSC, The First Years Inc. Announce Recall to Replace "Elmo Nitelights"
hazard_text: The faceplate on these nightlights can be broken off, exposing wiring and posing shock and electrocution hazards.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the "Elmo Nitelights" from their sockets and throw them away. If wires are exposed, turn off the power before removing. Consumers should contact The First Years to receive a free replacement nightlight at (800) 533-6708.
incidents_text: CPSC and The First Years have received three reports of the faceplates on these nightlights breaking off resulting in two 1-year-old girls and an adult receiving an electrical shock when touching the exposed wires.
sold_at: Discount, drug, grocery and toy stores sold these nightlights from July 1997 through March 2000 for between $5 and $6.

heading: CPSC, Cycle Express Inc. Announce Recall of Bicycle Helmets
hazard_text: These helmets fail impact testing and labeling required under CPSC's Safety Standard for Bicycle Helmets, violating the Consumer Product Safety Act. Riders wearing these helmets are not adequately protected from falls, and could suffer severe head injuries or death.
action: Consumers should stop using these bicycle helmets immediately, and return them to the store where purchased. They will receive a $7 refund, which is the assessed value of the helmet.
incidents_text: CPSC and Cycle Express are not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these helmets.
sold_at: Toys R Us stores sold these helmets with accessories nationwide from October 1999 through April 2000 for about $13.

heading: CPSC, Rand International Announce Recall of Bicycle Helmets
hazard_text: These bicycle helmets fail impact testing and labeling required under CPSC's Safety Standard for Bicycle Helmets, violating the Consumer Product Safety Act. Riders wearing these helmets are not properly protected from falls, and could suffer severe head injuries.
action: Consumers should stop wearing these bicycle helmets immediately, and return them to Rand International for a free replacement helmet.
incidents_text: CPSC and Rand International are not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these products.
sold_at: Kmart and Rose's stores nationwide sold these bicycle helmets from April 1999 through March 2000 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Burley Design Cooperative Announce Recall to Repair Burely-Bravo™ Bicycle Trailers
hazard_text: The wheel can separate from these trailers during use, and result in crashes and injuries to children riding inside. Loss of control to the bicycle pulling these trailers also can cause the riders to crash and suffer injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using these Burley-BravoTM trailers immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a free inspection and repair, if needed.
incidents_text: Burley has received one report of a wheel coming off of one of these trailers, causing the bicycle rider to fall and suffer minor injuries.
sold_at: Authorized Burley dealers and bicycle shops nationwide sold these trailers from November 1999 through June 2000 for about $350.

product_name: Kellogg's Nascar® Pull'N Go Hot Wheels
heading: CPSC, Kellogg Company Announce Recall of Toy Cars Inside Boxes of Cereal
hazard_text: The tires can detach from the wheels of these cars, posing a choking hazard for young children.
action: Consumers should take these toy cars away from young children immediately, and send the cars to Kellogg to get a free replacement item and reimbursement for postage. Send the car, along with your name and address to Kellogg Company, P.O. Box 185654, Battle Creek MI 49018-5654.
incidents_text: Kellogg has received two reports of the tires detaching from the wheels of these toy cars. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Various club and a few grocery stores nationwide sold these cars in specially marked packages of Kellogg's® Tri-Fun-PakTM 40-ounce box, Kellogg's® Froot Loops® 43.6-ounce box, Kellogg's® Mini-Wheats® Frosted Bite Size 58.8-ounce box, and Kellogg's® Crispix® 31.4-ounce box. The cars were distributed inside boxes of these cereals from March 2000 through June 2000.

heading: CPSC, Whitehall-Robins Healthcare Announce Recall of Teething Rings
hazard_text: When bent, these teething rings can fit into an infant's mouth and trigger a gagging reflex. This poses a risk of vomiting, which could result in choking and aspiration.
action: Consumers should take these teething rings away from infants immediately. Contact Whitehall-Robins Healthcare for information on returning the teething ring in order to receive a free Anbesol® product.
incidents_text: Whitehall-Robins Healthcare has received two reports from consumers of children gagging on the teething rings, including one report of a child starting to choke.
sold_at: Mass merchandise, drug and grocery stores nationwide sold Baby Anbesol with these teethers from May 1999 through June 2000 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Galoob Toys Inc. Announce Recall of Sky Dancers® Flying Dolls
hazard_text: The hard plastic Sky Dancers® dolls can fly rapidly in unpredictable directions, and can hit and injure both children and adults.
action: Consumers should stop using these flying dolls immediately and call Galoob® for instructions on how to return the toy sets to receive a product of equal value.
incidents_text: Galoob® has received 170 reports of the dolls striking children and adults resulting in 150 reports of injuries. They include eye injuries, including scratched corneas and incidents of temporary blindness, broken teeth, a mild concussion, a broken rib, and facial lacerations that required stitches.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and toy stores nationwide sold the dolls from November 1994 through June 2000 for between $8 to $25.

heading: CPSC, Today's Kids Announce Recall of Spinning Ride Toys
hazard_text: The center column can break, causing a child to suddenly fall backward or be hit in the face by the broken column.
action: Consumers should take these spinning ride toys away from children immediately, and discard or destroy these products. The firm is out of business and cannot be contacted, and a replacement toy is no longer available.
incidents_text: Today's Kids had received 1,427 reports of the toy's columns breaking off, resulting in five injuries. Injuries include bumps on heads, cut faces and split lips. Two children required stitches.
sold_at: Toy and discount department stores nationwide sold these spinning ride toys from July 1999 through May 2000 for about $20.

product_name: Little Smart Soft Songs Baby Phones
heading: CPSC, Vtech Industries Announce Recall of Toy Baby Phone
hazard_text: The toy phones have a ball-shaped antenna which can detach, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toy phones away from children. For more information, contact VTech at (800) 521-2010 between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. CT Monday through Friday for a replacement phone.
incidents_text: CPSC and Vtech Industries have received nine reports of the plastic ball detaching from these phones. One child reportedly started to choke on one of these plastic balls.
sold_at: Wal-Mart stores nationwide sold the toy phones from January 2000 through May 2000 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Jetmax International Ltd. Announce Recall to Repair Children's Rocking Chairs Sold at Target Stores
hazard_text: The rear legs of the chair can separate from the rocker's base causing it to collapse, and the child seated in the chair can fall.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these rockers, and contact Jetmax International to get a free repair kit with easy installation instructions.
incidents_text: Jetmax has received five reports of these chairs collapsing and children falling. One 13-month-old girl suffered a laceration requiring 18 stitches.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide sold the rocking chairs from November 1999 through March 2000 for about $20.

product_name: Tot Wheels® Entertainer® Activity Center infant walkers
heading: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall to Repair Tot Wheels® Entertainer® Infant Walkers
hazard_text: These walkers can collapse unexpectedly during use and injure infants.
action: Consumers should stop using these walkers immediately, and call Graco for a free repair kit, which includes a replacement tray, at (800) 345-4109 anytime.
incidents_text: Graco has received 27 reports of these walkers collapsing. Injuries to infants have included a cut toe, a bump on the head, a sprained foot, and scrapes and bruises to legs and feet.
sold_at: Mass merchandise, juvenile product and major discount department stores nationwide, including Wal-Mart and Toys R Us, sold the walkers from September 1999 through February 2000 for about $50.

product_name: Classic Patterns "Cherubs" and Soft Comfort latex pacifiers
heading: Playtex Products Voluntarily Announces Pacifier Recall in Cooperation with CPSC
hazard_text: Because the latex is aging faster than normal, the nipple can detach from the shield, presenting a choking hazard to babies.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled pacifiers immediately and return them directly to Playtex for a free replacement pacifier or a $3 coupon toward the purchase of another Playtex infant feeding or soothing product. Consumers should send the pacifiers to Playtex Pacifiers, Playtex Products Inc., 20 Troy Road, Whippany, NJ 07981. Playtex will reimburse consumers for postage.
incidents_text: Playtex has received 21 reports of pacifier nipples detaching from the shields. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Stores nationwide sold the pacifiers before June 2000 for about $2 to $4, depending on whether it was a single or double pack.

heading: CPSC, Ace Hardware Corp. Announce Recall of Vinyl Window Blinds
hazard_text: These blinds contain lead exceeding government guidelines, and do not have required labeling warning they contain lead. Over time, vinyl deteriorates from exposure to sunlight and heat, forming lead dust on the surface of the blind. Young children can ingest lead by wiping their hands on the blinds and then putting their hands in their mouths. Lead poisoning in children is associated with behavioral problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation.
action: Consumers should remove the window blinds from windows and keep them away from children. Consumers can return the window blinds to the store where they were purchased for a refund. For more information, call Ace Hardware Corp. toll-free at (877) 223-4391 between 7 a.m. and 6 p.m. CT Monday through Friday.
incidents_text: CPSC and Ace Hardware are not aware of any lead poisonings involving these window blinds.
sold_at: Ace Hardware and other hardware stores nationwide sold the window blinds from August 1999 through May 2000 for between $6 and $27.

heading: CPSC, Federated Department Stores Announce Recall of Children's Robes
hazard_text: The standards require sleepwear, including robes, to be flame resistant, and if the garment ignites, the flame must self-extinguish. Failure to meet the flammability standards presents a risk of serious burn injuries to children.
action: Parents should immediately stop their children from wearing these robes and return the robes to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: Federated Department Stores has not received any reports of injuries from these robes.
sold_at: These robes were sold at Bloomingdale's, Burdines, Goldsmith's, Lazarus, Macy's, Rich's, and The Bon Marché from July 1995 through January 2000 for about $25 to $52.

heading: CPSC, Promotional Resources Group Announce Recall of Bug Zapper Toys Sold With Children's Meals
hazard_text: The balloon tongue on this toy can detach, posing a choking and aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toys from young children, and return the toy to the restaurant where the children's meal was purchased for a free replacement toy. Consumers also can receive a free replacement toy directly from the company.
incidents_text: The Promotional Resources Group has received one report of the balloon tongue detaching from the toy. A 3-year-old boy reportedly removed the balloon tongue, placed it in his nose and inhaled it into his sinus cavity. He required medical treatment to remove the part from his nose.
sold_at: Fast food, drive-in and small franchise restaurants distributed these toys with children's meal from November 1998 through April 2000.

heading: Infant Cargo Skirts Recalled by Associated Merchandising Corp.
hazard_text: The snaps on the panty of these skirts can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these skirts immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund. Consumers also can return them by mail, and will be reimbursed for postage.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Clothing and department stores nationwide sold these cargo skirts from January 2000 through March 2000 for between $14 and $16.

heading: Children's Picnic Sets Recalled by Mervyn's
hazard_text: The paint on the bag contains high levels of lead that violates the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Act. Lead poisoning in children is associated with behavior problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation.
action: Consumers should stop using these bags immediately and return them to any Mervyn's store for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported
sold_at: Mervyn's stores nationwide sold the sets from April 2000 through May 2000 for about $13.

product_name: Kids II "Soft Toy Bouncer Seats" and "Comfort Me Bouncers"
heading: CPSC, Kids II Announce Recall of Bouncer Seats
hazard_text: The removable toy bar that attaches to the seat can suddenly release and cause injuries to babies.
action: Consumers should remove the semi-circular toy bars immediately and contact Kids II for an in-home repair kit. Consumers can continue to use the bouncer seat for the baby to sit in as long as the toy bar is removed.
incidents_text: Kids II has received 122 reports of toy bars suddenly releasing from bouncer seats, resulting in 31 injuries to babies, including a black eye, a scraped eye, and facial cuts.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and juvenile specialty stores nationwide sold the seats from October 1997 through April 2000 for about $25 to $35.

product_name: Tweety Rattle and Tweety girls' jelly swimwear sandals
heading: CPSC, Warner Bros. Studio Store Announce Recall of Tweety Rattles and SandalsCPSC, Warner Bros. Studio Store Announce Recall of Tweety Rattles and Sandals
hazard_text: Both products are being recalled because small parts of each product can detach and pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these products away from children immediately and return them to a Warner Bros. Store for a refund.
units: About 3,800 Tweety rattles and 1,000 pairs of Tweety sandals
incidents_text: CPSC and Warner Bros. Studio Store have received three reports of parents removing detached parts of sandals and a rattle from their babies' mouths. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Warner Bros. Stores nationwide sold the Tweety Bib, Rattle and Spoon Sets from August 1998 through January 2000 for about $15, and sold the Tweety sandals from February 2000 through April 2000 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Filter Tech Inc. Announce Recall of Windshield Washer Fluid
hazard_text: The bottles, which contain methyl alcohol, are not sealed with child-resistant closures as required by federal law. Methyl alcohol, also known as methanol, is toxic and can cause blindness or death if ingested.
action: Consumers immediately should return the bottles to the store where purchased for their choice of a full refund, exchange or child-resistant cap.
incidents_text: CPSC and Filter Tech are not aware of any injuries involving this product.
sold_at: Speedway Superamerica stores and other automotive stores in Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia sold the windshield washer fluid from October 1999 through April 2000 for about $1.50.

heading: CPSC, Hangouts Recall Baby Hammocks
hazard_text: These baby hammocks can suddenly become twisted around children's' necks and strangle them. Also, infants sleeping on soft bedding can become wedged in positions in which they cannot breathe.
action: Consumers with one of these hammocks should stop using it immediately, and return it to Hangouts for a free, standard single hammock (model MY-SS-1130).
incidents_text: No incidents or injuries have been reported in these hammocks, but between 1984 and 1995, CPSC received reports of 12 deaths of children in other mini-hammocks.
sold_at: The Hangout store in Boulder, Colo., and its catalogs sold these hammocks as model number MY-BB-1110 from January 1990 through September 1999 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Jack Rabbit Creations Recall Wooden Stacking Toys
hazard_text: The wooden peg in the black and white checked base can come off, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toys away from young children immediately and contact the company for a free replacement base and a small toy.
incidents_text: Jack Rabbit Creations has received four reports of the pegs coming loose. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty and Gift shops have sold these products from February 1999 through April 2000 for about $25.

product_name: Ballistic front suspension forks installed on Mongoose S-20 and MGX S-20 bicycles
heading: CPSC, By Us International Co. Ltd. Announce Recall of Bicycle Components
hazard_text: The forks on these bicycles can break apart, causing riders to lose control and fall.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these bicycles and call Brunswick Bicycles for information on receiving a free replacement fork, including installation.
incidents_text: By Us and Brunswick have received 18 reports of forks on these bicycles breaking resulting in nine riders, including teenagers, suffering serious head and bodily injuries, abrasions, bruises and chipped teeth.
sold_at: Discount department and toy stores nationwide sold these bicycles from September 1998 through May 2000 for between $125 and $150.

heading: CPSC, Weed Wizard Acquisition Corp. Announce Recall of Weed Trimmer Heads With Metal Chains
hazard_text: The end link of the trimmer's metal chain can rapidly and unexpectedly detach during use, propelling the link into the air at a high velocity. If the metal link strikes the user or a bystander, it can penetrate skin and bone, causing injury or death.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: Weed Wizard and CPSC have received 47 reports of metal links detaching from trimmers, resulting in 41 injuries, including the death of a 3-year-old girl in Alabama who was struck in the head by a metal link. The injuries included users and bystanders being struck by metal links in the head, neck, legs, ankles and feet, resulting in penetration wounds and lacerations.
sold_at: Home centers, mass merchants, discount stores, hardware stores and television advertisements nationwide sold Weed Wizards with metal chains from May 1987 through April 2000 for between $19 and $25. The replacement chain kits were sold from January 1992 through April 2000 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Jogging Strollers

product_name: BOB Sport Utility Stroller and BOB Sport Utility Stroller D'lux jogging strollers
heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Jogging Strollers
hazard_text: The stroller's front wheel connector can crack during use, causing the wheel to separate from the frame. A jogger could lose control of the stroller, or the stroller could suddenly collapse, resulting in injury to a child.
action: Consumers should stop using the stroller immediately, and return it to the store where purchased for repair. Consumers also can return the strollers to BOB Trailers for repair.
incidents_text: BOB Trailers has received seven reports of the wheel connector cracking causing the front wheel to become loose. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Bike, baby and outdoor product stores and websites retailers sold the strollers nationwide from November 1998 through March 2000 for about $280 to $370.

product_name: Healthtex® and Little Impressions® baby garments
heading: CPSC, Healthtex Announce Recall of Baby Garments
hazard_text: Snaps on these garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to babies.
action: Consumers should stop using these baby garments immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or exchange. Consumers also can return garments directly to the manufacturer.
incidents_text: CPSC and Healthtex have received 10 reports of snaps detaching from the baby garments. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Department stores and children's specialty stores nationwide as well as the Healthtex website sold these clothes from May 1999 through December 1999 for between $12 and $30.

heading: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall of Infant Swings
hazard_text: The restraint systems on the older swings consist of a waist belt only and a hinged or removable tray, which serves as a restraint. If parts are missing, the restraints are not used, or the tray pops off, infants can slip down into the seat and strangle or fall from the swing.
action: Consumers should stop using the swings immediately. To receive the free safety restraint, consumers should call Graco at (800) 345-4109 anytime. Consumers may also write to Customer Affairs, Graco Children's Products Inc., P.O. Box 100, Elverson, PA 19520.
incidents_text: There have been six deaths. These occurred when parts were missing or the restraints were not used and infants slid down the swings' seats and became tangled in the restraints. In five instances, the swings were second-hand. Of 209 incidents, 181 were reports of infants falling from the swing. In nine of the falls, infants suffered serious injuries including bone fractures and concussions. Twenty-two infants were caught at the neck or chest.
sold_at: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and major discount stores nationwide sold the Graco swings through approximately January 1998 for between $70 to about $120.

heading: CPSC, Kmart Corp. Announce Recall of Children's Lamps
hazard_text: The lamps can short circuit posing a fire hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately unplug the lamps and stop using them. Consumers should return the lamps to their local Kmart for a refund.
incidents_text: Kmart has received eight reports of the lamps short circuiting and catching fire, resulting in property damage. One of these fires resulted in more than $15,000 in damages, and another caused more than $3,000 in damages. No injuries or deaths have been reported.
sold_at: Kmart stores nationwide sold the lamps from January 1993 through March 2000 for between $13 and $15.

product_name: 3-in-1 Cradle Swing With Detachable Carrier and Bounce 'n PlayTM Activity Dome
heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Infant Products
hazard_text: Cradle Swing: The 3-in-1 Cradle Swing has a detachable seat that can be used as a carrier. When used as a carrier, the locks for the handle can unexpectedly release, causing the seat to flip forward. When this happens, infants can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.Activity Dome: The nylon bands that hold the surface level can detach allowing the surface to tilt. This can cause an infant to slide down against one end and be trapped in a position in which it is difficult to breathe, posing a suffocation hazard.
action: Carrier: Consumers should stop using the swing's seat as a carrier immediately. Fisher-Price will provide a free repair kit that will lock the carrier's handle in place. The repair can be done quickly and easily in the home. Consumers can continue to use the seat as intended as a cradle swing. Activity Dome: Consumers should stop using the Bounce 'n Play Activity Dome immediately. Fisher-Price has discontinued distribution of the repair kit for this product. Consumers should discontinue use of the item immediately and contact Fisher-Price for further information.
units: About 105,000 "3-in-1 Cradle Swings," and 235,000 "Bounce 'n Play Activity Domes"
incidents_text: Carrier: There have been 28 reports of the carrier's handle unexpectedly releasing when used as a carrier, resulting in injuries to 10 infants. The injuries include a skull fracture, bumps, bruises and scrapes to the head. According to the reports, some injuries occurred to infants who were restrained in the seat.Activity Dome: There have been 28 reports of the nylon band detaching and causing the play and nap surface to tilt. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Carrier: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and major discount stores sold the 3-in-1 Cradle Swings nationwide from March 1997 through January 1999 for about $100.Activity Dome: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and major discount stores have sold the Bounce 'n Play Activity Domes nationwide from December 1998 through March 2000 for about $50.

heading: Converters Recalled by Coast Electronics Supply
hazard_text: The product presents an electrical shock hazard because the unplugged end of the cord is energized when the other end is plugged in.
action: Stop using the product immediately and return it to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: A 4-year-old boy was shocked when he grasped the end of the cord.
sold_at: Small electronic stores in California, Colorado, Missouri, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon and Texas sold the product for $25 to $30.

heading: CPSC, Advance Thermo Control Announce Recall of Baby Wipe Warmers
hazard_text: Cracks in the interior tub of these wipe warmers can allow water to contact the electrical components. This can result in consumers receiving an electric shock.
action: Consumers should immediately unplug the warmers, remove the wipes, and check to see if the interior tub is cracked. If so, stop using the warmer immediately, and call ATC for information on receiving a free replacement unit.
incidents_text: Prince Lionheart has received four reports of electric shocks when consumers touched the wipes in the warmers with cracked tubs.
sold_at: Toy, department and baby specialty stores, including Toys "R" Us and Burlington Coat Factory, and mail order catalogs, sold these wipe warmers nationwide from February 1998 through December 1999 for about $25.

heading: CPSC, Russ Berrie & Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Rattles
hazard_text: The shape and size of the rattle's handle allow it to become lodged in the throats of babies, posing a choking hazard. The rattles violate the Federal Hazardous Substances Act for the design and construction of baby rattles.
action: Consumers should take these rattles away from babies immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Russ Berrie are not aware of any incidents or injuries involving these rattles.
sold_at: Specialty and drug stores, and flower and gift shops nationwide sold these rattles from November 1998 through December 1999 for about $14.

heading: CPSC, Maxim Enterprise Inc. and Zany Brainy Inc. Announce Recall of Wooden Pull Toy
hazard_text: The pull toy's wheels can break off and the bead can detach from the pull string, posing small parts choking hazards to young children.
action: No remedy available.
incidents_text: The firms have received a report of wheels coming off and a report of the bead detaching from the pull string. The detached bead was found in a child's mouth. No injuries were reported.

product_name: InSTEP and HEALTHRIDER single and double jogging strollers
heading: CPSC, InSTEP™ LLC Announce Recall of Jogging Strollers
hazard_text: The stroller's brake can fail, causing the stroller to unexpectedly roll away resulting in injury to a child.
action: Consumers should stop using the strollers immediately and contact InSTEP LLC to receive a free, easy-to-install repair kit.
incidents_text: InSTEP LLC has received five reports of brakes failing. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Burlington Coat Factory, J.C. Penney, Healthrider, The Sports Authority and Target stores nationwide, among others, sold the strollers from December 1998 through July 1999 for about $100 for a single jogger and $250 for a double jogger.

heading: CPSC Warns Against Baby Mattresses, Pads That Make Unfounded Claims About Reducing SIDS
hazard_text: CPSC is warning consumers that certain baby mattresses and mattress pads encourage the potentially deadly practice of placing babies to sleep on their stomachs, and claim that the products reduce the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS).

product_name: Tommy Hilfiger socks for infants and children
heading: CPSC, Mountain High Hosiery Ltd. Announce Recall of Tommy Hilfiger Socks for Infants and Children
hazard_text: The heat-sealed Tommy Hilfiger flag logo appliques on these socks can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these socks immediately, and call Mountain High to receive an exchange or a refund.
incidents_text: Mountain High has received three reports of the logo appliques detaching from these socks. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Department and specialty stores nationwide sold two-pair packages of the socks from January 1999 through January 2000 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Nordstrom Inc. Announce Recall of Infant and Toddler Jackets
hazard_text: Snaps located on the flap pockets of these jackets could be removed, presenting a choking hazard to infants and young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these jackets immediately and return them to any Nordstrom store for a refund.
incidents_text: Nordstrom is not aware of any injuries from these jackets.
sold_at: Nordstrom stores nationwide sold these jackets during January 2000 for about $34 to $36.

product_name: Pull toys: Enchanted Garden Inchworm (item number EG150); Merry Meadows Cow (item number FS150); and Sunny Safari Blue Elephant (item number SS150)
heading: Pull Toys Recalled by Manhattan Group LLC
hazard_text: The wooden wheels and pegs attached to the toy could come off, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toys away from young children immediately and return them to the stores where purchased for a refund or exchange for another soft toy.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Specialty stores and gift shops nationwide sold these toys from July 1999 through December 1999 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Prometheus International Inc. Announce Recall of Novelty Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters do not have any child-resistant mechanisms, as required by the Consumer Product Safety Act. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting a fire hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a free replacement lighter with a child-resistant mechanism.
incidents_text: CPSC and Prometheus International Inc. are not aware of any incidents or injuries involving these lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Tobacco stores nationwide sold these lighters from March 1997 through February 1999 from $50 to $75. The company advertised these lighters on their web site at www.prometheuskkp.com.

heading: Toy Chests Recalled by Thornwood Furniture
hazard_text: The lids on these toy chests could fall onto a child's head or neck. An investigator for the Georgia Office of Consumer Affairs discovered the problem with the toy chest while conducting retail surveillance for CPSC.
action: Consumers should immediately stop children from using the toy chests and contact the store where purchase for information on getting a free replacement.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Furniture stores nationwide, including Rooms To Go, Bedroom Superstores and MN Goldstein, sold the toy chests from January 1999 through November 1999 for about $170.

heading: CPSC, Shopko Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Baby Garments
hazard_text: The rose-shaped buttons on these garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these garments, and return them to Shopko for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Shopko Stores have received one report of a button found in a child's mouth. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: Shopko stores nationwide sold these garments from June 1999 through October 1999 for between $8 and $15.

product_name: Pokémon balls distributed with Burger King kids meals
heading: In Wake of Second Death, CPSC and Burger King Again Urge Consumers to Destroy and Discard Pokemon Balls
hazard_text: The balls pose a suffocation hazard to children under three years of age.
action: Consumers should immediately take the balls away from children under the age of three. They should discard the ball or return both halves of the ball and the clip to a Burger King restaurant for a free order of small fries. Children can continue to use the Pokémon toy that came inside the ball.
incidents_text: On January 25, 2000, a 4-month-old boy in Indianapolis, Ind., reportedly suffocated when one-half of a Pokémon ball that was in his crib became stuck on his face. In December, a 13-month-old girl reportedly suffocated when one-half of a Pokémon ball covered her nose and mouth. Also in December, an 18-month-old girl nearly suffocated when a ball-half got stuck over her face. On the second attempt, the girl's father was able to pull the ball-half from her face.
sold_at: Burger King restaurants nationwide distributed the Pokémon balls inside Burger King big kids meals and regular kids meals from early November through December 1999.

product_name: Miniature skateboard keychains attached to Z.Z. Jamboarder teddy bears
heading: CPSC, Vermont Teddy Bear Co.® and Zany Brainy, Inc.® Announce Recall of Skateboard Keychains Sold With Teddy Bears
hazard_text: The skateboards' wheels can come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these skateboard keychains away from young children immediately, and return them to any Zany Brainy® store to receive a Zooolennium bean-filled plush baby animal toy. Consumers also can return the teddy bear and skateboard keychain set to receive a refund.
incidents_text: The firms are aware of two reports of wheels coming off these skateboards, but no injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Zany Brainy® sold the teddy bears with keychains nationwide through their stores, website and catalog from November 1999 through December 1999 for $10 to $13 with the purchase of $50 of other merchandise.

heading: CPSC, L.L. Bean Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Overalls
hazard_text: Snaps on these overalls can detach from the garments, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these overalls, and return them to L.L. Bean for a refund. For more information, call L.L. Bean at (800) 555-9717 anytime or go to their web site at www.llbean.com.
incidents_text: L.L. Bean has received six reports from consumers of these snaps detaching from the overalls. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: L.L. Bean sold these overalls nationwide in their catalogs and on their web site, and in L.L. Bean stores in Maine, New Hampshire, Delaware and Oregon from January through December 1999 for $20 to $26.

heading: CPSC, Nordstrom Inc. Announce Recall of Infant and Girls' Sweatshirts
hazard_text: Zipper pulls on these sweatshirts can detach from the garments, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop wearing these sweatshirts immediately, and return them to any Nordstrom store for a refund.
incidents_text: Nordstrom is aware of one incident in which an infant choked on the zipper pull, but suffered no permanent injuries.
sold_at: Nordstrom stores nationwide sold these sweatshirts in December 1999 for between $22 and $28.

hazard_text: Either half of the Pokemon ball can become stuck on a child's face, covering the nose and mouth and may cause suffocation of a child under three years of age.
action: Consumers should immediately take the balls away from children under the age of three. They should discard the ball or return both halves of the ball to a Burger King restaurant for a free small order of french fries. Consumers may continue to use the Pokemon toy that came inside the ball.
incidents_text: A 13-month-old girl reportedly suffocated when one-half of a Pokemon ball covered her nose and mouth. An 18-month-old girl reportedly also had a ball-half stuck over her face, causing her distress. However, the girl's father (on the second attempt) pulled the ball-half from her face.
sold_at: Burger King restaurants nationwide distributed the Pokemon balls inside Burger King Kids Club Meals and regular kids meals from early November through December, 1999.

heading: CPSC, Kelty Announce Recall to Repair Backpack Child Carriers
hazard_text: The seat height adjustment strap on these carriers can slip out of the buckle. A child can slide downward in the seat unexpectedly and could fall out of the carrier.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these backpack carriers, and contact Kelty for instructions on getting the free repair kit.
incidents_text: Kelty has received two reports of children slipping down inside the carriers after the height adjustment strap came loose. Neither child fell out of the carrier, and there were no reports of injury.
sold_at: Specialty and sporting good retailers, including L.L. Bean, REI and Eastern Mountain Sports, sold the recalled backpack carriers nationwide from March 1999 through December 1999 for between $100 and $250.

heading: CPSC, Safari Ltd. Announce Recall of Magnet Games
hazard_text: Paint on the magnets' metal figures contains amounts of lead that exceed federal standards for children's products. Prolonged exposure to high levels of lead presents a lead poisoning hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the metal figures from the magnetic base and discard them. Consumers should call Safari Ltd. for replacement metal figures at (800) 615-3111.
incidents_text: CPSC and Safari Ltd. are not aware of any injuries involving these products.

heading: CPSC, NHTSA and Kolcraft Announce Recall of Infant Car Seats/Carriers
hazard_text: When used as an infant carrier, the handle can unexpectedly move from the intended carrying position, causing the seat to suddenly rotate. The infant can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.
action: Kolcraft will provide, free of charge, an easy-to-install repair kit.
incidents_text: There have been more than 3,000 reports of handle-related problems, the majority of which report that the handle of the infant car seat/carrier unexpectedly moved from the intended use position, resulting in 42 injuries to infants. Some children were restrained in the carrier and others were not. These injuries range from a skull fracture and concussions to cuts, scrapes and bruises.
sold_at: Juvenile product, mass merchandise and major discount stores nationwide sold the car seat/carriers beginning in January 1993 for about $30 to $60 when sold alone, or $100 to $150 when sold with strollers.

product_name: Selecta wooden toys: "Quatrino" wooden shape sorter toys, "Sorting Box" shape sorter toys, "Favola" shape sorter toys, and "Kugelbahn" ball chute toys
heading: CPSC, Käthe Kruse Doll Co. Announce Recall of "Selecta" Wooden Toys
hazard_text: The balls included with these toys are banned because they present a serious risk of choking deaths to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund. Consumers who purchased the toys from a website should contact the website to make arrangements for returning the toys for a refund.
incidents_text: The CPSC and Käthe Kruse Doll Co. are not aware of any injuries involving the small balls contained in these toys.

product_name: Children's pajamas sold at Gap and Old Navy stores
heading: CPSC, Gap Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Pajamas
hazard_text: The pajama sets fail to meet federal children's sleepwear flammability standards. Failure to meet the flammability standards presents a risk of serious burns to children.
action: Parents and caregivers should immediately stop allowing children to wear these pajamas and return them to any Gap or Old Navy location for a refund and a $10 gift certificate.
incidents_text: Gap Inc. has not received any reports of injuries related to these pajama sets.
sold_at: GapKids, babyGap, Gap Outlet and Old Navy stores nationwide sold these pajamas from August 1999 through December 1999 for between $20 and $39.

heading: CPSC, Southern Exchange Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Camp Mess Kits
hazard_text: The mess kit's sauce pan handle does not lock into place and the mess kit's fry pan handle can bend during use, spilling hot foods or liquids onto consumers and causing serious burns.
action: Consumers should stop using the mess kit immediately and return it to the store where purchased for a refund or replacement mess kit.
incidents_text: CPSC and Texsport have received one report of a 10-year-old boy who received second-degree burns to his ankle when boiling water spilled from the saucepan he was using.
sold_at: Camping, mass merchandise and army surplus stores nationwide and in Puerto Rico sold the mess kit from May 1994 through September 1999 for about $3.

heading: CPSC, JumpSport Recalls Trampoline Safety Net Enclosures
hazard_text: The straps on the bottom of the net can break. Children can fall out under the net and off the trampoline and be injured.
action: Consumers should stop using the safety nets immediately and contact JumpSport toll-free at (888) 567-5867 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday. JumpSport will send consumers free replacement bottom straps.
incidents_text: JumpSport has received two reports of children falling off the trampoline when the straps on the bottom of the enclosure broke. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Costco, BJ's, Academy and Bradlees stores nationwide sold the safety nets from February 1999 to July 1999 for about $150 to $230.

heading: CPSC, Manufacturers Announce Recall to Replace Toy and Youth Basketball Nets
hazard_text: Children could strangle on loops or openings in nets that come unhooked from the rim or have knots that slide. If children put their heads into these openings, the net can get tangled around their necks.
action: Consumers should remove and throw away nets that can unhook or have knots that slide. Manufacturers will send consumers new nets that securely attach to the rim and do not have sliding knots. The basketball set can be used without a net until the new net arrives. Consumers should not return the product to stores.
incidents_text: Franklin Sports has received one report of a 3-year-old boy getting his head and neck caught in a basketball net. Huffy Sports and Lifetime Products have received no incident reports. No injuries have been reported.In December 1998, Fisher Price, Little Tikes, Ohio Art and Today's Kids recalled 10.1 million toy basketball sets to replace their nets. This recall followed 20 reports of children under 5 getting their heads and necks caught in the nets, including the death of an 18-month-old child.
sold_at: Toy, sporting goods, mass merchandise and discount department stores nationwide sold the basketball sets since 1993 for $13 to $40.

heading: CPSC, J.C. Penney Announce Recall of Boys Jackets
hazard_text: There are 7-inch drawstrings at the bottom of the jackets. Children could be dragged if the drawstrings catch in a vehicle's door, and suffer injury or death.
action: Consumers should stop using the jackets immediately. Either remove the drawstrings or return the jacket to the nearest J.C. Penney store for a full refund.
incidents_text: J.C. Penney is not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these jackets. Since 1991, CPSC knows of 6 deaths and 8 injuries to children from coat drawstrings catching in bus or car doors.
sold_at: J.C. Penney stores nationwide sold the jackets from June 1999 to November 1999 for about $30.

heading: CPSC Announces Multiple Play Yard Recalls Due to Strangulation Hazard
hazard_text: Toddlers can strangle in these playpens if pacifier strings or loose (or loosely woven) clothing catches on the playpens' protruding rivets.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these playpens and call the manufacturers at the numbers given above (except for the three companies out of business) to participate in the recall.Consumers with Pride Trimble Corp. play yards, Pride-Trimble Inc. play yards and Strolee play yards should destroy or discard these products. No remedy is available as these three companies are out of business.
remedy_type: Dispose, Refund, Repair, No Remedy Available
incidents_text: Since 1983, CPSC has received eight reports of toddlers who strangled in their playpens when pacifier strings or clothing they were wearing caught on the playpens' protruding rivets.

heading: Century Offers Cash Reward for Recalled Infant Swings Four strangulation deaths reported
hazard_text: The swings have shoulder harness straps that are placed over each shoulder and buckled between the infant's legs. If the straps on these swings loosen or are unbuckled, an infant can become tangled in the straps and strangle.
action: The repair program is no longer available. Parents and caregivers should immediately stop using these infant swings and discard or destroy the product.If you have one of these swings, however, Century is still offering the $30 cash reward to compensate for having to discard or destroy the product.
incidents_text: These swings were recalled in 1997 following reports of three deaths and one near strangulation from entanglement in the swings' shoulder harness straps. CPSC and Century have since become aware of a fourth death to an 8-month old infant girl in Texas.

heading: CPSC & Dynacraft Industries Recall Mountain Bikes
hazard_text: These bikes could have defective handlebar stems which will not tighten sufficiently to lock onto the bicycles. This can cause the front wheel not to turn properly, resulting in serious injuries to the rider from falls.
action: Consumers should stop riding these bikes immediately and take them to the Fred Meyer Store where purchased for a free inspection and repair, if needed.
incidents_text: Dynacraft Industries is not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these bicycles. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Fred Meyer Stores in Alaska, Arizona, Idaho, Oregon, Utah and Washington sold these bikes from December 1998 through August 18, 1999 for about $160.

heading: CPSC, Fairlong International Recall Extension Cords
hazard_text: The cords have undersized wires, incorrect ratings, lack overcurrent protection and allow polarize plugs to be incorrectly inserted into the receptacles. These cords present fire, shock and electrocution hazards to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled cords immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund. Consumers also can return the cords directly to the company for a refund, plus the cost of postage.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Wholesale and discount stores in the Chicago area, and a few stores in Indiana, Iowa, Michigan and Ohio, sold the cords from July 1997 through October 1999 for about $1 to $2.

product_name: "North West Blue" boys hooded jackets and sweatshirts
heading: CPSC & Montgomery Wards Recall Boys Jackets and Sweatshirts
hazard_text: The jackets and sweatshirts have hood drawstrings. Children can get entangled and strangle in the drawstrings that catch on playground equipment, fences or tree branches.
action: Stop wearing the jackets and sweatshirts. Either remove the drawstrings from the hood or discard or destroy these products.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Montgomery Ward stores nationwide sold the garments from August 1999 to October 1999 for about $20.

heading: CPSC & Penda New York Recall Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters do not have any child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Small stores and souvenir shops in the New York and Miami areas sold the lighters from January 1999 through July 1999 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Shine International Trading Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: The lighter's child-resistant mechanisms fail to meet the requirements of the Consumer Product Safety Act. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards. Additionally, the lighters can leak fuel and remain on after consumers have used them, which also presents fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Shine International Trading Co. Inc. have received three incident reports with these lighters. One incident involved two lighters that continued to burn after the consumer put them down, one involved two lighters that spontaneously blew apart while unattended, and one involved a lighter that burst into flames resulting in minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

heading: CPSC, Gateway Announce Recall of Foam Rubber Toy Cows
hazard_text: Small pieces of these foam rubber cows can tear away, posing a serious choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should either throw these cows away immediately or take them to any Gateway Country store location in exchange for another Gateway-brand item of comparable value.
incidents_text: Gateway has received three reports, by consumers in the U.S., of small pieces of these cows tearing away. There have been no reports of any injuries.
sold_at: Gateway stores distributed the cows from September 1997 through September 1999 as a give-away with a computer purchase. A small number were sold separately for about $4.

product_name: Toy flashlight included with Playmobil's Coastal Search and Rescue Boats toy set
heading: CPSC & Sonca Products Recall Toy Flashlights
hazard_text: The spring in the flashlight's battery compartment can dislodge, causing the batteries to overheat or leak. Children can suffer burns from the leaking battery.
action: Consumers should take the flashlight away from children immediately. Consumers should call Sonca at (800) 669-6394 between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. CT Monday through Friday for instructions on returning the flashlight for a $5 refund.
incidents_text: Sonca has received four reports from Europe of batteries overheating or leaking. There have been two reports of minor property damage and two minor injuries, including eye irritation and skin burns.
sold_at: Independent toy stores nationwide sold the toy set containing the recalled flashlight from July 1999 to September 1999 for about $40.

product_name: Precious Moments® Tender Tails® stuffed toys
heading: CPSC, Enesco Corp. Announce Recall of Pom-poms on Precious Moments® Tender Tails® Stuffed Toys
hazard_text: The pom-poms on these toys can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately cut off the pom-poms from these stuffed toys. Consumers should return the pom-poms along with their name, address and phone number to Enesco to receive a free toy.
incidents_text: CPSC and Enesco are aware of three reports of pom-poms detaching from these stuffed toys. No injuries were reported.
sold_at: Gift, card and collectible stores sold these stuffed toys nationwide from May 1998 through August 1999 for about $7.

product_name: Spray string sold under the names "Crazy Ribbon" and "Crazy String"
heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Flammable Spray String
hazard_text: These spray strings' propellant is extremely flammable, creating a serious risk of burn injuries when sprayed near an open flame, such as birthday candles. Flammable products intended for use by children are banned by federal law.
action: Consumers should take these spray strings away from children and stop using them immediately. It can be returned to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC is aware of at least one report of a burn injury resulting from the use of these spray strings. An 11-year-old boy suffered serious burns during his birthday party that left permanent scars.
sold_at: Party and hobby stores nationwide sold the spray string from October 1996 through July 1999 for between $2 and $4.

product_name: Acrobatic trapeze swings sold with Backyard Escapes, Backyard Products and WOW Wooden Play Centers brand gyms
heading: CPSC, Backyard Products Announce Recall of Trapeze Swings on Backyard Gyms
hazard_text: These trapeze swings have exposed bolts that cause serious lacerations to children.
action: Consumers should remove the trapeze swings from the gyms immediately and discard or destroy them. The firm is out of business and the repair program is no longer available. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: Backyard Products had received reports of six children suffering severe lacerations that required stitches to the arms from contact with the trapeze bolts. Injuries occurred when children dropped down from the overhead ladder, or fell or climbed onto the exposed bolts.
sold_at: Department, toy, discount, lumber and hardware stores nationwide, Including Toys "R" Us, Service Merchandise, Costco and Sears, sold the gyms with trapeze swings from December 1998 through July 1999 for between $250 to $450.

heading: CPSC, GUESS? Inc. Announce Recall of Liquid-Filled Bubble Patch Girls' T-Shirts
hazard_text: The liquid in the vinyl bubble patch contains a petroleum distillate. If the bubble patch is punctured or leaks, the petroleum distillate can be harmful if ingested.
action: Consumers should immediately stop wearing these t-shirts, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and GUESS? are not aware of any injuries involving these t- shirts.
sold_at: GUESS? Inc. and other clothing stores nationwide sold the t-shirts from June 1997 through March 1999 for $10 to $26, depending on the style.

product_name: Graco® and Children On The Go® brand Stroller Snack and Activity Trays, Bathtime Activity Trays, and Bathtime Toy Netting products
heading: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall to Repair Activity Trays and Bath Sets
hazard_text: The suction cups can detach, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these products immediately. To receive a free repair kit, consumers should call Graco at (800) 345-4109 anytime.
incidents_text: Graco has received four reports of children starting to choke after putting the suction cups in their mouths, including one that required use of the Heimlich maneuver.
sold_at: Discount, department and juvenile product stores nationwide, including Toys "R" Us and Sears, sold these activity trays and bath sets from January 1998 until August 1999 for about $10 to $15.

heading: CPSC, Bentley Lingerie Announce Recall of Girls' "Esleep Juniors" Robes
hazard_text: The robes fail to meet federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear. The standards require sleepwear, including robes, to be flame resistant, and if the garment ignites, the flame must self-extinguish. Failure to meet the flammability standards presents a risk of serious burn injuries to children.
action: Consumers should stop using these recalled robes immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and these firms are not aware of any injuries involving these robes.
sold_at: JC Penney stores nationwide sold these robes from July 1998 through April 1999 for about $25.

heading: CPSC, Tiger Electronics, Ltd. Announce Recall to Replace "Pooh Poppin' Piano" Toys
hazard_text: The green "leafy" top section of the carrot-shaped microphone attached to the piano toy can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Parents and caregivers should take these toys away from children immediately, and contact Tiger for instructions on returning it for a free replacement Pooh Poppin' Piano toy.
incidents_text: Tiger has received three reports of the leafy top of the microphone breaking off. There are no reports of injuries.

heading: CPSC, Toys "R" Us Announce Recall of "Bathtub Baby" Doll Sets
hazard_text: These doll sets come with a small ball, which poses a serious choking hazard to children under 3 years old.
action: Consumers are urged to take the doll sets away from young children immediately and return them to the stores where purchased for a full refund. For more information, consumers should call their local Toys "R" Us store, or visit the Toys "R" Us web site at www.toysrus.com/recalls/index.cfm.
incidents_text: CPSC and Toys "R" Us are not aware of any injuries involving these doll sets.
sold_at: Toys "R" Us stores nationwide sold these doll sets from October 1998 through July 1999 for about $2.

heading: CPSC, Shopko Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Infant Garments
hazard_text: The snaps can detach, posing a choking hazard to children.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these garments, and return them to Shopko for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Shopko Stores are not aware of any reports of injuries from these creepers.
sold_at: Shopko stores nationwide sold these garments from December 1998 to June 1999 for $4 to $6.

heading: CPSC, Little Me Announce Recall of Children's Garments with Ornamental Cherries
hazard_text: The attached ornamental cherries on these garments pose a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these garments, and should return them to Little Me for a refund and a voucher for a 30 percent rebate on a future Little Me purchase.
incidents_text: Little Me is aware of one incident in which a child started to choke on one of the ornamental cherries. It was pulled from the child's throat by the attached string.

heading: Ceiling Fans Recalled by Emerson Electric
hazard_text: Over time, the bracket holding the fan can fail, causing the fan to fall or hang by its electric wires. The fans can fall at any time, possibly causing injuries to bystanders. In addition, exposed wires could pose an electric shock hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the ceiling fans installed with these kits and have them repaired. To verify a fan is part of this recall, to receive a repair kit or for more information, consumers should call Air Comfort at (877) FAN KITS between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. EDT Monday through Friday, or go to their website at www.emerson.com.
incidents_text: Emerson Electric is aware of 15 reports of the brackets failing, causing the fans to fall. A 13-year-old boy suffered a laceration on the nose from a falling ceiling fan.
sold_at: Lighting showrooms, electrical distributors and hardware stores nationwide sold these kits from December 1984 through December 1989 for about $20.

product_name: Reebok Classic Leather Zip children's sneakers
heading: CPSC, Reebok Announce Recall of Children's Side Zip Sneakers
hazard_text: The sneaker's side pocket has a pull tab on the zipper that can be twisted off, presenting a choking and ingestion hazard to children.
action: Consumers should take the sneakers away from their children immediately and return the sneakers to the store where purchased for a refund or exchange.
incidents_text: CPSC and Reebok are not aware of any injuries from these sneakers.
sold_at: Family shoe, children's shoe, athletic and sporting goods stores nationwide sold the sneakers from September 1998 through June 1999 for about $32 to $40.

heading: CPSC, Bush Industries Inc. Announce Recall of Television Carts
hazard_text: The cart can tip over. If the cart tips and the television falls, children and adults can be injured.
action: Bush Industries will help consumers identify if their cart is part of this recall and send them a free repair kit. The repair kit will help prevent the cart from tipping over.
incidents_text: Bush Industries has received two reports of these carts tipping over and the television falling, resulting in one minor injury.
sold_at: Discount, home and furniture stores nationwide sold these television carts from June 1992 through August 1998 for about $60 to $100. The carts were sold ready-to-assemble.

heading: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall to Replace Spillproof Cup Lids
hazard_text: The flexible spout on the cup can tear between the slitted opening, causing a small piece of material to come loose, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Parents and caregivers should stop young children from using these cups immediately, and contact Playskool to get a free, redesigned lid. To request a replacement lid or for more information, call Playskool at (800) 752-9755 anytime, or go to their website at www.hasbro.com.
incidents_text: Playskool has received 115 reports of the spouts on these cups tearing. Six children reportedly had pieces in their mouths. There have been no reported injuries.
sold_at: Major retailers, including Walmart and Target, sold these cups nationwide from January 1998 through July 1999 for between $3 and $6.

product_name: Cosco Arriva and Turnabout infant car seats/carriers
heading: CPSC, NHTSA and Cosco Announce Recall of Infant Car Seats/Carriers
hazard_text: When used as an infant carrier, the handle locks on each side of the seat can unexpectedly release, causing the seat to flip forward. The infant can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.
action: Cosco will provide, free of charge, an easy-to-install repair kit. Check the label on the side of the product for the manufacturing date and one of the model numbers listed above. Contact Cosco toll-free at (800) 221-6736 between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. EDT M-F, or visit Cosco's website for a free repair kit or more information. Until you install the repair kit do not carry the seat by its handle, but by the head and foot of the seat. The seat can and should still be used as a car seat.
incidents_text: There have been 151 reports of the handle of the car seat/carrier unexpectedly releasing, resulting in 29 injuries to children. These reports include skull fractures, a broken arm, bumps to the head, black eyes, scrapes and bruises. According to the reports, some injuries occurred to children who were restrained in the seat.
sold_at: Juvenile product, mass merchandise and major discount stores nationwide sold the car seats/carriers beginning in March 1995 for about $29 to $59 when sold alone, or $89 to $139 when sold with strollers.

product_name: Gerber LIL' SPORT Spill Proof Sport Bottles
heading: CPSC, Gerber Announce Recall of LIL' SPORT Spill Proof Sport Bottles
hazard_text: A valve inside the cap can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Parents and caregivers should stop children from using these bottles immediately, and return the bottles to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: Gerber and CPSC have received over 30 reports of valves detaching, including three reports of valves found in children's mouths. There have been no reported injuries.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and grocery stores sold these bottles nationwide from February 1999 to July 1999 for about $4 (individually) to $8 (twin-pack).

heading: Toddler Jeans Recalled by Gymboree
hazard_text: The waist snap on the jeans can come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should return the jeans to a Gymboree store for a refund.
incidents_text: Gymboree has received one report of the snap coming off these jeans, but there have been no reports of injuries.
sold_at: Gymboree stores nationwide sold these jeans from March 1999 through June 1999 for about $19.

heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Recalls of Hairdryers and Toddler Jeans

product_name: Recalled Star Wars Darth MaulTM Double-Bladed Lightsaber and Qui-Gon JinnTM Lightsaber toys
heading: CPSC, Hasbro Announce Recall to Repair Star WarsTM LightsaberTM Toys
hazard_text: The spring in the battery compartments of these toys can dislodge, causing the batteries to overheat or rupture. This can cause burns to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using these Lightsabers immediately, and call Hasbro to get a free repair kit. The repair kit contains instructions on how to install a battery protector. To get this repair kit or for more information, consumers should call Hasbro at (800) 327-8264 anytime, or go to their website at www.hasbro.com. Consumers also can write to: Hasbro Lightsaber Repair Program, P.O. Box 200, Pawtucket, RI 02862.
incidents_text: Hasbro has received 38 reports of Lightsaber batteries overheating, including six reports of batteries rupturing. There are three reports of minor burns to consumers, and one consumer reported experiencing eye irritation.

product_name: Snugli® Front & Back PackTM soft infant carriers
heading: CPSC, Evenflo Company, Inc. and Hufco-Delaware, Inc. Announce Recall to Replace Soft Infant Carriers
hazard_text: Small infants can shift to one side, slip through the leg openings of these carriers and fall. Infants under 2 months of age are at greatest risk.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these carriers and call Evenflo at (800) 398-8636 anytime to receive instructions on how to exchange their carrier for a free, new carrier with smaller leg openings.
incidents_text: CPSC is aware of 13 reports of infants slipping through the leg openings of these carriers. One infant reportedly suffered a fractured skull and two infants received bruises in falls to the ground from the carrier.

heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Swimming Pool Dive Stick Recall Because of Impalement Risk to Children
hazard_text: In shallow water, children can fall or land on a dive stick and suffer rectal or vaginal impalement. Facial and eye injuries also are possible when children attempt to retrieve the sticks under water.
action: Depending on the sticks owned, consumers can receive a refund, replacement or repair. Florida Pool: Get repair kit at Wal-Mart. Poolmaster: Call (800) 854-1492 for a replacement. J&M Industries: Get a replacement stick at the store where purchased. All Others: Return to store where purchased for a refund or repair.
incidents_text: CPSC knows of six impalement injuries and one facial injury to children 6 to 9 years old. Although the number of reported incidents is relatively low, the severity of the injuries that have occurred is very significant. Three of the children suffered rectal and three suffered vaginal impalements from dive sticks placed in backyard pools or, in one case, a hot tub. In four of the six incidents, the injuries that occurred required surgery and hospitalization. The facial injury occurred when a child bobbed down to retrieve a dive stick and lacerated her face just below her eye, requiring stitches.
sold_at: These dive sticks have been sold at grocery, drug, pool and discount department stores nationwide for about $4 to $7 per set under numerous brand names, most of which do not appear on the dive stick itself.

heading: CPSC, Crate & Barrel Announce Recall to Repair Children's Table
hazard_text: These tables have a 6-inch hole cut in the center. Children can stick their heads into these holes and become stuck. Head entrapment can be painful and it can be difficult to free the child.
action: Consumers should stop using these tables until the repair is made. To prevent a head entrapment, Crate & Barrel will provide a free repair disc that will permanently close the hole.
incidents_text: Crate & Barrel has received four reports of children becoming entrapped in the table openings. Two children required emergency personnel to free them.
sold_at: The children's tables were sold in Crate & Barrel stores nationwide and through the Crate & Barrel 1998 Holiday catalog between September 1998 and February 1999 for about $75 for the table alone and $135 for the table and chair set.

heading: CPSC, Restoration Hardware Inc. Announce Recall of Stuffed Sock Monkeys
hazard_text: Sewing needles or pins have been found in the stuffing of these monkeys presenting a laceration hazard.
action: Consumers should return the monkeys to any Restoration Hardware store for a refund and a discount merchandise certificate.
incidents_text: CPSC and Restoration Hardware are aware of one injury when an 18-month old girl in Utah received a needle stick on her lip. Restoration Hardware has since found an additional 17 monkeys in store inventory containing needles or pins.
sold_at: Restoration Hardware's stores, catalogs and web site sold the monkeys from October 1997 through May 1999 for about $29.

product_name: Novelty lighters: shapes of telephone recorder, cell phone and Godzilla
heading: Lighters Recalled by ZNY Enterprises
hazard_text: The lighters do not have any child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Small retail and souvenir stores nationwide sold these lighters from January through April 1999 for about $2 to $6.

heading: Magic Doll Feeding Sets Recalled by Creative Designs
hazard_text: The nipple on the orange baby bottle separates, presenting a serious choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these recalled toys away from young children immediately and return the toys to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Toy and variety stores in California, Connecticut, Kentucky, New York, Washington and Puerto Rico sold the sets from January 1998 through December 1998 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Recalls of Toys and Lighters

product_name: Beanbags sold with Barney Hopscotch Game Towels
heading: CPSC, Franco Manufacturing Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Beanbags Sold With BarneyTM Hopscotch Game Towels
hazard_text: The seams on these beanbags can separate and allow plastic pellets to be released, presenting an aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these beanbags away from children immediately, and send them to Franco Manufacturing for a refund, including the cost of postage. Only the beanbags should be sent to Franco Manufacturing Co. Inc., ATTN: Consumer Relations, 555 Prospect St., Metuchen, NJ 08840.
incidents_text: CPSC and Franco Manufacturing are not aware of any injuries involving these beanbags.
sold_at: Ames, Meijers and Walmart stores sold the game towels nationwide from March 1999 through May 1999 for about $15.
