heading: Tonka(r) Toy Trucks Recalled by Isaac Morris
hazard_text: The toy trucks contain small parts, presenting a choking hazard to young children. Only trucks distributed with toddler T-shirts are being recalled because the trucks' small parts pose a choking hazard for children under age 3.
action: Consumers should take the toy away from young children immediately and contact Isaac Morris Ltd. at Hasbro to obtain a $1 refund for the toy's value and postage reimbursement.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: The trucks involved in this recall are those distributed with Isaac Morris' line of Tonka toddler T-shirts, sized 2T and 3T. The trucks were packaged separately, but attached to the T-shirts. Discount and toy stores nationwide sold the T-shirts with the trucks attached from November 1998 through March 1999 for about $10.

product_name: Novelty lighters in shape of Gun, Car, Radio, Animals, and Telephones
heading: Lighters Recalled by C & H Trading
hazard_text: The lighters do not have any child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund. Consumers who bought the lighters at the trade show can obtain a refund directly through the company.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Small retail stores in Louisiana, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, Texas and Washington sold the lighters from October 1998 through March 1999 for about $1 to $3. A November 1998 C & H trade show in Louisiana also sold the lighters.

heading: Stairway Gates Recalled by North States Industries
hazard_text: The locking mechanism can release when the gate is shaken and the gate will no longer act as the barrier it is intended to be. If the gate is placed at the top of stairs and the lock fails, a child could fall down the stairs and be injured.
action: Consumers should stop using these gates immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: North States Industries Inc. has received one report of a gate's locking mechanism failing. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Ames, Ann & Hope, Hambleton & Carr, and Value City department stores nationwide sold the gates from March through April 1999 for about $15.

heading: Infant Cardigans Recalled by Tommy Hilfiger
hazard_text: The cardigans' snaps can detach, presenting a choking hazard to infants.
action: Consumers should stop using these cardigans immediately, and call Tommy Hilfiger Consumer Relations Department toll-free at (877) TOMMYCARES any time to arrange for an exchange or full refund.
incidents_text: Tommy Hilfiger has received one report of a snap detaching from a cardigan. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: High-end department stores nationwide sold the cardigans from August 1998 through October 1998 for about $36.

heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Recalls of Infant Cardigans and Stereo Speakers
CPSC, E and I Inc. Announce Recall of Bungee Baby Bouncer
hazard_text: Knots tied in the black rope that supports the bouncer can unravel, causing the baby to fall.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using their Bungee Baby Bouncer, and return only the bungee assembly to E and I Inc. for a free repair. Consumers will be reimbursed postage charges. Consumers can send their bungee assembly to: E and I Inc., P.O. Box 66, Bancroft ID 83217-0066.
incidents_text: CPSC and E and I Inc. have received six reports of knots failing. In four of these incidents, babies bumped their heads from falls.
sold_at: Chelsea and Scott's One Step Ahead catalogs, and baby specialty retailers in Utah and Idaho sold the bouncers from September 1998 through March 1999 for between $35 and $40.

heading: CPSC, Sauder Woodworking Co. Announce Recall of Television Carts
hazard_text: The carts can tip over and injure children and adults when the cart and the television fall.
action: Consumers should remove their televisions and VCR's from the carts immediately and call Sauder. Sauder will help consumers identify if their cart is part of this recall, and send them a free repair kit. The repair kit will help prevent the cart from tipping over.
incidents_text: Sauder has received 13 reports of these carts tipping over and the television falling. Two injuries have been reported. A 3-year-old girl suffered a skull fracture, and an adult woman suffered a bump to the head and a cut finger.
sold_at: Discount stores, home centers and furniture stores nationwide sold these television carts from March 1989 through September 1998 for about $35 to $49. The carts were sold ready-to-assemble.

heading: CPSC, IKEA Announce Voluntary Recall of Wooden Stacking Ring Toys to Replace Top Red Ball Pieces
hazard_text: The red ball that tops this toy poses a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the red ball that tops this toy away from children immediately. Consumers can mail the ball to IKEA or take it to any IKEA store to receive a redesigned top piece. The red ball can be mailed to IKEA U.S. Inc., 496 West Germantown Pike, Plymouth Meeting, PA 19462. Postage costs will be reimbursed. Consumers also can return the stacking ring toy to any IKEA store for a refund.
incidents_text: IKEA has received one report of a 4-year-old boy in Europe choking to death on the top ball portion of the stacking ring toy. No other injuries have been reported.
sold_at: IKEA stores nationwide sold these stacking toys from October 1991 through April 1999 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Generation 2 Worldwide Announce Recall to Repair Pisces Baby Cribs
hazard_text: The slats on the headboards and footboards of these cribs can come loose, creating a large opening between the slats. CPSC standards limit the space between side rail slats to no more than 2 3/8 inches. Spacing larger than this enables an infant to become entrapped in the side rails, which can result in serious injury or death.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these recalled cribs and discard or destroy them. The firm is out of business and a remedy is no longer available.
incidents_text: Generation 2 Worldwide has received 12 reports of slats on these cribs coming loose. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Retail stores and juvenile furniture stores nationwide sold these cribs from March 1997 through December 1998 for about $199.

heading: Wooden Shape Sorter Toys Recalled by Zany Brainy
hazard_text: Wooden pegs from the shape sorters can break off, presenting a small parts choking hazard to children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the shape sorters away from children, and return them to any Zany Brainy store for a refund.
incidents_text: Zany Brainy is aware of one incident where a peg broke off one of these sorters. There have been no reports of injuries.
sold_at: Zany Brainy stores nationwide sold the sorters from October 1998 through March 1999 for about $18.

heading: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Wooden Shape Sorter Toys and Pistol Grip Soldering Guns
CPSC, Walgreen Co. Announce Recall of Kid's Sipper Bottles
hazard_text: The bottles' caps can be pulled off, creating a potential choking hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using these bottles immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Walgreen are not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these bottles. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Walgreens nationwide sold these bottles between March 1999 and April 1999 for $1.69 or two for $3.

heading: CPSC, Toro Co. Remind Consumers of Lawn-Boy Power Mower Recall
hazard_text: Interference with the mower's mulching fan can cause the mower blade to crack and break off. Broken pieces of the blade can be propelled from underneath the mower, possibly injuring the operator or a bystander.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these recalled mowers until they are repaired. Consumers with these recalled mowers can have the repair performed for free at their local Lawn-Boy service dealer.
incidents_text: Toro has received one report of a consumer who was struck on the ankle by a piece of a broken mower blade while mowing, resulting in a bruised tendon.
sold_at: Lawn-Boy Dealers and mass merchant retail outlets, including Sears, Lowe's and the Home Depot, sold these mowers from January 1997 through November 1998 for between $280 and $400.

heading: CPSC, L.L. Bean Inc. Announce Recall of Second Model of Backpack Child Carriers
hazard_text: Small children can work their way out of the harness and fall through a leg opening or topple out of the top of the carrier, which can cause head and body injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using both of these carriers immediately and call L.L. Bean at (800) 555-9717 anytime or visit its website at www.llbean.com/recall to receive instructions for returning the carrier for a refund or for any other information about these recalls.
incidents_text: L.L. Bean received 23 reports of children falling out of the harnesses of the model AC25 carriers by slipping through a leg opening or toppling out of the top of the carrier. It was reported that 10 of these children received injuries, including head bumps, bruises, abrasions and contusions. Four of these children became entangled by the harness straps around their necks.
sold_at: The L.L. Bean website and catalogs, and L.L. Bean retail stores in Maine, Oregon, New Hampshire and Delaware sold these carriers between January 1997 and October 1998 for about $99.

product_name: Novelty lighters: lamp and flying saucer
heading: CPSC, Kikkerland Designs Inc. Announce Recall of Novelty Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters do not have any child-resistant mechanisms, as required by the Consumer Product Safety Act. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting a fire hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Kikkerland Designs Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Small retail stores and souvenir shops nationwide sold these lighters from March 1997 through February 1999 for about $10.

product_name: Navy Velvet Baby Garments - cardigans, coveralls and long-sleeve tees
heading: Velvet Baby Garments Recalled by Spiegel Catalog
hazard_text: The metal snaps can come off of these baby clothing items, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these recalled baby clothes, and return them to a Spiegel Ultimate Outlet store for a refund.
incidents_text: Spiegel is aware of five customers returning these garments because of snaps coming off. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The garments' collar tags read "elements baby ... exclusively spiegel." Spiegel Ultimate Outlet stores, Spiegel Ultimate Outlet catalogs and elements exclusively Spiegel catalogs sold these garments from November 1998 through February 1999.

heading: CPSC & Firms Announce Recall of Velvet Baby Garments & Oster Hair Dryers
CPSC, Colorbök Announce Recall of Blue's CluesTM Toy Notebooks
hazard_text: The ends of the notebooks' coils can break off, presenting a small parts choking hazard to children.
action: Consumers immediately should take the notebooks away from children and call Colorbök anytime toll free at (800) 366-4660 to obtain a free replacement coil. Consumers should not return the notebooks to stores.
incidents_text: CPSC is aware of four incidents where the end piece of the coil broke off. In three of these incidents, the end piece was removed from the mouth of a child by a parent. There have been no reports of injuries.
sold_at: Chain and toy stores nationwide sold the notebooks from June 1998 through January 1999. The notebooks sold separately for about $5 and as part of an activity set that cost about $10.

heading: CPSC, Newco Announce Recall to Repair Bunk Bed Assembly Kits
hazard_text: Some kits did not include hardware or instructions for installing guardrails on the top bunk. A child could fall or become entrapped between the wall and the mattress if there are no guardrails on the top bunk. Other kits had incorrect assembly instructions for the guardrails, which caused spaces on the top bunk to be larger than 3.5 inches. This space could be large enough for a child's body to fall through, but small enough to entrap a child's head and possibly strangle.
action: Consumers should stop using any bunk bed assembled from this kit until they have repaired the bed. To receive the repair kit, which consists of instructions for properly placing guardrails on the top bunk and the necessary hardware, consumers should call Newco Inc. at (256) 997-5212.
sold_at: Menards, Payless Cashways, Cotter-Miller, and Woodworker's Supply stores mainly in the Midwest sold the kits from January 1994 through September 1998 for about $40.

heading: CPSC, Peg Perego Announce Recall of Children's Riding Vehicles
hazard_text: Pedals can stick and electrical components can overheat, presenting fire and injury hazards to children.
action: Consumers should remove the vehicles' batteries right away and not let children use the vehicles until the repair has been made. Consumers should contact Peg Perego at (800) 728-2108 to order a free repair kit, which can be installed by the consumer or by an authorized Peg Perego service center. Service centers will not have repair kits.
incidents_text: CPSC and Peg Perego have received about 320 reports of electrical components overheating or pedals sticking. Thirty fires have been reported, resulting in one child suffering second-degree burns to his hand and at least $55,000 in property damage. One child suffered a concussion and six children received bruises when accelerator pedals stuck and the vehicles hit trees, fences, walls or parked automobiles.
sold_at: Toy stores and retail catalogs sold the vehicles nationwide from 1990 through 1997 for about $100 to $550.

heading: CPSC, Safari Ltd. Announce Recall of Toy Puzzles
hazard_text: The puzzle has two shapes that are small parts, presenting a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these puzzles away from young children and return them to Safari Ltd. for either a refund or a replacement.
incidents_text: CPSC and Safari Ltd. are not aware of any complaints or injuries involving these puzzles.

heading: CPSC, Sanapac Co. Announce Recall of Dietary Supplements
hazard_text: The supplements being recalled are not packaged in child-resistant packaging as required under the Poison Prevention Packaging Act. If accidentally swallowed by children in toxic amounts, these supplements can cause serious injury or death.
action: Consumers should immediately return the products to the store where purchased for a refund or a child-resistant package.
incidents_text: CPSC and Sanapac Co. are not aware of any injuries involving these products.
sold_at: Pharmacies, health food, vitamin and grocery stores nationwide sold the supplements from January 1998 through December 1998 for about $6 to $20.

product_name: VeggieTales' Dave and the Giant Pickle playsets
heading: CPSC, Chariot Victor Publishing Announce Recall of VeggieTales' Dave and the Giant Pickle Playset
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: CPSC and Chariot Victor Publishing are aware of one report of a 2-year-old child found with a plug from the playset in his mouth. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Major Christian bookstores and catalog companies sold these playsets nationwide from September 1998 through February 1999 for about $20.

product_name: NIKE Little Air Jordan XIV infant shoes
heading: CPSC, NIKE Announce Recall of Infant's "Little Air Jordan" Sneakers
hazard_text: NIKE testing determined the red trim paint on these shoes contain amounts of lead that exceed Federal standards for children's products. Prolonged exposure to high levels of lead presents a poisoning hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the NIKE Little Air Jordan XIV shoes away from children and return them to the store where purchased to receive a substitute product or a store credit.
incidents_text: NIKE has received one consumer complaint regarding the shoe and possible ingestion of a paint chip.
sold_at: Major athletic shoe stores and department stores nationwide sold these shoes from January 1999 through March 1999 for about $40.

product_name: Mattresses sold with Cosco model "M" tubular metal cribs
heading: CPSC, Cosco Announce Recall to Replace Crib Mattresses
hazard_text: When a baby stands up in the crib, the mattress can compress and be pushed between the bars on the crib's platform. The baby can slip between the bars on the crib's platform and become entrapped.
action: Cosco is offering consumers a $25 check for consumers to purchase a new mattress on their own. Consumers should contact Cosco at (800) 221-6736 between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. EST Monday through Friday or at www.coscoinc.com to participate in this recall. Cosco will help consumers identify whether their cribs are involved in this recall. Once they get the new mattress, they should destroy the old mattress by cutting it into at least three pieces.
incidents_text: Cosco has received 12 complaints of mattresses compressing and entrapping babies. An 11-month old baby boy died after becoming entrapped.
sold_at: The mattresses were sold with Cosco model "M" tubular metal cribs, manufactured from July 1994 through September 1997.

product_name: Cosco GeobyTM Two WaysTM tandem stroller
heading: CPSC, Cosco Announce Recall to Repair Two WaysTM Tandem Strollers
hazard_text: The plastic locks on the folding mechanisms can break during use, causing the strollers to suddenly collapse. If strollers collapse, babies can suffer injuries from the fall, including head injuries from hitting concrete sidewalks. The child's arms, hands or fingers can be cut if they are on the locking mechanism when the stroller collapses.
action: Consumers should stop using the strollers immediately and call Cosco at (800) 221-6736 between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. EST Monday through Friday to receive the free repair kit, or go to their website at http://www.djgusa.com.
incidents_text: Cosco has received about 3,000 complaints of locks failing, which includes 250 reports of strollers unexpectedly collapsing. This resulted in more than 200 injuries to babies, including head injuries, a fractured forearm, finger and arm lacerations requiring stitches, and bumps, bruises and cuts.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and juvenile products stores nationwide sold these strollers for about $110 (model 01-644) and $170 (model 01-645).

heading: CPSC, KMC USA Inc. Announce Recall of Flammable Spray String
hazard_text: The product is hazardous if sprayed near an open flame due to the flammability of the propellant. Because it is a flammable product intended for use by children, it is a banned hazardous substance. Use of the spray string around flame sources, such as candles, could result in serious burns.
action: Consumers should take this spray string away from children and stop using it immediately. It can be returned to any Dollar Tree store for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC is aware of two reports of burns resulting from the use of this spray string. A 4-year-old boy that was burned when some of the string ignited while he was blowing out candles on his birthday cake. He suffered first- and second-degree burns on his face and arm. A woman sustained burns on her ear in another incident.
sold_at: "Dollar Tree," "Dollar Bills" and "Only $1" stores nationwide sold the spray string between October 1998 and January 1999 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Baby Swede, LLC Announce Recall to Repair "Baby Bjorn" Infant Carrier
hazard_text: Small infants can slip through the leg openings and fall. Infants that are under 2 months of age are at greatest risk.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these carriers for children under 2 months of age. All carriers need to be repaired. Baby Swede, LLC is offering consumers a free retrofit kit that, when attached to the carrier, will reduce the size of the leg openings.
sold_at: Juvenile specialty stores and mail-order catalogs nationwide sold these carriers from January 1991 through October 1998 for about $75.

heading: CPSC, Limited Too Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Fleece Robes
hazard_text: The robes fail to meet federal flammability standards for children's-sized sleepwear. The standards require sleepwear, including robes, to be flame resistant, and if the garment ignites, the flame must self-extinguish. Failure to meet the flammability standards presents a risk of serious burn injuries to children.
action: Parents should immediately stop their children from wearing these robes. Return these robes to any Limited Too store for a refund of the full retail price or exchange.
incidents_text: Limited Too has not received any reports of injuries from these robes.
sold_at: Limited Too stores nationwide sold the robes from September 1998 through December 1998 for between $60 and $64.

heading: CPSC, Elegant Headwear Co. Announce Recall to Repair Infant and Toddler Hats
hazard_text: The hats have a one-piece chin strap. These one-piece chin straps can lead to strangulation if they get caught on playground equipment, riding toys or other catch points.
action: Consumers should cut the one-piece chin straps on the infant and toddler hats in half.
incidents_text: CPSC and Elegant Headwear Co. are not aware of any injuries associated with these hats.
sold_at: Mass merchandisers and discount stores sold the infant and toddler hats from 1985 through 1998 for about $2 to $4.

heading: CPSC, Emerson Electric Co. Announce Recall to Repair Ceiling Fans
hazard_text: Over time, the bracket holding the fan can fail, causing the fan to fall or hang by its electric wires. The fans can fall at any time, possibly causing injuries to bystanders. In addition, exposed wires could pose an electrical shock hazard.
action: Air Comfort will arrange to help consumers identify if their ceiling fans are part of this recall and provide installation if needed. Consumers should immediately stop using the ceiling fans installed with these kits and have them repaired.
incidents_text: Emerson Electric is aware of 12 reports of the brackets failing, causing the fans to fall. A 13-year-old boy suffered a laceration on the nose from a falling ceiling fan.
sold_at: Lighting showrooms, electrical distributors and hardware stores sold these ceiling fan kits from December 1984 through December 1989 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Toro Co. Announce Recall of Lawn-Boy Power Mowers
hazard_text: Interference with the mower's mulching fan can cause the mower blade to crack and break off. Broken pieces of the blade can be propelled from underneath the mower, possibly injuring the operator or a bystander.
action: Consumers should stop using these recalled mowers immediately. The company is mailing consumers free repair kits which include a new mower blade and modified mulching fan. Consumers can have the repair performed for free at a local Lawn-Boy service dealer after receiving the repair kit. Consumers who sent in their mower's registration card will automatically be mailed a repair kit. Consumers who have not been notified should contact their local Lawn-Boy service dealer for assistance.
incidents_text: Toro has received one report of a consumer who was struck on the ankle by a piece of a broken mower blade while mowing, resulting in a bruised tendon.
sold_at: Lawn-Boy Dealers and mass merchant retail outlets, including Sears, Lowe's and the Home Depot, sold these mowers from January 1997 through November 1998 for between $280 and $400.

product_name: First Alert True Fit safety gates
heading: CPSC, BRK Announce Recall of First Alert True Fit Safety Gates
hazard_text: Plastic parts of the gate can break off into small pieces, creating a potential choking hazard to young children. In some cases, when parts break off, the gate will no longer be secure.
action: Consumers should stop using these gates immediately and call BRK toll-free at (888) 777-5599 (available 24 hours a day) to obtain a refund.
incidents_text: BRK has received more than one thousand reports of plastic parts including bumpers, hinges, and parts of the handle breaking, sometimes into small pieces. BRK has received six reports of children having broken pieces in their mouths. No choking incidents were reported.
sold_at: Toys R Us, Hills and other stores sold the gates nationwide beginning in October 1996 for about $35.

heading: CPSC, American Hua Mao Enterprises Announce Recall of Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: These cigarette lighters, which operate with push-button electronic ignition mechanisms to produce the flame, have child-resistant mechanisms that do not work. Young children could ignite the lighters.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these cigarette lighters and return them to the store where they were purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and American Hua Mao Enterprises are not aware of any injuries involving these lighters.
sold_at: Small retail stores and souvenir shops in New York and Maryland sold these lighters from March 1997 through November 1998 for about $4 to $6.

heading: CPSC, Toy Manufacturers Announce Recall to Replace Toy Basketball Nets
hazard_text: Children could strangle on loops or openings in the nets that come unhooked from the rim, or have knots that slide. If children put their heads into these openings, the net can get tangled around their necks.
action: Consumers should remove and throw away nets that can unhook or have knots that slide, and call the manufacturer. However, one of the manufacturers, Today's Kids, is out of business and a replacement part is no longer available, so either that set should either be used without the net, or that set should be discarded or destroyed. Consumers should have the manufacturer's name and model on hand before calling the other manufacturers, who will send consumers new nets that securely attach to the rim, and do not have sliding knots. The basketball set can be used without a net until the new net arrives. Consumers should not return the product to retailers.
incidents_text: Since 1988, CPSC and the manufacturers have received 20 reports of children under 5 years old getting their heads and necks caught in the nets of toy basketball sets. In 1992, an 18-month-old child died after becoming entangled in a partly unhooked net.
sold_at: Toy stores nationwide sold the toy basketball sets for about $10 to $50. While most have been sold since 1988, some were sold as early as 1976.

product_name: Garden Play Yard Pals crib and play yard rail toys
heading: CPSC, Summer Infant Products Inc. Announce Recall of Crib Rail Toys
hazard_text: The plastic flower toy stem on this toy can break when bent, creating a sharp edge hazard for young children, and possibly causing cuts or puncture injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using the Garden Play Yard Pals immediately and contact Summer Infant Products to get a replacement product or refund.
incidents_text: Summer Infant Products, Inc. has received three reports of flower stem breaking. There have been no reported injuries.
sold_at: Retail and specialty stores, including Babies R Us, Ross Stores, TJ Maxx, and Value City, sold the toy from February 1998 through November 1998 for approximately $12.

product_name: L.L. Bean backpack child carriers, model number AC25
heading: CPSC, L.L. Bean Inc. Announces Recall of Backpack Child Carriers
hazard_text: Small children can become entangled in the carrier's harness,which poses a strangulation risk. Also, small children can work their way out of the harness and fall through a leg opening or topple out of the top of the carrier, which can cause head and body injuries.
action: Consumers should stop using the carriers immediately and call L.L. Bean at (800) 555-9717 anytime to receive instructions for returning the carrier for a refund or for any other information about this recall.
incidents_text: L.L. Bean has received 23 reports of children falling out of the harnesses by slipping through a leg opening or toppling out of the top of the carrier. It was reported that 8* of these children received injuries, including head bumps, bruises, abrasions and contusions and four of these children became entangled by the harness straps around their necks.
sold_at: The L.L. Bean website and catalogs, and L.L. Bean retail stores in Maine, Oregon, New Hampshire and Delaware sold the carriers between January 1997 and October 1998 for about $99.

heading: CPSC, IRIS U.S.A. Announce Recall of Plastic Toy Storage Chests
hazard_text: These chests, that were originally marketed for the storage of toys, lack a lid-support device, do not have adequate ventilation when the lid is closed, and have latches that secure the lids. Children could become entrapped and suffocate inside the chests.
action: Consumers should immediately prevent children from having access to these chests, and stop using them for toy storage. Consumers in households with young children can return the chests to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and IRIS U.S.A. are not aware of any injuries involving these chests.
sold_at: Retail and department stores, such as Target, sold these chests nationwide since January 1996 for about $25.

heading: CPSC, Rubbermaid Inc. Announce Recall of Icy RiderTM Toboggan
hazard_text: The flexible, bowed front of the toboggan can break away while in use, causing loss of control and injury.
action: Consumers should stop using these toboggans immediately. To make arrangements to get a replacement toboggan with a reinforced bowed front, contact Rubbermaid at (330) 264-6464, ext. 2500 between 9 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.
incidents_text: Rubbermaid is aware of six reports of the fronts of these toboggans breaking off, resulting in two injuries. These injuries were a broken leg suffered by an adult, and facial bruises and lacerations suffered by a 4-year-old girl when the broken piece hit her in the face.
sold_at: Toy and warehouse club stores nationwide, including Toys R Us, Sam's Club and BJ Warehouse Clubs, sold these toboggans beginning in September 1997 for about $50.

heading: Kolcraft, Playskool Double Reward for Return of Recalled Portable Cribs
hazard_text: The cribs have rotating top rail hinges. These top rails can collapse, entrapping children and suffocating them. In all, six children have died in Playskool Travel-Lite portable cribs.
action: Consumers who own these cribs should stop using them immediately. Anyone who sees one in a day care center, at a baby-sitters, in the home of a friend or relative, or at a garage sale or secondhand store, should inform the caregiver or seller about the recall and reward. For instructions on how to return the crib and receive a $120 Child Saver Reward, call Kolcraft at (800) 453-7673.
incidents_text: The crib's top rails can collapse, entrapping children and suffocating them. In all, six children have died in Playskool Travel-Lite portable cribs.

heading: "Henry" Gym Sets Recalled by Menard
hazard_text: If assembled incorrectly, the glider support tube on these gym sets could bend or break, causing the riders to fall or be thrown from the glider.
action: Consumers should not allow children to ride on the gym set glider until they check if their gym set is assembled correctly. To determine this and to receive revised assembly instructions, consumers should call Menard Inc. toll-free at (888) 215-3349 anytime.
incidents_text: A three-year-old boy was thrown to the ground when the support tube on the gym set broke. He did not suffer any injuries.
sold_at: The 18 Menard retail stores in the North Central region of the U.S. sold these gym sets from July 1991 through August 1998 for about $50.

heading: Bedside Cradles Recalled by W.C. Redmon
hazard_text: The legs on the cradles can become loose and can separate, causing the cradle to tip.
action: Consumers should stop using the Cuddle Me Close cradle immediately and call Redmon collect at (765) 473-6683 Monday through Friday between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. EST for free replacement legs.
incidents_text: Redmon has received about 50 reports of the cradles' legs becoming loose or separating, including two reports of cradles tipping. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Infant product catalogs, including One Step Ahead and Popular Club, and juvenile product stores, including Babies R Us and several small independent stores, sold the cradles nationwide for about $149 beginning in February 1998.

heading: Bedside Cradles and "Henry" Gym Sets Recalls
CPSC, Manufacturers Announce Recall of Wooden Bunk Beds
hazard_text: The beds have spaces on the top bunk that present potential entrapment and strangulation hazards to young children. The spaces can be large enough for a child's body to pass through, but small enough to entrap a child's head.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled beds immediately and call the company for a replacement guardrail, retrofit kit or instructions that will eliminate the potential entrapment hazard.
incidents_text: CPSC is not aware of any deaths associated with the beds being recalled by these five manufacturers. However, since 1990, 39 children have died from becoming entrapped in wooden or metal bunk beds with similar spaces on the top bunk. Thirty-seven of those children were 3 years old or younger. Since 1994, more than half a million hazardous bunk beds have been recalled.
sold_at: The recalled beds were sold through flea markets and in specialty and furniture stores, including Workbench furniture store.

product_name: Children's vampire capes and witch brooms
heading: CPSC, Rubie's Costume Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Vampire Capes and Witch Brooms
hazard_text: The capes and the brooms, which fail to meet federal mandatory standards for flammability, could ignite readily and present a serious risk of burn injuries to children.
action: Consumers should not let their children wear the vampire capes or use the 27-inch witch brooms this Halloween. Consumers should return the products to the stores where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Rubie's Costume Co. Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these capes or brooms.
sold_at: Toy, party, costume, discount and drug stores nationwide sold the capes and brooms for about $2 each from September 1997 to October 1998.

heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall to Repair Power Wheels Ride-On Battery-Powered Vehicles
hazard_text: CPSC and Fisher-Price have received approximately 700 reports of electrical components failing and overheating while the cars and trucks were being ridden, charged, parked or stored.
action: Consumers should remove the vehicles' batteries right away and not let children use these Power Wheels vehicles. The firm will be providing pro-rated refunds based on the age of the recalled products.
incidents_text: CPSC and Fisher-Price have received approximately 700 reports of electrical components failing and overheating while the cars and trucks were being ridden, charged, parked or stored. About 150 fires have been reported. Nine children suffered minor burns to the hands, legs, or feet; and up to $300,000 in property damage to 22 houses and garages have been reported. There have also been 71 reports of vehicles not stopping. Six children suffered bruises, scratches or bumps when their vehicles hit a car, truck, pole, window or fence.
sold_at: Toy and mass merchandise stores nationwide sold the cars and trucks since 1984 for about $70 to $300.

heading: Bi-fold Doors Repair by Schweiss Distributing
hazard_text: The doors lack a safety shield which could allow door operators and bystanders to become entrapped in moving door parts, such as the drive drums and cables, causing serious injuries such as amputations and fractures.
action: Schweiss is offering a free safety shield to help prevent further injuries. To receive a shield, consumers should immediately call Schweiss Distributing Co. at (800) 746-8273 any time. Until the safety shield is installed, consumers should use extreme caution when operating the doors.
incidents_text: CPSC and Schweiss are aware of three injuries involving these doors. All the injuries involved children having fingers amputated, with one child having six fingers amputated and both arms broken.
sold_at: Home improvement stores, lumber yards and custom builders nationwide sold these bi-fold doors from January 1984 to August 1993 for between $800 and $4,500, depending on the size of the door.

heading: Stuffed Animal Recalled by Great American Toy Co.
hazard_text: The crab's antennas have sharp wires, presenting a puncture wound hazard to children.
action: Stop using the stuffed crabs immediately, and return them to: Great American Toy Co. Inc., 22A Sintsink Drive East, Port Washington, N.Y. 11050. The company will provide consumers with either a refund or replacement toy.
incidents_text: None reported.
sold_at: Traveling fairs and carnivals gave the crab toys away as prizes from March 1998 to July 1998. The toy has a retail value of about $1 to $27, depending on the size of the stuffed crab.

product_name: Individually sold xylophones, Little Ones® Infant three-piece musical gift sets, and Little Ones® Infant five-piece musical gift sets
heading: CPSC, Playwell Toy Announce Recall of Xylophone Mallets
hazard_text: The rounded ends of the xylophone mallets are smaller in diameter than the 1.75-inch standard for small balls. The mallets can get stuck in the throats of young children, blocking their airways, and possibly causing death.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
units: Approximately 200,000 individually sold xylophones, 150,000 Little Ones® Infant three-piece musical gift sets, and 1,800 Little Ones® Infant five-piece musical gift sets
incidents_text: CPSC and Playwell Toy were aware of one serious injury to a 6-month-old baby girl who suffered severe brain damage when the mallet became lodged in her throat.
sold_at: Target and other retail stores sold the individual xylophones from February 1996 to April 1998 for about $7. Kmart stores nationwide sold the three-piece musical set exclusively from May 1996 to April 1998 for about $10. Right Start Stores nationwide sold the five-piece musical gift set from November 1997 to August 1998 for about $24.

heading: CPSC, Deckers Outdoor Corp. Announce Recall of Children's Teva Sandals
hazard_text: The straps attached to the footbed of the sandals can come apart. This can cause falls.
action: Consumers should stop using these sandals immediately. To get information on obtaining a refund, contact Deckers at (800) 781-9928 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. PDT Monday through Friday.
incidents_text: Deckers is aware of a 2-year-old who reportedly fell when one of the sandals he was wearing came apart, injuring his lip, gum and tooth.
sold_at: Shoe retailers sold these sandals nationwide from December 1997 through August 1998 for about $25.

heading: CPSC, Kmart Corp. Announce Recall of Inflatable Baby Floats
hazard_text: The seat of the pool toy can tear at the seam causing children to unexpectedly fall into the water and possibly drown.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these baby floats, and return them to their nearest Kmart store for a refund.
incidents_text: Kmart has received one report of the float's seat tearing and causing a child to fall into the water. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Kmart stores nationwide sold the kiddie floats from September 1996 through August 1998 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Atico International USA Inc. Announce Recall of Pacifiers Sold at Bath & Body Works
hazard_text: The nipples on these pacifiers could separate from the base, posing a choking hazard to children.
action: The firm is out of business, the remedy is no longer available, and the product should be discarded or destroyed.
incidents_text: CPSC and Atico are not aware of any injuries involving these pacifiers.
sold_at: Bath & Body Works stores nationwide sold the pacifiers in the gift set and the pacifier with clip between June 1998 and September 1998. The diaper bag gift set sold for about $28 and the pacifier with clip sold for about $4.

heading: CPSC, TV Guard Inc. Announce Recall to Repair TV Guards
hazard_text: Children can tip the television over onto themselves by pulling on the TV Guard, and sustain bodily injury.
action: Consumers should immediately remove the guard from the television and call the company's 24-hour toll-free hotline at (877) TVGUARD. Consumers will receive a free, low-skid pad for use with TV Guard, to help prevent the television set from tipping.
incidents_text: TV Guard Inc. has received three reports of young children suffering injuries when they pulled on the guard and the television fell on top of them. A broken leg, a severely bruised pelvic area, and facial cuts along with a bruised leg and foot have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile catalogs and juvenile product stores nationwide sold the TV Guard from April 1993 to September 1998 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall to Repair Stationary Entertainers
hazard_text: The screw securing the clicker toy to the Entertainer's tray can come out, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should remove the clicker toy from the Entertainer immediately. To receive the free repair kit, consumers should call Graco at (800) 345-4109 anytime or write to Customer Affairs, Graco Children's Products Inc., P.O. Box 100, Elverson, PA 19520.
incidents_text: CPSC and Graco have received eight reports of children rotating the toy until the screw came out, and either handling the toy's screw or placing it in their mouths. One child started choking on the screw and sustained scratches in the throat, and two others sustained scratches on the face or stomach.
sold_at: Discount, department and juvenile product stores nationwide, including Toys R Us and Sears, sold the Entertainers from April 1998 to September 1998 for about $59 to $69.

heading: CPSC, Limited Too Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Satin Sleepwear
hazard_text: The pajamas fail to meet federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear. The standards require sleepwear to be flame resistant, and if the fabric ignites, the flame must self-extinguish. Failure to meet the flammability standards presents a risk of serious burn injuries to children.
action: Parents should immediately stop their children from wearing these pajama sets and return them to a Limited Too store for a full refund.
incidents_text: Limited Too has not received any reports of injuries from these pajama sets.
sold_at: Limited Too stores nationwide sold the pajamas from December 1995 through July 1998 for about $15 to $39.

heading: CPSC, Evenflo Co. Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Child Carriers
hazard_text: Small children can slip sideways into the leg openings, creating a potential strangulation risk.
action: Evenflo is offering a free seat insert to reduce the size of the leg openings and provide a more secure fit. Consumers should stop using the carriers immediately and call Evenflo at (800) 649-0071 anytime to receive the free seat insert.
incidents_text: Evenflo has received 16 reports of children slipping into the leg openings, with some reports of red marks on the child's neck. No serious injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile product stores nationwide sold these carriers from June 1996 through June 1998 for about $65.

heading: CPSC, PJ Toys Announce Recall of Children's Furniture Sold at Target
hazard_text: Some of the paint on this furniture contains lead, which is toxic if ingested by children. High levels of lead in paint violate the Consumer Product Safety Act.
action: Consumers should take these items away from young children immediately and return them to any Target store for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and PJ Toys are not aware of any illnesses or injuries involving this furniture.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide sold the recalled furniture from April 1998 through July 1998 for between about $15 and $80, depending on the item.

heading: CPSC, Century Announced Recall to Repair Fold-N-Go® Care Centers
hazard_text: The care center's bassinet could have loose fabric, which can create a pocket near the floorboard in which an infant can become entrapped and suffocate.
action: The repair is no longer available. Consumers should destroy the product.
incidents_text: Century has received four reports of babies getting their head caught between the bassinet's mesh side and floorboard, including one child who reportedly required overnight hospitalization.
sold_at: Juvenile product stores nationwide sold these care centers from March 1998 through August 1998 for about $100 to $130.

heading: CPSC, Tara Toy Corp. Announce Recall of Flying Dolls
hazard_text: During use, the wings of these flying dolls can break off, causing serious injuries to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using the dolls immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Tara Toy Corp. have received four reports of the doll's wing breaking off during use. Two children suffered serious eye injuries, including a shattered iris and cataract development that required an artificial lens, and resulted in partial loss of sight. A cut under the eye and a broken front tooth also have resulted.
sold_at: Toy stores nationwide sold the dolls from April 1995 through December 1997 for about $7.

heading: CPSC, MacKenzie-Childs Ltd. Announce Recall of Paper Candle Shades
hazard_text: Use of the paper shade with a candle presents a fire hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the paper shades with candles. Consumers should return the original paper shade to the store where purchased to receive a free, replacement paper shade that is fire-resistant.
incidents_text: MacKenzie-Childs has received three reports of the paper shades igniting after contacting the flame of the accompanying candle. There is one report of minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty gift and department stores nationwide sold the paper shades from January 1992 through April 1998 for about $38 to $95.

heading: In Wake of Another Death, CPSC Again Urges Search for Previously Recalled Portable Cribs and Play Yards
hazard_text: The top rails can collapse, entrapping children and suffocating them. Thirteen children have died from suffocation in collapsed play yards and portable cribs manufactured by various firms.
action: Kolcraft is offering $60 to consumers for the return of each Travel-Lite portable crib. Consumers with Playskool Travel-Lite cribs should call Kolcraft at (800) 453-7673 for instructions on receiving the refund and disposing of the products.
incidents_text: According to the Asbury Park Press newspaper, a 10-month-old New Jersey infant died on Wednesday after becoming trapped in a collapsed Playskool Travel-Lite portable crib. CPSC issued this same warning in June, following the death of a 17-month-old Chicago toddler in the Playskool Travel-Lite portable crib.

heading: CPSC, Lexington Furniture Announce Recall of Wooden Bunk Beds
hazard_text: If the top bunk bed is mis-assembled, there could be a space between the end of the mattress and the end of the bed on the top bunk. This space could be large enough for a child's body to fall through, but small enough to entrap a child's head.
action: Consumers should inspect the top bunk to determine whether a space of 3-1/2 inches or more exists between the end of the mattress and the end of the bed. If such a space exists, consumers should stop using the bed and call Lexington for a free modification kit to close the gap.
incidents_text: Lexington Furniture has received one report of a child falling through the space between the end of the mattress and the end of the bed when set up as a twin bed. No injury was reported.
sold_at: The beds were sold in furniture stores and department stores with furniture departments nationwide from January 1980 through August 1997 for approximately $200 to $1,200.

heading: CPSC, Pyramid Accessories Inc. Announces Recall of "Mulan" Backpacks and Rolling Luggage
hazard_text: The backpacks' and rolling luggage's artwork contains paint with high levels of lead, which is toxic if ingested by children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these items away from children and return them to the place of purchase for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Pyramid Accessories are not aware of any illnesses or injuries involving these products.
sold_at: Retail stores nationwide sold these items from June 1998 through July 1998. The backpacks sold for about $12 and $14, and the luggage sold for about $25 to $30.

heading: CPSC, Kmart Corp. Announce Recall of Inflatable Kiddie Boats
hazard_text: The seat of these pool toys can tear, causing small children to unexpectedly fall into the water and possibly drown.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these kiddie boats, and return them to their nearest Kmart store for a refund.
incidents_text: Kmart has received four reports of the boat's seats tearing and causing children to fall into the water. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Kmart stores nationwide sold the kiddie boats from September 1996 through July 1998 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Almar Sales Co. Announce Recall of Children's Jewelry Sets
hazard_text: The necklaces and bracelets involved in this recall can break, releasing small plastic beads that pose potential choking and aspiration hazards to young children.
action: Consumers should take the recalled jewelry away from children immediately, and return them to the store where purchased or directly to Almar Sales Co., 17 West 37th St., New York, NY 10018 for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Almar Sales are not aware of any injuries involving these jewelry sets.
sold_at: Toy and novelty stores nationwide sold the jewelry sets from January 1994 through June 1998 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Crate & Barrel Announce Recall to Repair Toy Chests
hazard_text: The toy chest's lid support can fail, allowing the lid to fall onto a child's head or neck. A child could become entrapped at the neck and strangle.
action: Consumers should immediately stop young children from using the toy chests, and call Crate & Barrel at (800) 352-0688 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. CDT Monday through Friday. Crate & Barrel will provide a new lid support, free of charge, to stop the lid from falling to prevent a child from being injured or fatally trapped. Consumers can make this repair easily using a regular screwdriver.
incidents_text: CPSC and Crate & Barrel have received two reports of lids falling. In one instance, a lid fell onto a woman's head, causing her chin to strike the front edge of the chest. Through their retail stores, Crate & Barrel has received about 116 consumer requests for replacement lid supports.
sold_at: Crate & Barrel stores and catalogs sold the toy chests nationwide from September 1994 through March 1998 for about $130.

heading: CPSC, Warns That Old Servel Gas Refrigerators Still In Use Can Be Deadly
hazard_text: There have been at least 39 incidents in the U.S. involving these old Servel gas refrigerators, causing 22 carbon monoxide-related deaths and 55 injuries nationwide. There also have been incidents reported in Ontario, Canada, causing 60 deaths.
action: Consumers can call the Servel Corrective Action Committee (SCAC) toll free at (800) 782-7431 anytime to receive a rebate package that includes instructions for disposing of their Servel gas refrigerator. Consumers who properly dispose of their old Servels will receive a $100 rebate plus reimbursement for reasonable disposal costs.
incidents_text: There have been at least 39 incidents in the U.S. involving these old Servel gas refrigerators, causing 22 carbon monoxide-related deaths and 55 injuries nationwide. There also have been incidents reported in Ontario, Canada, causing 60 deaths.

heading: CPSC, AMF Bowling Products Announce Recall to Repair or Replace Bowling Ball Returns
hazard_text: Consumers' fingers can become entrapped and injured in the ball return's belt.
action: For AMF-owned establishments, AMF will install plastic guards on either side of the Sure-Pik ball returns to raise the sides around the moving belt. Large warning labels will be placed on the guards. These labels are colorful pictographs warning children to keep their hands and fingers out of the ball return. For non-AMF-owned establishments, AMF will offer each owner the option of either obtaining the repair kit at cost, plus shipping and handling, or receiving a trade-in allowance of $900 toward the purchase of a new AMF C-90 ball return. AMF also will make special lease financing available for qualified owners.
incidents_text: CPSC and AMF have received 14 reports of children's fingers becoming entrapped in these ball returns. Injuries range from bruises and lacerations, to partial amputations and fractures.

heading: CPSC, T.S. Toys Announce Recall of Activity Block Sets
hazard_text: Rods on one of the blocks could break, releasing small hollow cylinders. Young children could choke on these cylinders.
action: Consumers should take the recalled toys away from children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and T.S. Toys are not aware of any injuries involving these toys.
sold_at: Meijer, Ocean State Job Lot, Johnny's Toys and Cook Brothers stores in the East and Midwest sold the Activity Blocks from May 1997 to June 1998 for about $7 to $8.

product_name: Animal squeeze toys (gopher, penguin, rabbit, tiger, bear and mouse) and jet fighter toy
heading: CPSC, In-Mar Trading Inc. Announce Recall of Jet Fighter Toy and Various Squeak Toys
hazard_text: The squeeze toys that are part of this recall each contain a squeaker, and the jet fighter toy contains small parts, all of which can become separated from the toy. These small parts present a choking hazard to young children, and in some cases, an aspiration hazard which could result in death.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately and return the toy to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and In-Mar are not aware of any injuries involving these toys.
sold_at: The toys were sold in various discount stores in Puerto Rico. The squeeze toys were sold from January 1997 through June 1998, and the jet fighter toys were sold from December 1996 through June 1998. All the toys sold for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Laiko International Announce Recall of Knock-A-Block Wooden Toy
hazard_text: The balls in this toy are less than 1.75 inches in diameter, which poses a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Laiko International Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving this toy.
sold_at: Toy stores and other small retail stores nationwide sold these wooden toys from August 1997 to June 1998 for about $10.

heading: CPSC, Michael Friedman Corp. Announce Recall of Rattles
hazard_text: Small parts can break off of the rattles, presenting choking and aspiration hazards to infants.
action: Consumers should take the rattles away from infants immediately and discard or destroy them, or if possible, return the rattles to the store where purchased for a refund. However, the firm, Michael Friedman Corp., is out of business and cannot be contacted.
incidents_text: CPSC has received one report of a rattle separating and releasing small plastic balls from inside. No injury was reported.

heading: CPSC, STK International Announce Recall of Baby Rattles
hazard_text: The handles of these rattles could present a serious choking hazard to infants and young children. Because of the rattle handles' shape, they could block a child's airway if inserted in the throat.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and STK International Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving this rattle.
sold_at: Discount dollar stores nationwide sold the recalled rattle from December 1997 through May 1998 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Payless ShoeSource Announce Recall of Children's Sneakers
hazard_text: The teddy bear or heart metal clasps on the zippers of these shoes can come off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these sneakers away from children and return them to their local Payless ShoeSource store for a refund.
incidents_text: Payless knows of two children ingesting the teddy bear metal clasps, and one of these children reportedly started to choke.
sold_at: Payless ShoeSource stores nationwide sold these sneakers from March 1998 through June 1998 for about $10.

heading: CPSC Urges Search for Previously Recalled Portable Cribs and Play Yards
hazard_text: Top rail hinges must be turned to set up the cribs and play yards. These top rails can collapse, entrapping children and suffocating them.
action: Kolcraft has gone to great lengths to renew their recall efforts. Kolcraft is offering a $60 refund to consumers for the return of the Travel-Lite portable cribs. They also are notifying pediatricians and childcare providers about the recall. Consumers should call Kolcraft at (800) 453-7673 for instructions on disposing of the products and receiving the refund.
incidents_text: In May of 1998, a Chicago toddler died after a Playskool Travel-Lite portable crib collapsed. Twelve children have died from suffocation in collapsed play yards and portable cribs manufactured by various firms.

heading: CPSC and Safety 1st Announce Recall to Replace Bouncing Buggy Toys
hazard_text: The cat "Stop" sign and dog "Go" sign toys attached to the snack tray may be broken-off by a child, creating a sharp plastic edge.
action: If either toy breaks or shows signs of breaking, consumers should remove the toys from the tray immediately. ALL consumers should call Safety 1st at (800) 723-3065 Monday through Friday between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. EDT for free replacement toys with installation instructions.
incidents_text: Safety 1st has received more than 700 reports of children breaking-off the toys while sitting in the buggy. There have been 33 reports of children being scratched, cut or bruised from the broken-off toys, and one report of a child starting to choke.
sold_at: Toy stores nationwide sold the Bouncing Buggy from May 1997 through April 1998 for about $50.

heading: CPSC, K?B ToysTM Announce Recall of Bubble BeautiesTM Floating Balls
hazard_text: These floating balls contain a petroleum distillate, similar to kerosene, that could be harmful or fatal if ingested.
action: Consumers should immediately take these floating balls away from children, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and K·B ToysTM are not aware of any injuries involving these floating balls.
sold_at: K·B ToyTM Stores nationwide sold these floating balls in May 1998 for about $3 to $4.

heading: CPSC, GapKids Announce Voluntary Recall of Kids' Anoraks
hazard_text: The anoraks have paint on the zipper pull that contains an unacceptable level of lead. While exposure to the defective zippers presents no immediate health danger, exposure to high levels of lead over an extended period of time presents a potential poisoning hazard to young children if ingested.
action: Consumers should immediately stop wearing the anoraks and stop using the accompanying zippered pouches, and return them to any GapKids store for a refund.
sold_at: The defective anoraks were sold in GapKids stores from January 1998 to June 2, 1998 throughout the United States, Canada, Japan, Germany, France and the United Kingdom. The recall does not include anoraks sold before January 1998.

heading: CPSC, Oscar Mayer Announce Recall to Replace Decals on Pedal Cars Because of Lead Hazard
hazard_text: These decals contain high levels of lead. High levels of lead presents a poisoning hazard to young children if ingested.
action: Consumers should immediately stop children from playing with these pedal cars. Consumers should call (800) 323-0768 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. CDT Monday through Friday for instructions on how to receive new decals to replace the old decals.
incidents_text: Oscar Mayer is not aware of any illnesses or injuries involving this product.
sold_at: Grocery stores in the U.S. and Canada distributed many of these pedal cars through special promotions and also sold a small number by mail order from June 1995 through May 1998. The cars were not available for purchase in retail stores.

heading: CPSC, Payless ShoeSource Announce Recall of Child's Novelty Purses
hazard_text: The purses contain a petroleum distillate, used as a decorative liquid in the purse flap, that could be harmful or fatal if ingested.
action: Consumers should immediately take these purses away from children, and return them to their local Payless ShoeSource store for a refund and an additional $10 gift certificate.
incidents_text: CPSC and Payless are not aware of any injuries involving these purses.
sold_at: The purses were sold at Payless ShoeSource stores nationwide from Feb 1998 through May 1998 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Castrol North America Inc. Announce Recall of Super Clean Aerosol Foam
hazard_text: The defective cans could allow the cleaner to gradually leak out through the seams. Direct contact with the cleaner could burn or irritate consumers' eyes and skin.
action: Consumers should stop using these 22-ounce aerosol cans of the cleaner. Consumers should call Castrol North America Inc. at (800) 307-2164 between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. EDT Monday through Friday for information on how to dispose of the cans and how to receive a refund or rebate.
incidents_text: CPSC and Castrol have not received any reports of the cans leaking.
sold_at: Large and small retail stores nationwide, including Advance Auto, Auto Zone, Chief Auto, CSK, Kmart, Pep Boys, Strauss Discount, Wal-Mart and Western Auto, sold the cleaner from January 1997 through March 1998 for about $3.

product_name: Toy Saxophones distributed with Arby's Adventure Meals
heading: CPSC, Arby's Announce Recall of Toy Saxophones
hazard_text: The small keys and part of the mouthpiece on the saxophone could separate from the toy, presenting a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toys away from young children and return them to their local Arby's restaurant for a free replacement toy.
incidents_text: Arby's is not aware of any injuries involving these toys.
sold_at: The toy was distributed with Adventure Meals at Arby's restaurants nationwide from January through March 1998.

heading: CPSC and Sanrio Inc. Announce Recall of Mascot Plushes Animal Toys
hazard_text: The small bells on these stuffed toys can become detached, presenting an aspiration hazard to young children, which could result in death.
action: Consumers should take these stuffed toys away from young children immediately, and either remove the bell from the toy, or return the toy to the store where purchased for a full refund. The toy also can be returned by mail for a full refund plus the cost of postage to Sanrio, Attn: Quality Assurance Dept., 570 Eccles Ave., South San Francisco, CA 94080.
incidents_text: CPSC and Sanrio Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these toys.
sold_at: The plush toys were sold at Sanrio's stores and various other retail stores nationwide in October 1997 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Rand/Ross Bicycle Co. Announce Recall to Repair Mountain Bikes
hazard_text: The front suspension fork can separate from the frame of these bikes, causing riders to lose control and fall.
action: Consumers should stop using the bicycles immediately and call Rand/Ross toll free at (800) 338-7677, extension #263 between 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. EDT Monday through Friday. Consumers will be given the name of a local bicycle dealer/shop/technician who will make the appropriate tightening adjustment with a torque wrench free of charge. If consumers wish to make the adjustment themselves, they will be sent a free retro-fit kit. The retro-fit kit contains a 6-inch 6mm Allen wrench and instructions for tightening the bolts.
incidents_text: Rand/Ross is aware of five reports of serious injuries which reportedly occurred when an improperly adjusted front suspension fork separated from the frame. These injuries included facial fractures and lacerations.
sold_at: Target, Price-Costco, Toys R Us and a limited number of bicycle shops sold these bicycles nationwide from February 1997 to March 1998 for about $200 to $300.

heading: CPSC, ERA Intermarketing Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Disposable Lighters
hazard_text: The lighters do not meet the 1994 requirement for child-resistant mechanisms in violation of the Consumer Product Safety Act. This act requires a mechanism on disposable and novelty lighters shown to prevent ignition of the lighters by most children under 5 years old.
action: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to ERA Intermarketing for a full refund, including postage, at: Product Recall, ERA Intermarketing Co., Inc., 200 S. 5th Avenue, City of Industry, CA 91746.
incidents_text: CPSC and ERA Intermarketing are not aware of any injuries involving these cigarette lighters.
sold_at: Small retailers sold the Elite-2 cigarette lighters nationwide from June 1997 to March 1998 for about $1.

product_name: Tweety Water Timer Game Key Rings
heading: CPSC, Warner Bros. Stores Announce Recall of Tweety Key Rings
hazard_text: The key rings contain ethylene glycol, commonly found in antifreeze, that could leak. Ethylene glycol can poison young children if swallowed.
action: Consumers should take these key rings away from children immediately and return them to Warner Bros. Stores for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Warner Bros. Stores are not aware of any injuries involving these key rings.
sold_at: Warner Bros. Stores nationwide sold the key rings from April 1996 through April 1997 for about $5.

product_name: Halloween Floating Eyeballs and Smiley Face Floating Balls
heading: CPSC, Atico International Announce Recall of "Eyeball" and Smiley Face Floating Balls
hazard_text: These balls contain kerosene. If the ball cracks or breaks, kerosene leaking out could poison young children if swallowed. The smaller of these balls also present a serious choking hazard to young children. They lack warning labels required for small balls.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
units: About 329,000 Halloween Floating Eyeballs and about 100,000 Smiley Face Floating Balls
incidents_text: CPSC and Atico International USA, Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these balls.
sold_at: These balls were sold nationwide by retail chain stores such as Arbor Drug, Eckerd Drugs, Thrift Drugs, K&B, Inc and Walgreen drug stores from June 1995 through October 1997 for about $1.

product_name: Gerry Clear Choice model 618 baby monitors
heading: CPSC, Gerry Baby Products Announce Recall to Repair Baby Monitors
hazard_text: When an electrical short occurs, the rechargeable battery can cause the monitor's "parent" unit to smoke and flame.
action: Consumers should disconnect and throw away the blue battery pack from the parent unit immediately. Consumers should contact Evenflo's Parent Link Consumer Resource Center at (800) 233-5921 for assistance (Gerry Baby Products is out of business, but the Evenflo Company has now taken over in responding to this recall).
incidents_text: Gerry has received one report of flames and four reports of smoke coming from the monitor's parent unit. No injuries or property damage have been reported.
sold_at: Mass merchandise and baby stores throughout the United States sold the baby monitors from April 1996 to March 1998 for about $40.

heading: CPSC, Norco Products USA Announce Recall of Bike Passenger Trailers
hazard_text: Metal fatigue could cause failure at the hitch arm pivot bracket, resulting in the trailer breaking loose from the bicycle, causing injury to the occupant of the trailer.
action: Consumers should stop using these bike trailers immediately and call the store where purchased or Norco Products to arrange to have a safety upgrade kit installed at no charge.
incidents_text: Norco Products is not aware of any injuries involving these trailers.
sold_at: Small independent bicycle shops in Washington, Oregon, Northern California, Idaho and Colorado sold the trailers from January 1997 through February 1998 for about $200 to $350.

product_name: Evenflo On My Way infant car seats/carriers
heading: NHTSA, CPSC Announce Recall of Evenflo On My Way Infant Car Seats/Carriers
hazard_text: The red push button assembly on each side of the seat that is used to latch and adjust the carrying handle can unexpectedly release and cause the seat to flip forward. This can cause serious injuries to children while the seats are being used as infant carriers.
action: Evenflo will provide a repair kit, free of charge, with redesigned latch buttons that will make the handle latch much stronger. The repair can be done in the home with a Phillips head screwdriver. Until the seats are repaired, NHTSA and the CPSC advise owners not to carry a seat by its handle, but to use the hand holds at the head and foot of the seat.
incidents_text: There have been 176 reports in which the carrying handle latch unexpectedly released, resulting in 89 injuries to children, including bruises, concussions and skull fractures. The injuries occurred to both restrained and unrestrained children.
sold_at: Juvenile product, mass merchandise and major discount stores nationwide sold the car seats beginning in January 1996 for about $60 to $70, and the car seat with stroller for $150 to $175.

product_name: Fisher-Price cookie-shaped refrigerator magnet toys and Magic Motion Mobiles
heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Infant Toys
hazard_text: The magnet can come apart and release small plastic pieces, presenting a choking hazard to young children. Part of the mobile can detach and fall into the crib, presenting a risk of injury to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from children immediately and call Fisher-Price toll-free at 800-233-4004 between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. EST Monday through Friday. Consumers will receive a free replacement cookie magnet or replacement parts for the mobile, as applicable.
units: About 21,000 cookie-shaped refrigerator magnet toys and 49,000 crib mobiles
incidents_text: Fisher-Price has received 59 reports of cookie magnets coming apart. One report involved a child ingesting plastic pieces and nine reports involved children putting plastic pieces in their mouths, which were removed by adults. Fisher-Price has received 78 reports of mobile parts detaching. Forty-one reports involved the mobile's rotating ring and mirror detaching and falling into cribs, resulting in 15 injuries, such as bumps and bruises.
sold_at: Major toy and mass merchandise stores nationwide sold the recalled cookie magnet with the Refrigerator Activity Magnet Set beginning in September 1997 for about $6 and sold the Magic Motion Mobile beginning in June 1997 for about $24.

product_name: First Years High Chair Gym toys
heading: CPSC, The First Years Announce Recall to Repair High Chair Gym Toys
hazard_text: The clacker balls hanging from the center of the toy present a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toy away from children immediately and call The First Years at (800) 533-6708 anytime for the free repair kit and installation instructions or write to The First Years at One Kiddie Drive, Avon, MA 02322-1171.
incidents_text: CPSC and The First Years have received 2 reports of children getting one of the clacker balls stuck in the throat and blocking the airway. Nearby adults were able to pull the balls free and prevent the children from choking.
sold_at: Discount and toy stores sold the First Years High Chair Gym toy nationwide from January 1995 through November 1997 for about $10.

product_name: Cyber Fighter and Flying Angel dolls
hazard_text: During use, the wings of these flying dolls can break off, and possibly cause serious eye injuries to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using the dolls immediately and return them to any Rite Aid store for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Rite Aid have received one report of a doll's wing breaking off during use,resulting in a laceration above the eye of a nearby child.
sold_at: Rite Aid drug stores in the eastern U.S. sold the dolls from February 1997 through January 1998 for about $3.

heading: CPSC, Baby's Dream Furniture Announce Recall to Repair Cribs
hazard_text: The cribs have a drop gate (a rail that folds down) on the front of the crib, rather than a rail that slides up and down. A baby's fingers can be trapped in the folding drop gate and injured.
action: Consumers should immediately lock the drop gate of these cribs in the closed position and call Baby's Dream toll-free at (888) 866-4217 between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. EST Monday through Friday for the free repair kit and installation instructions. Consumers should not use the drop gate until the new hinge is installed.
incidents_text: Baby's Dream has received eight reports of babies' fingers being trapped in the drop gate, including seven reports of severe lacerations and one report of an adult's finger being injured.
sold_at: Independent juvenile furniture stores nationwide sold the cribs from December 1994 through June 1997 for about $500 to $700.

product_name: Miniature rocking chair, sold as part of Wee Patsy Travel Set
heading: CPSC, Effanbee Doll Company Announce Recall of Miniature Rocking Chairs
hazard_text: The chair has excessive levels of lead in the paint, presenting a potential lead poisoning hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the miniature rocking chair away from children immediately. Effanbee is offering consumers a $5 refund, including postage, for the return of the miniature rocking chair.
incidents_text: CPSC and Effanbee are not aware of any illnesses or injuries involving this product.
sold_at: Doll, gift, collectible and specialty toy stores nationwide, J.C. Penney catalogs and the Effanbee Collector's Society sold the Wee Patsy Travel Set from June 1996 through December 1996 for about $115.

heading: CPSC, Nancy Sales Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Bean Bag Crab Toys
hazard_text: The toys' seams can separate and allow plastic pellets to be released, presenting an aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Nancy Sales Co. Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these toys.
sold_at: Arcade and gift shops nationwide sold the toys from January 1997 through October 1997 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Step 2 Announce Recall of Toy Chests for In-Home Repair
hazard_text: The lids of the toy chests can fall down onto a young child's head or neck, which could result in the child being entrapped and possibly strangled.
action: Consumers should immediately stop young children from using these toy chests, and call Step 2 for a free lid support kit. The repair kit will stop the lid from closing all the way until closed by an adult.
incidents_text: CPSC and Step 2 are aware of 16 incidents where the lid fell onto a child's head or neck causing some minor injuries, such as scratches and bruised necks.
sold_at: Toys R Us, Kmart and other retailers nationwide sold the toy chests from February 1992 to November 1997 for about $40.

product_name: Glide Rides, sold with backyard gym sets
heading: CPSC, Hedstrom Announce Recall of Glide Rides
hazard_text: The Glide Ride's "J-bolt" assembly can break, causing children to fall or drop to the ground and be injured.
action: Consumers should stop using and discard or destroy this product immediately. The firm is out of business and the remedy is no longer available.
incidents_text: Hedstrom had received 17 reports of children falling or dropping to the ground when the "J-bolt" broke, resulting in scrapes, bumps, bruises and one reported bone fracture.
sold_at: Department, toy and discount stores nationwide, including J.C. Penney, Toys R Us, Kmart and Wal-Mart, sold Hedstrom gym sets with the Glide Ride from April 1993 through December 1997 for about $150. The Glide Ride also has been sold separately for about $45.

product_name: Fleece garments: children's vests and pants; infant shirts; men's shirts; and ladies' tops, top and pants sets, and robes
heading: CPSC, Hardwick Knitted Fabrics Inc. Announce Recall of Fleece Garments
hazard_text: These garments, which fail to meet federal mandatory standards for fabric flammability, could ignite readily and present a serious risk of burn injuries in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act. Fabrics that do not comply with the standard typically burn faster than newspaper.
action: Consumers should stop using these garments immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: Hardwick Knitted Fabrics Inc. and CPSC are not aware of any injuries involving these garments.

heading: CPSC, Toys "R" Us Announce Recall of Children's Soap Craft Set
hazard_text: If consumers melt pieces of the soap disks that come with the set in a microwave oven for 10 minutes, as instructed, the soap could ignite in the microwave. The instructions should have read 10 seconds rather than 10 minutes.
action: Consumers should immediately return the craft set to the nearest Toys "R" Us store for a full refund.
incidents_text: Toys "R" Us has received two reports of the soap and its container melting together in a microwave and one report of flames inside the oven. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Toys "R" Us stores nationwide sold the soap craft sets from November 1997 to December 1997 for about $15.

heading: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall to Repair Carriers and Carrier/Swing Seats
hazard_text: The handle on the seats can unlock unexpectedly, causing an infant to fall and be injured.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled carrier and carrier/swing seat immediately. Consumers who previously contacted Graco by returning registration cards or ordering parts or accessories for one of these models will receive a free repair kit directly from Graco.
incidents_text: Graco has received 45 reports of handles unlocking unexpectedly, including reports of four skull fractures and two concussions.
sold_at: Juvenile product and major discount stores, such as Toys R Us and Service Merchandise, sold the carrier and carrier/swing seat nationwide from August 1993 through August 1997. The carrier sold for about $30 and the carrier/swings sold for about $100.

heading: CPSC, B&B Stores Announce Recall of Mesh-Sided Cribs
