hazard_text: The mattress pad compresses, a gap can occur between the side panels and the bed frame, and the snaps can separate from the frame, presenting suffocation hazards. In addition, the side rails can bend, presenting an entrapment hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using these cribs immediately and discard or destroy them. The firm is out of business and a remedy is no longer available.
incidents_text: CPSC and B&B Stores are not aware of any injuries involving these cribs. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: B&B Stores in Puerto Rico sold these cribs from August 1996 through January 1997 for about $30.

heading: CPSC, Cosco Announce Recall for In-Home Repair of VoyagerTM Car Seat/Strollers
hazard_text: The VoyagerTM Car Seat/Stroller is a combination product with an infant car seat that snaps into a frame for use as a stroller. When used as the stroller, the car seat could become dislodged and fall to the ground. Infants could be injured from the fall.
action: Consumers should call Cosco at (800) 221-6736 between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. EST Monday through Friday for the repair instructions. Until the repair is completed, consumers should not use the car seat as a stroller. The problem does not affect the product's use as a car seat or carrier. Consumers can write to Cosco at 2525 State Street, Columbus, IN 47201.
incidents_text: Cosco has not received any reports of car seats becoming dislodged from the stroller. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: The Cosco VoyagerTM Car Seat/Stroller was sold nationwide from September 1997 through November 1997, primarily through Wal-Mart, Target, Ames, Service Merchandise, Caldor and Montgomery Ward retail stores, for about $79.

heading: CPSC, Retailers Announce Recall of Curtain-Style Holiday Lights
hazard_text: The electrical wiring can pull out from the splices of these decorative light sets, exposing live wires and presenting an electrocution hazard.
action: Consumers should stop using these light sets immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC is not aware of any injuries involving these lights. This recall is being issued to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Retail stores, including BJ's Wholesale, Builders Square, CVS Pharmacy, Caldor, Frank's Nursery & Crafts, Hechinger, Hobby Lobby, Home Quarters, M J Designs, Montgomery Ward, Rite Aid Pharmacy, Sam's Club, Shopko, Venture, Walgreens and Wal-Mart sold the lights nationwide from September 1995 to November 1997 for between $6 and $19, depending on the size of the sets purchased.

heading: CPSC, MTS Products Inc. Announce Recall of Infant Carriers
hazard_text: The carrier's handle can break causing the carrier to fall. Infants can be injured from the fall.
action: Consumers should stop using these infant carriers immediately and call MTS at (800) 242-1922 between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. PST Monday through Friday to receive a free replacement infant carrier.
incidents_text: CPSC and MTS have received seven reports of handles breaking, resulting in infants sustaining bruises, scratches and cuts.
sold_at: Kmart, Rose and State Enterprises stores nationwide sold the infant carriers from April 1996 through August 1997 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Kid's Patrol Announce Recall of Zippered Vest
hazard_text: The zipper "pulls" can slide off the top of the vest and become a choking hazard to young children.
incidents_text: CPSC and Kid's Patrol are not aware of any injuries involving these vests. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Athletic Team zippered vests sold exclusively at Wal-Mart stores.

heading: CPSC, BRIO Announce Recall of Wooden Clown Toys to Replace Hats
hazard_text: The hats present a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the clown's hat away from children immediately and send the hat to BRIO Corp.
incidents_text: BRIO has received one report of a 22-month-old child in Germany reportedly choking to death on the clown's hat. No other injuries or complaints have been reported.
sold_at: Specialty stores and mail order catalogs nationwide sold the toy from 1977 through September 1997, most recently for about $19. BRIO clown toys currently being sold have the redesigned hat and are in boxes labeled, "CONTAINS NEW HAT DESIGN."

heading: CPSC, STK International Announce Recall of Clock Tambourine Toys
hazard_text: Small pieces could break off the toys, presenting potential choking and aspiration hazards to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately and return the toys to STK International Inc. for a refund and postage reimbursement.
incidents_text: CPSC and STK International Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving this toy. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Discount and dollar-type stores nationwide sold the toys from June 1995 through June 1997 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Novi Kids Announce Recall of Halloween Bounce Balls
hazard_text: The balls present a serious choking hazard to young children, which can result in death.
action: Consumers should take these balls away from young children immediately and return them to the Target store were purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: A sticker on the package suggests the balls are "GREAT for FAVORS and TRICK or TREATS!" If used as Halloween treats, the balls could be given to children under 3 years old. Small balls marketed to young children are banned by the Federal Hazardous Substances Act.
sold_at: Target stores nationwide sold the packages of balls beginning October 4, 1997, for about $2.

heading: CPSC, Safety 1st Announce Recall of Nursery Monitor Batteries
hazard_text: The dry cell battery can rupture and irritate the skin.
action: Consumers should stop using the monitors immediately, and call Safety 1st at (800) 964-8489 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. EST Monday through Friday for instructions on returning the recalled batteries and receiving replacement batteries.
incidents_text: Safety 1st has received 76 reports of batteries rupturing. One consumer reported discomfort and swelling when the battery ruptured in her hand.
sold_at: Retail stores nationwide sold the monitors from June 1997 through August 1997 for between $35 and $45.

heading: CPSC, Halcyon WaterSpring Inc. Announce Recall of Wipe Warmers
hazard_text: The Wipe Warmers, distributed by Dex Products Inc., of Benicia, Calif., could overheat and melt.
action: Consumers should stop using the Wipe Warmer immediately and call Halcyon WaterSpring Inc. at (888) 735-5585 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. EDT Monday through Friday for information on how to receive a full refund or replacement. Consumers also can write to Halcyon WaterSpring Inc., 355 Champagne Drive, Donsview Ontario, Canada M3J266.
incidents_text: Halcyon WaterSpring is aware of six incidents involving melting of the product and one alleged fire of undetermined cause where other products were present.
sold_at: Various retail stores nationwide sold the Wipe Warmers from January 1994 through December 1996 for about $10 to $15.

heading: CPSC, Nadel & Sons Toy Corp. Announce Recall of Stuffed Bears
hazard_text: The eyes of the bears can become detached, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these stuffed bears away from young children immediately and return them to Nadel & Sons Toy Corp. for a $5 refund plus the cost of postage.
incidents_text: CPSC and Nadel & Sons are aware of one incident where a child started to choke as a result of a detached eye from one of these bears.
sold_at: Amusement parks and roadside entertainment centers, including Busch Gardens Theme Park in Tampa, Fla.; Dutch Wonderland in Lancaster, Pa.; and Play Day Amusements in Seaside Heights, N.J.; distributed the stuffed bears from October 1995 to May 1997 as prizes at game booths or in game machines.

heading: CPSC, Chiquita Brands Announce Recall of Sports Blast™ Drink Bottles
hazard_text: These bottles have plastic pull-up tops that can separate from the cap, presenting a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers can safely drink the product by completely removing and destroying the plastic cap. Consumers can return unopened bottles to the store where purchased for a refund.
incidents_text: Chiquita has received 10 reports of children pulling the bottle tops off with their teeth.
sold_at: Costco Wholesale, Sam's Club and BJ's Wholesale Club stores nationwide sold cases of Sports BlastTM bottles from March 1997 through August 1997 for about $6.

heading: CPSC, Al-Dan Trading Inc. Announce Recall of Wooden Vehicle Toys
hazard_text: The toys have small parts that could separate and present a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the recalled toys away from children immediately and discard or destroy them, or if possible, return them to the store where purchased for a full refund. However, the firm, Al-Dan Trading Inc., does not have contact information at this time.
incidents_text: CPSC and Al-Dan are not aware of any injuries involving these toys.
sold_at: These toys were mainly sold in the following Florida discount stores: All for 99 Cents, Always 99 Cents, Dollar Store, Dollar Dave's, Daniel Club Wholesalers, and Swamis Trading from June 1996 through June 1997 for about $1.

product_name: Children's toy bracelets (packaged as party favors)
heading: CPSC, Multiple Firms Announce Recall of Children's Toy Jewelry
hazard_text: The necklaces and bracelets involved in this recall can break, releasing small beads that pose a choking and aspiration hazard to children under three years of age.
action: Consumers should take the toy jewelry sets away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and the firms involved in the recall are not aware of any injuries involving the toy jewelry.
sold_at: All these toys were sold in children's, dollar-type and discount stores nationwide through March 5, 1997 for about $1.

product_name: Hot Pet Car battery-operated toy cars
heading: CPSC, United Tradeline Announce Recall of Toy "Hot Pet Car"
hazard_text: Small pieces could break off the cars, presenting a serious aspiration hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately, and call United Tradeline Inc. at (888) 898-9296 between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. PDT Monday through Friday, or write to the company at 11800 E. Clark Street, Arcadia, CA 91006 for information on a refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and United Tradeline Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving this toy.
sold_at: Small retail and toy stores sold the toy cars primarily in the Los Angeles, Calif., area from April 1997 through May 1997 for about $3.

heading: CPSC, J.C. Penney Announce Recall of Francisca Full-Size Baby Cribs
hazard_text: The cribs' side rail spindles are too short and can loosen and separate, creating a space greater than 2-3/8 inches between the slats. Babies could be strangled if their heads become entrapped between the slats. In addition, babies could be seriously injured if they fall out of the crib.
action: Consumers should stop using these cribs immediately. Consumers should return the crib to the nearest J.C. Penney store to receive a refund or replacement crib. If consumers cannot get to a store, they can receive the refund or replacement by calling J.C. Penney at (800) 709-5777. This number is operational 24 hours a day.
incidents_text: CPSC is aware of four reports of missing or loose side rail spindles. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: J.C. Penney Catalogs sold the cribs from August 1996 through April 1997 for about $200.

product_name: First Alert® True FitTM Safety Gate
heading: CPSC, BRK Announce Recall of First Alert® True Fit™ Safety Gates
hazard_text: Plastic parts of the gate can break off into small pieces, creating a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these gates immediately and call BRK toll-free at (888) 777-5599 anytime to obtain a free replacement gate.
incidents_text: BRK has received over 200 reports of plastic parts, including bumpers, hinges and handle pieces breaking off, sometimes into small pieces. No choking injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Toys R Us, Hills and other retail stores nationwide sold the gates beginning in October 1996 for about $35.

heading: CPSC, Manufacturers, Importers Announce Recall of Wooden and Metal Bunk Beds
hazard_text: The spaces can be large enough for a child's body to pass through, but small enough to entrap the child's head.
action: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
incidents_text: Since 1990, CPSC has received reports of 35 children who died from becoming caught in the top of wooden bunk beds. Thirty-four of those children were 3 years old or younger. In addition, CPSC has received reports of five children who died from becoming caught in the top of metal bunk beds. All five children were 2 years old or younger. A recent death occurred on April 24, 1997. A 3-year-old girl died from becoming caught in a wooden bunk bed manufactured by Heartland Furniture. CPSC is not aware of any additional deaths related to the other manufacturers and importers participating in this recall.

heading: CPSC, Walgreen Co. Announce Recall of "Smoke Tote" Cigarette Lighters
hazard_text: These lighters' child-resistant mechanisms could fail to reset themselves, potentially allowing young children to ignite the lighters.
action: Consumers should stop using the lighters immediately and return them to the Walgreen store where it was purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Walgreen are not aware of any injuries involving these lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.
sold_at: Walgreen drug stores nationwide sold the lighters within the Smoke Tote set from August 1996 through August 1997 for about $3.

heading: CPSC, Camil Corp. Ltd. Announce Recall of Aguarras Floor Cleaner
hazard_text: The product's packaging is not child- resistant; not labeled with the necessary warnings, cautions for use and instructions for appropriate first aid in case of ingestion; and resembles a liquor flask.
action: Consumers should stop using the product immediately and return it to Almacenes Topeka Loiza for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Camil are not aware of any injuries involving this product. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: The entire 1,000-bottle lot was sold at Almacenes Topeka Loiza, in Santurce, Puerto Rico, from December 1996 through July 1997 for 89 cents.

heading: CPSC, Century Announce Recall to Repair Lil' Napper Infant Swings
hazard_text: These swings have shoulder harness straps that are placed over each shoulder and buckled between the child's legs. If the straps on these swings loosen or are unbuckled, a child can become tangled in the straps and strangle.
action: Consumers should stop using the Lil' Napper swings immediately and discard or destroy the product. Graco, which now owns the "Century" brand name, is offering a $30.00 incentive to anyone who has one to destroy it.
incidents_text: CPSC and Century were aware of three deaths and one near-strangulation that occurred when children from 6 to 9 months old became entangled with the harness straps around their necks.
sold_at: Juvenile product, department, and discount stores nationwide sold the swings beginning in 1991 for about $90.

heading: CPSC, Placo Announce Recall of Star Wonders Flying Dolls
hazard_text: During use, the wings of the flying dolls can break off, causing serious eye injuries to consumers.
action: Consumers should stop using the dolls immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Placo Products Company have received seven reports of the dolls' wings breaking off during use, resulting in serious eyes injuries, including corneal abrasions, torn retinas and blindness.
sold_at: Toy, drug and discount stores nationwide sold the dolls from January 1996 through August 1997 for about $6.

heading: CPSC and Industry Announce Corrective Action to Improve Safety of Halogen Torchiere Floor Lamps
hazard_text: The halogen bulbs in these lamps can cause fires.
action: The industry is making free wire guards available to consumers through a cooperative effort with many retail stores. Installing the wire guard over the glass bulb shield will reduce the potential fire hazard by making it harder for flammable materials to touch the lamp's halogen bulb. For the guard to be effective, consumers must use only halogen bulbs of 300 watts or less in the lamp.
incidents_text: CPSC is aware of at least 189 fires and 11 deaths since 1992 involving halogen torchiere floor lamps.
sold_at: These lamps first became available in the United States in 1983 and sales have grown significantly in the 1990s.

heading: CPSC and Kreiner Imports Announce the Recall of Kinder Chocolate Eggs Containing Toys
hazard_text: Some of the toys have small parts that present a serious choking and aspiration hazard to children under three years of age.
action: Consumers should take these toys away from children under three years of age immediately. If purchased at the above listed stores, consumers should return the toys to the store for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Ferrero are not aware of any injuries in the United States involving these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury to children under three years of age.
sold_at: Kreiner Imports Inc. imported and distributed Kinder eggs from March 1997 through August 1997 through the following small candy and specialty stores in the South, Midwest and West: Continental Imports, 17115-E West Bluemound Rd., Brookfield, WI; Rosemarie's Restaurant & Deli, 2445 Ridge Rd., Lansing, IL; Edelweiss Delicatessen, 136 W. Northwest Hwy., Palatine, IL; Van Nuys German Delicatessen, 16155 Roscoe Blvd., North Hills, CA; Geier's Sausage Kitchen, 7447 S. Tamiami Trail, Sarasota, FL; Wolf's Delicatessen, 2019 S. Lumpkin Rd., Columbus, GA; Heinz Bavarian Bakery, 3419 Noland Rd., Independence, MO; Ehmer's Chef's Market, 7804 Fairview Rd., Charlotte, NC; Himmel Haus Imports, 3444 Main St., Elkhart, IN; German Specialties, 515 N. Western Ave., Peoria, IL; Katy's Catering, 2732 7th St., Moline, IL; Deutsche Ecke Bakery & Cafe, 451 N. Wilson Blvd., Radcliff, KY; Mainzer's Delicatessen, 12113 S. Dixie Hwy., Miami, FL.

heading: CPSC, Gymboree Corp. Announce Recall of Children's Umbrellas
hazard_text: The children's umbrellas that have surface coating decorations with high levels of lead. This violates the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Act. Ingestion of high levels of lead can present a risk of lead poisoning to young children. Lead poisoning in children is associated with behavior problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation.
action: Consumers should take these umbrellas away from children immediately and return them to any Gymboree store for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Gymboree are not aware of any reports of illness involving these umbrellas. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of illness.
sold_at: Gymboree stores sold the umbrellas nationwide from September 1996 through May 1997 for about $12 to $30, depending on the model.

heading: CPSC, Mardo International Distributors Announce Recall of Aguarras Paint Thinner
hazard_text: The product's packaging is not child-resistant; not labeled with the necessary warnings, cautions for use and instructions for appropriate first aid in case of ingestion; and resembles a liquor flask. The packaging violates the Federal Hazardous Substances Act and the Poison Prevention Packaging Act.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the product and return it to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Mardo are not aware of any injuries involving this product. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Small retail stores, some referred to as "Botanicas," throughout Puerto Rico sold the paint thinner from July 1996 through April 1997 for about $1.

product_name: Men's Model 8546-23 MAGNA High Impact Mountain-Style Bicycles
heading: CPSC and Dynacraft Industries Inc. Announce Recall of Men's Bicycles
hazard_text: The bicycle's left crank, which connects the pedal to the frame of the bike, can loosen and detach. If the crank detaches, the rider's leg can be injured by contact with the crank or the rider can lose control of the bike, fall and be injured.
action: Consumers should stop using these bicycles immediately and call Dynacraft Industries Inc. at (800) 551-0032 between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. EDT Monday through Friday or write to the company at 200 Butterfield Drive, Ashland, MA 01721 to receive instructions on repairing the crank. Consumers also can call their local Toys "R" Us stores to arrange for the store to repair the bicycle free of charge.
incidents_text: Dynacraft Industries Inc. has received four reports of the left crank loosening and detaching, resulting in riders falling from the bicycles sustaining cuts or bruises.
sold_at: Toys "R" Us stores nationwide were the sole distributors of the bicycles. They sold the bicycles from April 1997 through June 1997 for about $100.

heading: CPSC, Lex Pharmaceutical Inc. Announce Recall of Vitamins and Medicines
hazard_text: The bottles do not have child-resistant packaging as required by the Poison Prevention Packaging Act. If accidentally swallowed by children, these products can cause serious injury or death.
action: Consumers should immediately discontinue use of the recalled products and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC is not aware of any injuries involving these products. However, about 50 children each year die from poisoning after swallowing medicines and other toxic substances.
sold_at: The vitamins and medicines were mainly sold at small pharmacies, and discount drug and retail stores in Puerto Rico, New York, Florida and the Southeastern United States from January 1996 through June 1997 for about $5.

heading: CPSC, Ohio Art Company Announce Recall of Splash Off Water Rockets
hazard_text: When being filled, the rockets can break apart under the water's pressure. Consumers can be injured seriously if they are hit by broken rocket pieces.
action: Consumers should stop using the Splash Off Water Rockets immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Ohio Art Company have received 37 reports of these rockets breaking apart while being filled, resulting in lacerations of a hand, shoulder, and forehead.
sold_at: Toy and major retail stores nationwide sold the Splash Off Water Rockets from April 1997 through June 1997 for about $20.

heading: CPSC, Al-Dan Trading Inc. Announce Recall of Infant Toys
hazard_text: The toy is marketed for use in a crib. The toy presents a risk of strangulation if hung across a crib or playpen. It is not labeled according to the ASTM voluntary standard to warn consumers about the strangulation risk if the toy is attached to a crib or playpen.
action: Consumers should take the recalled toys away from children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Al-Dan Trading are not aware of any injuries involving the recalled toys.However, the Commission is aware of at least three deaths resulting from the use of similar toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent future deaths and injuries.
sold_at: These toys mainly were sold by Daniel Club Wholesalers and Swamis Trading in Miami, Fla., from to March 1996 to June 1997 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Creative Products Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Jewelry Sets
hazard_text: The necklaces and bracelets of two different sets can break, releasing small beads. The earring clasps of a third set can come off. Young children can choke on the earring clasps and inhale the beads into their lungs which could lead to death.
action: Consumers should take the jewelry sets away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Creative Products Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these toy jewelry sets. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Dollar-type and discount stores in the East, Midwest, and South sold the jewelry sets from August 1995 through November 1995 for about $1.

heading: CPSC, Cosco Announce Recall for In-Home Repair of Full-Size Baby Cribs
hazard_text: Cribs may have been mis-assembled with the mattress platform being used as a side rail. The crib side rail and mattress platform are the same size and have been used in place of one another. CPSC standards limit the space between side rail slats to no more than 2 3/8 inches. If the crib's mattress platform is used as a side rail, the distance between the slats would be about 5 inches. Spacing this large enables an infant to become entrapped in the side rails, which could result in serious injury or death.
action: To prevent death or injury, do not use a mis-assembled crib until it has been repaired. Cosco is offering all owners of mis-assembled cribs a free gift to encourage them to repair their cribs. Cosco is also offering all consumers who own these cribs an identification/warning sticker for placement on the mattress platform to prevent future mis-assembly. Consumers should call Cosco for this important sticker.
incidents_text: Cosco has received more than 47 reports of cribs being mis-assembled with the mattress platform being used as a side rail, including 27 reports of babies becoming entrapped, resulting in one death.
sold_at: Major national retail stores and baby specialty stores sold the cribs beginning in 1995 for about $90 to $150.

heading: CPSC, Importers Announce Recall of Cigarette Lighters
incidents_text: CPSC is not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Small retail stores in California, Washington, Nevada, Florida, Georgia, Texas, Arizona, and Montana sold the Kassir lighters from September 1994 through December 1996 for about $5 to $7.

heading: CPSC, Evenflo Announce Recall of Happy Camper Portable Play Yards
hazard_text: If the hinges on the product are not fully rotated, the product can collapse, possibly trapping the child in the "V" formed by the folded top rails. Additionally, if leaned or sat upon, the rotating plastic hinges in the middle of the folding top rails can crack or break, presenting a sharp edge or possibly allowing the child to escape.
action: Consumers who have one of these recalled play yards with a broken hinge should immediately discontinue using it and properly dispose of it. Evenflo will not be providing a fix (hinge cover kit) in such cases. The kits are now only being offered to consumers that have a fully operational play yard.
incidents_text: Evenflo and CPSC are aware of three deaths involving the play yards. In two incidents, the hinges collapsed and entrapped the child and in one incident an infant was placed into a broken play yard. Evenflo has received 107 reports of children receiving cuts and bruises from broken hinges.
sold_at: Major department, discount and juvenile products stores nationwide have sold these Evenflo play yards since January 1990 for about $60 to $130.

heading: CPSC, C & T International Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Side Rails on Baby Cribs
hazard_text: The side rails can loosen and separate, creating a space greater than 2-3/8 inches between the slats. Babies could be strangled if their heads become entrapped between the slats. In addition, babies could be seriously injured if they fall out of the crib.
action: Consumers should stop using the cribs immediately and call C & T toll-free at (888) 470-1260 between 9 a.m and 5 p.m. EDT Monday through Friday for free replacement rails.
incidents_text: CPSC is aware of five reports where the cribs' side rails were missing or loose. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Juvenile product stores in Massachusetts, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Virginia, and Florida sold the cribs from February 1994 through March 1996 for about $350.

product_name: Chinese jump ropes sold with children's activity books
heading: CPSC, Klutz Inc. Announce Recall of Chinese Jump Ropes
hazard_text: The ends of the elasticized ropes are joined together by metal crimps that may fail in use. Children using the ropes or standing nearby can be hit by an end of the rope as it snaps back.
action: Consumers should take the recalled jump ropes away from children immediately and call Klutz Inc. collect. Alternatively, consumers can make their own repair by cutting the ends of the ropes, removing the metal crimps, and tying the ends of the rope together with a square knot.
incidents_text: Klutz has received 17 reports of the ropes breaking apart and one report in which a child was struck and scratched near the eye, but did not require medical attention.
sold_at: Klutz sold the jump ropes with the activity books directly through its catalog and through major retail book stores as well as many independent gift, toy and book stores nationwide beginning in March 1997 for $10.95.

heading: CPSC, IKEA Announce Recall of Stuffed Animals
hazard_text: The stuffed animals' eyes can become detached, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these stuffed animals away from young children immediately and return them to the nearest IKEA store for a full refund or exchange for another soft toy.
incidents_text: CPSC and IKEA are not aware of any injuries involving these stuffed animals. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: IKEA stores nationwide sold the stuffed animals from January 1997 through May 1997 for between $3 and $15.

heading: CPSC, Levi Strauss & Co. Announce Recall of Girls' Dresses
hazard_text: The dresses' snaps can become detached, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these dresses immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: Levi Strauss & Co. is aware of one report of several snaps becoming detached from a dress. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Department stores nationwide, including Macy's, Mervyn's, and J.C. Penney, sold the dresses from April 1996 through February 1997 for about $25.

product_name: Sweet Suzana brand infants' shirt-and-pant sets
heading: CPSC, Little Laura of California Inc. Announce Recall of Infants' Garments
hazard_text: The shirts have tulip-shaped buttons that can break apart, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should stop using these garments immediately and return them to the nearest Kids R Us store for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Little Laura of California Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these garments. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Kids R Us stores nationwide sold the garments from January 1997 through March 1997 for about $14.

product_name: Pencils with Pacifiers where erasers go
heading: CPSC, Papel Freelance Inc. Announce Recall
hazard_text: These miniature pacifiers detach very easily from the pencils, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take these pencils away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Papel Freelance Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these pencils. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Various retail stores nationwide, including Winn Dixie and Hallmark, sold the pencils from September 1996 through April 1997 for about $2.

heading: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall to Repair Seat Rings on Stationary Entertainers
hazard_text: The white plastic seat rings on the stationary entertainers have sharp edges that can cut or scratch a child's legs during use.
action: Consumers should stop using the stationary entertainers and call Graco immediately for a free replacement seat ring and installation instructions.
incidents_text: Graco has received more than 400 reports of children's legs being cut, scratched, or scraped, usually as the child was lifted from the seat.
sold_at: The Graco stationary entertainers were sold nationwide in juvenile products and discount stores beginning in November 1995 for about $59 to $69.

heading: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Toy Police Cars
hazard_text: The back of some cars could crack and break apart, presenting a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers who have purchased the vehicle set since February 1997 should take the police car away from young children immediately and call Fisher-Price toll-free at 800-233-4004. Consumers will receive a replacement vehicle free of charge.
incidents_text: CPSC and Fisher-Price Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these toy cars. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Major toy stores and mass merchandise outlets nationwide have sold the vehicle set since February 1997 for about $8.

heading: CPSC, Coaster Company of America Inc. Announce Recall of Baby Cribs
hazard_text: The cribs pose entrapment or choking hazards to babies that could lead to serious injury or death.
action: Consumers should stop using the cribs immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund or replacement.
incidents_text: CPSC and Coaster Company of America Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these cribs. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Both models of cribs were sold by small independent retail stores nationwide, including furniture, mattress, baby, gift, and appliance stores, for about $169 to $199. The crib with scrolls (item no. 2364) was sold from June 1996 through April 1997. The crib without scrolls (item no. 2368) was sold from January 1995 through December 1996.

heading: CPSC, Charming Shoppes Inc. Announce Recall of Necklaces
hazard_text: Charming Shoppes Inc. of Bensalem, Penn., is voluntarily recalling about 4,800 metallic heart-shaped medallion necklaces that contain high levels of lead. CPSC regulations ban children's products containing high levels of lead due to the risk of lead poisoning resulting from contact with these products. Young children might get lead on their hands and then put their hands in their mouth or swallow lead directly from the necklace.
action: Consumers should take these necklaces away from young children immediately and return the necklaces to any Fashion Bug store for a replacement lead-free necklace.
incidents_text: Charming Shoppes Inc. has not received any reports of illness or injury. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: The clothing and necklace sets were sold nationwide through Fashion Bug stores from October 1996 through January 1997 for about $15 to $20.

heading: CPSC, Chamberlain Group Announce Recall to Repair Garage Door Openers in Puerto Rico
action: Sears is sending letters to all customers in Puerto Rico known to have purchased the garage door opener. Consumers who purchased these door openers for swinging or sliding doors but did not have them installed by a Sears authorized installer should test the garage door opener's safety reversal system according to instructions in the Owner's Manual. Consumers should allow the door to close on the narrow side of a 2-inch by 4-inch piece of wood held in its path. Consumers should not place themselves in the path of the swinging or sliding door!
incidents_text: The Chamberlain Group is aware of a 4-year old boy in Puerto Rico who died from being caught in a swinging door operated by a Sears Craftsman garage door opener when the safety reversing sensor did not operate.
sold_at: Sears

product_name: Teddy Precious Indian girl and boy stuffed bear
heading: CPSC and The Mazel Co. Announce Teddy Bear Recall
hazard_text: The bears' Native American style clothing has beads on the headband and at the waist or neck. The beads can detach and young children can choke on the beads or inhale them into their lungs, which could lead to death.
action: Consumers should take the bears away from young children immediately and return the bears to the store where purchased for a full refund or a replacement toy.
incidents_text: CPSC is not aware of any injuries involving these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Independent discount and 50-Off stores sold the bears nationwide from July 1996 through December 1996 for about $13.

heading: CPSC, Cosco Announce Recall to Repair Quiet TimeTM Infant Swings
hazard_text: Screws connecting the metal hanger tubes and the U-shaped seat support can loosen and fall out, causing the seat support and seat to fall. Infants can be injured from the fall.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled swings immediately. Repair kit no longer available. New cash incentive is being offered. Do not use these products. Please discard or destroy these products.
incidents_text: Cosco has received over 300 complaints concerning the screws, including 44 reports of injuries such as bumps and bruises on the head and one reported concussion.
sold_at: Juvenile products and discount department stores sold the swings nationwide beginning in February 1993 for about $45 to $49.

heading: CPSC, Etna Products Inc. Announce Recall of Wooden Toy Cars
hazard_text: The glue holding the toy together deteriorates causing the hub caps, headlights, and blocks to separate. Young children could choke on the headlights and blocks or inhale the hub caps into their lungs, which could lead to death.
action: Consumers should take the recalled toys away from children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Etna Products are not aware of any injuries involving these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: The toys were sold nationwide by Benton-Kirby and Walter Drake & Sons mail order catalogues. The toys were also sold by Boardman's (Small Wonders, Something Special, Small Delights), Odd-Job Trading stores, J.D. Yeatts Imports, and Burton Distributors. The toys were sold from 1994 through March 1997 for about $5.

heading: CPSC and Division Sales Inc. Announce Wooden Toy Truck Recall
hazard_text: The toy trucks have wooden balls and figures in the cab that are a small parts choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the recalled toys away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Division Sales Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Dollar-type, discount, hardware, thrift, and drug stores nationwide sold the toys from October 1993 through November 1996 for about $1 to $5.

heading: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall of "Weebles Tractor" Toys
hazard_text: The red plunger located on top of the toy can crack and break apart, presenting a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the toys away from young children immediately and call Playskool for a free replacement.
incidents_text: Playskool has received 42 reports of the toy's plunger cracking or breaking apart. One minor non-choking injury has been reported.
sold_at: Major toy stores and mass merchandise outlets nationwide have sold the toys since January 1996 for about $13.

heading: CPSC, Century Announce Recall to Repair TraveLite SPORT Strollers
hazard_text: Certain models of these strollers have restraint buckles that could unlatch and fold locks that could break causing the stroller to fold unexpectedly if the front wheels of the stroller hit a curb or other stationary object. If the restraint buckle unlatches or the fold locks fail, a child could fall out of the stroller and be injured.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these strollers and discard or destroy the product. The recall program is no longer available.
incidents_text: Century has received approximately 1,400 reports from consumers about these problems, including 78 injuries, such as bumps and bruises.
sold_at: Department, juvenile products, and discount stores nationwide sold these strollers beginning in February 1995 for about $60 to $80.

heading: CPSC, Catton Brothers Corp. Announce Recall of Disney Babies Romper Sets for Boys and Girls
hazard_text: Some of the romper's crotch snaps were improperly attached, exposing a sharp prong. The exposed prong could cause injury to infants.
action: Consumers should stop using the rompers immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Catton Brothers Corp. are not aware of any injuries involving these rompers. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Department and discount stores nationwide sold the romper sets from October 1996 through February 1997 for about $10 to $14.

heading: CPSC, OddzOn Products Inc. Announce Recall of Children's "Starfish" Swimming Vests: Buckles Can Unlatch
hazard_text: The vest's buckles can unlatch unexpectedly while in use, releasing a child into the water. Children could drown if they are released into the water without the aid of the swimming vest.
action: Consumers should take the "Starfish" swimming vests away from children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: OddzOn Products Inc. has received one report of the buckles unlatching. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Toy, sporting goods, and gift stores nationwide sold the swimming vests from May 1996 through March 1997 for about $14.

heading: CPSC Announces Recall of Wooden and Metal Bunk Beds
hazard_text: The bunk beds have openings on the top bunk that present a potential entrapment hazard to young children. The spaces can be large enough for a child's body to pass through, but small enough to entrap a child's head.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled beds immediately and call the company or contact the retailer for a replacement guardrail, retrofit kit, or instructions to help eliminate the potential entrapment hazard. If this cannot be done (for example, firm out of business) then consumers should discard or destroy the product.
incidents_text: CPSC has received reports of 34 children who died from becoming caught in spaces in the top of wooden bunk beds. Thirty-three of those children were 3 years old or younger. In addition, CPSC has received reports of four children who died from becoming caught in spaces in the top of metal bunk beds. All four children were 2 years old or younger.

heading: CPSC and Chandur Hasso Inc. Announce Recall of Extension Cords and Power Strip Surge Protectors
hazard_text: The extension cords and power strip surge protectors present fire, shock, and electrocution hazards.
action: Consumers should stop using these extension cords and power strip surge protectors immediately, and return them to the stores where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Chandur Hasso Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these products. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Retailers in New York and Illinois., such as Hyundai Electronics, Jack's 99? Stores, Star Distributors, and Universal Electronics, sold these cords from February to April 1996 for about $1.

heading: CPSC and Keysheen International Corp. Announce Recall of Children's Chaise Lounge Chairs
hazard_text: If the support leg of the chair's footrest is not fully extended when a child sits down, a child's fingers can get trapped between the support leg and the metal frame, causing a pinching or amputation injury.
action: Consumers should take the chairs away from children immediately. To receive a full refund, consumers should call Keysheen
incidents_text: CPSC has received one report of a 4-year-old child's fingertip being amputated as the child sat down in the folding chaise lounge chair.
sold_at: Retail stores nationwide, including Linens 'n Things, Hecht's, Kohl's, Fred Meyer, Robinsons May, and Hills, sold the chairs from 1994 to 1997 for about $15 to $20.

heading: CPSC and Gold Bug Announce Recall of Carter's Infant Carriers
hazard_text: The adjustable shoulder strap of the carrier can become unfastened or separate from the buckles, resulting in an infant falling from the carrier.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the carrier and call Gold Bug to receive a free replacement.
incidents_text: Gold Bug has received eight reports of straps unfastening or separating, including two reports of infants falling from the carrier and hitting their heads.
sold_at: J.C. Penney sold the infant carriers in some of its stores across the country beginning in June 1996 for about $30.

heading: CPSC and Wear Me Apparel Corp. Recall Infant Boys' Rompers

product_name: Model 10-6200 main drain covers in spas, hot tubs, and swimming pools
heading: CPSC and Hydro-Air Industries Recall Main Drain Covers in Spas, Hot Tubs, and Swimming Pools
hazard_text: Under certain circumstances, a bather's head can be held under water if the bather's hair becomes entangled in the drain cover as the water and hair are drawn through the drain.
action: Consumers should inspect their spas, hot tubs, and swimming pools to determine if the model 10-6200 drain cover is installed. If so, consumers should immediately stop using their spas, hot tubs, and pools and contact Hydro-Air at (800) 230-9560 to receive a free replacement part. Swimming pool owners can contact Hydro-Air at (800) 230-9560 for guidance in the inspection process.
incidents_text: Hydro-Air is aware of two drownings and one near drowning resulting from hair getting trapped in the drain cover.
sold_at: This drain cover was installed in spas, hot tubs, and swimming pools from 1980 to 1995.

heading: CPSC, Tonka Announce Recall of Soft Walkin' Wheels Toy Vehicles
hazard_text: The small wheel hubs can separate from the axle, creating a potential choking hazard.
action: Consumers should take these recalled toys away from children immediately. To receive a free replacement, consumers may call Tonka at 1 (800) 327-8264. Consumers may also return the toys to the store where purchased for a free replacement or full refund.
incidents_text: Tonka has received about 40 reports of wheel hubs separating from the axle, including two reports of children starting to choke. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Major toy stores and mass merchandise outlets nationwide sold these toys beginning in January 1994 for about $15.

heading: CPSC and Division Sales Announce Recall of Baby Buzz Infant Toys
hazard_text: The toy presents a risk of strangulation if hung across a crib or playpen.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled toys immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Division Sales are not aware of any injuries involving these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Dollar Value and other discount stores sold the toys nationwide from December 1995 to December 1996 for about $1.

product_name: Restraint Bars of the Playskool 1-2-3 High Chairs
heading: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall to Repair Restraint Bar of the 1-2-3 High Chair
hazard_text: The restraint bar can crack or break off, which may allow a child who is not secured with the high chair's seat belt to fall from the chair and be injured.
action: As replacement components are no longer available, Playskool is offering consumers $15.00 compensation if they still own this high chair with the affected restraint bar. Consumers should not return the high chairs to retailers, but rather should discard or destroy it.
incidents_text: Playskool has received hundreds of complaints of cracking and breaking restraint bars and 40 reports of injuries to children falling from the high chairs. Injuries primarily involve bumps and bruises; one child sustained a broken collarbone.
sold_at: The Playskool 1-2-3 High Chair was available nationwide at discount juvenile product and department stores for about $65.

product_name: Cabbage Patch Kids® Snacktime Kids dolls, Mattel, Inc.
heading: Mattel and the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission Announce Voluntary Refund Program for Cabbage Patch Kids & Snacktime Kids Dolls
hazard_text: Mattel is taking this action following reports of people getting their hair and fingers caught in the mouths of the dolls.
action: Mattel will offer consumers a full cash refund of $40.
incidents_text: Mattel is taking this action following reports of people getting their hair and fingers caught in the mouths of the dolls. Neither Mattel's nor CPSC's testing of the product has identified a serious safety hazard associated with the dolls.

heading: CPSC and Dairy Queen Recall Toy Water Batons
hazard_text: The end-cap and the balls present a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take these toy batons away from young children, and return them to their local Dairy Queen store. Dairy Queen stores are offering consumers a free kids meal or ice cream sundae for each baton returned.
incidents_text: IDQ has received eight reports of the baton's end-cap coming off. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The toy batons were distributed with kids meals at Dairy Queen stores nationwide from June through October 1996.

heading: CPSC & Mattel Announce Warning for Cabbage Patch Doll
hazard_text: The hazard involves long hair and fingers becoming entangled in the doll's mouth due to its chewing action.
action: CPSC urges consumers to discard the product.
incidents_text: CPSC and Mattel, Inc. are aware of 35 incidents where a child's hair or finger was caught in the mouths of these dolls. No serious injuries have been reported.

heading: CPSC and MDK Inc. Recall Model Trains
hazard_text: If the train derails, the coupler coil spring could overheat creating a potential fire hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop operating the recalled cars, and call MDK Inc. at 800) 866-9986 for information on receiving a free repair.
incidents_text: CPSC and MDK Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these model trains. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Cars were sold through hobby wholesalers and distributed to hobby and specialty retail stores nationwide.

heading: CPSC and Levi Strauss Announce Infant and Toddler Koverall and Shortall Recall
hazard_text: The snap fasteners on the inside legs of these garments may separate, creating a potential choking risk to children.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using these garments and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Levi Strauss are not aware of any injuries involving these garments. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

heading: CPSC and Speidel Announce Children's Identification Bracelet Recall
hazard_text: The bracelets present a choking hazard to children under age 3.
action: Consumers should immediately take these bracelets away from children under age 3, and return the bracelet to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Speidel are not aware of any injuries involving these bracelets. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: The bracelets sold at Wal-Mart, JCPenney, Hills, Cole Gift Centers, and Meijer stores along with other department, discount, and jewelry stores nationwide from June 1995 through December 1996 for about $11 to $16.

heading: CPSC Recalls Highly Flammable Chenille Sweaters
hazard_text: The sale of these sweaters violates the federal Flammable Fabrics Act, and the sweaters present a serious risk of burn injuries. In fact, these sweaters burn faster than newspaper.
action: CPSC urges consumers to immediately stop wearing sweaters they believe may be involved in this recall. These flammable sweaters should be returned to the retailers where purchased. Retailers taking part in this recall will provide a refund or credit.
incidents_text: Although CPSC has not received reports of injuries from these sweaters to date, the agency is issuing this safety notice and recalling the sweaters to prevent injuries from these dangerous products.
sold_at: BCBG Bloomingdale's Dillard's Express Foley's Lerner of New York Limited Too Lord & Taylor Macy's Neiman Marcus Nordstrom Parisian, Inc. Robinson-May

heading: CPSC and Evenflo Warn of Potential Choking Hazard on Houdini Portable Playyards
hazard_text: Small plastic covers from "push caps" used to secure various parts of the playyards together may crack and separate, posing a chocking hazard.
action: Consumers should look for loose, cracked, or missing plastic covers. If any are found, consumers should call Evenflo at (800) 490-7549 immediately to obtain free replacement push caps and installation instructions. Even if no loose, cracked, or missing plastic covers are found, consumers should call for a free warning label.
incidents_text: Evenflo and the CPSC are aware of a number of reports of the plastic caps separating. Although no injuries have been reported, this action is being taken to prevent young children from choking or cutting themselves.

product_name: Santa Candle Holders and Potpourri Simmer Pots
heading: CPSC and Importers Announce Recall of Holiday Candle Holders and Potpourri Simmer Pots
hazard_text: The paint on the Santa candle holders is flammable and the candle accompanying the potpourri simmer pots generates an excessive flame. An additional importer is issuing a warning about a candle that poses a potential fire hazard.
action: Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled candle holders, and return the holders to the store where purchased for a refund. Consumers should immediately discard the votive candle accompanying the candle holder. Consumers should replace the votive candle with one of the same size and only burn the candle in its metal holder.
units: 32,000 Santa candle holders and potpourri simmer pots
incidents_text: Giftco has received two reports of the defective candle setting the candle holder on fire. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The candle holders were sold through dollar-type stores nationwide from October 1995 through November 1996 for about $1.

heading: CPSC and Shelby Ltd. Announce Novelty Product Recalls
hazard_text: The items contain kerosene or other petroleum distillates and many were sold to children. If the paperweights or pens break and leak, the liquid can be hazardous if inhaled into the lungs or swallowed. The liquid could also be combustible, presenting a flammability hazard.
action: Consumers should take the paperweights and pens away from children immediately, and discard or destroy them. The firm is out of business and cannot be contacted.
incidents_text: Shelby Ltd. has received at least 10 reports of the paperweights breaking and releasing their contents. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: The paperweights and pen were sold nationwide through school stores to children from kindergarten through the sixth grade from October through December 1996 for about $4 to $5.

heading: Wooden Toys Recalled Because of Lead Paint
hazard_text: Some of the paint on the toys contains high levels of lead. CPSC standards ban toys containing high levels of lead. Young children might swallow lead if they chewed on these toys.
action: Consumers who purchased these wooden toys from toy stores should return them for a full refund or full credit. Consumers who purchased the toys through Oriental Trading's catalog should call the company at (800) 228-0045 to obtain refund instructions.
incidents_text: Although no reports of illness or injury have been received, this recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of lead poisoning.
sold_at: These two toys were sold from September 1994 to November 1996 through the firm's catalogs for under $4 and through retail stores.

heading: CPSC Announces Recall of Additional Wooden Bunk Beds
hazard_text: The spaces can be large enough for a child's body to pass through, but small enough to entrap the child's head.
action: The manufacturers listed below are participating in this recall to improve the safety of these beds and to meet the requirements of the voluntary standard. Consumers should stop using the recalled beds immediately and call the company or contact the retailer for a replacement guardrail, retrofit kit, or instructions to help eliminate the potential entrapment hazard.
incidents_text: Since 1990, CPSC has received reports of 32 children who died from becoming caught in bunk beds with similar spaces in the top bunk. Thirty-one of those children were ages 3 and under. The most recent death occurred on September 28, 1996. A 3-year-old boy died from becoming caught in a bunk bed manufactured by the Bedder Bunk Company.

heading: CPSC, Price Stern Sloan Announce Exploring Nature Science Activity Kit Recall
hazard_text: The kit is packaged with a compass that may leak fluid containing kerosene. The compass can be hazardous to young children if they ingest the kerosene or inhale it into their lungs.
action: Consumers should take these recalled kits away from children immediately. The firm is out of business. Please discard or destroy these products.
incidents_text: Price Stern Sloan Inc. has received one report of a 16-month-old child who vomited after ingesting fluid from the compass. The kit is intended for children 8 and older.
sold_at: Warehouse clubs, bookstores, chain stores, and whole salers sold the kits nationwide from March 1996 through August 1996 for about $13 to $22.

heading: CPSC Warns of Strangulation Hazard with All Our Kids Portable Cribs/Playpens
hazard_text: The playpens, also known as travelyards or playards, pose a strangulation hazard. They have rotating top rails, which can collapse unexpectedly, trapping a child at the neck in the "V" formed by the collapsed top rail.
action: Consumers who own All Our Kids model 741, 742 and 761 portable cribs/playards should stop using them immediately and destroy them to prevent future use.
incidents_text: The CPSC is aware of 7 babies who strangled in collapsed portable playpens with similar top rail designs made by three other manufacturers. The most recent of these deaths occurred on October 15, 1996.
sold_at: A variety of retailers sold the playpens nationwide from 1992 to 1995.

heading: CPSC, Century Announce Recall to Repair Model 10-710 and 10-810 Playards
hazard_text: The top rails on these playards may collapse unexpectedly, trapping a child at the neck in the "V" formed by the collapsed top rail.
action: Consumers with either a Century Model 10-710 or Model 10-810 Fold-N-Go Playard should stop using the product immediately and call Graco, which now owns the "Century" brand name for a free repair kit and installation instructions. Consumers should not use the playard until the new top rails are installed.
incidents_text: An 18-month-old boy died recently in Centreville, Va., when a Century playard collapsed.
sold_at: The Century Model 10-710, measuring 26 inches by 38 inches, was sold in Toys R Us stores beginning in June 1994 for about $50. The Model 10-810, measuring 28 inches by 41 inches, was sold nationwide beginning in February 1993 in juvenile products and discount stores for about $80.

heading: CPSC and So's U.S.A. Company Announce Recall of "Wood Lock Medicated Balm"
hazard_text: The product, containing more than five percent of methyl salicylate, does not have the required child resistant packaging. Methyl Salicylate can poison young children if ingested, seriously injuring or killing them.
action: Consumers should return the balm to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and So's are not aware of any injuries involving this product. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Drug stores, health food stores, Chinese groceries, and health stores sold the balm in California and Oregon from 1994 through July 1996 for approximately $2.30 for the .85-oz. bottle and $3.45 for the 1.7-oz. bottle.

heading: CPSC, Dolgencorp Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Telephones
hazard_text: The toy's telephone antenna and pieces of plastic from around the base of the antenna can break off, presenting a choking hazard to children under age 3.
action: Consumers should take the toy telephones away from young children immediately and discard or destroy them, or if possible, return them to their nearest Dollar General store for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Dolgencorp Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these toy telephones. The recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Dolgencorp distributed the toys in Dollar General stores in the central part of the country from mid-August to mid-September 1996 for $5 retail.

heading: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall To Repair Mesh on Playards
hazard_text: The mesh on playards made between November 1995 and September 1996 may unravel from the seam, resulting in a possible choking or entanglement hazard.
action: Consumers should call Graco at (800) 345-4109 for a free repair kit and application instructions or write to Customer Affairs, Graco Children's Products Inc., P.O. Box 100, Elverson, PA 19520. Consumers should not use the playard if the netting has started to unravel.
incidents_text: Graco has received 9 reports of toddlers unraveling a strand from the mesh and becoming entangled in it or mouthing it. No serious injuries resulted.
sold_at: The recalled playards were sold nationwide in juvenile products and discount stores such as Toys R Us and Walmart for $35 to $55 each.

heading: CPSC and NBO Group Inc. Announce Lighter Recall
hazard_text: The lighters, which operate with push-button electronic ignition mechanisms to produce the flame, do not have safety devices that prevent young children from igniting the lighters.
action: Consumers should stop using the lighters immediately and return them to the place where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and NBO are not aware of any injuries involving these lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: The lighters were sold individually or from display trays nationwide from September 1994 to March 1996 for $5 to $10 by small retailers of every type.

heading: CPSC, Direct Source International Announce Plastic Halloween Bucket Recall
hazard_text: Dillon Stores of Hutchinson, Kan., and CPSC found prohibited levels of lead in the black, red, and yellow paint, which peels readily from the buckets. The lead paint can cause lead poisoning in young children, who may ingest the paint from the banned buckets.
action: Consumers should take the buckets away from children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund of the purchase price.
incidents_text: CPSC received one report of a child who may have ingested some of the paint from the buckets.
sold_at: Various retail stores, including Dillon Stores and Kroger Company, sold the buckets from August 1996 to October 1996 for about $1 per package.

heading: CPSC and Paik International Announce Cigarette Lighter Recall
hazard_text: The lighters do not have safety devices that prevent young children from igniting the lighters.
action: Consumers should stop using the cigarette lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Paik International are not aware of any injuries involving these cigarette lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Convenience and retail stores in New York sold these cigarette lighters from June 1995 to April 1996 for less than $1 each.

heading: CPSC and Radio Flyer Announce Recall of Little Wood Wagon
hazard_text: The wagons contain a prohibited level of lead in the red painted sides that can cause lead poisoning in young children, who may ingest the paint.
action: Consumers should immediately take the wagons away from children and look for a manufacturing date decal on the bottom of the wagon. If there is no decal, consumers should return the wagon to the store where purchased for an exchange or refund. Consumers may also call Radio Flyer at (800) 621-7613, 24 hours a day, to receive free-of-charge a replacement wagon without leaded paint.
incidents_text: Radio Flyer Inc. and CPSC are not aware of any injuries involving the wagons. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Retailers, including Mills Fleet Farm, The Right Start Catalog and Stores, and True Value Hardware, sold the wagons nationwide from June 1996 through September 1996 for between $20 and $25 each.

heading: CPSC and Candle-lite Announce Recall of Clearfire Candles
hazard_text: The candles could flare up during use, causing the candles' glass holders to overheat and break. Consumers could be burned or injured by broken glass.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled candles immediately, pull out the wick, and then dispose of the gel-like substance. Consumers should remove the UPC label from the bottom of the glass container. In order to receive a $6.00 refund, consumers should mail the wick and the UPC label, along with their name and complete address to: Candle-lite, Post Office Box 42486, Cincinnati, OH 45242.
incidents_text: Candle-lite is aware of 142 instances of candles flaring-up and glass breaking. Several consumers have been burned by hot gel or cut by broken glass.
sold_at: Major discount chain stores sold these candles nationwide from October 1995 through April 1996 for approximately $4.00.

heading: CPSC, Gerry Baby Products Announce Model 602 Deluxe Baby Monitor Recall
hazard_text: Wires inside the monitor may be improperly connected, resulting in the product overheating with the possibility of the monitor causing fire.
action: Consumers should contact Evenflo's Parent Link Consumer Resource Center at (800) 233-5921 for assistance (Gerry Baby Products is out of business, but the Evenflo Company has now taken over in responding to this recall).
incidents_text: Gerry is aware of one fire without injuries involving a Model 602 monitor with this manufacturing error. This information was brought to CPSC's attention by a member of the International Association of Arson Investigators (IAAI). In addition, CPSC has also received reports alleging Model 602 Baby Monitor involvement in two other fires, including one with a fatality and an injury, and 13 incidents of the monitors getting warm to the touch, including one skin burn. Gerry stated that only one report (no injuries) of these 16 claims was conclusively determined to have been caused by the Model 602 monitor.
sold_at: Juvenile product and baby supply stores and department stores sold the recalled monitors nationwide from June 1988 through May 1990.

heading: CPSC and Gerber Products Co. Announce "Flip Fingers Rattle" Recall
hazard_text: The spherical end-caps of the rattle may separate releasing small parts, such as spinning pieces and noise-making beads, which present a choking and inhalation hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the rattles away from children immediately and call Gerber at (800) 4-GERBER. Gerber will send consumers mailing materials and instructions for returning the rattles to the company to receive a refund.
incidents_text: Gerber received five reports of these rattles breaking. CPSC and Gerber have not received any reports of injuries. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: Grocery stores and a few specialty stores sold the rattles nationwide from May 1996 through September 1996 for about $1.40. The rattles came in clear plastic packages on a blue card labeled in part, "Gerber Flip Fingers Rattle ... number 76250.

heading: CPSC, EZ Sales, Twin Oaks Hammock Company, and Safesport Manufacturing Company Announce Recall of Mini-Hammocks
hazard_text: Some hammocks do not have spreader bars. Without spreader bars to hold the mini-hammock bed open, the mini-hammock can twist around a child's neck as he/she is getting into or out of the mini-hammock, resulting in strangulation and death.
action: Consumers should immediately take down mini-hammocks from porches, decks, trees, recreation rooms and other locations. Consumers should return the mini-hammocks to the store where they were purchased for a full refund or a replacement hammock. If consumers do not know the retailer or manufacturer of their net mini-hammock, they should destroy the mini-hammock immediately to prevent strangulation death or injury.
incidents_text: Between 1984 and 1995, CPSC received reports of 12 children between the ages of five and 17 years old who became entangled and died when using net mini-hammocks without spreader bars. CPSC is also aware of an injury to a seven-year-old girl who suffered permanent brain damage from a near-strangulation in a mini-hammock. Another near-fatal incident involved a five-year-old boy who was found entangled in a mini-hammock but was resuscitated by his mother.
sold_at: Sporting goods stores, such as Herman's World of Sports, sold the EZ Sales "Hang Ten" mini-hammocks nationwide from 1979 to 1991 for $6 to $16. Small outdoor equipment stores sold the Twin Oaks mini-hammocks nationwide since the early 1980s for $8 to $14. The Twin Oaks mini-hammocks were also sold through catalogues. Surplus and sporting goods stores sold the Safesport mini-hammocks nationwide from 1994 through 1996 for about $8.

heading: CPSC and Christmas Tree Shops Announce Toy Truck Recall
hazard_text: The toys contain small parts, such as the "driver" figure in the truck's front cab, which may break off during use presenting a potential choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the truck away from young children immediately and return the toy either to the store where purchased or the nearest Christmas Tree Shop.
incidents_text: CPSC is not aware of any injuries involving this toy. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury. The State of Connecticut identified the small parts hazard.
sold_at: Christmas Tree Shops in New England sold the "Engineering Truck" toys from April 1994 through March 1996 for $1 each.

heading: CPSC and Playskool Baby Announce Recall of Playskool Baby Fold N' Travel Infant Carrier
hazard_text: Infants may fall out of the carrier.
action: Consumers who own Fold N' Travel infant carriers should stop using them immediately and return the carriers to Playskool or to the store where purchased, for a full refund. To receive pre-paid shipping materials and for information on returning the carriers, consumers should call Playskool at (800) 752-9755.
units: To receive pre-paid shipping materials and for information on returning the carriers, consumers should call Playskool at (800) 752-9755.
incidents_text: Playskool has received 10 reports of children falling from the carrier, including reports of seven infants who suffered serious head injuries.
sold_at: Children's products retailers sold the Fold N' Travel carriers nationwide from April 1991 through 1993 for approximately $35.00.

heading: CPSC and Kraft Issue Warning for Chillers Sticks for Jell-O Instant Pudding
hazard_text: The plastic Chillers Sticks may break, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately discard the Chillers Sticks. Kraft Foods has recalled the Chillers Sticks from store shelves and will no longer distribute the sticks.
incidents_text: Kraft has received 71 reports of the Chillers Sticks breaking. Kraft is not aware of any injuries. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: An outside supplier manufactured the sticks, which were packaged in sets of six. Kraft distributed the sticks nationwide through an 800-number and supermarkets from early June through mid-July 1996 as part of a promotion for Jell-O pudding.

heading: CPSC, Now Products Announce Recall To Repair Children's Chair
hazard_text: Children can unzip the chair's fabric cover, exposing a thin, clear plastic liner, which could cause choking.
action: Consumers should take the chairs away from children until the chairs have been repaired. For a free repair kit, consumers should call Now Products at (800) 535-3218, extension 33, between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Central time, Monday through Friday.
incidents_text: Now Products is aware of two incidents of children who removed the plastic from the furniture and placed the plastic in their mouth. One child required medical treatment.
sold_at: Department stores sold the chairs with matching ottomans and sofas nationwide from January 1994 through June 1996 for approximately $50.

heading: CPSC and PL Development Announce Recall of CVS Sleep Caplets
hazard_text: The bottles lack the child-resistant packaging required by the Poison Prevention Packaging Act. Diphenhydramine is toxic if accidentally ingested by children and can cause them serious injury or be fatal.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled sleep caplets immediately and return the bottle to the store where purchased for an exchange or full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC, PL Development, and CVS are not aware of any injuries involving this product. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: CVS sold 3,798 bottles of these sleeping caplets from February 26, 1996, to March 19,1996, for approximately $3.89 a bottle.

heading: CPSC and Kids II Announce Recall of SnackTime Stroller Toy Bar
hazard_text: A rattle attached to the bar can break open, releasing small beads. Children could inhale the beads into their lungs, causing serious injury.
action: Consumers should stop using the toy bar immediately and return it to Kids II at 1015 Windward Ridge Parkway, Alpharetta, GA 30202. Kids II will send consumers a replacement stroller toy bar.
incidents_text: Kids II and CPSC are aware of one incident in which a child swallowed a piece of the toy, but was not injured. Kids II reported the hazard to CPSC.
sold_at: Various retail stores and discount centers sold the stroller toy bars nationwide from July 1995 to June 1996 for about $13 to $15.

heading: CPSC, Catton Brothers Corp. Announce Recall of Minnie Mouse Nautical Outfits
hazard_text: A small cloth loop on a bow around the neckline can slide off, presenting a choking hazard to infants.
action: Consumers should stop using the recalled garments immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: Catton Brothers is aware of one incident in which the cloth loop detached from the garment. CPSC and Catton Brothers are not aware of any injuries involving the nautical outfits.
sold_at: Independent retailers sold the garments nationwide from November 1995 through April 1996 for between $10 and $14.

heading: CPSC, Pacific Cycle USA Announce Recall of "Posi Track" Suspension Forks
hazard_text: The forks may crack or separate, causing a rider to lose control of the bicycle and fall.
action: Consumers who own bicycles with the defective suspension forks should stop using the bicycles immediately and call Pacific's service department at (800) 283-3303 for a free replacement fork.
incidents_text: Pacific Cycle USA has received 150 reports of these forks cracking or separating. Eight of these incidents resulted in injuries, including facial and dental injuries, a concussion, a fractured nose, a fractured jaw, cuts, and bruises.
sold_at: Toys "R" Us and Target stores sold the forks nationwide from May 1994 through August 1995 as original equipment on 1994 and 1995 26-inch Pacific Conquest, Cyclone, and Conqueror bicycles.

heading: CPSC, Hedstrom Issue Safety Warning for My Pet Bear Ride-On Toy
hazard_text: The foam covering from the two horizontal, metal support tubes pose a choking hazard on the foam.
action: The firm is out of business and can no longer be contacted.
incidents_text: Hedstrom has received four reports of children biting off pieces of the protective foam. No injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Retail stores sold the My Pet Bear ride-on toy nationwide from January 1995 through May 1996 for about $45.

heading: CPSC and Gibson Greetings Announce Stuffed Animal Recall
hazard_text: The stuffed animals' eyes may separate from the toy, presenting a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should take the bears and cats away from young children immediately and return the toys to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: Gibson Greetings and CPSC are not aware of any injuries involving this toy. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
sold_at: The toys were sold nationwide at a price of approximately $15 each in grocery stores, card shops, and specialty retailers from March 15, 1996 to April 22, 1996.

heading: CPSC and Lerma Import Announce Pacifier Recall
hazard_text: The pacifiers are banned under the Federal Hazardous Substances Act because they can break apart, releasing small parts, which present a choking hazard to young children.
action: Consumers should immediately take the pacifiers away from small children and return the pacifiers to the store where purchased for a full refund.
incidents_text: CPSC and Lerma Import are not aware of any injuries associated with these pacifiers. CPSC requested that Lerma Import conduct this recall to prevent the possibility of injury. CPSC identified the hazardous pacifiers during routine surveillance.
sold_at: Retail stores in the Dallas, Texas area sold the pacifiers from May 1995 through May 1996 for $.25 each.

heading: CPSC and Little Tikes Announce Cozy Highback Swing Recall
hazard_text: The swing may tip forward and possibly flip over while a child is swinging in it.
action: Consumers should stop using the swing and call Little Tikes at (800) 321-0183 to exchange it for a different model swing, or comparable Little Tikes product.
incidents_text: Little Tikes has received 55 reports of the swing tipping forward. No serious injuries have been reported.
sold_at: Toy stores, department stores, and discount stores sold the swing nationwide from January 1996 through April 1996 for about $15 to $18.

heading: CPSC and Man's Trading Co. Announce Recall of Rolling Clock Push Toy
hazard_text: If the toy is dropped, it can break into small parts, such as the toy's decorative beads and the arms of the clock. Small children can choke on or inhale these small parts.
action: Consumers should take the toys away from children immediately and return the toys to the store where purchased for a full refund.
